title: Polar Nights
source: Disney Frozen Polar Nights Cast Into Darkness (Jen Calonita, Mari Mancusi) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).epub

chapters.title: Chapter One: Elsa
chapters.en:
THUMP…

Thump…

Thump…

Queen Anna of Arendelle awoke with a start. She jerked up in bed, her heart beating madly in her chest. Her gaze darted from left to right—she pricked up her ears. The hairs on the back of her neck stood on end. What was that noise? That horrible noise? It seemed to be coming from outside, somewhere in the garden….

Thump…

Thump…

Thump…

Anna slipped out of bed. Headed to the door. As queen, she was responsible for keeping her people safe. Which meant she needed to investigate. Even if she was scared. Even if she was terrified at what she would find outside.

Her hand wrapped slowly around the door handle. She turned the knob—

“No, Anna! Don’t do it! It’s a trap! I know it’s a trap!” Olaf, the talking snowman, cried out in horror.

He anxiously leapt out of his seat, somehow managing to lose both stick arms. Racing around the campfire, he bounced over Bruni—the salamander-like Fire Spirit, who had been curled up on a small pile of magical snow—and then threw himself between Anna and Sven the reindeer, who had been “telling” the tale of terror in a voice that sounded suspiciously like Kristoff’s.

“Don’t you hurt my Anna!” he yelled at Sven.

Sven snorted and sniffed the snowman’s carrot nose. Olaf took a wary step backward, bumping into Anna and almost losing his head in the process—literally. She laughed and set it back on straight before giving it an affectionate pat.

“Don’t worry, Olaf,” she said comfortingly. “It’s only a story.”

“Also,” Elsa added, retrieving Olaf’s detached arms and tossing them to her sister, who reaffixed them to his body, “I’m pretty sure I know where this is going.”

“Shh!” scolded Kristoff, wagging a finger at Elsa. “No spoilers!” He turned to his reindeer encouragingly. “Go ahead, Sven. They’re obviously just jealous of your superior spooky storytelling skills.”

Elsa couldn’t suppress a small smile as she watched the reindeer give another longing look at Olaf’s carrot nose, which was no longer within nibbling reach. She wondered, not for the first time, how badly Sven must wish he could talk for real, without having his buddy Kristoff “interpret” for him. Then again, Sven did a pretty good job of letting everyone know what he was feeling without having to speak a word. Even if that feeling was just concern over where his next carrot to munch on might be coming from.

Olaf sighed and retreated back to his seat on the log next to Elsa. She gave him a comforting squeeze, then looked around the campfire circle, her heart suddenly feeling very full. The Enchanted Forest camping trip had been her idea, and she was thankful her sister, Anna, had found the time to get away from her queenly duties for a night to join her. Elsa knew all too well that being queen of Arendelle was a full-time job. After all, it had been her position for years before Anna took over two months earlier. She was proud of her younger sister for taking it all on without a complaint. In fact, Anna seemed to enjoy the challenge. And Elsa knew the people of Arendelle loved Anna as much as she loved them.

But that was nothing compared to the love between these two sisters. Even though they now lived apart, they both made sure they were never too busy to spend time together regularly, either in the Enchanted Forest like they were now, or for weekly family game nights back in Arendelle, which still felt like a second home to Elsa. (Anna had even let Elsa keep her bedroom, which had once been their mother and father’s, knowing how much it meant to her sister.) And, starting the next day, Elsa was planning to spend an extended holiday in Arendelle to help Anna prepare for her very first Polar Nights celebration as queen.

The Polar Nights festivities came once a year to Arendelle around the time of the winter solstice—and Elsa’s birthday! It was a time when the land was wrapped in perpetual twilight, the sun never fully rising for an entire week. But it wasn’t dull or too dark, like it could be in some kingdoms further to the north. Instead, the Arendellian skies were bathed in a beautiful dusky blue haze with plenty of light to see by. Some years, if they were lucky, they would even be treated to breathtaking views of the Northern Lights themselves, the aurora borealis painting the sky in brilliant emerald green.

Once upon a time, according to the history books, people had been frightened by the Polar Nights phenomenon, believing the sun had died and that the world would soon expire along with it. But now they knew this was only a temporary pause. Soon the sun would rise again, like a phoenix from the ashes, and life would begin anew.

But in the meantime, it was a great excuse to party.

It was also a time of migration for the Northuldra. No longer stuck in the Enchanted Forest, they were looking forward to journeying across the land, leading their reindeer to new and fertile pastures. So Elsa had said her temporary goodbyes to her new friends as they headed north, assuring them she’d see them soon.

After all, even the Snow Queen needed a little rest and relaxation every once in a while.

She turned back to Kristoff and Sven, realizing they were continuing their story.

Anna crept quietly out of the house and into the gardens beyond. It was dark—so dark she could not see her hands in front of her face—and she held her breath as she walked, too fearful to even make a sound. Suddenly, lightning flashed from the sky, illuminating the field in front of her. Anna gasped at what she saw. Or rather, what she didn’t see. And suddenly she realized what night this truly was: the night she thought would never come.

Sven drummed his hooves against the ground dramatically. Olaf’s eyes grew wide with fright. He cuddled a little closer to Elsa.

“The night…the night completely…the night completely without…” Kristoff teased.

“Hope?” Olaf squeaked. “Life? A slim but real chance for a better tomorrow?”

“Or maybe…carrots?” Elsa suggested wryly.

“Carrots!” Sven/Kristoff roared after giving Elsa a scolding look. “It was the night without carrots.”

Olaf screeched in horror, grabbing his nose protectively. Sven snorted while Kristoff guffawed in glee.

Elsa rolled her eyes. “A night without carrots,” she deadpanned. “How…terrifying.”

“Oh, please! That’s not terrifying! That’s not even remotely scary!” Anna protested, looking a lot more annoyed by the silly twist in the tale than she probably had any right to be. She shook her head, her copper-colored locks swinging from side to side. “I mean, so what? No carrots! We could just eat broccoli instead. Or lettuce. Or chocolate.” She pursed her lips. “Now, a night without chocolate. That would be scary.” She poked Kristoff playfully in the arm. “Which is why I’m really hoping you didn’t forget our—”

“Choco-versary,” Kristoff finished with a grin. He slung his arm around Anna’s shoulders and pulled her close. “Come on now. Give me a little credit. How could I possibly forget the sixth anniversary of our very first time eating chocolate together? I mean, it’s downright historic. By all rights, it should be added to the annals of Arendelle history someday!”

Anna beamed. Meanwhile, Elsa couldn’t help emit-ting a small snort. Choco-versary. How ridiculously cute could one couple be? Even though Kristoff drove her crazy sometimes, she had to admit he was the perfect match for her sister. She couldn’t wait for them to get married someday and have little Annas and Kristoffs running around Arendelle. She was definitely planning on being the cool aunt. Literally.

Anna leaned against Kristoff, looking up at him with wide, overly innocent blue eyes. “And to celebrate this momentous, historical occasion, you’re going to…?”

Kristoff shook his head, pushing her back upright. “Nope. Not a chance. Good try, though.”

Anna groaned. “No fair,” she said, pretending to be grumpy. “We’re engaged now, which means there should be no secrets between us.”

“He’s not keeping a secret!” Olaf piped in helpfully. “He just hasn’t come up with anything yet!”

“Olaf!” Kristoff cried. “You weren’t supposed to—”

“Wait, what?” Anna cried in mock horror. “You don’t have a plan for our Choco-versary yet? It’s less than a week away!”

“I know,” Kristoff assured her, shooting Olaf a deadly look. “I’m just deciding which of my epic anniversary ideas is the right one to move forward with. I want to make sure everything is absolutely perfect for the love of my life, that’s all.” He reached for her hand, pressing his mouth against her palm.

“Oh.” Anna pursed her lips, as if trying to decide if he was teasing or not. “I guess that makes sense….”

Elsa stifled a laugh, deciding it was time for a subject change before poor Kristoff got in any more trouble. “How are the preparations for the Polar Nights festivities going?”

Anna sat up straight, all thoughts of chocolate visibly stampeding out of her head. This was her favorite topic these days. “Oh, they’re going amazing!” she declared. “I’ve planned all sorts of activities: ice-carving contests, reindeer racing…and dance parties! So many dance parties!”

“I can’t wait,” Elsa said. “I know it’s going to be great.”

“I’m just glad you’re coming,” Anna said, smiling at her sister. “And just think! This year we’ll have the Spirits to help, too!” She turned to Bruni, who had gone back to lounging on a rock. “Are you going to help us light our bonfires, little one?”

Bruni bounced up and down, sparks of purple flame sputtering from its back, clearly excited about the task. Elsa smiled and beckoned to the Fire Spirit. It leapt into her lap and curled up happily as she stroked it with an icy finger, helping it cool down again.

“Sounds amazing. Sure to be the best week ever. Now can we get back to the scary stories?” Olaf begged, bouncing on his log. “I’ve got the best one! It’s all about Samantha and her—”

“Sorry, Olaf,” Kristoff interjected. “But it’s my turn, actually.”

“Uh, didn’t you just have a turn?” Anna asked.

“Nope. That was Sven, remember?” Kristoff said with a mischievous grin.

“Oh. Right.” Anna snorted. “Sven told the story.”

“And it was the best story ever!” Kristoff declared in Sven’s voice. The reindeer, who was standing beside him, just rolled his eyes.

“By all means, Kristoff,” Elsa said with an impish smile, “go right ahead.”

“Why, thank you, your Snow Queen-ness,” Kristoff replied, clearing his throat. He leaned forward, his blue eyes shining brightly in the firelight. “Okay, here’s my tale, which I once heard from the ice harvesters I worked with when I was growing up. But be warned, it is truly terrifying. Horribly horrific. Younger viewers”—he glanced knowingly at Olaf—“might want to leave the campfire.”

Olaf huffed, crossing his arms in front of his chest. “Please. As long as it’s not about carrots, I’ll be fine.”

Kristoff shrugged. “Don’t say I didn’t warn you.” He turned back to the two sisters. “You see, this isn’t just any old story. It’s actually true. It happened not very far from Arendelle, either. In fact, it happened on this very night, fifty years ago today.”

Elsa leaned forward, curious despite herself. “Oh, yeah?”

“You know the kingdom of Vesterland, right?”

“Of course. That’s King Jonas and his daughter Princess Mari’s kingdom,” Anna replied, naming her friends who lived in a neighboring land. She and Mari had become great buddies a few years earlier, and they still kept in touch.

Kristoff nodded. “Right. But, you see, it wasn’t always theirs. Once upon a time, it belonged to two sisters. Two princesses, to be precise.”

“Hmm…” Elsa said with a smile. “Sounds vaguely familiar.”

“Actually, no.” Kristoff shook his head. “These princesses were nothing like you and Anna. In fact, they did not get along at all. The younger sister, Inger, hated her older sister, Sissel. Sissel, you see, had everything that Inger always wanted. Sissel was beautiful. She was kind. She was special in every way. She was to be Vesterland’s future queen when she came of age. And Inger, well, she was…”

“Completely ordinary?” Olaf guessed. Anna shot him an impatient look.

“Consumed with jealousy,” Kristoff corrected. “She wanted nothing more than to get rid of her older sister so she could ascend the throne herself.”

“Unlike me!” Anna broke in. “I thought Elsa made an amazing queen. Not that I wasn’t fine with taking over for her, of course. We’re both exactly where we should be now.” She threw a smile to her sister. Elsa smiled back, reaching across to squeeze Anna’s hand.

Kristoff groaned. “Can I get back to my scary story now?”

“Please do! It’s absolutely riveting so far!” Olaf declared. He was sitting on the edge of his log.

“Why, thank you, Olaf,” Kristoff said. He leaned in again. “Well, one day, Inger got her wish. While on a trip to Arendelle, she caught her sister standing by the rushing river—alone. Seeing her moment, Inger snuck behind her and shoved her in! Sissel struggled to swim, but the current was too strong. She screamed for help, begging her sister to save her. But Inger only laughed at her, watching with cruel glee as Sissel went over a huge waterfall and drowned.”

“Whoa!” Anna burst out. “So not where I thought this was going!” Kristoff shot her a look. “Oh…sorry.” She clamped a hand over her mouth. “Please continue.”

Kristoff clasped his hands together. “Well, after that, Inger thought she had won. That she would go back home and take her sister’s place as queen. But someone witnessed her evil deed and reported it back to your grandfather, King Runeard. He arrested Inger and put her on a prison ship. She was to be banished from Arendelle—and Vesterland—forever.”

“Our grandfather doing something just and good? That’s…unexpected,” Elsa remarked dryly, raising an eyebrow.

After all, their grandfather hadn’t exactly been a model king during his reign. Power hungry, fearmongering, yes. Not to mention all the harm he’d done to the Northuldra, their mother’s people, by deceiving them into supporting his dam project, which would dry up their lands and destroy their way of life.

“Right? But, sadly, Sissel never got justice. The prison ship Inger was on went down at sea before it could ever reach its destination,” Kristoff declared with a dramatic flourish. “And Inger—like her sister—also drowned.”

“Well!” Olaf piped up. “That story was indeed terrifying. Okay, Kristoff. You win. Perhaps we can toast marshmallows now?” He looked hopefully at the group.

“Hold on, Olaf. That’s not the end of my story,” Kristoff scolded. “In fact, it’s only the beginning. Because Sissel, you see, didn’t really die. Or at least she didn’t stay dead. Instead, she came back as a horrible creature known as a draugr.”

Something about the word sent an involuntary shiver down Elsa’s spine. She felt a slight shift in the wind, and goose bumps formed on her arm. She tried to smooth them down with her hand. “A draugr? What’s a draugr?” she asked, even though she wasn’t entirely sure she wanted to know.

Anna raised her hand eagerly. “Ooh! I know! I know!” she cried. “I read all about them in this book I found in the secret room in the castle library. They’re creatures of old folklore, and they supposedly cause terrible storms when they show up. People used to blame them when the weather got bad.”

Kristoff nodded approvingly. “That’s exactly right.”

“You’re so smart,” Elsa teased, poking Anna. Anna shrugged sheepishly.

“And so the evil draugr who used to be sweet Sissel began to roam the land,” Kristoff continued, “leaving havoc in its wake. No longer human, no longer kind or good. It was now nothing more than a soulless monster ready to seek revenge against those who did it wrong.”

“Moral of the story? Always be nice to your sister,” Anna concluded. She grinned at Elsa. “Got it!”

Elsa smiled back at her, though for some reason she still felt a little uneasy. Maybe because it was such an unsettling story. Or perhaps it was the fact that she hadn’t always been the best sister herself. She tried to imagine Anna coming back as an evil monster to seek revenge, but couldn’t exactly picture it. Mostly because the only monstrous thing about Anna was her appetite for chocolate.

“So where is the draugr now?” Olaf asked, his eyes still wide and terrified. “You said this story was true. Does that mean the draugr’s still out there somewhere?”

“Of course it is,” Kristoff replied, turning his attention back to the snowman. His thick eyebrows furrowed. He lowered his voice by a menacing octave. “And it’s said that if you tell its story—especially tonight, the night it all happened—you will awaken it from its slumber and it will rise again, renewing its never-ending quest for revenge.”

Kristoff raised his arms in front of him, casting dark shadows across Olaf’s frightened face. “So, my little snowman friend, the next time the skies grow dark…or the rain begins to fall…beware. Because it could be a simple storm. Or it could be Sinister Sissel, lurking just behind you in the shadows. Ready to—”

CRACK!

Suddenly thunder boomed from above. Lightning streaked across the sky. Olaf screamed, leaping into Elsa’s arms.

“The draugr! It’s Sinister Sissel!” he cried. “She’s come to get us all!”

咚……咚……咚……阿伦黛尔的安娜女王猛地惊醒。

她从床上弹坐起来，心在胸口疯狂地跳。

她的目光左右扫视——竖起了耳朵。

她后脖颈的寒毛都竖了起来。

那是什么声音？

那可怕的声响？

似乎是从外面传来的，在花园的某个地方……

咚……咚……咚……安娜悄悄溜下床。

朝门口走去。

身为女王，她有责任保护子民的安全。

也就是说，她得去查看一下。

就算她害怕。

就算她对外面会发现什么吓得要命。

她的手缓缓握住了门把手。

她转动把手——"不，安娜！

别开门！

这是个陷阱！

我知道这是个陷阱！"会说话的雪人奥拉夫惊恐地喊道。

他慌张地从座位上跳起来，不知怎么竟把两根树枝手臂都甩掉了。

他绕着篝火飞奔，从火灵布伦尼身上蹦了过去——那只像火蜥蜴一样的火灵正蜷缩在一小堆魔法雪上——随后一下子插到安娜和驯鹿斯文中间；斯文刚才正用一种听起来特别像克斯托夫的声音"讲述"那个恐怖故事。"你别想伤我的安娜！"他对着斯文大吼。

斯文打了个响鼻，嗅了嗅雪人那胡萝卜鼻子。

奥拉夫警惕地后退一步，撞上了安娜，差点把脑袋也弄掉了——字面意义上的掉。

安娜笑了，把他的头摆正，又亲昵地拍了拍。"别担心，奥拉夫，"她安慰道，"只是个故事而已。" "还有，"艾莎接过奥拉夫掉下来的手臂，丢给妹妹，妹妹把它们重新装回雪人身上，补充道，"我差不多知道这故事要往哪儿发展了。" "嘘！"克斯托夫朝艾莎晃着手指训斥，"不许剧透！"他鼓励地转向自己的驯鹿，"继续，斯文。

他们明显只是嫉妒你高超的鬼故事讲述技巧。"艾莎忍不住露出一丝微笑，看着驯鹿又恋恋不舍地瞅了一眼奥拉夫的胡萝卜鼻子——那鼻子已经够不着嚼了。

她不止一次地想，斯文该多希望自己能真的说话，而不用让伙伴克斯托夫替他"翻译"。

不过话说回来，斯文即使一言不发，也挺能让大家知道他在想什么。

哪怕那种想法只是担心下一根要啃的胡萝卜从哪儿来。

奥拉夫叹了口气，退回艾莎身边圆木上的座位。

她给了他一个安慰的拥抱，然后环顾篝火一圈，心里忽然满满的。

这次魔法森林露营是她的主意，她很感激妹妹安娜能抽空放下女王的职责，陪她过一夜。

艾莎太清楚了，当阿伦黛尔的女王是份全职工作。

毕竟，在安娜两个月前接任之前，这位置她坐了好些年。

她为妹妹毫无怨言地扛起一切而感到骄傲。

事实上，安娜似乎还挺享受这份挑战。

而且艾莎知道，阿伦黛尔的百姓爱安娜，正如她爱他们一样。

但比起这两姐妹之间的爱，那都不算什么。

尽管如今她们分开居住，但两人都确保自己再忙也会定期相聚——要么像现在这样在魔法森林，要么回阿伦黛尔过每周的家庭游戏之夜，那里对艾莎来说仍像个第二故乡。

（安娜甚至让艾莎保留了她那间卧室，那曾是父母亲的房间，因为她知道这对妹妹意义非凡。）而从第二天起，艾莎打算在阿伦黛尔长住一阵，帮安娜筹备她作为女王的首个极夜节庆典。

极夜节每年冬天至日前后降临阿伦黛尔——也正是艾莎的生日！

那段时间大地笼罩在永恒的暮色里，整整一周太阳都不会完全升起。

但不像更北边的一些王国那样沉闷或太黑。

相反，阿伦黛尔的天空浸在美丽的暮蓝色微光中，光线充足，足以看清明亮。

有些年份，运气好的话，他们还能欣赏到北极光本身的震撼景象，极光把天空染成明亮的翡翠绿。

据史书记载，从前人们曾对极夜现象感到恐惧，以为太阳死了，世界也将随之终结。

但现在他们知道，这不过是一段暂时的停顿。

很快太阳会像凤凰涅槃般重新升起，生命也将重新开始。

不过在此期间，这倒是个开派对的好借口。

对北地人来说，这也是迁徙的时节。

他们不再被困在魔法森林，正盼着跨越大地，引领驯鹿前往肥沃的新牧场。

所以艾莎在向新朋友们道别时，他们正朝北进发，她向他们保证很快会再相见。

毕竟，连冰雪女王偶尔也需要休息放松一下。

她转回克斯托夫和斯文，发现他们还在继续讲故事。

安娜悄悄溜出屋子，走进屋外的花园。

四周漆黑——黑得她连眼前的手都看不见——她屏住呼吸走着，害怕得连声都不敢出。

突然，天空中闪过一道闪电，照亮了她面前的田野。

安娜看到眼前的景象，倒吸一口凉气。

或者说，是她没看到的景象。

她忽然意识到，这究竟是哪一个夜晚：那个她以为永远不会到来的夜晚。

斯文戏剧性地用蹄子敲打着地面。

奥拉夫吓得瞪大了眼睛。

他往艾莎身边缩了缩。"那个夜晚……那个完全……那个完全没有……"克斯托夫逗他。"希望？"奥拉夫尖声问。"生命？

一个渺茫却真实、通往更美好明天的机会？""或者……胡萝卜？"艾莎挖苦地提议。"胡萝卜！"斯文/克斯托夫在瞪了艾莎一眼后吼道。"那是没有胡萝卜的夜晚。"奥拉夫惊恐地尖叫，护住自己的鼻子。

斯文打了个响鼻，克斯托夫则乐得哈哈大笑。

艾莎翻了个白眼。"没有胡萝卜的夜晚，"她面无表情地说，"多……吓人啊。""噢，得了吧！

那才不吓人！

那根本一点都不可怕！"安娜抗议道，对这个荒唐的转折比她本该有的样子还要恼火。

她摇摇头，铜色的发丝随之左右摆动。"我是说，那又怎样？

没有胡萝卜！

我们可以吃西兰花代替。

或者生菜。

或者巧克力。"她抿起嘴唇。"现在，一个没有巧克力的夜晚。

那才叫吓人。"她顽皮地戳了戳克斯托夫的胳膊。"所以我才真希望你没有忘记我们的——""巧克力纪念日，"克斯托夫咧嘴笑着接了下去。

他一把搂住安娜的肩膀，把她拉近。"好啦。

给我点信任嘛。

我怎么可能忘了我们一起第一次吃巧克力的六周年纪念日？

我是说，这简直具有历史意义。

按理说，将来总有一天该写进阿伦黛尔史册！"安娜眉开眼笑。

与此同时，艾莎忍不住轻轻哼了一声。

巧克力纪念日。

一对情侣能可爱到什么地步啊。

尽管克斯托夫有时把她逼疯，她不得不承认，他是妹妹的绝配。

她等不及他们哪天结婚，让小安娜们和小克斯托夫们在阿伦黛尔满地跑。

她绝对打算当那个最酷的姨妈。

字面意义上的。

安娜靠在克斯托夫身上，抬起头用那双过分天真的大蓝眼睛望着他。"为了庆祝这个重大、有历史意义的日子，你要……？"克斯托夫摇摇头，把她推直。"没门。

想都别想。

不过试得不错。"安娜嘟囔着。"不公平，"她装出一副不高兴的样子说，"我们现在都订婚了，也就是说我们之间不该有秘密。""他可没保密！"奥拉夫热心地插嘴，"他只是还没想出来呢！""奥拉夫！"克斯托夫叫道，"你不该——""等等，什么？"安娜假装惊恐地叫，"你还没想好我们的巧克力纪念日计划？

离现在不到一周了！""我知道，"克斯托夫向她保证，给了奥拉夫一个要命的眼神，"我只是在决定，我那些超棒的纪念日点子里，哪一个才该推进。

我只想确保为我生命中的挚爱，一切都绝对完美，仅此而已。"他伸手握住她的手，把嘴贴在她的掌心。"噢。"安娜抿起嘴唇，像在判断他是不是在逗自己。"我想那说得通……"艾莎憋住笑，觉得是时候换个话题，免得可怜的克斯托夫再惹上麻烦。"极夜节的筹备进行得怎么样？"安娜立刻坐直，关于巧克力的念头明显从脑中撤了个精光。

这是她近来最爱的话题。"噢，棒极了！"她宣布，"我策划了各种各样的活动：冰雕比赛、驯鹿赛跑……还有舞会！

好多好多的舞会！""我等不及了，"艾莎说，"我知道一定会很精彩。""你能来我太高兴了，"安娜对妹妹笑着说，"而且你想想！

今年我们还有精灵们帮忙呢！"她转向布伦尼，它已经回去趴在石头上歇着了。"小家伙，你会帮我们点燃篝火吗？"布伦尼上下蹦跳，背上噗噗喷出紫色火苗，显然对这任务很兴奋。

艾莎微笑着向火灵招手。

它跳进她怀里，开心地蜷起来，她用冰冷的手指抚摸它，帮它再次降温。"听起来太棒了。

绝对是有史以来最棒的一周。

现在能回到吓人故事吗？"奥拉夫在圆木上蹦着恳求，"我有一个最棒的！

是关于萨曼莎和她——""抱歉，奥拉夫，"克斯托夫打断，"但其实轮到我了。""呃，你不是刚讲完一轮吗？"安娜问。"没啊。

那是斯文，记得吗？"克斯托夫淘气地笑着说。"噢。

对。"安娜哼了一声，"斯文讲了故事。""那是有史以来最棒的故事！"克斯托夫用斯文的声音宣布。

站在他身旁的那头驯鹿只是翻了个白眼。"请便，克斯托夫，"艾莎带着顽皮的微笑说，"讲吧。""哎哟，谢啦，冰雪女王阁下，"克斯托夫清了清嗓子回答。

他凑上前，蓝眼睛在火光中闪闪发亮。"好，这是我的故事，是我小时候和一起采冰的工友那儿听来的。

不过先警告你们，这真的吓人。

恐怖至极。

年轻观众"——他意味深长地瞥了奥拉夫一眼——"也许该离开篝火了。"奥拉夫哼了一声，双臂交叉在胸前。"拜托。

只要不是关于胡萝卜，我没事。"克斯托夫耸耸肩。"别说我没警告过你们。"他转回两姐妹。"你们看，这可不只是一个老掉牙的故事。

这是真事。

而且就发生在离阿伦黛尔不远的地方。

事实上，就发生在今天的这个夜晚，五十年前的今天。"艾莎好奇地凑上前，连自己都意外。"噢，是吗？""你们知道维斯特兰王国吧？""当然。

那是乔纳斯国王和他女儿玛丽公主的王国，"安娜回答，提到了住在邻国的朋友们。

她和玛丽几年前成了好朋友，至今还保持联络。

克斯托夫点点头。"对。

不过你们看，它并不一直是他们的。

从前，它属于两姐妹。

准确说，是两位公主。""嗯……"艾莎笑着说，"听起来有点耳熟。""其实不是，"克斯托夫摇摇头，"这两位公主跟你和安娜一点都不像。

事实上，她们相处得糟透了。

妹妹英格，恨死了姐姐西塞尔。

你们看，西塞尔拥有英格一直想要的一切。

西塞尔很美。

她善良。

她在各方面都很特别。

她成年后将成为维斯特兰未来的女王。

而英格嘛，她……""完全平凡？"奥拉夫猜道。

安娜不耐烦地瞪了他一眼。"被嫉妒吞噬了，"克斯托夫纠正，"她只想除掉姐姐，好自己登上王位。""不像我！"安娜插嘴，"我觉得艾莎是个超棒的女王。

当然，我接她的班也没问题。

我们现在都处在该在的位置。"她朝妹妹笑了笑。

艾莎回以微笑，伸手过去捏了捏安娜的手。

克斯托夫叹气。"我现在能回到我的吓人故事了吗？""请讲！

目前简直引人入胜！"奥拉夫宣布。

他坐在圆木边上。"哎哟，谢啦，奥拉夫，"克斯托夫说。

他又凑近了些。"好吧，有一天，英格如愿以偿。

在一次前往阿伦黛尔的旅途中，她撞见姐姐独自站在湍急的河边。

英格看准时机，悄悄绕到她身后，把她推进了河里！

西塞尔挣扎着游泳，但水流太急。

她尖叫求救，求姐姐救她。

但英格只是嘲笑她，残忍地幸灾乐祸，看着西塞尔跌下巨大的瀑布溺亡。""哇！"安娜脱口而出，"我完全没想到会往这方向走！"克斯托夫瞥了她一眼。"噢……抱歉。"她用手捂住嘴。"请继续。"克斯托夫双手交握。"嗯，之后，英格以为自己赢了。

以为能回家取代姐姐当上女王。

但有人目睹了她的恶行，报告给了你们的祖父鲁内尔德国王。

他逮捕了英格，把她送上了一艘囚船。

她将被永远逐出阿伦黛尔——还有维斯特兰。""我们的祖父做了公正而善良的事？

这……真意外，"艾莎扬起眉毛，干巴巴地说。

毕竟，他们的祖父在位时可算不上模范国王。

野心勃勃、制造恐慌，没错。

更别提他为了大坝工程欺骗北地人——他们母亲的民族——让他们支持建坝，那会抽干他们的土地，毁掉他们的生活方式。"对吧？

但可悲的是，西塞尔从未得到正义。

英格所在的囚船还没抵达目的地就沉入了海中，"克斯托夫夸张地一挥手宣布，"而英格——和她的姐姐一样——也淹死了。""好哇！"奥拉夫插嘴，"那故事确实吓人。

好吧，克斯托夫。

你赢了。

或许我们现在可以烤棉花糖了？"他满怀希望地看着大家。"等等，奥拉夫。

我的故事还没完呢，"克斯托夫训斥，"事实上，这还只是个开头。

因为你们看，西塞尔并没有真的死。

至少她没一直死着。

相反，她变成了一个叫亡者（draugr）的可怕怪物回来了。"这个词让艾莎不由自主地背脊一凉。

她感到风微微一变，手臂上起了鸡皮疙瘩。

她试着用手把疙瘩抚平。"亡者？

什么是亡者？"她问，尽管不太确定自己是否想知道。

安娜急切地举起手。"噢！

我知道！

我知道！"她喊道，"我在城堡图书馆密室找到的那本书里，全读到过它们。

它们是古老传说里的生物，据说出现时会引来可怕的暴风雨。

以前天气一坏，人们就怪它们。"克斯托夫赞许地点头。"完全正确。""你真聪明，"艾莎逗她，戳了戳安娜。

安娜不好意思地耸耸肩。"于是，曾经温柔的西塞尔变成的邪恶亡者开始在大地上游荡，"克斯托夫继续，"所到之处一片狼藉。

不再是人类，不再善良或美好。

它现在不过是个没有灵魂的怪物，准备向那些亏待它的人复仇。""故事的寓意？

永远对你好妹妹，"安娜总结。

她对艾莎咧嘴一笑。"明白啦！"艾莎回她一个微笑，尽管不知为何她仍觉得有点不安。

也许是因为这是个让人不安的故事。

又或许是因为，她自己并非一直都是个好姐姐。

她试着想象安娜变成邪恶怪物回来复仇，却怎么也想不出那画面。

主要是因为安娜身上唯一"怪物"的地方，就是她对巧克力的胃口。"那亡者现在在哪儿？"奥拉夫问，眼睛仍瞪得大大的，满是恐惧。"你说这故事是真的。

那是不是说亡者还在外面的某个地方？""当然在，"克斯托夫回答，把注意力转回雪人身上。

他浓密的眉毛皱了起来。

他把声音压低了一个危险的八度。"据说，如果你讲它的故事——尤其是在今晚，一切发生的那个夜晚——你就会把它从沉睡中唤醒，它会再次崛起，重燃那永无止境的复仇之路。"克斯托夫在身前举起双臂，在奥拉夫惊恐的脸上投下黑暗的阴影。"所以，我的小雪人朋友，下次天色变暗……或雨开始落下……可要当心。

因为那可能只是一场普通的暴风雨。

也可能那是"阴森西塞尔"，正潜伏在你身后的阴影里。

准备——" 咔嚓！

突然，头顶炸响一声惊雷。

闪电划过天空。

奥拉夫尖叫着，跳进艾莎怀里。"亡者！

是阴森西塞尔！"他喊道，"她来抓我们所有人了！"

sentences.en: THUMP… Thump… Thump… Queen Anna of Arendelle awoke with a start.
sentences.zh: 咚……咚……咚……阿伦黛尔的安娜女王猛地惊醒。

sentences.en: She jerked up in bed, her heart beating madly in her chest.
sentences.zh: 她从床上弹坐起来，心在胸口疯狂地跳。

sentences.en: Her gaze darted from left to right—she pricked up her ears.
sentences.zh: 她的目光左右扫视——竖起了耳朵。

sentences.en: The hairs on the back of her neck stood on end.
sentences.zh: 她后脖颈的寒毛都竖了起来。

sentences.en: What was that noise?
sentences.zh: 那是什么声音？

sentences.en: That horrible noise?
sentences.zh: 那可怕的声响？

sentences.en: It seemed to be coming from outside, somewhere in the garden….
sentences.zh: 似乎是从外面传来的，在花园的某个地方……

sentences.en: Thump… Thump… Thump… Anna slipped out of bed.
sentences.zh: 咚……咚……咚……安娜悄悄溜下床。

sentences.en: Headed to the door.
sentences.zh: 朝门口走去。

sentences.en: As queen, she was responsible for keeping her people safe.
sentences.zh: 身为女王，她有责任保护子民的安全。

sentences.en: Which meant she needed to investigate.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，她得去查看一下。

sentences.en: Even if she was scared.
sentences.zh: 就算她害怕。

sentences.en: Even if she was terrified at what she would find outside.
sentences.zh: 就算她对外面会发现什么吓得要命。

sentences.en: Her hand wrapped slowly around the door handle.
sentences.zh: 她的手缓缓握住了门把手。

sentences.en: She turned the knob— “No, Anna!
sentences.zh: 她转动把手——"不，安娜！

sentences.en: Don’t do it!
sentences.zh: 别开门！

sentences.en: It’s a trap!
sentences.zh: 这是个陷阱！

sentences.en: I know it’s a trap!” Olaf, the talking snowman, cried out in horror.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是个陷阱！"会说话的雪人奥拉夫惊恐地喊道。

sentences.en: He anxiously leapt out of his seat, somehow managing to lose both stick arms.
sentences.zh: 他慌张地从座位上跳起来，不知怎么竟把两根树枝手臂都甩掉了。

sentences.en: Racing around the campfire, he bounced over Bruni—the salamander-like Fire Spirit, who had been curled up on a small pile of magical snow—and then threw himself between Anna and Sven the reindeer, who had been “telling” the tale of terror in a voice that sounded suspiciously like Kristoff’s. “Don’t you hurt my Anna!” he yelled at Sven.
sentences.zh: 他绕着篝火飞奔，从火灵布伦尼身上蹦了过去——那只像火蜥蜴一样的火灵正蜷缩在一小堆魔法雪上——随后一下子插到安娜和驯鹿斯文中间；斯文刚才正用一种听起来特别像克斯托夫的声音"讲述"那个恐怖故事。"你别想伤我的安娜！"他对着斯文大吼。

sentences.en: Sven snorted and sniffed the snowman’s carrot nose.
sentences.zh: 斯文打了个响鼻，嗅了嗅雪人那胡萝卜鼻子。

sentences.en: Olaf took a wary step backward, bumping into Anna and almost losing his head in the process—literally.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫警惕地后退一步，撞上了安娜，差点把脑袋也弄掉了——字面意义上的掉。

sentences.en: She laughed and set it back on straight before giving it an affectionate pat. “Don’t worry, Olaf,” she said comfortingly. “It’s only a story.” “Also,” Elsa added, retrieving Olaf’s detached arms and tossing them to her sister, who reaffixed them to his body, “I’m pretty sure I know where this is going.” “Shh!” scolded Kristoff, wagging a finger at Elsa. “No spoilers!” He turned to his reindeer encouragingly. “Go ahead, Sven.
sentences.zh: 安娜笑了，把他的头摆正，又亲昵地拍了拍。"别担心，奥拉夫，"她安慰道，"只是个故事而已。" "还有，"艾莎接过奥拉夫掉下来的手臂，丢给妹妹，妹妹把它们重新装回雪人身上，补充道，"我差不多知道这故事要往哪儿发展了。" "嘘！"克斯托夫朝艾莎晃着手指训斥，"不许剧透！"他鼓励地转向自己的驯鹿，"继续，斯文。

sentences.en: They’re obviously just jealous of your superior spooky storytelling skills.” Elsa couldn’t suppress a small smile as she watched the reindeer give another longing look at Olaf’s carrot nose, which was no longer within nibbling reach.
sentences.zh: 他们明显只是嫉妒你高超的鬼故事讲述技巧。"艾莎忍不住露出一丝微笑，看着驯鹿又恋恋不舍地瞅了一眼奥拉夫的胡萝卜鼻子——那鼻子已经够不着嚼了。

sentences.en: She wondered, not for the first time, how badly Sven must wish he could talk for real, without having his buddy Kristoff “interpret” for him.
sentences.zh: 她不止一次地想，斯文该多希望自己能真的说话，而不用让伙伴克斯托夫替他"翻译"。

sentences.en: Then again, Sven did a pretty good job of letting everyone know what he was feeling without having to speak a word.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，斯文即使一言不发，也挺能让大家知道他在想什么。

sentences.en: Even if that feeling was just concern over where his next carrot to munch on might be coming from.
sentences.zh: 哪怕那种想法只是担心下一根要啃的胡萝卜从哪儿来。

sentences.en: Olaf sighed and retreated back to his seat on the log next to Elsa.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫叹了口气，退回艾莎身边圆木上的座位。

sentences.en: She gave him a comforting squeeze, then looked around the campfire circle, her heart suddenly feeling very full.
sentences.zh: 她给了他一个安慰的拥抱，然后环顾篝火一圈，心里忽然满满的。

sentences.en: The Enchanted Forest camping trip had been her idea, and she was thankful her sister, Anna, had found the time to get away from her queenly duties for a night to join her.
sentences.zh: 这次魔法森林露营是她的主意，她很感激妹妹安娜能抽空放下女王的职责，陪她过一夜。

sentences.en: Elsa knew all too well that being queen of Arendelle was a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 艾莎太清楚了，当阿伦黛尔的女王是份全职工作。

sentences.en: After all, it had been her position for years before Anna took over two months earlier.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，在安娜两个月前接任之前，这位置她坐了好些年。

sentences.en: She was proud of her younger sister for taking it all on without a complaint.
sentences.zh: 她为妹妹毫无怨言地扛起一切而感到骄傲。

sentences.en: In fact, Anna seemed to enjoy the challenge.
sentences.zh: 事实上，安娜似乎还挺享受这份挑战。

sentences.en: And Elsa knew the people of Arendelle loved Anna as much as she loved them.
sentences.zh: 而且艾莎知道，阿伦黛尔的百姓爱安娜，正如她爱他们一样。

sentences.en: But that was nothing compared to the love between these two sisters.
sentences.zh: 但比起这两姐妹之间的爱，那都不算什么。

sentences.en: Even though they now lived apart, they both made sure they were never too busy to spend time together regularly, either in the Enchanted Forest like they were now, or for weekly family game nights back in Arendelle, which still felt like a second home to Elsa.
sentences.zh: 尽管如今她们分开居住，但两人都确保自己再忙也会定期相聚——要么像现在这样在魔法森林，要么回阿伦黛尔过每周的家庭游戏之夜，那里对艾莎来说仍像个第二故乡。

sentences.en: (Anna had even let Elsa keep her bedroom, which had once been their mother and father’s, knowing how much it meant to her sister.) And, starting the next day, Elsa was planning to spend an extended holiday in Arendelle to help Anna prepare for her very first Polar Nights celebration as queen.
sentences.zh: （安娜甚至让艾莎保留了她那间卧室，那曾是父母亲的房间，因为她知道这对妹妹意义非凡。）而从第二天起，艾莎打算在阿伦黛尔长住一阵，帮安娜筹备她作为女王的首个极夜节庆典。

sentences.en: The Polar Nights festivities came once a year to Arendelle around the time of the winter solstice—and Elsa’s birthday!
sentences.zh: 极夜节每年冬天至日前后降临阿伦黛尔——也正是艾莎的生日！

sentences.en: It was a time when the land was wrapped in perpetual twilight, the sun never fully rising for an entire week.
sentences.zh: 那段时间大地笼罩在永恒的暮色里，整整一周太阳都不会完全升起。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t dull or too dark, like it could be in some kingdoms further to the north.
sentences.zh: 但不像更北边的一些王国那样沉闷或太黑。

sentences.en: Instead, the Arendellian skies were bathed in a beautiful dusky blue haze with plenty of light to see by.
sentences.zh: 相反，阿伦黛尔的天空浸在美丽的暮蓝色微光中，光线充足，足以看清明亮。

sentences.en: Some years, if they were lucky, they would even be treated to breathtaking views of the Northern Lights themselves, the aurora borealis painting the sky in brilliant emerald green.
sentences.zh: 有些年份，运气好的话，他们还能欣赏到北极光本身的震撼景象，极光把天空染成明亮的翡翠绿。

sentences.en: Once upon a time, according to the history books, people had been frightened by the Polar Nights phenomenon, believing the sun had died and that the world would soon expire along with it.
sentences.zh: 据史书记载，从前人们曾对极夜现象感到恐惧，以为太阳死了，世界也将随之终结。

sentences.en: Not to mention all the harm he’d done to the Northuldra, their mother’s people, by deceiving them into supporting his dam project, which would dry up their lands and destroy their way of life. “Right?
sentences.zh: 更别提他为了大坝工程欺骗北地人——他们母亲的民族——让他们支持建坝，那会抽干他们的土地，毁掉他们的生活方式。"对吧？

sentences.en: But, sadly, Sissel never got justice.
sentences.zh: 但可悲的是，西塞尔从未得到正义。

sentences.en: The prison ship Inger was on went down at sea before it could ever reach its destination,” Kristoff declared with a dramatic flourish. “And Inger—like her sister—also drowned.” “Well!” Olaf piped up. “That story was indeed terrifying.
sentences.zh: 英格所在的囚船还没抵达目的地就沉入了海中，"克斯托夫夸张地一挥手宣布，"而英格——和她的姐姐一样——也淹死了。""好哇！"奥拉夫插嘴，"那故事确实吓人。

sentences.en: Okay, Kristoff.
sentences.zh: 好吧，克斯托夫。

sentences.en: You win.
sentences.zh: 你赢了。

sentences.en: Perhaps we can toast marshmallows now?” He looked hopefully at the group. “Hold on, Olaf.
sentences.zh: 或许我们现在可以烤棉花糖了？"他满怀希望地看着大家。"等等，奥拉夫。

sentences.en: That’s not the end of my story,” Kristoff scolded. “In fact, it’s only the beginning.
sentences.zh: 我的故事还没完呢，"克斯托夫训斥，"事实上，这还只是个开头。

sentences.en: Because Sissel, you see, didn’t really die.
sentences.zh: 因为你们看，西塞尔并没有真的死。

sentences.en: Or at least she didn’t stay dead.
sentences.zh: 至少她没一直死着。

sentences.en: Instead, she came back as a horrible creature known as a draugr.” Something about the word sent an involuntary shiver down Elsa’s spine.
sentences.zh: 相反，她变成了一个叫亡者（draugr）的可怕怪物回来了。"这个词让艾莎不由自主地背脊一凉。

sentences.en: She felt a slight shift in the wind, and goose bumps formed on her arm.
sentences.zh: 她感到风微微一变，手臂上起了鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: She tried to smooth them down with her hand. “A draugr?
sentences.zh: 她试着用手把疙瘩抚平。"亡者？

sentences.en: What’s a draugr?” she asked, even though she wasn’t entirely sure she wanted to know.
sentences.zh: 什么是亡者？"她问，尽管不太确定自己是否想知道。

sentences.en: Anna raised her hand eagerly. “Ooh!
sentences.zh: 安娜急切地举起手。"噢！

sentences.en: I know!
sentences.zh: 我知道！

sentences.en: I know!” she cried. “I read all about them in this book I found in the secret room in the castle library.
sentences.zh: 我知道！"她喊道，"我在城堡图书馆密室找到的那本书里，全读到过它们。

sentences.en: They’re creatures of old folklore, and they supposedly cause terrible storms when they show up.
sentences.zh: 它们是古老传说里的生物，据说出现时会引来可怕的暴风雨。

sentences.en: People used to blame them when the weather got bad.” Kristoff nodded approvingly. “That’s exactly right.” “You’re so smart,” Elsa teased, poking Anna.
sentences.zh: 以前天气一坏，人们就怪它们。"克斯托夫赞许地点头。"完全正确。""你真聪明，"艾莎逗她，戳了戳安娜。

sentences.en: Anna shrugged sheepishly. “And so the evil draugr who used to be sweet Sissel began to roam the land,” Kristoff continued, “leaving havoc in its wake.
sentences.zh: 安娜不好意思地耸耸肩。"于是，曾经温柔的西塞尔变成的邪恶亡者开始在大地上游荡，"克斯托夫继续，"所到之处一片狼藉。

sentences.en: No longer human, no longer kind or good.
sentences.zh: 不再是人类，不再善良或美好。

sentences.en: It was now nothing more than a soulless monster ready to seek revenge against those who did it wrong.” “Moral of the story?
sentences.zh: 它现在不过是个没有灵魂的怪物，准备向那些亏待它的人复仇。""故事的寓意？

sentences.en: Always be nice to your sister,” Anna concluded.
sentences.zh: 永远对你好妹妹，"安娜总结。

sentences.en: She grinned at Elsa. “Got it!” Elsa smiled back at her, though for some reason she still felt a little uneasy.
sentences.zh: 她对艾莎咧嘴一笑。"明白啦！"艾莎回她一个微笑，尽管不知为何她仍觉得有点不安。

sentences.en: Maybe because it was such an unsettling story.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为这是个让人不安的故事。

sentences.en: Or perhaps it was the fact that she hadn’t always been the best sister herself.
sentences.zh: 又或许是因为，她自己并非一直都是个好姐姐。

sentences.en: She tried to imagine Anna coming back as an evil monster to seek revenge, but couldn’t exactly picture it.
sentences.zh: 她试着想象安娜变成邪恶怪物回来复仇，却怎么也想不出那画面。

sentences.en: Mostly because the only monstrous thing about Anna was her appetite for chocolate. “So where is the draugr now?” Olaf asked, his eyes still wide and terrified. “You said this story was true.
sentences.zh: 主要是因为安娜身上唯一"怪物"的地方，就是她对巧克力的胃口。"那亡者现在在哪儿？"奥拉夫问，眼睛仍瞪得大大的，满是恐惧。"你说这故事是真的。

sentences.en: Does that mean the draugr’s still out there somewhere?” “Of course it is,” Kristoff replied, turning his attention back to the snowman.
sentences.zh: 那是不是说亡者还在外面的某个地方？""当然在，"克斯托夫回答，把注意力转回雪人身上。

sentences.en: His thick eyebrows furrowed.
sentences.zh: 他浓密的眉毛皱了起来。

sentences.en: He lowered his voice by a menacing octave. “And it’s said that if you tell its story—especially tonight, the night it all happened—you will awaken it from its slumber and it will rise again, renewing its never-ending quest for revenge.” Kristoff raised his arms in front of him, casting dark shadows across Olaf’s frightened face. “So, my little snowman friend, the next time the skies grow dark…or the rain begins to fall…beware.
sentences.zh: 他把声音压低了一个危险的八度。"据说，如果你讲它的故事——尤其是在今晚，一切发生的那个夜晚——你就会把它从沉睡中唤醒，它会再次崛起，重燃那永无止境的复仇之路。"克斯托夫在身前举起双臂，在奥拉夫惊恐的脸上投下黑暗的阴影。"所以，我的小雪人朋友，下次天色变暗……或雨开始落下……可要当心。

sentences.en: Because it could be a simple storm.
sentences.zh: 因为那可能只是一场普通的暴风雨。

sentences.en: Or it could be Sinister Sissel, lurking just behind you in the shadows.
sentences.zh: 也可能那是"阴森西塞尔"，正潜伏在你身后的阴影里。

sentences.en: Ready to—” CRACK!
sentences.zh: 准备——" 咔嚓！

sentences.en: Suddenly thunder boomed from above.
sentences.zh: 突然，头顶炸响一声惊雷。

sentences.en: Lightning streaked across the sky.
sentences.zh: 闪电划过天空。

sentences.en: Olaf screamed, leaping into Elsa’s arms. “The draugr!
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫尖叫着，跳进艾莎怀里。"亡者！

sentences.en: It’s Sinister Sissel!” he cried. “She’s come to get us all!”
sentences.zh: 是阴森西塞尔！"他喊道，"她来抓我们所有人了！"

chapters.title: Chapter Two: Anna
chapters.en:
ANNA WATCHED AS ELSA GENTLY SET the panicked snowman back down. “Olaf, it’s just a storm coming,” she assured him. A moment later there was a second flash of lightning, followed by a roll of approaching thunder. “Not some monster from a story.”

Olaf glanced nervously up at the sky. “You sure about that? The timing here feels a bit coincidental.”

“Yes, Kristoff was only telling a story,” Anna said soothingly, shooting the ice harvester a look. “And, clearly, he wins for scariest.” She checked the sky again. “But we should get into our tents.”

“Because of the draugr?” Olaf whispered.

“Because of the rain,” Elsa reassured him, holding out a hand. “I’m already feeling drops.”

“But we didn’t even get a chance to roast marshmallows!” Sven said, courtesy of Kristoff.

“Sorry, guys.” Anna ruffled the reindeer’s fur. “We’ll save them for next time.” Then she stood up on tippy-toes to kiss Kristoff. “Now, get a good night’s sleep and try not to scare each other too much with your tales of terror.”

“Ooh! That’s right! It’s my turn!” Olaf’s eyes widened. He waddled over to Kristoff and Sven. “Hey, have you guys ever heard about the time I lost my bottom half for three hours? Now that’s a scary story….”

“See you guys in the morning!” Anna said as she watched the boys head off to their larger tent, which was big enough to hold the reindeer. Then she turned to Elsa and grinned. “Girl time! I mean, sister time!”

Anna loved when it was the five of them playing charades, having dinner together, or engaging in lively discussions, like the answer to the question What’s the best season in Arendelle? (Fall! No, summer! Maybe spring? Then again, winter was lovely, too—as long as it wasn’t eternal winter….) But as much as she enjoyed being with Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf, who felt entirely like family, there was something special about one-on-one time with Elsa, too.

“Is it wrong I’m secretly excited that we get a whole night to ourselves to just talk?” Anna wondered aloud. “Or do I sound like Olaf?”

“You sound like Anna,” Elsa said with a small smile. She stood up and used her ice magic to douse the fire, which was dimming in the rain. “And no, it’s not wrong. I love when it’s just the two of us sometimes as well.”

They grinned at each other, then felt the raindrops falling fatter and faster and quickly grabbed their things. Elsa scooped up Bruni and they ran to their tent, then closed themselves inside just as the storm arrived, thunder booming and rain coming down in buckets. The drops pelted the tent, sounding like the Earth Giants bowling, but inside Anna thought things were cozy and warm (partially because Bruni could brighten up the tent with its Fire Spirit flames).

“Olaf is not going to be able to sleep a wink, is he?” she mused as she curled up under the reindeer-hide blankets and nestled into the pillows.

“Seems unlikely,” Elsa agreed as she checked to make sure the tent ties were secure. “Poor Olaf. Or should I say, poor Kristoff and Sven.”

“Maybe Kristoff and Sven can try serenading him with a lullaby.” Anna pictured her fiancé, Olaf, and Sven cuddled up tight with Kristoff’s lute for entertainment. “They’ve been working on something they call ‘The Ballad of the Persnickety Proprietor.’ I suspect it’s about Oaken’s sauna.”

“Nothing says ‘sleep tight’ like a song about a sauna,” Elsa joked, settling in beside her sister under the warm hides.

The wind was picking up, making the tent blow a bit in the breeze, but Anna knew it would hold firm. Still, she snuggled against her sister, saying the words they’d heard their mother say a thousand times before bed when they were children: “Now cuddle close. Scooch in. And tell me everything you’ve been up to.”

“Since when? Last Friday’s game night at the castle?” Elsa teased.

“That was days ago!” Anna said indignantly. “You’ve probably done a gazillion amazing things since then!”

“Which I talk about in my daily letters you get from Gale,” Elsa reminded her.

“I know! But letters are different from actual talking.” Anna placed her head against Elsa’s. “Our letters are all about silly things like Olina’s latest recipe for lingonberries or where I can find Father’s book on that headstrong mermaid who decided she wanted to be human just because she met a good-looking prince. Or questions, like ‘What’s a five-letter word for ice?’”

“Frost!” Elsa burst out.

Anna knew Elsa was trying to be funny, but she also wasn’t about to let her big sister shove her feelings aside. She might have been the younger sibling, but she felt protective of Elsa after all Elsa had been through the last few years. “I just want to make sure you’re doing okay,” she said quietly.

“I’m doing better than okay. I’m great,” Elsa promised. She looked at Bruni, whose flames illuminated the small patch of snow that kept him cool. “I’ve been learning so much from the spirits, Honeymaren, Ryder, and all the Northuldra about the ways of the forest. And my trips to Ahtohallan have been”—Elsa looked too overwhelmed to even put her experiences with the magical river that contained memories of the past into words—“truly magical.”

Anna beamed. This was exactly what she wanted to hear. “I’m so happy for you, Elsa. So, you’ve been learning more about your powers?”

“Yes, I’m even working on new ways to bring up memories. It’s really—”

Lightning lit up the whole tent, causing Bruni to snort in excitement. For a moment, Elsa looked startled, and then she shook her head. “But enough about me,” she said. “What I really want to talk about is how you’re doing. How do you like all your new duties?”

“Me?” Anna’s head popped up from the pillow. She knew Elsa was trying to change the subject, but she was going to give her a pass this time. She’d been wanting to talk to Elsa about the kingdom anyway. “I love them! All of them. Being queen and working with the people of Arendelle to make the kingdom a better place is magical, too. It feels so satisfying getting stuff done, you know?”

She started to tick off tasks on her fingers. “This week alone, I had Mr. Aldring make a new clock to give as a welcome present to the queen of Chatho when she visits next month, did a ribbon-cutting ceremony at a new shop in the village, and also sat in on a three-hour meeting about soil!”

“Let me guess—with Oskar Anders?” Elsa asked with a groan. “So painful, right?”

“Actually, it was riveting!” Anna gushed. “He was going on and on about how Arendelle’s soil is the richest in all the connected kingdoms.” She shook her head, remembering. “Just fascinating stuff, really! I could have listened to him all day!”

Elsa snorted. “And this is why you make such a good queen,” she teased.

“I’m trying,” Anna said modestly. “Though it’s not always easy. At least I have Mattias. He’s been such a great help. Especially with the whole pirate thing.” She made a face.

Elsa sat up. “Pirate thing? This is new.”

“Oh.” Anna waved a hand. “It’s probably not a big deal. It’s just that some pirate ships have been rumored to be lurking just off Arendelle’s coast for about a week now. Supposedly helmed by a legendary pirate queen they call Old Blue Eyes. They haven’t done anything bad or given our ships trouble, so I guess that’s good. I’m just worried they’re going to try to pull something right before the festival, you know? Like I don’t have enough to deal with. Anyway, Mattias assures me he’s got his eye on them. And I trust him to take care of things.”

“I wish he had been around when I was queen,” Elsa said, thinking back to the dashing lieutenant—now a general—who had been stuck in the Enchanted Forest for so many years. He’d been a friend to their father when Agnarr was a child. Now he split his time between protecting Arendelle, advising Anna, and…well…courting his girlfriend, Halima. The two of them had been thick as thieves ever since he returned to the kingdom, and Elsa and Anna had both made bets on how quickly they would tie the knot.

“I’m not sure what I would do without him,” Anna agreed. “It’s nice to have help in the castle. You know, because running the kingdom is such a big task and all.”

“Oh, I remember,” Elsa assured her. “It’s more than a job. It’s a lifestyle.”

“Right? And I’m always worried I’m forgetting something important that needs to be done. Or that things are going to go wrong and it’ll be my fault,” Anna said, stressed, the words now tumbling out of her mouth before she could stop them. “Like with the Polar Nights! What if the ice sculptures of Aren of Arendelle end up looking like Flemmingrad the troll? Or the band forgets to show up?” Now that she was worrying, she was on a roll and couldn’t stop. Not that she wanted to bring it up, but Elsa’s birthday fell during the Polar Nights, too—on the winter solstice! She was secretly planning a party on the final night of the festival for her sister. If she could get it all done in time. “What if everything I have planned is a huge flop?”

“It’s all going to work out okay. I promise,” Elsa said. “And you have me at your disposal, don’t forget. I’ll help you, too.”

Anna knew her sister was right, but she still felt worried. She just had to concentrate on happy thoughts, like Elsa being back in the castle. “It’s just that this is my first festival as queen, and I want the people to enjoy themselves. I want you to enjoy yourself! You’ve been working so hard.”

Elsa put her hand over Anna’s. “So have you, and the people of Arendelle know that. You’re a great leader, Anna. You’re juggling a million different tasks at the same time, and look at you—you still have a smile on your face.”

Anna raised an eyebrow.

Elsa laughed. “Okay, maybe not at this very second. But you know what I mean. Arendelle is lucky to have you. I’m so proud of you.”

Anna put her free hand on top of Elsa’s. “And I’m proud of you! The forest and spirits are lucky to have you.” She cocked her head to one side. “If only Mother and Father could see us now, huh?”

The thought made each of them quiet, the only sound the rain pelting their tent. Anna couldn’t help imagining, and not for the first time, what their world would be like if their parents were still around to watch her ascend the throne and to witness a self-assured Elsa using her powers for all the kingdom to see. But all they had were memories.

“You know,” Elsa suddenly spoke up, “I remember one Polar Nights festival as a child when the weather was so warm, there wasn’t enough snow to make the traditional courtyard ice sculpture.”

Anna looked at her, aghast. “No.”

“Yes.” Elsa nodded. “It had been a particularly warm fall, and it just didn’t feel like the start of winter yet. You were little, but I remember Father panicking. ‘How can it be a Polar Nights party without an ice sculpture?’ I offered to make one, but, of course, they didn’t want to risk me revealing my powers. So Mother took matters into her own hands and decided to have someone carve a sculpture out of something other than ice.”

“What did they use?” Anna asked, riveted as she always was when Elsa recalled a memory of their parents that she did not have.

Elsa started to laugh. “They used cheese!”

“Cheese?” Anna snorted. “I didn’t realize you could carve cheese!” She stopped laughing and thought for a moment. “Wow, this changes everything.”

“Yep,” Elsa confirmed, sitting up now, too. “But it gets better! Mother thought it would be fun to surprise Father with the sculpture, so she had it made in secret. She told me, but we kept it from you, of course.”

Anna shrugged. “I can’t say I blame you. I would have blabbed. What kind of cheese did they use?” All this food talk was making her hungry. She really wished they’d had a chance to toast marshmallows.

“I think it was cheddar or Gouda or some semihard cheese. It was carved into the Arendelle coat of arms. It was beautiful!” Elsa gushed. “Mother kept it hidden in the kitchen so Father wouldn’t see it, but there was one problem.” Elsa started to laugh, making it harder to understand her. “Father got hungry in the middle of the night, went down to the kitchen, and…”

“No!” Anna interrupted, laughing so hard she had to cover her mouth. Bruni was looking from her to Elsa with interest. “He didn’t! Tell me he didn’t!”

“He did!” Elsa cried. “He cut off a whole piece of the crest and ate it! When Mother came down the next morning, she was horrified. I remember she was actually a little mad and said, ‘What did you think this was for?’ And Father said something like ‘Dinner?’”

The two of them threw their heads back, laughing.

“I wish I could remember that,” Anna said wistfully.

“Hmm. Maybe I can show it to you….” Elsa pushed back the reindeer hide and stood up, her head touching the top pole of the tent.

Anna watched as her sister seemed to concentrate on her magic. She could only imagine what Elsa’s ice memory would look like. Anna pictured Father and Mother standing over the table with the half-eaten coat of arms made from cheese, and Father’s guilty look as he realized he was busted. As Elsa swirled her arms around, Anna saw ice begin to form…then disappear in a plume of mist.

Anna cocked her head. “What happened?” It wasn’t like Elsa’s magic to just fizzle out like that.

Elsa frowned, looking upset. “I don’t know,” she murmured. “I mean, I had it. The memory was right there, but then…” She trailed off and then shrugged, giving her sister an apologetic look. “I’m sorry, Anna. Even now that I’ve taken my place among the spirits, magic isn’t always easy.”

Anna pulled Elsa into a hug. “Neither is being queen, but we’ll both get there.”

They stood there for a moment, each listening to the thunder continue to crash, the wind whistle, and the rain pounding on the tent’s roof. For a moment, Anna felt like they were the only two people in the world. As long as they had each other’s backs, she knew they’d be okay.

Suddenly, though, a giant clap of thunder made both of them jump.

“Wow, this is some storm!” Anna commented, watching the top of the tent continue to ripple.

“It can’t go on for much longer,” Elsa guessed, “but it is a rough one.” She dropped back to her knees, settling the reindeer hide over her lap. Anna joined her, wondering if they were ever going to get any sleep.

It was then that she heard something. Or at least she thought she heard something. The faintest of sounds, but one that definitely didn’t sound like the wind or rain.

In fact, it sounded a lot like someone…moaning.

“Do you…hear something?” she asked Elsa nervously.

“Um, you mean besides the deafening rainstorm outside our tent?”

Anna shook her head. Right. Of course there was nothing. It was just her mind playing tricks on her. Clearly, she was still spooked after Kristoff’s silly story.

But then it came again: the moan so low it seemed to go right through her. And it sounded a little closer this time. Anna involuntarily pulled the covers up to her chin.

“Are you okay?” asked Elsa as she peered at her worriedly.

“Yeah! Of course! I’m totally fine,” Anna insisted, shoving the covers back down in embarrassment. “Sorry. I’m sure it was just—”

Her words, however, were cut off by a sudden ear-piercing scream.

安娜看着艾莎轻轻把惊慌的雪人放下。"奥拉夫，只是暴风雨要来了，"她向他保证。

片刻后，第二道闪电划过，紧接着滚来一阵逼近的雷声。"不是故事里的什么怪物。"奥拉夫紧张地抬头望天。"你确定？

这时机感觉有点太巧了。""是啊，克斯托夫只是讲了个故事，"安娜安抚地说，朝那个采冰工递了个眼神，"而且显然，最吓人的故事是他赢了。"她又看了看天。"不过我们该进帐篷了。""因为亡者？"奥拉夫小声问。"因为雨，"艾莎伸手安抚他，"我已经感觉到雨点了。""可我们连烤棉花糖的机会都没有！"斯文说道，借的是克斯托夫的口。"抱歉啦，各位。"安娜揉了揉驯鹿的毛。"留着下次吧。"然后她踮起脚尖吻了克斯托夫。"现在，好好睡一觉，别再用你们的恐怖故事把彼此吓太惨。""噢！

对哦！

轮到我了！"奥拉夫瞪大了眼睛。

他一摇一摆地走到克斯托夫和斯文跟前。"嘿，你们听没听说过我有一次下半身不见了足足三个小时？

那才叫吓人的故事……""明早见，各位！"安娜看着男孩们走向他们那顶更大的帐篷——大得能装下驯鹿——说道。

然后她转向艾莎，咧嘴一笑。"闺蜜时间！

我是说，姐妹时间！"安娜喜欢他们五个一起玩猜词游戏、共进晚餐，或是热烈讨论，比如"阿伦黛尔哪个季节最好？"这种问题。

（秋天！

不，夏天！

也许春天？

不过话说回来，冬天也很美——只要不是永恒的冬天……）但尽管她很喜欢和感觉完全像家人的克斯托夫、斯文和奥拉夫在一起，和艾莎单独相处也有种特别的感觉。"我暗中兴奋，我们能有一整晚独处聊天，这有错吗？"安娜自言自语，"还是说我听起来像奥拉夫？""你听起来像安娜，"艾莎微微笑着说。

她站起来，用冰魔法浇灭了在雨中渐暗的火。"而且不，这没错。

我也喜欢偶尔只有我们俩的时候。"她们相视一笑，随后感到雨点越来越密、越来越急，赶紧抓起东西。

艾莎一把捞起布伦尼，她们跑向帐篷，刚好在暴风雨抵达、雷声轰鸣、大雨倾盆时把自己关了进去。

雨点砸在帐篷上，像大地巨人在打保龄球，但安娜觉得里面既舒适又温暖（部分因为布伦尼能用火灵的火焰把帐篷照亮）。"奥拉夫今晚肯定睡不着了，对吧？"她一边在驯鹿皮毯子下蜷起来、窝进枕头里，一边若有所思地说。"似乎不太可能，"艾莎一边确认帐篷的系绳牢固，一边表示同意，"可怜的奥拉夫。

或者我该说，可怜的克斯托夫和斯文。""也许克斯托夫和斯文能用摇篮曲给他唱安眠曲。"安娜想象着未婚夫、奥拉夫和斯文紧紧依偎，用克斯托夫的鲁特琴助兴。"他们一直在写一首叫《挑剔店主之歌》的曲子。我猜是关于奥肯的桑拿房的。""一首关于桑拿房的歌最让人'睡得香'了，"艾莎开玩笑，在温暖的兽皮下挨着妹妹坐下。

风渐渐大起来，吹得帐篷在微风中轻轻晃动，但安娜知道它撑得住。

她还是依偎着姐姐，说出她们小时候睡前听母亲说过一千遍的话："现在靠紧点。

往里挤挤。

跟我说说你最近都在忙什么。""从什么时候算起？

上周五城堡里的游戏之夜？"艾莎逗她。"那都是几天前了！"安娜愤愤地说，"那之后你肯定又做了无数了不起的事！""那些我都写在每天让风灵捎给你的信里了，"艾莎提醒她，"我知道！

但信跟真正聊天不一样。"安娜把头靠在艾莎头上。"我们的信里全是些傻事，比如奥丽娜最新的越橘食谱，或者我在哪儿能找到父亲那本关于倔强美人鱼的书——她只因为遇见一位帅气王子，就决定要变成人。

或者像"冰的五字母单词是什么？"这种问题。""霜！"艾莎脱口而出。

安娜知道艾莎是想逗她，但她也不打算让姐姐把自己的感受推开。

她虽是妹妹，但在艾莎过去几年经历的一切之后，她对艾莎有种保护欲。"我只是想确认你还好吧，"她轻声说。"我比好还要好。

我棒极了，"艾莎保证。

她看着布伦尼，它的火焰照亮了让它保持凉爽的那小片雪。"我从精灵、霍妮玛伦、莱德和所有北地人那儿学到了很多森林的奥秘。

而我前往阿托哈兰的旅程——"艾莎激动得连话都说不出，无法用言语形容她在那条蕴含过去记忆的魔法河中的经历——"真的像魔法一样。"安娜眉开眼笑。

这正是她想听到的。"我真为你高兴，艾莎。

那么，你对自己的力量又多了些了解？""是的，我甚至在研究唤起记忆的新方法。

这真的——"一道闪电照亮了整个帐篷，惹得布伦尼兴奋地喷鼻息。

有那么一刻，艾莎显得有些惊愕，随后她摇摇头。"不过不说我了，"她说，"我真正想聊的是你过得怎么样。

你喜欢你那些新职责吗？""我？"安娜从枕头上抬起头。

她知道艾莎在转移话题，但这次她打算放过她。

反正她一直想跟艾莎说说王国的事。"我爱它们！

全都爱。

当女王，和阿伦黛尔的百姓一起把王国变得更好，也像魔法一样。

把事情做成，那种满足感你懂吧？"她开始掰着手指列举任务。"就这周，我让奥尔丁先生做了个新钟，作为下个月查托女王来访时的欢迎礼物；在村里一家新店参加了剪彩；还列席了一场长达三小时、关于土壤的会议！""让我猜——是和奥斯卡·安德斯？"艾莎呻吟着问，"巨痛苦，对吧？""其实，那简直引人入胜！"安娜滔滔不绝，"他翻来覆去地讲，阿伦黛尔的土壤在所有相连王国里最肥沃。"她摇着头回忆。"真的，太有意思了！

我本来能听他讲一整天！"艾莎哼了一声。"这就是为什么你是个好女王，"她逗道。"我在努力，"安娜谦逊地说，"虽然这并不总容易。

至少我还有马蒂亚斯。

他帮了大忙。

尤其是对付那桩海盗的事。"她做了个鬼脸。

艾莎坐直了。"海盗的事？

这是新情况。""噢。"安娜挥挥手。"大概不是什么大事。

只是大概一周来，一直有传闻说有些海盗船在阿伦黛尔海岸外游荡。

据说由一位人称"蓝眼"的传奇海盗女王统领。

他们没干坏事，也没给我们的船找麻烦，所以我想还算好。

我只是担心他们会在节日前搞点事，你懂吧？

好像我操心的事还不够多似的。

总之，马蒂亚斯向我保证，他正盯着他们呢。

我信他能处理好。""我真希望我当女王时他就在，"艾莎说，想起那位帅气的副官——如今已是将军——曾在魔法森林里被困多年。

在安格瑞还是个孩子时，他就是国王的朋友。

如今他把时间分给守护阿伦黛尔、辅佐安娜，还有……嗯……追求女友哈利玛。

他回到王国后，两人就黏得像贼一样亲密，艾莎和安娜还打赌他们多久会结婚。"没他我真不知道怎么办，"安娜表示同意，"城堡里有人帮忙真好。

你知道，治理王国可是个大工程。""噢，我记得，"艾莎向她保证，"这不止是份工作。

这是一种生活方式。""对吧？

而且我总担心自己忘了什么重要的事没做。

或者事情会出错，而那都怪我，"安娜紧张地说，话没等刹住就涌了出来。"比如极夜节！

万一阿伦黛尔之阿伦的冰雕最后看起来像地精弗莱明格拉德怎么办？

或者乐队忘了来？"她一旦担心起来就停不住了。

她本不想提，但艾莎的生日也在极夜节期间——就在冬至此日！

她正偷偷为妹妹筹备一场在节日最后一晚的生日派对。

如果她能及时把一切准备好。"要是我计划的全都搞砸了怎么办？""一切都会好起来的。

我保证，"艾莎说，"而且你还有我可用，别忘了。

我也会帮你的。"安娜知道姐姐是对的，但她仍放心不下。

她只能集中想些开心的事，比如艾莎回到城堡。"这只是我当女王后的第一个节日，我希望百姓们玩得开心。

我希望你也玩得开心！

你一直那么努力。"艾莎把手覆在安娜手上。"你也是，阿伦黛尔的百姓都知道。

你是个出色的领袖，安娜。

你同时应付着无数任务，看看你——脸上还带着微笑。"安娜挑了挑眉。

艾莎笑了。"好吧，也许不是这一秒。

但你知道我的意思。

阿伦黛尔有你真幸运。

我为你骄傲。"安娜把空着的手搭在艾莎手上。"我也为你骄傲！

森林和精灵有你真幸运。"她把头歪向一边。"要是爸爸妈妈能看到现在的我们就好了，嗯？"这个念头让两人都安静下来，唯一的声响是雨点敲打帐篷。

安娜忍不住想象——也不是第一次了——如果父母还在，能看着她登上王位，能见证自信的艾莎当着整个王国施展力量，世界会是什么样。

但他们只剩下回忆了。"你知道，"艾莎忽然开口，"我记得小时候有一次极夜节，天气暖得连做传统的庭院冰雕都不够雪。

你还小，但我记得父亲慌了神。'没有冰雕，这算什么极夜节派对？'我自告奋勇要做一座，但当然，他们不想冒险让我暴露力量。

于是母亲亲自出马，决定让人用冰以外的材料雕一座。""他们用了什么？"安娜问，每当艾莎回忆起她没有的、关于父母的记忆，她总是听得入迷。

艾莎笑了起来。"他们用了奶酪！""奶酪？"安娜哼了一声，"我都不知道奶酪也能雕！"她停下笑，想了想。"哇，这改变了一切。""没错，"艾莎确认，这会儿也坐直了，"但更精彩的呢！

母亲觉得用雕像给父亲个惊喜会很有趣，于是秘密地让人做了。

她告诉了我，但当然，我们瞒着你。""安娜耸耸肩。"我不能怪你。

我肯定早说漏嘴了。

他们用的什么奶酪？"这一通关于食物的话让她饿了。

她真希望他们有机会烤了棉花糖。"我想是切达或高达，或者某种半硬奶酪。

它被雕成了阿伦黛尔的盾徽。

美极了！"艾莎赞叹，"母亲把它藏在厨房，免得父亲看见，但有个问题。"艾莎笑得话都说不利索了。"父亲半夜饿了，下楼去厨房，然后……""不！"安娜打断，笑得不得不捂住嘴。

布伦尼饶有兴趣地在她和艾莎之间看来看去。"他不会的！

告诉我他没干！""他干了！"艾莎叫道，"他切下一大块盾徽吃掉了！

第二天早上母亲下楼，吓坏了。

我记得她其实有点生气，说：'你以为这是拿来干嘛的？'父亲说了句类似'晚餐？'的话。"两人仰头大笑。"我真希望能记得那一幕，"安娜怅然若失地说。"嗯。

也许我能让你看看……"艾莎掀开驯鹿皮，站起来，头碰到了帐篷顶杆。

安娜看着姐姐似乎在集中精神运用魔法。

她只能想象艾莎的冰之记忆会是什么样。

安娜想象父亲和母亲站在桌前，桌上摆着那座吃了一半的奶酪盾徽，父亲意识到自己露馅时那副心虚的表情。

随着艾莎双臂旋转，安娜看见冰开始成形……随后在一阵薄雾中消散。

安娜歪了歪头。"怎么回事？"艾莎的魔法可不该这样虎头蛇尾。

艾莎皱起眉，显得不安。"我不知道，"她低声说，"我是说，我刚才明明有。

记忆就在那儿，但然后……"她话说一半，耸耸肩，给了妹妹一个歉意的眼神。"对不起，安娜。

即使现在我在精灵中有了归处，魔法也不总是一帆风顺。"安娜把艾莎拉进怀里。"当女王也是，但我们都终会做到的。"她们在那站了一会儿，各自听着雷声继续炸响、风在呼啸、雨点砸在帐篷顶上。

有那么一刻，安娜觉得世界上只有她们两人。

只要彼此扶持，她知道她们会没事的。

然而突然，一声巨雷让两人都跳了起来。"哇，这暴风雨可真猛！"安娜看着帐篷顶继续起伏，评论道。"它持续不了多久了，"艾莎猜测，"但确实够猛的。"她跪回去，把驯鹿皮盖在腿上。

安娜也凑过去，琢磨着她们到底还能不能睡着。

就在这时，她听见了什么。

或者至少她觉得听见了什么。

极微弱的声音，但绝对不像风或雨。

事实上，那听起来很像有人在……呻吟。"你……听见什么了吗？"她紧张地问艾莎。"嗯，你是说除了帐篷外那震耳欲聋的暴雨？"安娜摇摇头。

对。

当然什么都没有。

只是她自己在疑神疑鬼。

显然，克斯托夫那个傻故事之后，她还没缓过神来。

但接着那声音又来了：那呻吟低得仿佛直穿她身体。

而且这次听起来近了一点。

安娜不由自主地把被子拉到下巴。"你还好吗？"艾莎担忧地看着她问。"好啊！

当然！

我完全没事，"安娜坚持道，尴尬地把被子推下去。"抱歉。

我肯定那只是——"但她的话被一声突然刺耳的尖叫打断了。

帐篷帘子猛地掀开，上气不接下气的奥拉夫冲了进来，水从身上飞溅，树枝手臂挥舞着。"亡者！

sentences.en: Anna cocked her head. “What happened?” It wasn’t like Elsa’s magic to just fizzle out like that.
sentences.zh: 艾莎皱起眉，显得不安。"我不知道，"她低声说，"我是说，我刚才明明有。

sentences.en: Elsa frowned, looking upset. “I don’t know,” she murmured. “I mean, I had it.
sentences.zh: 记忆就在那儿，但然后……"她话说一半，耸耸肩，给了妹妹一个歉意的眼神。"对不起，安娜。

sentences.en: The memory was right there, but then…” She trailed off and then shrugged, giving her sister an apologetic look. “I’m sorry, Anna.
sentences.zh: 即使现在我在精灵中有了归处，魔法也不总是一帆风顺。"安娜把艾莎拉进怀里。"当女王也是，但我们都终会做到的。"她们在那站了一会儿，各自听着雷声继续炸响、风在呼啸、雨点砸在帐篷顶上。

sentences.en: Even now that I’ve taken my place among the spirits, magic isn’t always easy.” Anna pulled Elsa into a hug. “Neither is being queen, but we’ll both get there.” They stood there for a moment, each listening to the thunder continue to crash, the wind whistle, and the rain pounding on the tent’s roof.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，安娜觉得世界上只有她们两人。

sentences.en: For a moment, Anna felt like they were the only two people in the world.
sentences.zh: 只要彼此扶持，她知道她们会没事的。

sentences.en: As long as they had each other’s backs, she knew they’d be okay.
sentences.zh: 然而突然，一声巨雷让两人都跳了起来。"哇，这暴风雨可真猛！"安娜看着帐篷顶继续起伏，评论道。"它持续不了多久了，"艾莎猜测，"但确实够猛的。"她跪回去，把驯鹿皮盖在腿上。

sentences.en: Suddenly, though, a giant clap of thunder made both of them jump. “Wow, this is some storm!” Anna commented, watching the top of the tent continue to ripple. “It can’t go on for much longer,” Elsa guessed, “but it is a rough one.” She dropped back to her knees, settling the reindeer hide over her lap.
sentences.zh: 安娜也凑过去，琢磨着她们到底还能不能睡着。

sentences.en: Anna joined her, wondering if they were ever going to get any sleep.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，她听见了什么。

sentences.en: It was then that she heard something.
sentences.zh: 或者至少她觉得听见了什么。

sentences.en: Or at least she thought she heard something.
sentences.zh: 极微弱的声音，但绝对不像风或雨。

sentences.en: The faintest of sounds, but one that definitely didn’t sound like the wind or rain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那听起来很像有人在……呻吟。"你……听见什么了吗？"她紧张地问艾莎。"嗯，你是说除了帐篷外那震耳欲聋的暴雨？"安娜摇摇头。

sentences.en: In fact, it sounded a lot like someone…moaning. “Do you…hear something?” she asked Elsa nervously. “Um, you mean besides the deafening rainstorm outside our tent?” Anna shook her head.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 当然什么都没有。

sentences.en: Of course there was nothing.
sentences.zh: 只是她自己在疑神疑鬼。

sentences.en: It was just her mind playing tricks on her.
sentences.zh: 显然，克斯托夫那个傻故事之后，她还没缓过神来。

sentences.en: Clearly, she was still spooked after Kristoff’s silly story.
sentences.zh: 但接着那声音又来了：那呻吟低得仿佛直穿她身体。

sentences.en: But then it came again: the moan so low it seemed to go right through her.
sentences.zh: 而且这次听起来近了一点。

sentences.en: And it sounded a little closer this time.
sentences.zh: 安娜不由自主地把被子拉到下巴。"你还好吗？"艾莎担忧地看着她问。"好啊！

sentences.en: Anna involuntarily pulled the covers up to her chin. “Are you okay?” asked Elsa as she peered at her worriedly. “Yeah!
sentences.zh: 当然！

sentences.en: Of course!
sentences.zh: 我完全没事，"安娜坚持道，尴尬地把被子推下去。"抱歉。

sentences.en: I’m totally fine,” Anna insisted, shoving the covers back down in embarrassment. “Sorry.
sentences.zh: 我肯定那只是——"但她的话被一声突然刺耳的尖叫打断了。

sentences.en: I’m sure it was just—” Her words, however, were cut off by a sudden ear-piercing scream.
sentences.zh: 帐篷帘子猛地掀开，上气不接下气的奥拉夫冲了进来，水从身上飞溅，树枝手臂挥舞着。"亡者！

chapters.title: Chapter Three: Elsa
chapters.en:
THE TENT FLAPS FLEW OPEN and a breathless Olaf ran in, water spraying off his body, his stick arms flying.

“The draugr! It’s real! And it’s here!” He catapulted himself at the two sisters, who caught him and held him jointly.

Elsa gave him a look. “Olaf, we’ve been through this. There is no draugr—it’s just the storm, and—”

Two more figures barreled into the tent, making it entirely too tight to even move.

“Olaf isn’t joking,” Kristoff said, breathing as hard as if he’d just run a mile. “There’s something out there. Sven and I both saw it!” Sven nodded, shivering in his wet coat.

Elsa felt the briefest of chills go through her body, and it had nothing to do with the blast of icy air blowing through the tent now that the flaps were rippling free in the wind. The storm was so intense she couldn’t even see the boys’ tent, which was only a few feet away. “You guys aren’t just trying to scare us, are you?” she asked, half hoping it was the case.

“Yeah, ’cause we don’t scare easily, you know,” Anna piped in, puffing out her chest a little. “I mean, I’ve faced down deadly wolves, bad boyfriends…not to mention gigantic snow monsters created by my own sister to throw me out of her icy fortress of solitude!”

Elsa shot an apologetic look at Anna. Not her best sisterly moment, for sure. “Look,” she said, prying Olaf off her and setting him down on the ground, “I’m sure you were just spooked by the story Kristoff told. And then the wind blew in a weird way, and—”

“No,” Kristoff stated firmly, his chest still rising and falling fast. “It wasn’t just the wind. There was a shadow, too. A shadow that was definitely not wind-shaped. Right, Sven?”

Sven demonstrated by waving his front hooves menacingly in the air. They caught the flicker of Bruni’s light, casting eerie shadows on the tent’s walls. Elsa felt a shimmer of unease swim through her stomach.

“And then there was the moaning,” Olaf added. “A lot of evil-sounding moaning.”

“I thought I heard moaning, too,” Anna mused, looking at Elsa worriedly. “Just before the boys came in.”

“The wind can moan,” Elsa tried, feeling as if she were grasping at straws. She wanted to keep everyone calm, but even she was admittedly starting to get a little creeped out. She tried to tell herself that the spirits of the Enchanted Forest would never let anything harm her or her family. But even Bruni was starting to act a little nervous, darting from one end of the tent to the other.

“Look, we’re not messing around.” Kristoff glanced back out into the storm, and the others followed his gaze. “I’m telling you, something or someone is out there.”

“Not just any something! A draugr!” Olaf insisted. “Just like in the story!” He tried to hide behind Sven. “I think it wants to eat us alive!”

Elsa drew in a breath, resigning herself to the inevitable. It wasn’t that she believed there was really some draugr out in the woods. But something was going on, and she was positive no one was going to get any sleep if they didn’t get some answers. She crawled over to the tent’s entrance.

“Where are you going?” demanded Anna, looking concerned.

“I’m going to investigate.”

“Not without me, you aren’t!”

Elsa sighed. “You’ll get soaked.”

“I’m happy to get soaked if it saves you from becoming draugr dinner,” Anna shot back.

Elsa groaned. Here we go again. She loved her little sister’s bravery, but she worried it would be her downfall someday. “Anna—” she started.

“Look, we’ll all go,” Kristoff declared.

“All?” Olaf squeaked, clearly not comfortable with this suggested plan.

“All humans,” Kristoff clarified, patting him on the head. “Olaf, we need you and Sven to guard the tent.”

Sven huffed, giving Kristoff an indignant look. Kristoff shrugged apologetically.

Elsa stepped toward the tent entrance, squinting out into the rain. “Ready?” she asked, not entirely sure if she was asking Kristoff and Anna—or herself.

“Born ready!” Anna proclaimed, evidently not having the same misgivings. She pushed past Elsa without hesitation, stumbling into the rainy night. Elsa shook her head, then scrambled after her, Kristoff hot on her heels.

The sky boomed a menacing greeting as they stepped out into the elements. It was pouring so hard it was practically impossible to see. Elsa waved a hand, creating an icy canopy across two trees, and the three of them dove for cover. Once underneath, Elsa drew in a breath, trying to regain her bearings, and spotted the boys’ tent. She inhaled sharply. Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf’s tent had been completely knocked down, which could have been explained by the wind. Except…

“Are those…claw marks?” Elsa asked, shouting to be heard over the wind. Her eyes traveled up the sides of the tent, where it looked as if it had been sheared by a knife. She glanced at Kristoff. “Did something attack your tent?”

“I don’t know.” Kristoff looked as baffled as she felt. “When we heard the moaning and saw the shadow, we ran to your tent.” He paused, then squared his shoulders. “I mean, just to make sure you guys were okay and all. Not ’cause we were scared.”

“Of course, honey,” said Anna as she comforted him, putting a supportive hand on his back. Then she turned to Elsa. “Maybe the tent caught on a tree branch.”

“Maybe,” Elsa said. Her eyes rose up to scout the forest behind the tent. But the tent wasn’t close enough to any trees to have gotten tangled in the branches.

She bit her lower lip uneasily. She didn’t believe for a second it could be a monster out of a spooky story, but at the same time it had to be something. A wolf? Wolves were smart enough not to be out in this mess. Also, they were usually only after food—and yet there was a whole plate of leftover grillpolser they’d cooked over the fire for dinner sitting on a nearby log. Soaked, but definitely still edible by wolf standards.

But what else could it be?

She lifted her eyes to the sky and sang a few notes. A moment later, Gale whipped in, swirling around them in question. The storm, of course, didn’t bother the Wind Spirit one bit.

“Can you go and look around?” Elsa asked it. “See if you see anything out of the ordinary?”

Gale swept up and out, disappearing into the darkness. Elsa shrugged and turned to her sister and Kristoff. “If anything’s out there, Gale will find it,” she assured them.

Anna shivered. Kristoff put his arm around her, holding her close. “Are you okay?” he asked.

“I’m fine!” Anna protested, surprising Elsa by pushing him away with more force than necessary. “I’m just freezing! And soaking wet, too.” She scowled. “Why are we out here again?”

Elsa frowned. “I never said you had to come,” she reminded her sister. “You could have stayed in the tent with Olaf and Sven.”

“The tent…” Kristoff’s eyes fell to his collapsed tent. “Wait! What happened to my tent?”

“Excuse me?” Elsa turned to him, really confused now. “What are you talking about?”

“It’s…ruined. My beautiful tent. And…is that a tear down the side of it? I just paid that off, you know!” He glanced accusingly at Anna, who shrugged back at him like she had no idea what he was talking about.

A small worry fluttered in Elsa’s stomach. She looked from Kristoff to Anna, who looked back at her in confusion. Were they just playing around? If so, it wasn’t funny.

“Look, why don’t you two get back to our tent. Check on Olaf and Sven,” she said, trying to swallow down her concern. “I’ll wait for Gale to return.”

She expected Anna to argue, but to her surprise, her sister nodded vacantly, taking Kristoff by the arm and leading him back to the tent. They crawled inside, pulling the flaps closed behind them. Elsa shook her head. That was weird, right?

But she didn’t have time to dwell on it. For at that moment Gale returned, swirling around her and tickling her ears.

“Anything?” she asked. But the Wind Spirit moved Elsa’s skirt from side to side, the spirit’s version of saying nope. Elsa sighed.

“Okay, then,” she replied. “It must have been the wind. And maybe it blew some tree branches down, which caused the tent to tear.” It didn’t seem likely, but she was out of explanations. And everything seemed quiet now; even the storm was starting to subside. Whatever it was, it was gone. Her shoulders slumped in relief.

“Thanks, Gale,” she said to the spirit. “I’ll see you in the morning. Remember, we’re going to Arendelle tomorrow!”

Gale swept up a big pile of wet leaves in excitement. The Wind Spirit loved going to Arendelle, especially now that Anna had commissioned that beautiful statue of their parents in the town square. Gale loved to spend hours swirling around the sculpture of Queen Iduna. They clearly had been special friends back when their mother was young. If only the Wind Spirit could talk. Elsa was sure it had so many wonderful stories. She wondered, not for the first time, if Gale missed her mother as much as she did.

After saying goodbye to the spirit, Elsa made her way to the tent that was still intact. The rain had stopped completely now, but she was wet and freezing, not to mention wide awake from the whole crazy saga. With that, and the fact that there were now five bodies sharing their tiny tent, she was pretty sure none of them would get much sleep.

But to Elsa’s surprise, when she crawled back into the tent, all she heard was snoring. Olaf, Sven, Kristoff, and Anna were all snuggled up under the reindeer hides—with Olaf using Sven’s body as a pillow.

They were all peacefully asleep. As if nothing had happened at all.
chapters.zh:
它是真的！

它在这里！"他像炮弹一样扑向两姐妹，她们一起接住他、抱住他。

艾莎看了他一眼。"奥拉夫，我们说过了。

根本没有亡者——只是暴风雨，而且——"又有两道身影冲进帐篷，挤得几乎没法动。"奥拉夫没开玩笑，"克斯托夫说，喘得像是刚跑了一英里，"外面有东西。

斯文和我都看见了！"斯文点点头，湿漉漉的毛里直发抖。

艾莎感到一丝寒意掠过身体，而这和此刻帘子在风中翻飞、灌进帐篷的冷风丝毫无关。

风暴太猛烈，她连几英尺外男孩们的帐篷都看不见了。"你们不是故意吓我们吧？"她问，半希望真是这样。"是啊，因为我们可不好吓，你知道的，"安娜插嘴，微微挺起胸膛，"我是说，我面对过致命的恶狼、糟糕的男友……更别提我亲姐姐造出的巨型雪怪，把我从她那冰封孤堡里扔出去！"艾莎朝安娜投去一个歉意的眼神。

那肯定不是她最姐妹情深的时刻。"听着，"她说，把奥拉夫从身上扒下来放到地上，"我敢说你们只是被克斯托夫讲的故事吓到了。

然后风以奇怪的方式吹进来，然后——""不，"克斯托夫坚定地说，胸口仍快速起伏，"不只是风。

还有个影子。

一个绝对不是风形的影子。

对吧，斯文？"斯文示威似的在空中挥了挥前蹄。

它们映出布伦尼火光的闪烁，在帐篷壁上投下诡异的影子。

艾莎感到一丝不安在胃里游动。"还有那呻吟声，"奥拉夫补充，"很多听起来很邪恶的呻吟。""我想我也听见呻吟了，"安娜若有所思地说，担忧地看着艾莎，"就在男孩们进来之前。""风也会呻吟，"艾莎试图说，觉得自己像在抓救命稻草。

她想让所有人冷静，但连她自己都承认开始有点发毛了。

她试着告诉自己，魔法森林的精灵绝不会让任何东西伤害她或她的家人。

但连布伦尼都开始有点紧张，从帐篷一头窜到另一头。"听着，我们没在开玩笑。"克斯托夫回头望向风暴，其他人也顺着他的目光看去。"我告诉你们，外面有某个东西或某个人。""不只是某个东西！

是亡者！"奥拉夫坚持，"就像故事里那样！"他试图躲到斯文背后。"我觉得它想把我们活活吃掉！"艾莎吸了口气，认命地接受这不可避免的事。

倒不是她真信树林里有什么亡者。

但确实有事在发生，而且她确信，如果不弄清楚，谁都别想睡。

她爬向帐篷入口。"你要去哪儿？"安娜关切地问。"我去查看。""没我你不行！"艾莎叹气。"你会淋透的。""只要能救你不被亡者当晚餐，我乐意淋透，"安娜回敬。

艾莎呻吟。

又来了。

她爱小妹妹的勇敢，但担心哪天这会害了她。"安娜——"她刚开口。"听着，我们一起去，"克斯托夫宣布。"全都去？"奥拉夫尖声问，显然对这个提议不太自在。"所有人类，"克斯托夫澄清，拍拍他的头，"奥拉夫，我们需要你和斯文守着帐篷。"斯文呼了口气，给了克斯托夫一个愤愤的眼神。

克斯托夫歉意地耸耸肩。

艾莎走向帐篷入口，眯眼望向雨中。"准备好了？"她问，不太确定自己是在问克斯托夫和安娜——还是问自己。"生来就准备好了！"安娜宣称，显然没有同样的顾虑。

她毫不犹豫地推开艾莎，跌跌撞撞冲进雨夜。

艾莎摇摇头，随即慌忙追上，克斯托夫紧跟在她身后。

当他们踏进风雨，天空发出一声险恶的问候般轰鸣。

雨下得那么大，几乎什么都看不见。

艾莎一挥手，在两棵树间造出一片冰棚，三人赶紧躲了进去。

一到棚下，艾莎深吸一口气，试图辨清方向，然后瞥见了男孩们的帐篷。

她猛地吸了口气。

克斯托夫、斯文和奥拉夫的帐篷被完全掀翻了，这或许能用风来解释。

可是……"那些是……爪痕吗？"艾莎喊着问，好盖过风声。

她的目光沿帐篷侧面往上，那里像是被刀划过。

她瞥了克斯托夫一眼。"有什么东西袭击了你们的帐篷？""我不知道。"克斯托夫和她一样困惑。"我们听见呻吟、看见影子，就跑到你们帐篷来了。"他顿了顿，挺起胸膛。"我是说，只是确认你们没事。

不是因为害怕。""当然啦，亲爱的，"安娜安慰他，把手支在他背上。

然后她转向艾莎。"也许帐篷挂到树枝上了。""也许吧，"艾莎说。

她的目光抬起来侦察帐篷后的树林。

但帐篷离任何树都不够近，不可能缠到树枝。

她不安地咬住下唇。

她一秒都不信那是鬼故事里的怪物，但与此同时，那必定是某种东西。

狼？

狼够聪明，不会在这团混乱里出来。

而且，它们通常只为食物——然而附近圆木上还放着一盘他们晚餐在火上烤的剩香肠。

湿透了，但按狼的标准绝对还能吃。

但还能是什么呢？

她抬眼望天，唱了几个音符。

片刻后，风灵盖尔疾冲而来，绕着他俩打着转，像在问怎么了。

当然，风暴一点没影响到这位风之精灵。"你能去四周看看吗？"艾莎问它，"看看有没有什么不对劲的东西？"盖尔卷起身子飞出去，消失在黑暗中。

艾莎耸耸肩，转向妹妹和克斯托夫。"外面要是有什么，盖尔会找到的，"她向他们保证。

安娜打了个寒战。

克斯托夫搂住她，把她拉近。"你还好吗？"他问。"我好得很！"安娜抗议，用力推开他，让艾莎意外。"我只是冻坏了！

而且浑身湿透。"她板起脸。"我们到底为什么在这儿？"艾莎皱眉。"我可没说你必须来，"她提醒妹妹，"你本可以留在帐篷里陪奥拉夫和斯文。""帐篷……"克斯托夫的目光落到他塌掉的帐篷上。"等等！

我的帐篷怎么了？""抱歉？"艾莎转向他，这下真糊涂了。"你在说什么？""它……毁了。

我漂亮的帐篷。

而且……侧面那是道裂口吗？

我刚付清钱呢，知道吗！"他责备地瞥了安娜一眼，安娜耸耸肩，像完全不懂他在说什么。

一丝担忧在艾莎胃里扑腾。

她从克斯托夫看向安娜，安娜困惑地回望她。

他们只是在闹着玩？

如果是，那一点都不好笑。"听着，你们俩回我们帐篷吧。

看看奥拉夫和斯文，"她努力咽下担忧，"我等盖尔回来。"她以为安娜会争辩，但出乎意料，妹妹木然地点点头，挽着克斯托夫的胳膊，把他领回帐篷。

他们爬进去，拉上帘子关在身后。

艾莎摇摇头。

那很怪，对吧？

但她没时间细想。

就在这时，盖尔回来了，绕着她打转，挠她的耳朵。"有发现吗？"她问。

但风之精灵把艾莎的裙子左右摆动，那是精灵版的"没有"。

艾莎叹气。"好吧，那么，"她回答，"那一定是风。

也许它吹断了一些树枝，把帐篷刮破了。"这似乎不太可能，但她已无解释。

而现在一切似乎都安静了；连风暴都开始平息。

不管那是什么，它走了。

她松了口气，肩膀垮下来。"谢了，盖尔，"她对精灵说，"明早见。

记住，我们明天要去阿伦黛尔！"盖尔兴奋地卷起一大堆湿叶子。
