sentences.zh: 不，还是那么黑。"我想我该去找索伦森谈谈，"她说，指的是那位住在离镇子有些距离的阿伦黛尔科学家。

sentences.en: He had been helpful the last time Arendelle had fallen under a curse. “He might have some answers.” “Good idea,” Anna agreed. “I’ll go saddle up Havski.” The swift stallion had been her horse since childhood. “It’s a few hours’ ride, but if we leave now, we can be back by…” She stopped, glancing up at the sky. “Well, maybe not dark…” Elsa shook her head. “Anna, you should stay here.
sentences.zh: 上次阿伦黛尔被诅咒时，他帮过忙。"说不定他能给些答案。""好主意，"安娜表示同意。"我去给哈夫斯基备鞍。"这匹骏马从她小时候起就是她的坐骑。"骑上几个时辰就到，但如果我们现在出发，应该能在……"她停住，抬眼看了看天。"嗯，也许不至于天黑……"艾莎摇摇头。"安娜，你该留在这儿。

sentences.en: Keep getting ready for the Polar Nights festivities.
sentences.zh: 继续筹备极夜节的庆典。

sentences.en: You said yourself that there’s a lot to do.” “It can wait,” Anna declared, placing her hands on her hips. “I mean, the festival is important, yes.
sentences.zh: 你自己也说了，有很多事要做。""可以等等，"安娜双手叉腰，果断地说。"我是说，庆典固然重要，没错。

sentences.en: But so are you.
sentences.zh: 但你也很重要。

sentences.en: And I’m not about to let you go wandering off on your own when there could be a monster on the loose.” “Oh, so now you believe in the draugr?” Elsa raised an eyebrow.
sentences.zh: 而且外面可能有个怪物在游荡，我绝不会让你一个人乱跑。""哦，这么说来你现在相信有亡灵了？"艾莎挑起眉毛。

sentences.en: She knew she could argue with her sister about this.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己可以就此跟妹妹争论一番。

sentences.en: But she also knew she wouldn’t win.
sentences.zh: 但她也知道自己争不赢。

sentences.en: And deep down, she realized she preferred to have Anna by her side.
sentences.zh: 而在内心深处，她意识到自己更希望安娜陪在身边。

sentences.en: Their best adventures, after all, had always been ones they had together.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，她们最棒的冒险，向来是一起经历的。

sentences.en: And they still had a lot of catching up to do. “I believe in keeping my sister safe,” Anna declared. “Besides, Kristoff can stay and be in charge.
sentences.zh: 而且她们还有好多话没聊完呢。"我相信让我妹妹平安无事，"安娜坚定地说。"再说了，克斯托夫可以留下主持大局。

sentences.en: He’s going to be a member of the royal family soon.
sentences.zh: 他很快就要成为王室的一员了。

sentences.en: Might as well get his feet wet.” Kristoff, who had been walking by with an armful of snow cones, stopped in his tracks. “Wait, what?” Anna beamed at him. “You can stay here and keep everyone on task, right?
sentences.zh: 不妨先让他练练手。"正抱着一摞刨冰走过的克斯托夫，一下子停住了脚步。"等等，什么？"安娜冲他粲然一笑。"你留在这儿，盯着大家把事情办好，对吧？

sentences.en: While Elsa and I try to figure out what’s going on?” “Of course,” Kristoff declared without the slightest pause. “Whatever you need.
sentences.zh: 我和艾莎去搞清楚到底怎么回事？""当然，"克斯托夫毫不犹豫地宣布。"你需要什么尽管说。

sentences.en: I’m your man.” He tapped his chest proudly, accidentally dropping one of the snow cones on the ground in the process.
sentences.zh: 我听你吩咐。"他骄傲地拍了拍胸口，结果不小心把其中一份刨冰掉在了地上。

sentences.en: Sven quickly slurped it up. “Thanks, honey!
sentences.zh: 斯文飞快地把它舔了个干净。"谢啦，亲爱的！

sentences.en: You’re the best!” Anna stood on her tiptoes to give him a kiss, then dashed toward the stables.
sentences.zh: 你最棒了！"安娜踮起脚尖给了他一个吻，然后朝马厩飞奔而去。

sentences.en: Kristoff looked at Elsa, his easy smile fading a little. “You’ll keep her safe?” he asked. “We’ll keep each other safe,” she told him, laying a reassuring hand on his shoulder. “Nothing will happen.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫望着艾莎，轻松的笑容淡了些。"你会保证她的安全？"他问。"我们会互相保护，"她把手安慰地搭在他肩上，对他说。"不会有事的。

sentences.en: I promise.” “I’m holding you to that,” he said with a wag of his finger before turning to distribute his remaining cones.
sentences.zh: 我保证。""这话我可记下了，"他晃着手指说，然后转身去分发剩下的刨冰。

sentences.en: Elsa watched him for a moment, then turned toward the castle, figuring she’d stop by the kitchen to grab some food for the road before she called for her own steed, the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 艾莎看了他一会儿，转身朝城堡走去，心想在唤来自己的坐骑水马之前，先去厨房拿点路上吃的东西。

sentences.en: As she walked across the bridge, she took one last look at the dark sky.
sentences.zh: 走过吊桥时，她最后望了一眼漆黑的天空。

sentences.en: An involuntary shiver slipped down her spine. “Surely, there’s got to be a logical explanation,” she told herself as she stepped into the castle. “And Sorenson will be able to make sense of it all.” “This doesn’t make any sense!” Sorenson paced the tower room, flipping his long beard over his shoulder as he stared at some astronomical charts he had hung on the walls.
sentences.zh: 一阵不由自主的寒意顺着脊背滑下。"一定会有合乎逻辑的解释，"她踏进城堡时对自己说。"而索伦森一定能把这团乱象理出头绪。""这根本说不通！"索伦森在塔楼房间里踱步，把长胡子甩到肩后，盯着墙上挂的几张星象图。

sentences.en: He picked up an old copper sundial, turning it over in his hands before setting it back down on the desk.
sentences.zh: 他拿起一个旧铜制日晷，在手里翻来转去，又把它放回桌上。

sentences.en: Elsa glanced at Anna.
sentences.zh: 艾莎瞥了安娜一眼。

sentences.en: So much for an easy scientific explanation. “Could it just be that the Polar Nights came early?” she asked, knowing she was grasping at straws. “No.” Sorenson shook his head. “I’ve mapped out the sun in its relation to the planet, and it’s not due to slip below our horizon for another week.
sentences.zh: 轻松的科学解释，这下泡汤了。"会不会只是极夜提前到了？"她问，明知自己是在抓最后一根稻草。"不是，"索伦森摇摇头。"我已经把太阳与地球的相对位置绘成图，它还要再过一周才会落到我们的地平线以下。

sentences.en: Besides, around these parts, the Polar Nights only give off a soft blue glow.
sentences.zh: 况且，在咱们这一带，极夜只会散发柔和的蓝色微光。

sentences.en: Not this suffocating blackness.
sentences.zh: 而不是这种令人窒息的漆黑。

sentences.en: It’s almost as if we’re experiencing a solar eclipse.
sentences.zh: 简直就像我们正在经历一场日食。

sentences.en: But there isn’t one scheduled for the next twenty-five years.” He raked a hand through his graying hair, shaking his head. “I don’t know what to tell you.
sentences.zh: 但未来二十五年里都没有日食预报。"他用手耙过花白的头发，摇着头。"我实在不知道该怎么跟你们说。

sentences.en: There is no scientific explanation for any of this.” Elsa sank down into a nearby chair, discouraged.
sentences.zh: 这一切都没有任何科学解释。"艾莎泄气地跌坐在近旁的椅子上。

sentences.en: It hadn’t been easy getting here.
sentences.zh: 来这一趟并不容易。

sentences.en: Sorenson lived in the middle of nowhere, and navigating their way through the darkness had been a challenge even with the Water Nokk guiding her.
sentences.zh: 索伦森住在荒郊野外，即便有这个水马引路，摸黑赶路也是个挑战。

sentences.en: She’d really been hoping it would at least be worth the trip.
sentences.zh: 她原本真希望，这趟至少能不虚此行。

sentences.en: Instead, it seemed, it was a complete dead end. “You don’t think it could be something…magical?” she asked hesitantly.
sentences.zh: 可看来，这完全是个死胡同。"你觉得……会不会是魔法的缘故？"她迟疑地问。

sentences.en: She didn’t want to mention the silly draugr theory, but could there be something else out there causing this?
sentences.zh: 她不想提那荒唐的亡灵说法，可会不会是别的什么东西在作祟？

sentences.en: Sorenson shook his head. “I’m a scientist,” he reminded them. “I deal in facts and logic.
sentences.zh: 索伦森摇摇头。"我是科学家，"他提醒她们。"我只讲事实和逻辑。

sentences.en: If it’s magical answers you seek, you need to check with the trolls.
sentences.zh: 如果你们要找魔法层面的答案，得去问地精。

sentences.en: That’s more their thing.” Anna frowned. “The trolls are really busy this time of year with their crystal celebration.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的专长。"安娜皱起眉。"每年这个时候，地精们都在忙着他们的水晶庆典。

sentences.en: I don’t want to bother them unless it’s really necessary.” “You might not have a choice,” Sorensen said grimly. “Sometimes things are out of the realm of science, and while it pains me to admit it, this is not the first time I’ve seen this sort of strange change in the weather.” He pulled at his beard. “The last time it happened, I was just a boy, but I remember everyone saying it was the work of a draugr.” Elsa and Anna looked at each other. “Wait, you believe in draugrs?” Anna asked. “But you’re a scientist!” “I know, but I remember my father being certain he saw a draugr once—and my father was not a man easily fooled,” Sorenson said, leaning against a long table for support. “He talked about that draugr and its relation to the weather with such detail that I found myself believing him.” Elsa couldn’t suppress a shudder.
sentences.zh: 除非真有必要，否则我不想打扰他们。""你们也许别无选择，"索伦森面色凝重地说。"有些事情超出了科学的范畴，尽管我痛心地承认这一点，但这已不是我第一次见到这种诡异的天气变化。"他揪着胡子。"上次发生时，我还只是个孩子，但我记得大家都说是亡灵在作祟。"艾莎和安娜对视一眼。"等等，你相信有亡灵？"安娜问。"可你是科学家啊！""我知道，但我记得父亲确信自己曾见过一次亡灵——而我父亲可不是那么容易上当的人，"索伦森倚着长桌支撑身体说道。"他把那亡灵以及它与天气的关系讲得极为详细，让我不由得信了他。"艾莎忍不住打了个寒颤。

sentences.en: If Sorenson believed in draugrs, maybe they should be concerned.
sentences.zh: 如果索伦森都相信有亡灵，那她们也许真该担心了。

sentences.en: Sorenson shrugged. “But then again, I didn’t see the creature myself.
sentences.zh: 索伦森耸耸肩。"不过话说回来，那怪物我毕竟没亲眼见过。

sentences.en: In any case, it might be something you want to mention to the trolls.” Anna side-eyed Elsa nervously. “We will bring it up to them.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这事你们或许该跟地精提一提。"安娜紧张地斜眼瞟向艾莎。"我们会向他们提起的。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sorenson.” Elsa rose to her feet. “Let’s go back to Arendelle,” she said. “We’ll check on everyone first.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，索伦森。"艾莎站起身。"我们回阿伦黛尔吧，"她说。"先去看看大家情况如何。

sentences.en: Then we’ll figure out the next steps—if that’s even necessary.” She shrugged. “Who knows?
sentences.zh: 然后再决定下一步——如果还有必要的话。"她耸耸肩。"谁知道呢？

sentences.en: Maybe the sun will rise tomorrow and everything will be back to normal.” The two sisters said their goodbyes to Sorenson and headed home by horseback, the Water Nokk once again leading the way.
sentences.zh: 也许明天太阳就会升起，一切恢复如常。"两姐妹向索伦森道别，骑马回家，水马再次在前面引路。

sentences.en: But even the water horse’s icy glow seemed a little dimmer as they pushed through the marsh.
sentences.zh: 但即便水马冰蓝色的光芒，在她们穿过沼泽时也显得黯淡了些。

sentences.en: The blackness hovered over them as if it were a living thing. “This is getting really creepy,” Anna remarked, reaching up to push away a low-hanging branch from a nearby tree. “Especially after Sorenson brought up the draugr thing, too.
sentences.zh: 黑暗笼罩在她们头顶，仿佛一个有生命的活物。"这越来越瘆人了，"安娜一边说，一边伸手拨开旁边树木低垂的枝桠。"尤其是索伦森也提到了亡灵那档子事之后。

sentences.en: I mean, that man only believes in facts.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那个人只信事实。

sentences.en: Could Kristoff’s story really have summoned Sinister Sissel?” “Oh, don’t start with that nickname again.” Elsa choked out a laugh, but it no longer felt very funny. “Even if there is a draugr out there, that doesn’t mean it’s the reanimated corpse of some random princess who died years ago.” “But it could be,” Anna argued. “And to be honest, I wouldn’t blame the girl one bit!
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫的故事真的能把"阴森的西塞尔"召唤出来吗？""哦，别再叫那个外号了。"艾莎干笑了一声，但那笑已不那么好笑了。"就算外面真有亡灵，也不代表那就是多年前死去的哪个公主复活后的尸体。""但有可能啊，"安娜争辩道。"老实说，那姑娘我一点都不会怪她！

sentences.en: I mean, being murdered by your own sister in cold blood?
sentences.zh: 我是说，被自己的亲姐妹冷血地谋杀？

sentences.en: I might decide to come back as an unhinged evil monster ready to seek revenge, too!” Elsa couldn’t help cringing a little after Anna spoke.
sentences.zh: 我大概也会化作一个疯狂的恶怪回来复仇吧！"安娜说完后，艾莎不禁微微一缩。

sentences.en: Suddenly she wasn’t thinking of the Vesterland sisters anymore, but of seeing her own sister, Anna, ice cold on the ballroom floor when they were children.
sentences.zh: 她忽然不再想维斯特兰姐妹，而是想起小时候，亲眼看见自己的妹妹安娜冰冷地躺在舞厅地板上。

sentences.en: And herself, screaming desperately for their parents.
sentences.zh: 还有她自己，绝望地哭喊着找父母。

sentences.en: If anything had happened to her sister that night… Anna’s face turned ashen in the darkness. “Oh my gosh!
sentences.zh: 要是那一晚妹妹出了什么意外……安娜在黑暗中脸色煞白。"天哪！

sentences.en: I’m so sorry.
sentences.zh: 我太抱歉了。

sentences.en: I didn’t mean…” She clamped a hand over her mouth. “I’ll just shut up now.” “No.
sentences.zh: 我不是故意……"她用手捂住嘴。"我现在还是闭嘴吧。""不。

sentences.en: It’s okay,” Elsa assured her with a small smile. “I know that you know I’d never hurt you on purpose.” “Of course not,” Anna affirmed. “The whole thing was just an accident, pure and simple.
sentences.zh: 没关系的，"艾莎微微笑着安慰她。"我知道你明白，我绝不会故意伤害你。""当然不会，"安娜肯定地说。"整件事不过是个意外，再简单不过。

sentences.en: I know that for a fact, even if I don’t remember it happening.” Elsa cringed again.
sentences.zh: 这一点我十分确定，尽管我自己并不记得当时发生了什么。"艾莎又缩了一下。

sentences.en: Anna had never recovered the memories the trolls had taken from her the night of the accident.
sentences.zh: 安娜始终没能找回地精在意外那晚从她脑中取走的记忆。

sentences.en: So many memories of them growing up together, lost forever.
sentences.zh: 她们一起长大的那么多记忆，永远地遗失了。

sentences.en: Which meant it was up to Elsa to keep them alive.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，让那些记忆留存下去的责任落在了艾莎肩上。

sentences.en: She paused for a moment, thinking. “I know we don’t talk about what happened when we were kids very much.
sentences.zh: 她停顿片刻，思索着。"我知道，我们很少谈起小时候发生的事。

sentences.en: And I get it—I really do.
sentences.zh: 我理解——真的理解。

sentences.en: But if you ever wanted to…well, I wouldn’t mind, you know.” Anna’s eyes widened. “Really?” “It’s good to look back sometimes,” Elsa assured her. “At all our memories—even the bad ones.
sentences.zh: 但如果你哪天想谈……嗯，我不会介意的，你懂的。"安娜睁大了眼睛。"真的吗？""偶尔回顾一下是好的，"艾莎向她保证。"回顾我们所有的记忆——哪怕是糟糕的那些。

sentences.en: I’ve been doing that a lot in Ahtohallan, and it’s actually helped me get over some things.
sentences.zh: 我在阿托哈兰经常这样做，它确实帮我走出了一些心结。

sentences.en: And I’d love to share some of them with you….” She stroked the Water Nokk’s mane thoughtfully, feeling its icy waves ripple through her fingers. “Our whole childhood was filled with secrets.
sentences.zh: 而且我很乐意跟你分享其中的一些……"她若有所思地抚摸着水马的鬃毛，感受着冰冷的波纹从指间流过。"我们的整个童年都充满了秘密。

sentences.en: Our parents’, mine…” She cocked her head. “Did you have any secrets?” “Wouldn’t you like to know!” Anna grinned mischievously.
sentences.zh: 父母的，我的……"她歪了歪头。"你有什么秘密吗？""你倒是想知道！"安娜俏皮地咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: Elsa laughed. “Okay, fine.” Elsa mock-pouted. “In any case, I’m glad we’ve put all that behind us and we can talk openly.” “Me too!” Anna declared.
sentences.zh: 艾莎笑了起来。"好吧，好吧。"艾莎故意撅了撅嘴。"总之，我很高兴我们都把那些抛在了身后，现在能坦诚交谈了。""我也是！"安娜大声说。

sentences.en: Then she sighed. “What’s wrong?” Elsa asked, concerned by her sister’s expression. “It’s just…” Anna shrugged. “I don’t know.
sentences.zh: 接着她叹了口气。"怎么了？"艾莎问，被妹妹的神情惹得担心起来。"只是……"安娜耸耸肩。"我也不知道。

sentences.en: Nothing, I guess.” “No secrets, remember?” “Okay, right.
sentences.zh: 大概没什么吧。""说好了不藏秘密的，记得吗？""哦对，没错。

sentences.en: It’s just that…sometimes I can’t help but be sad about all the time we lost together when we were growing up,” Anna noted. “I don’t mean just the missing memories.
sentences.zh: 只是……有时候我不由得为我们成长中错失的相处时光感到难过，"安娜说道。"我指的不仅是那些缺失的记忆。

sentences.en: But all those years we spent apart.
sentences.zh: 还有我们分开的那些年。

sentences.en: I should have tried harder to talk to you….” Elsa shuddered, remembering that terrible time when she’d locked herself in her room.
sentences.zh: 我本该更努力地试着跟你说话……"艾莎打了个寒颤，想起那段可怕的岁月——她把自己锁在房间里。

sentences.en: How lonely she’d been.
sentences.zh: 那时她是多么孤独。

sentences.en: How desperate and sad. “I regret that, too,” she said softly. “I could have really used a sister back then.
sentences.zh: 多么绝望又悲伤。"那件事我也后悔，"她轻声说。"那时候我真的很需要一个姐妹在身边。

sentences.en: But instead, I pushed you away.
sentences.zh: 可我却把你推开了。

sentences.en: I was just so scared of hurting you again.
sentences.zh: 我只是太害怕再次伤到你。

sentences.en: And yet, in the end, I did hurt you.
sentences.zh: 然而到头来，我还是伤了你。

sentences.en: Just in a different way.” “It wasn’t your fault,” Anna insisted. “You were just a kid.
sentences.zh: 只是换了一种方式。""那不是你的错，"安娜坚持说。"你当时只是个孩子。

sentences.en: And you were scared.
sentences.zh: 而且你很害怕。

sentences.en: I don’t blame you for any of it.
sentences.zh: 那些事我都不怪你。

sentences.en: I’m just glad you’re all right now.
sentences.zh: 我只高兴你现在没事了。

sentences.en: That you’re not afraid of your powers anymore.
sentences.zh: 高兴你不再害怕自己的魔力。

sentences.en: And that they’ve become an important part of who you are.
sentences.zh: 高兴它们已成为你本身重要的一部分。

sentences.en: You’re the Snow Queen.
sentences.zh: 你是冰雪女王。

sentences.en: You’re powerful.
sentences.zh: 你强大有力。

sentences.en: Magical.” She smiled warmly. “And yet, at the end of the day, you’ll always be my sister.” Elsa’s heart clenched when she gazed at her sister’s face.
sentences.zh: 充满魔力。"她温暖地微笑着。"然而说到底，你永远都是我的妹妹。"艾莎凝视着妹妹的脸，心头一紧。

sentences.en: She hadn’t always deserved Anna’s love.
sentences.zh: 她并非一直配得上安娜的爱。

sentences.en: But she was so grateful to have it. “And you’ll always be mine…Queen of Arendelle.” Anna blushed hard. “I still get weirded out by that title sometimes.” “Well, you’ve more than earned it,” Elsa assured her.
sentences.zh: 但她很感恩能得到这份爱。"而你永远是我的……阿伦黛尔女王。"安娜脸涨得通红。"那个头衔有时还是让我有点不自在。""嗯，你早挣来了，"艾莎向她保证。

sentences.en: She met her sister’s eyes with her own. “In any case, we can’t change the past,” she added. “All we can do is keep moving forward.
sentences.zh: 她与妹妹目光相接。"总之，我们无法改变过去，"她补充道。"我们所能做的，就是继续向前。

sentences.en: And make new memories, together.” Anna grinned. “Sounds good to—” Her words were cut off by a sudden wailing sound. “What was that?” Elsa whispered, slowing the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 一起去创造新的记忆。"安娜咧嘴一笑。"听起来不错——"一阵突如其来的哀嚎打断了她的话。"那是什么？"艾莎压低声音，放慢了水马。

sentences.en: The spirit pricked its ears.
sentences.zh: 那精灵竖起了耳朵。

sentences.en: Clearly it had heard it, too. “Wolves?” Anna shook her head, looking just as confused—and scared—as Elsa felt. “That didn’t sound like wolves.” “No,” Elsa agreed, feeling the hairs on the back of her neck stand on end. “It sounded like…” She trailed off.
sentences.zh: 显然它也听见了。"是狼？"安娜摇摇头，神情和艾莎一样困惑——也一样害怕。"那听起来不像狼。""不像，"艾莎附和，感到后颈的汗毛都竖了起来。"听起来像……"她声音低了下去。

sentences.en: What did it sound like?
sentences.zh: 那听起来像什么？

sentences.en: Like nothing she’d ever heard before.
sentences.zh: 是从未听过的声音。

sentences.en: She squinted into the darkness, urging the spirit onward.
sentences.zh: 她眯起眼睛望向黑暗，催促那精灵继续前行。

sentences.en: ARRR!!!
The Water Nokk reared backward, icy water spraying from its mane and soaking Elsa’s dress as something leapt out of the bushes.
sentences.zh: 水马猛地向后扬起前蹄，鬃毛里溅出冰水，打湿了艾莎的衣裙，与此同时有什么东西从灌木丛中一跃而出。

sentences.en: Or was it someone?
sentences.zh: 还是说，那是个人？

sentences.en: Elsa couldn’t take her eyes off it, heart pounding in her chest.
sentences.zh: 艾莎目不转睛地盯着它，心在胸腔里狂跳。

sentences.en: It was clearly human-shaped, but that was where all similarities ended.
sentences.zh: 它的轮廓分明是人形，但也仅此而已。

sentences.en: It had blackened skin, misshapen bones that jutted out at weird angles, and green slime oozing from its pores.
sentences.zh: 它皮肤黝黑，畸形的骨头以诡异的角度凸出，毛孔里渗着绿色的黏液。

sentences.en: Elsa shuddered as the thing seemed to grin madly at them.
sentences.zh: 那东西仿佛朝她们疯狂地咧嘴笑着，艾莎打了个寒颤。

sentences.en: Its teeth were broken, darkened, and dripping with something suspiciously red. “Oh my gosh,” Anna whispered. “Is that…is that…?” “The draugr!” Elsa cried in horror. “It’s real!”
sentences.zh: 它的牙齿残缺发黑，滴淌着可疑的红色液体。"天哪，"安娜低声说。"那是不是……那是不是……？""亡灵！"艾莎惊恐地喊道。"它是真的！

chapters.title: Chapter Six: Anna
chapters.en:
ANNA FROZE.

Had Elsa just said draugr? As she stared at the ghastly creature slowly gliding toward them, Anna knew there was no other explanation. Olaf and Kristoff had been right.

The draugr looked from Elsa to Anna, reaching out for them with blackened hands and sharp nails, gnashing what was left of its rotting teeth. Anna jumped, her heartbeat quickening as the draugr hissed. It sounded like a snake. Then it let out the eeriest of moans. The sound went right through her.

Thunder rumbled in the distance and Anna felt the wind pick up, making some of the trees around them sway violently. She glanced at the sky; it was just as dark as it had been before in the village, but this time a storm was moving in fast.

“Anna, we need to go now! Follow me!” Elsa cried as the Water Nokk instantly reacted, racing out of the draugr’s reach.

“On it! Havski, let’s move!” Anna turned to follow the Water Spirit’s icy path when CRACK!

Lightning struck a massive tree in front of her, sending it crashing to the ground. Anna pulled on Havski’s reins just in time to keep them from being hit. The trunk hit the ground with a quake. Startled, Havski reared on his back legs.

“Easy!” Anna cried out, reaching for the reins again to calm the horse. But she was too late. Anna flew off his back, landing hard on the ground, her head smacking against what felt like a rock. Pain seared through her body and the world lost focus for a second, but Anna fought her way back, sitting up in time to see Havski bolt in the opposite direction.

“Anna! Where are you!” Elsa cried out from somewhere on the other side of the downed tree.

“Here! I’m all right!” Anna lied. Her hands flew to her head and she winced as she felt something wet. Sticky. Was she bleeding? Was it bad? How was she getting out of there? The downed tree seemed to have hit two more as it dropped, and they had fallen like huge dominos, forming a giant barricade so tall and wide Anna couldn’t even see her sister through it. It was amazing she hadn’t been killed. “But I don’t know how I’m getting around this.”

“We’ll get to you!” Elsa said, her voice sounding strained. “Just keep away from the draugr!”

Anna’s eyes shot open. Draugr. How had she forgotten about the draugr? She whipped her head around just in time to see the creature stalking toward her, red slime dripping from its grotesque mouth. She had to get out of there!

“Sissssstterrrrrrr….”

Anna froze. What was that? Was that the draugr? Had it just said sister? A chill tripped down her spine.

“Sissssstterrrrrrr….”

The draugr could talk! “Sister? No, thank you! I’ve already got one.” She couldn’t wait for Elsa and the Water Nokk to reach her. Her head was pounding so hard she wasn’t sure she could stand.

“Myyyyyy sisssssstttterrrrr,” the draugr hissed, dragging what was left of its wretched body in tattered clothing toward her.

Thump. Drag.

Thump. Drag.

Thump. Drag.

Run! Anna told herself, pushing her body to stand even as her vision blurred. She tried to step forward, but her left leg wouldn’t budge. She looked down in surprise. Her foot was caught in between several thick, winding roots. She must have gotten ensnared when she fell. Anna tugged on her leg—hard—but it was stuck, seemingly fastened in place.

The draugr lunged forward again, and Anna winced as it reached out with blackened hands. This is it, she thought, holding her breath, and then exhaling fast when nothing happened. She looked up in surprise. The draugr was holding her folded copy of the Village Crown. It must have fallen from her satchel when she had been thrown from Havski. The draugr looked from Anna to the paper and back at Anna again. What was left of its face curled into a snarl.

Could the draugr read? Anna suddenly thought of Wael’s story about how Anna, the younger sister, had replaced the queen on the throne.

Oh, no.

“Sissel?” Anna whispered.

The creature’s face was even more grotesque than before. “Sissssterrrrr!” It lunged straight toward her.

Anna thought fast.

The draugr is Sissel.

Its sister tried to take its crown.

I took the crown from Elsa.

Oh, no…

“You don’t understand,” Anna begged, trying to pull her leg free once again. “Elsa gave me the crown!”

But the draugr wasn’t listening. It kept coming, moaning even louder.

Thump. Drag.

It was almost on top of her now. Panic gripped Anna as she tried to yank her foot free in desperation. Her boot was completely wedged. “Come on, come on, come on,” Anna begged, willing her foot to miraculously loosen somehow, trying to wiggle her toes, her ankle, grip her boot harder—anything—to pull herself free. But it was no use. The draugr was bearing down on her. Elsa wasn’t going to make it to her in time. The thing was so close, Anna could smell the rot coming off it, making her want to vomit. Her mind suddenly went to the villagers’ talk of draugrs. If this thing sneezed on her, would she turn into a draugr?

Anna spun around, looking for something to defend herself with. Her eyes landed on a bare branch from the tree she was tangled in. Reaching up with two hands, she snapped one of the largest twigs off clean. She whirled around, brandishing it like a sword.

“Stay back!” Anna commanded. “Back!”

For a moment, the draugr seemed confused; its creepy smile disappeared.

“That’s right! I’m in charge here!” Anna said, feeling slight relief. She was the boss! Not this icky, crawly thing that had slipped through the darkened day trying to terrify her and her horse. A flash of lightning lit up the midnight path. “Stay away from me and my sister!”

The draugr’s hollowed eyes widened and its smile returned, appearing even more gruesome than it had before. Anna cringed as a worm slid its way out of the draugr’s mouth.

“Sissstttterrrrrrrr!” it moaned again.

“No!” Anna shouted. “I won’t let you hurt us!” Anna swatted the air in front of the creature with her branch, trying to scare it.

The creature roared, pushing forward again, bearing down on Anna now. She leaned back, and that was when she heard it—whoosh!

Ice cracked across the ground, forming a sheet beneath Anna and the draugr’s feet.

Whoosh! Elsa and the Water Nokk had made it around the barricade and were running her way. Elsa shot sheet after sheet of ice at the draugr.

The ice formed around Anna’s feet and more importantly around the roots Anna’s boot was caught in. She watched as it crackled, freezing in place over the vines and branches. Maybe now she could crack the roots, brittle from the ice on them, and free herself. She whacked at them with the branch and heard a snap. Anna yanked on her foot again and felt herself free-falling backward. Unable to right herself in time, she landed on her behind.

Angered, the draugr shot forward toward Anna yet again. Anna scurried back on her hands and feet, racing to get out of its way.

Whoosh! More ice appeared, forming a barrier between them that lasted but a moment. Seconds later, the draugr broke through it with its nails.

“Sisterrrrrrrrrrrr,” it moaned. “Myyyyyyyyy!”

The Water Nokk skidded to a stop by Anna’s side, and Elsa reached down with a free hand and yanked Anna up off the ground, helping her stand. But the draugr kept coming at them even as Elsa wielded more ice and snow in an attempt to form a huge wall between them. For a moment, it was working, but then to Anna’s surprise, her sister’s ice-forming capabilities seemed to sputter out, coming in drips rather than spurts, like a well running dry.

“It isn’t working!” Anna cried, holding her head, which was still throbbing.

“I know!” Elsa said, looking anguished as she tried again and again to make sheets of solid ice. But only small shots of ice appeared. The ice wall thickened, but not enough to keep the draugr at bay. “Something’s wrong!”

“We have to get out of here, but Havski took off!” Anna said as the wind started moaning, its sounds matching the draugr’s as the creature pushed its way against the ice separating them, trying to clear a path to reach them.

“You’re riding with me!” ordered Elsa as she reached for Anna’s hand to pull her up on the Water Nokk.

Anna stepped forward and, whoa—stumbled. She felt her knees buckle. The world spun around her. Black spots appeared before her eyes.

“Anna!” Elsa cried, jumping off the horse and grabbing her sister.

“I’m okay, I just feel dizzy, and my ankle isn’t helping much, either,” Anna admitted.

Elsa touched Anna’s head, seeing the blood on her fingertips. “You can’t ride like this. It isn’t safe.”

Crack! Anna watched as the draugr’s razor-sharp nails sliced through the protective sheet of ice, sending snow flying everywhere. The wall was coming down. They were running out of time.

“Sissttteerrrrrrr!” it moaned again, trying desperately to reach them.

Elsa leapt in front of Anna, facing off with the draugr. She stared down the creature, a fierce look on her face, as if daring it to come closer.

“Elsa! No!” Anna cried.

The draugr lunged forward, grabbing Elsa’s hand with its twisted claws. Anna watched in horror as her sister tried to jerk her hand away, but the creature seemed too strong. For a moment, they just stared at each other. Then Elsa’s eyes began to soften. A strange expression began to come over her face. Like she was going into a trance.

“Elsa!” Anna tried again.

Elsa seemed to come back at the sound of Anna’s voice. She jerked her hand away, and this time she was successful at breaking free. The draugr screeched in rage and tried to grab her again, but the Water Nokk charged at the creature, blocking its path.

Elsa turned to Anna, her face frantic. “We need to find someplace to hide. Let’s go that way!” She pointed to a break in the trees behind them and a narrow path that looked like it could be navigated—even in the dark. “The Water Nokk will hold it off.”

The draugr let out a loud moan that made the hair on Anna’s arms stand on end. She watched as the water horse faced off with the creature, whinnying fiercely. Drawing in a breath, Anna tried to stumble forward, with Elsa guiding her. But after only a few steps, the world spun again and her ankle gave out. The two sisters toppled over each other and onto the ground. Anna looked up at Elsa, her body trembling. “I’m sorry! I can’t—”

Suddenly, she realized Elsa’s eyes were no longer on her, but staring behind her. Fear gripped her heart. “It’s right behind us, isn’t it?” she croaked.

“Actually…” Elsa shook her head in disbelief. “Actually, it’s not.”

“Wait, what?” Anna whipped her head around, fully expecting to come face to face with a monster. But no…Elsa was right. Her mouth dropped open in shock. There was nothing there.

The draugr had completely disappeared.
chapters.zh:
安娜僵住了。

艾莎刚刚是说"亡灵"吗？

当她盯着那缓缓朝她们飘来的可怖怪物时，安娜知道没有别的解释了。

奥拉夫和克斯托夫是对的。

亡灵的目光在艾莎和安娜之间游移，伸出黝黑的双手和尖利的指甲，咬磨着残剩的腐牙。

安娜猛地一跳，亡灵发出嘶嘶声，她的心跳骤然加快。

那声音像蛇。

接着它发出一声最诡异的呻吟。

那声音直透她的身体。

远处雷声隆隆，安娜感到风势渐起，周围一些树木剧烈摇晃。

她瞥了眼天空；天色和之前在村庄时一样黑，但这一回暴风雨正迅速逼近。"安娜，我们得立刻走！

跟我来！"艾莎喊道，水马立刻作出反应，冲出亡灵的触及范围。"收到！

哈夫斯基，走！"安娜转身要沿着水灵的冰路跟上，就在这时——咔嚓！

一道闪电击中她面前一棵巨树，将它劈得轰然倒地。

安娜及时勒住哈夫斯基的缰绳，才没被砸中。

树干落地，震得大地一颤。

哈夫斯基受惊，用后腿直立起来。"别慌！"安娜叫道，再次伸手去抓缰绳安抚马儿。

但她已经晚了。

安娜从马背上飞了出去，重重摔在地上，头磕在像是石头的东西上。

剧痛灼遍全身，眼前的世界失焦了一瞬，但安娜奋力回了神，及时坐起来，正看见哈夫斯基朝相反方向狂奔而去。"安娜！

你在哪儿！"艾莎在被伐倒的大树另一侧某处喊道。"这儿！

我没事！"安娜撒了谎。

她的手猛地捂住头，摸到湿湿的东西，疼得缩了一下。

黏糊糊的。

她在流血吗？

伤得重吗？

她该怎么离开这里？

那棵倒下的树在坠落时似乎又撞倒了另外两棵，它们像巨大的多米诺骨牌般倒下，形成一道又高又宽的硕大路障，安娜连妹妹的影子都看不见了。

她居然没被砸死，简直是个奇迹。"但我不知道怎么绕过这堆东西。""我们会到你那边的！"艾莎说，声音听起来很吃力。"只要别靠近亡灵！"安娜猛然睁大眼睛。

亡灵。

她怎么把亡灵给忘了？

她猛地转过头，恰好看见那怪物正朝她潜行而来，丑陋的嘴里滴着红色黏液。

她必须离开这里！"妹——妹——啊……"安娜僵住了。

那是什么？

那是亡灵吗？

它刚刚说的是"妹妹"？

一阵寒意顺着脊背蹿下。"妹——妹——啊……"亡灵居然会说话！

"妹妹？

不，谢了！

我已经有了一个。"她等不及艾莎和水马赶到她身边了。

她头痛欲裂，都不确定自己能不能站得起来。"我——的——妹——妹，"亡灵嘶嘶地说，拖着破衣烂衫下残破不堪的身体朝她爬来。

咚。

拖。

咚。

拖。

咚。

拖。

快跑！

安娜对自己说，即便视线模糊，也逼着自己站起身。

她想迈步向前，左腿却动弹不得。

她诧异地低头看去。

她的脚卡在几根粗壮盘绕的树根之间。

她摔下来的时候一定是被缠住了。

亡灵又向前猛扑，它伸出黝黑的双手，安娜疼得缩了一下。

完了，她屏住呼吸想，可什么也没发生后便急速呼了口气。

她惊讶地抬头。

亡灵手里正拿着她那份折叠的《村庄之冠》。

那一定是从她被甩下哈夫斯基时掉出的挎包里滑落的。

亡灵的目光在安娜和报纸之间来回游移，又落回安娜身上。

它残存的脸上扭曲出一个咆哮的表情。

亡灵会认字吗？

安娜忽然想起韦尔讲的故事：妹妹安娜如何取代女王登上了王位。

哦，不。"西塞尔？"安娜低声说。

那怪物的脸比之前更狰狞了。"妹——妹——！"它直直朝她扑来。

安娜脑子飞转。

这亡灵就是西塞尔。

它的妹妹想夺走它的王冠。

我从艾莎手里接过了王冠。

哦，不……"你误会了，"安娜恳求道，再次试图把腿抽出来。"是艾莎把王冠交给我的！"可亡灵根本不听。

它继续逼近，呻吟得更大声了。

咚。

拖。

它现在已经几乎压到她身上了。

安娜陷入恐慌，拼命想把脚拽出来。

她的靴子彻底卡死了。"快啊，快啊，快啊，"安娜恳求着，巴不得脚能奇迹般松脱，试着扭动脚趾、踝关节，更用力地蹬住靴子——什么办法都试了——只为把自己挣脱出来。

可毫无用处。

亡灵正压向她。

艾莎赶不及到她身边了。

那东西近在咫尺，安娜能闻到它散发的腐臭，直想作呕。

她的思绪忽然飘到村民们关于亡灵的议论。

要是这东西冲她打个喷嚏，她会不会也变成亡灵？

安娜转过身，寻找可以防身的东西。

她的目光落定在被缠住的树上的一根光秃枝桠。

她双手举起，干脆利落地折断其中一根最粗的细枝。

她转过身，像握剑一样挥舞着它。"退后！"安娜命令道。"退后！"有那么一瞬，亡灵显得困惑；它诡异的笑容消失了。"这就对了！

这里我说了算！"安娜说，稍稍松了口气。

她才是老大！

而不是这个在黑暗白昼里溜出来、想把她和她的马吓个半死的黏糊爬物。

一道闪电照亮了如夜的小路。"离我和我妹妹远点！"亡灵凹陷的双眼瞪大，笑容重现，显得比之前更可怕。

一条虫子从亡灵嘴里爬出来，安娜直缩。"妹——妹——啊！"它又呻吟起来。"不！"安娜喊道。"我不会让你伤害我们！"安娜用树枝朝那怪物面前空中挥打，想把它吓退。

那怪物咆哮着，再次向前逼近，此刻正压向安娜。

她向后一仰，就在这时她听见了——嗖！

冰在地面蔓延裂开，在安娜和亡灵脚下结成一片冰面。

嗖！

艾莎和水马已绕过路障，正朝她奔来。

艾莎一片接一片地向亡灵射出冰层。

冰在安娜脚边成形，更重要的是，也冻住了卡住安娜靴子的树根。

她看着冰噼啪作响，把藤蔓和枝桠冻结在原地。

也许现在她能击碎那些被冰冻得脆硬的树根，从而脱身。

她用树枝猛敲，听见"咔"的一声响。

安娜再次猛拽脚，感到自己向后自由坠落。

她来不及稳住身形，一屁股摔在地上。

亡灵被激怒，又一次朝安娜猛扑过来。

安娜手脚并用慌忙后退，急着躲开它。

嗖！

更多冰出现，在她们之间筑起一道屏障，却只维持了片刻。

几秒后，亡灵用指甲破开了它。"妹——妹——啊，"它呻吟着。"我——的——！"水马在安娜身旁一个急停，艾莎腾出一只手探下，把安娜从地上拽起，扶她站好。

但亡灵仍不断逼近，尽管艾莎挥出更多冰雪，试图在她们之间筑起一堵高墙。

一度似乎奏效，可接着让安娜惊讶的是，妹妹的造冰能力像是噗噗地泄了气，只零星滴落而非喷涌，犹如一口枯井。"不管用了！"安娜抱着仍隐隐作痛的头喊道。"我知道！"艾莎一脸痛苦地说，一次次试图造出坚实的冰片。

但只冒出零星的细小冰屑。

冰墙增厚了，却不足以挡住亡灵。"不对劲！""我们得离开这儿，可哈夫斯基跑掉了！"安娜说，此时风开始哀号，声调和亡灵相和，那怪物正顶着隔开它们的冰层，想清出一条路够到她们。"你跟我一起骑！"艾莎命令道，伸手去抓安娜的手，要把她拉上水马。

安娜向前迈步，哎呀——一个趔趄。

她感到双膝发软。

世界在她周围旋转。

她眼前冒出黑点。"安娜！"艾莎喊着跳下马，扶住妹妹。"我没事，只是觉得晕，脚踝也不太争气，"安娜承认道。

艾莎摸了摸安娜的头，看见指尖沾了血。"你这样没法骑。

不安全。"咔嚓！

安娜看着亡灵剃刀般锋利的指甲划穿那层保护性的冰片，雪花四溅。

墙快塌了。

她们时间不多了。"妹——妹——啊！"它又呻吟起来，拼命想够到她们。

艾莎跳到安娜身前，与亡灵对峙。

她居高临下地瞪着那怪物，脸上神情凶悍，仿佛在挑衅它再靠近些。"艾莎！

不！"安娜喊道。

亡灵猛扑上前，用扭曲的爪子抓住艾莎的手。

安娜惊恐地看着妹妹想把手抽回，可那怪物似乎太强壮了。

有那么一会儿，她们只是互相盯着。

接着艾莎的眼神开始柔和下来。

一种奇异的神情浮上她的脸。

仿佛陷入了出神状态。"艾莎！"安娜再试一次。

听到安娜的声音，艾莎似乎回了神。

她猛地抽回手，这一次成功挣脱了。

亡灵狂怒地尖叫，又想抓住她，可水马冲向那怪物，挡住了它的去路。

艾莎转向安娜，神色慌乱。"我们得找个地方躲起来。

走那边！"她指向身后树林间的一处缺口和一条窄径，看起来即便在黑暗中也走得通。"水马会拖住它。"亡灵发出一声响亮的呻吟，听得安娜手臂上的汗毛都竖了起来。

她看着水马与那怪物对峙，猛烈地嘶鸣。

安娜深吸一口气，在艾莎的搀扶下踉跄前行。

可才走几步，世界又旋转起来，她的脚踝撑不住了。

两姐妹互相绊倒，一起摔在地上。

安娜抬头望着艾莎，身体发抖。"对不起！

我做不到——"突然，她发现艾莎的目光已不在她身上，而是盯着她身后。

恐惧攫住了她的心脏。"它就在我们身后，对不对？"她声音沙哑地说。"其实……"艾莎难以置信地摇摇头。"其实，它不在。""等等，什么？"安娜猛地转过头，满以为会迎面撞上一只怪物。

但是没有……艾莎是对的。

她惊讶得张开了嘴。

那儿空空如也。

亡灵彻底消失了。

sentences.en: ANNA FROZE.
sentences.zh: 安娜僵住了。

sentences.en: Had Elsa just said draugr ?
sentences.zh: 艾莎刚刚是说"亡灵"吗？

sentences.en: As she stared at the ghastly creature slowly gliding toward them, Anna knew there was no other explanation.
sentences.zh: 当她盯着那缓缓朝她们飘来的可怖怪物时，安娜知道没有别的解释了。

sentences.en: Olaf and Kristoff had been right.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫和克斯托夫是对的。

sentences.en: The draugr looked from Elsa to Anna, reaching out for them with blackened hands and sharp nails, gnashing what was left of its rotting teeth.
sentences.zh: 亡灵的目光在艾莎和安娜之间游移，伸出黝黑的双手和尖利的指甲，咬磨着残剩的腐牙。

sentences.en: Anna jumped, her heartbeat quickening as the draugr hissed.
sentences.zh: 安娜猛地一跳，亡灵发出嘶嘶声，她的心跳骤然加快。

sentences.en: It sounded like a snake.
sentences.zh: 那声音像蛇。

sentences.en: Then it let out the eeriest of moans.
sentences.zh: 接着它发出一声最诡异的呻吟。

sentences.en: The sound went right through her.
sentences.zh: 那声音直透她的身体。

sentences.en: Thunder rumbled in the distance and Anna felt the wind pick up, making some of the trees around them sway violently.
sentences.zh: 远处雷声隆隆，安娜感到风势渐起，周围一些树木剧烈摇晃。

sentences.en: She glanced at the sky; it was just as dark as it had been before in the village, but this time a storm was moving in fast. “Anna, we need to go now!
sentences.zh: 她瞥了眼天空；天色和之前在村庄时一样黑，但这一回暴风雨正迅速逼近。"安娜，我们得立刻走！

sentences.en: Follow me!” Elsa cried as the Water Nokk instantly reacted, racing out of the draugr’s reach. “On it!
sentences.zh: 跟我来！"艾莎喊道，水马立刻作出反应，冲出亡灵的触及范围。"收到！

sentences.en: Havski, let’s move!” Anna turned to follow the Water Spirit’s icy path when CRACK!
sentences.zh: 哈夫斯基，走！"安娜转身要沿着水灵的冰路跟上，就在这时——咔嚓！

sentences.en: Lightning struck a massive tree in front of her, sending it crashing to the ground.
sentences.zh: 一道闪电击中她面前一棵巨树，将它劈得轰然倒地。

sentences.en: Anna pulled on Havski’s reins just in time to keep them from being hit.
sentences.zh: 安娜及时勒住哈夫斯基的缰绳，才没被砸中。

sentences.en: The trunk hit the ground with a quake.
sentences.zh: 树干落地，震得大地一颤。

sentences.en: Startled, Havski reared on his back legs. “Easy!” Anna cried out, reaching for the reins again to calm the horse.
sentences.zh: 哈夫斯基受惊，用后腿直立起来。"别慌！"安娜叫道，再次伸手去抓缰绳安抚马儿。

sentences.en: But she was too late.
sentences.zh: 但她已经晚了。

sentences.en: Anna flew off his back, landing hard on the ground, her head smacking against what felt like a rock.
sentences.zh: 安娜从马背上飞了出去，重重摔在地上，头磕在像是石头的东西上。

sentences.en: Pain seared through her body and the world lost focus for a second, but Anna fought her way back, sitting up in time to see Havski bolt in the opposite direction. “Anna!
sentences.zh: 剧痛灼遍全身，眼前的世界失焦了一瞬，但安娜奋力回了神，及时坐起来，正看见哈夫斯基朝相反方向狂奔而去。"安娜！

sentences.en: Where are you!” Elsa cried out from somewhere on the other side of the downed tree. “Here!
sentences.zh: 你在哪儿！"艾莎在被伐倒的大树另一侧某处喊道。"这儿！

sentences.en: I’m all right!” Anna lied.
sentences.zh: 我没事！"安娜撒了谎。

sentences.en: Her hands flew to her head and she winced as she felt something wet.
sentences.zh: 她的手猛地捂住头，摸到湿湿的东西，疼得缩了一下。

sentences.en: Sticky.
sentences.zh: 黏糊糊的。

sentences.en: Was she bleeding?
sentences.zh: 她在流血吗？

sentences.en: Was it bad?
sentences.zh: 伤得重吗？

sentences.en: How was she getting out of there?
sentences.zh: 她该怎么离开这里？

sentences.en: The downed tree seemed to have hit two more as it dropped, and they had fallen like huge dominos, forming a giant barricade so tall and wide Anna couldn’t even see her sister through it.
sentences.zh: 那棵倒下的树在坠落时似乎又撞倒了另外两棵，它们像巨大的多米诺骨牌般倒下，形成一道又高又宽的硕大路障，安娜连妹妹的影子都看不见了。

sentences.en: It was amazing she hadn’t been killed. “But I don’t know how I’m getting around this.” “We’ll get to you!” Elsa said, her voice sounding strained. “Just keep away from the draugr!” Anna’s eyes shot open.
sentences.zh: 她居然没被砸死，简直是个奇迹。"但我不知道怎么绕过这堆东西。""我们会到你那边的！"艾莎说，声音听起来很吃力。"只要别靠近亡灵！"安娜猛然睁大眼睛。

sentences.en: Draugr .
sentences.zh: 亡灵。

sentences.en: How had she forgotten about the draugr?
sentences.zh: 她怎么把亡灵给忘了？

sentences.en: She whipped her head around just in time to see the creature stalking toward her, red slime dripping from its grotesque mouth.
sentences.zh: 她猛地转过头，恰好看见那怪物正朝她潜行而来，丑陋的嘴里滴着红色黏液。

sentences.en: She had to get out of there! “Sissssstterrrrrrr….” Anna froze.
sentences.zh: 她必须离开这里！"妹——妹——啊……"安娜僵住了。

sentences.en: What was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Was that the draugr?
sentences.zh: 那是亡灵吗？

sentences.en: Had it just said sister ?
sentences.zh: 它刚刚说的是"妹妹"？

sentences.en: A chill tripped down her spine. “Sissssstterrrrrrr….” The draugr could talk! “Sister?
sentences.zh: 一阵寒意顺着脊背蹿下。"妹——妹——啊……"亡灵居然会说话！

sentences.en: No, thank you!
sentences.zh: "妹妹？

sentences.en: I’ve already got one.” She couldn’t wait for Elsa and the Water Nokk to reach her.
sentences.zh: 不，谢了！

sentences.en: Her head was pounding so hard she wasn’t sure she could stand. “Myyyyyy sisssssstttterrrrr,” the draugr hissed, dragging what was left of its wretched body in tattered clothing toward her.
sentences.zh: 我已经有了一个。"她等不及艾莎和水马赶到她身边了。

sentences.en: Thump.
sentences.zh: 她头痛欲裂，都不确定自己能不能站得起来。"我——的——妹——妹，"亡灵嘶嘶地说，拖着破衣烂衫下残破不堪的身体朝她爬来。

sentences.en: Drag.
sentences.zh: 咚。

sentences.en: Thump.
sentences.zh: 拖。

sentences.en: Drag.
sentences.zh: 咚。

sentences.en: Thump.
sentences.zh: 拖。

sentences.en: Drag.
sentences.zh: 咚。

sentences.en: Run!
sentences.zh: 拖。

sentences.en: Anna told herself, pushing her body to stand even as her vision blurred.
sentences.zh: 快跑！

sentences.en: She tried to step forward, but her left leg wouldn’t budge.
sentences.zh: 安娜对自己说，即便视线模糊，也逼着自己站起身。

sentences.en: She looked down in surprise.
sentences.zh: 她想迈步向前，左腿却动弹不得。

sentences.en: Her foot was caught in between several thick, winding roots.
sentences.zh: 她诧异地低头看去。

sentences.en: She must have gotten ensnared when she fell.
sentences.zh: 她的脚卡在几根粗壮盘绕的树根之间。

sentences.en: Anna tugged on her leg—hard—but it was stuck, seemingly fastened in place.
sentences.zh: 她摔下来的时候一定是被缠住了。

sentences.en: The draugr lunged forward again, and Anna winced as it reached out with blackened hands.
sentences.zh: 亡灵又向前猛扑，它伸出黝黑的双手，安娜疼得缩了一下。

sentences.en: This is it, she thought, holding her breath, and then exhaling fast when nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 完了，她屏住呼吸想，可什么也没发生后便急速呼了口气。

sentences.en: She looked up in surprise.
sentences.zh: 她惊讶地抬头。

sentences.en: The draugr was holding her folded copy of the Village Crown .
sentences.zh: 亡灵手里正拿着她那份折叠的《村庄之冠》。

sentences.en: It must have fallen from her satchel when she had been thrown from Havski.
sentences.zh: 那一定是从她被甩下哈夫斯基时掉出的挎包里滑落的。

sentences.en: The draugr looked from Anna to the paper and back at Anna again.
sentences.zh: 亡灵的目光在安娜和报纸之间来回游移，又落回安娜身上。

sentences.en: What was left of its face curled into a snarl.
sentences.zh: 它残存的脸上扭曲出一个咆哮的表情。

sentences.en: Could the draugr read?
sentences.zh: 亡灵会认字吗？

sentences.en: Anna suddenly thought of Wael’s story about how Anna, the younger sister, had replaced the queen on the throne.
sentences.zh: 安娜忽然想起韦尔讲的故事：妹妹安娜如何取代女王登上了王位。

sentences.en: Oh, no . “Sissel?” Anna whispered.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。"西塞尔？"安娜低声说。

sentences.en: The creature’s face was even more grotesque than before. “Sissssterrrrr!” It lunged straight toward her.
sentences.zh: 那怪物的脸比之前更狰狞了。"妹——妹——！"它直直朝她扑来。

sentences.en: Anna thought fast.
sentences.zh: 安娜脑子飞转。

sentences.en: The draugr is Sissel.
sentences.zh: 这亡灵就是西塞尔。

sentences.en: Its sister tried to take its crown.
sentences.zh: 它的妹妹想夺走它的王冠。

sentences.en: I took the crown from Elsa.
sentences.zh: 我从艾莎手里接过了王冠。

sentences.en: Oh, no… “You don’t understand,” Anna begged, trying to pull her leg free once again. “Elsa gave me the crown!” But the draugr wasn’t listening.
sentences.zh: 哦，不……"你误会了，"安娜恳求道，再次试图把腿抽出来。"是艾莎把王冠交给我的！"可亡灵根本不听。

sentences.en: It kept coming, moaning even louder.
sentences.zh: 它继续逼近，呻吟得更大声了。

sentences.en: Thump.
sentences.zh: 咚。

sentences.en: Drag.
sentences.zh: 拖。

sentences.en: It was almost on top of her now.
sentences.zh: 它现在已经几乎压到她身上了。

sentences.en: Panic gripped Anna as she tried to yank her foot free in desperation.
sentences.zh: 安娜陷入恐慌，拼命想把脚拽出来。

sentences.en: Her boot was completely wedged. “Come on, come on, come on,” Anna begged, willing her foot to miraculously loosen somehow, trying to wiggle her toes, her ankle, grip her boot harder—anything—to pull herself free.
sentences.zh: 她的靴子彻底卡死了。"快啊，快啊，快啊，"安娜恳求着，巴不得脚能奇迹般松脱，试着扭动脚趾、踝关节，更用力地蹬住靴子——什么办法都试了——只为把自己挣脱出来。

sentences.en: But it was no use.
sentences.zh: 可毫无用处。

sentences.en: The draugr was bearing down on her.
sentences.zh: 亡灵正压向她。

sentences.en: Elsa wasn’t going to make it to her in time.
sentences.zh: 艾莎赶不及到她身边了。

sentences.en: The thing was so close, Anna could smell the rot coming off it, making her want to vomit.
sentences.zh: 那东西近在咫尺，安娜能闻到它散发的腐臭，直想作呕。

sentences.en: Her mind suddenly went to the villagers’ talk of draugrs.
sentences.zh: 她的思绪忽然飘到村民们关于亡灵的议论。

sentences.en: If this thing sneezed on her, would she turn into a draugr?
sentences.zh: 要是这东西冲她打个喷嚏，她会不会也变成亡灵？

sentences.en: Anna spun around, looking for something to defend herself with.
sentences.zh: 安娜转过身，寻找可以防身的东西。

sentences.en: Her eyes landed on a bare branch from the tree she was tangled in.
sentences.zh: 她的目光落定在被缠住的树上的一根光秃枝桠。

sentences.en: Reaching up with two hands, she snapped one of the largest twigs off clean.
sentences.zh: 她双手举起，干脆利落地折断其中一根最粗的细枝。

sentences.en: She whirled around, brandishing it like a sword. “Stay back!” Anna commanded. “Back!” For a moment, the draugr seemed confused; its creepy smile disappeared. “That’s right!
sentences.zh: 她转过身，像握剑一样挥舞着它。"退后！"安娜命令道。"退后！"有那么一瞬，亡灵显得困惑；它诡异的笑容消失了。"这就对了！

sentences.en: I’m in charge here!” Anna said, feeling slight relief.
sentences.zh: 这里我说了算！"安娜说，稍稍松了口气。

sentences.en: She was the boss!
sentences.zh: 她才是老大！

sentences.en: Not this icky, crawly thing that had slipped through the darkened day trying to terrify her and her horse.
sentences.zh: 而不是这个在黑暗白昼里溜出来、想把她和她的马吓个半死的黏糊爬物。

sentences.en: A flash of lightning lit up the midnight path. “Stay away from me and my sister!” The draugr’s hollowed eyes widened and its smile returned, appearing even more gruesome than it had before.
sentences.zh: 一道闪电照亮了如夜的小路。"离我和我妹妹远点！"亡灵凹陷的双眼瞪大，笑容重现，显得比之前更可怕。

sentences.en: Anna cringed as a worm slid its way out of the draugr’s mouth. “Sissstttterrrrrrrr!” it moaned again. “No!” Anna shouted. “I won’t let you hurt us!” Anna swatted the air in front of the creature with her branch, trying to scare it.
sentences.zh: 一条虫子从亡灵嘴里爬出来，安娜直缩。"妹——妹——啊！"它又呻吟起来。"不！"安娜喊道。"我不会让你伤害我们！"安娜用树枝朝那怪物面前空中挥打，想把它吓退。

sentences.en: The creature roared, pushing forward again, bearing down on Anna now.
sentences.zh: 那怪物咆哮着，再次向前逼近，此刻正压向安娜。

sentences.en: She leaned back, and that was when she heard it— whoosh!
sentences.zh: 她向后一仰，就在这时她听见了——嗖！

sentences.en: Ice cracked across the ground, forming a sheet beneath Anna and the draugr’s feet.
sentences.zh: 冰在地面蔓延裂开，在安娜和亡灵脚下结成一片冰面。

sentences.en: Whoosh!
sentences.zh: 嗖！

sentences.en: Elsa and the Water Nokk had made it around the barricade and were running her way.
sentences.zh: 艾莎和水马已绕过路障，正朝她奔来。

sentences.en: Elsa shot sheet after sheet of ice at the draugr.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一片接一片地向亡灵射出冰层。

sentences.en: The ice formed around Anna’s feet and more importantly around the roots Anna’s boot was caught in.
sentences.zh: 冰在安娜脚边成形，更重要的是，也冻住了卡住安娜靴子的树根。

sentences.en: She watched as it crackled, freezing in place over the vines and branches.
sentences.zh: 她看着冰噼啪作响，把藤蔓和枝桠冻结在原地。

sentences.en: Maybe now she could crack the roots, brittle from the ice on them, and free herself.
sentences.zh: 也许现在她能击碎那些被冰冻得脆硬的树根，从而脱身。

sentences.en: She whacked at them with the branch and heard a snap.
sentences.zh: 她用树枝猛敲，听见"咔"的一声响。

sentences.en: Anna yanked on her foot again and felt herself free-falling backward.
sentences.zh: 安娜再次猛拽脚，感到自己向后自由坠落。

sentences.en: Unable to right herself in time, she landed on her behind.
sentences.zh: 她来不及稳住身形，一屁股摔在地上。

sentences.en: Angered, the draugr shot forward toward Anna yet again.
sentences.zh: 亡灵被激怒，又一次朝安娜猛扑过来。

sentences.en: Anna scurried back on her hands and feet, racing to get out of its way.
sentences.zh: 安娜手脚并用慌忙后退，急着躲开它。

sentences.en: Whoosh!
sentences.zh: 嗖！

sentences.en: More ice appeared, forming a barrier between them that lasted but a moment.
sentences.zh: 更多冰出现，在她们之间筑起一道屏障，却只维持了片刻。

sentences.en: Seconds later, the draugr broke through it with its nails. “Sisterrrrrrrrrrrr,” it moaned. “Myyyyyyyyy!” The Water Nokk skidded to a stop by Anna’s side, and Elsa reached down with a free hand and yanked Anna up off the ground, helping her stand.
sentences.zh: 几秒后，亡灵用指甲破开了它。"妹——妹——啊，"它呻吟着。"我——的——！"水马在安娜身旁一个急停，艾莎腾出一只手探下，把安娜从地上拽起，扶她站好。

sentences.en: But the draugr kept coming at them even as Elsa wielded more ice and snow in an attempt to form a huge wall between them.
sentences.zh: 但亡灵仍不断逼近，尽管艾莎挥出更多冰雪，试图在她们之间筑起一堵高墙。

sentences.en: For a moment, it was working, but then to Anna’s surprise, her sister’s ice-forming capabilities seemed to sputter out, coming in drips rather than spurts, like a well running dry. “It isn’t working!” Anna cried, holding her head, which was still throbbing. “I know!” Elsa said, looking anguished as she tried again and again to make sheets of solid ice.
sentences.zh: 一度似乎奏效，可接着让安娜惊讶的是，妹妹的造冰能力像是噗噗地泄了气，只零星滴落而非喷涌，犹如一口枯井。"不管用了！"安娜抱着仍隐隐作痛的头喊道。"我知道！"艾莎一脸痛苦地说，一次次试图造出坚实的冰片。

sentences.en: But only small shots of ice appeared.
sentences.zh: 但只冒出零星的细小冰屑。

sentences.en: The ice wall thickened, but not enough to keep the draugr at bay. “Something’s wrong!” “We have to get out of here, but Havski took off!” Anna said as the wind started moaning, its sounds matching the draugr’s as the creature pushed its way against the ice separating them, trying to clear a path to reach them. “You’re riding with me!” ordered Elsa as she reached for Anna’s hand to pull her up on the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 冰墙增厚了，却不足以挡住亡灵。"不对劲！""我们得离开这儿，可哈夫斯基跑掉了！"安娜说，此时风开始哀号，声调和亡灵相和，那怪物正顶着隔开它们的冰层，想清出一条路够到她们。"你跟我一起骑！"艾莎命令道，伸手去抓安娜的手，要把她拉上水马。

sentences.en: Anna stepped forward and, whoa —stumbled.
sentences.zh: 安娜向前迈步，哎呀——一个趔趄。

sentences.en: She felt her knees buckle.
sentences.zh: 她感到双膝发软。

sentences.en: The world spun around her.
sentences.zh: 世界在她周围旋转。

sentences.en: Black spots appeared before her eyes. “Anna!” Elsa cried, jumping off the horse and grabbing her sister. “I’m okay, I just feel dizzy, and my ankle isn’t helping much, either,” Anna admitted.
sentences.zh: 她眼前冒出黑点。"安娜！"艾莎喊着跳下马，扶住妹妹。"我没事，只是觉得晕，脚踝也不太争气，"安娜承认道。

sentences.en: Elsa touched Anna’s head, seeing the blood on her fingertips. “You can’t ride like this.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摸了摸安娜的头，看见指尖沾了血。"你这样没法骑。

sentences.en: It isn’t safe.” Crack!
sentences.zh: 不安全。"咔嚓！

sentences.en: Anna watched as the draugr’s razor-sharp nails sliced through the protective sheet of ice, sending snow flying everywhere.
sentences.zh: 安娜看着亡灵剃刀般锋利的指甲划穿那层保护性的冰片，雪花四溅。

sentences.en: The wall was coming down.
sentences.zh: 墙快塌了。

sentences.en: They were running out of time. “Sissttteerrrrrrr!” it moaned again, trying desperately to reach them.
sentences.zh: 她们时间不多了。"妹——妹——啊！"它又呻吟起来，拼命想够到她们。

sentences.en: Elsa leapt in front of Anna, facing off with the draugr.
sentences.zh: 艾莎跳到安娜身前，与亡灵对峙。

sentences.en: She stared down the creature, a fierce look on her face, as if daring it to come closer. “Elsa!
sentences.zh: 她居高临下地瞪着那怪物，脸上神情凶悍，仿佛在挑衅它再靠近些。"艾莎！

sentences.en: No!” Anna cried.
sentences.zh: 不！"安娜喊道。

sentences.en: The draugr lunged forward, grabbing Elsa’s hand with its twisted claws.
sentences.zh: 亡灵猛扑上前，用扭曲的爪子抓住艾莎的手。

sentences.en: Anna watched in horror as her sister tried to jerk her hand away, but the creature seemed too strong.
sentences.zh: 安娜惊恐地看着妹妹想把手抽回，可那怪物似乎太强壮了。

sentences.en: For a moment, they just stared at each other.
sentences.zh: 有那么一会儿，她们只是互相盯着。

sentences.en: Then Elsa’s eyes began to soften.
sentences.zh: 接着艾莎的眼神开始柔和下来。

sentences.en: A strange expression began to come over her face.
sentences.zh: 一种奇异的神情浮上她的脸。

sentences.en: Like she was going into a trance. “Elsa!” Anna tried again.
sentences.zh: 仿佛陷入了出神状态。"艾莎！"安娜再试一次。

sentences.en: Elsa seemed to come back at the sound of Anna’s voice.
sentences.zh: 听到安娜的声音，艾莎似乎回了神。

sentences.en: She jerked her hand away, and this time she was successful at breaking free.
sentences.zh: 她猛地抽回手，这一次成功挣脱了。

sentences.en: The draugr screeched in rage and tried to grab her again, but the Water Nokk charged at the creature, blocking its path.
sentences.zh: 亡灵狂怒地尖叫，又想抓住她，可水马冲向那怪物，挡住了它的去路。

sentences.en: Elsa turned to Anna, her face frantic. “We need to find someplace to hide.
sentences.zh: 艾莎转向安娜，神色慌乱。"我们得找个地方躲起来。

sentences.en: Let’s go that way!” She pointed to a break in the trees behind them and a narrow path that looked like it could be navigated—even in the dark. “The Water Nokk will hold it off.” The draugr let out a loud moan that made the hair on Anna’s arms stand on end.
sentences.zh: 走那边！"她指向身后树林间的一处缺口和一条窄径，看起来即便在黑暗中也走得通。"水马会拖住它。"亡灵发出一声响亮的呻吟，听得安娜手臂上的汗毛都竖了起来。

sentences.en: She watched as the water horse faced off with the creature, whinnying fiercely.
sentences.zh: 她看着水马与那怪物对峙，猛烈地嘶鸣。

sentences.en: Drawing in a breath, Anna tried to stumble forward, with Elsa guiding her.
sentences.zh: 安娜深吸一口气，在艾莎的搀扶下踉跄前行。

sentences.en: But after only a few steps, the world spun again and her ankle gave out.
sentences.zh: 可才走几步，世界又旋转起来，她的脚踝撑不住了。

sentences.en: The two sisters toppled over each other and onto the ground.
sentences.zh: 两姐妹互相绊倒，一起摔在地上。

sentences.en: Anna looked up at Elsa, her body trembling. “I’m sorry!
sentences.zh: 安娜抬头望着艾莎，身体发抖。"对不起！

sentences.en: I can’t—” Suddenly, she realized Elsa’s eyes were no longer on her, but staring behind her.
sentences.zh: 我做不到——"突然，她发现艾莎的目光已不在她身上，而是盯着她身后。

sentences.en: Fear gripped her heart. “It’s right behind us, isn’t it?” she croaked. “Actually…” Elsa shook her head in disbelief. “Actually, it’s not.” “Wait, what?” Anna whipped her head around, fully expecting to come face to face with a monster.
sentences.zh: 恐惧攫住了她的心脏。"它就在我们身后，对不对？"她声音沙哑地说。"其实……"艾莎难以置信地摇摇头。"其实，它不在。""等等，什么？"安娜猛地转过头，满以为会迎面撞上一只怪物。

sentences.en: But no…Elsa was right.
sentences.zh: 但是没有……艾莎是对的。

sentences.en: Her mouth dropped open in shock.
sentences.zh: 她惊讶得张开了嘴。

sentences.en: There was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 那儿空空如也。

sentences.en: The draugr had completely disappeared.
sentences.zh: 亡灵彻底消失了。

chapters.title: Chapter Seven: Elsa
chapters.en:
“COME ON, ANNA. Just a few more steps.”

Elsa helped her sister to the entrance of the little hut and used her foot to kick open the door. Anna stumbled inside.

“How did you find an old shepherd’s hut out here?” Anna asked, looking around once she’d caught her breath.

“I caught a glimpse of it as we were walking and hoped it was still intact,” Elsa replied, after lighting some of the candles around the room. “I’m just glad it’s here for us to use for the night.” Their parents had commissioned these structures to be erected all over Arendelle years before so shepherds could use them to shelter with their animals when the weather got bad. (Which meant that while the huts were usually dry, they also often smelled like wet sheep.)

“It seems okay. Though it doesn’t look like anyone’s used this one for a while,” Anna noted, running a finger along a table and leaving a dusty trail. She sneezed.

“Doesn’t seem like it,” Elsa agreed, settling down on a stool across from her sister. When she’d realized how bad Anna’s ankle was, not to mention her throbbing head, she knew better than to try to get her on the Water Nokk and whisk her back to Arendelle. Anna needed time to rest and recover before making a long journey on horseback. “At least it’s dry,” Elsa added. A drip of water from the roof then landed on her shoulder. She frowned. “Well, semidry anyway.”

“It’s perfect. And so are you,” Anna said, reaching up to rub her head as she settled onto her own stool.

“Are you okay?” Elsa asked worriedly, noting the blood crusting in her sister’s hair. How hard, she wondered, had Anna hit her head on that rock?

Anna nodded, pulling her hand away. “It probably looks much worse than it is,” she assured her. “I hardly feel it anymore.” She reached down to her ankle. “This, on the other hand…” She grimaced. “I can’t believe I got stuck in a tree and wrapped around a stupid root while a draugr was coming after us! That thing would have killed me if you hadn’t come back.”

“It could have killed both of us,” Elsa mused, half to herself. “But instead, it just disappeared. Where do you think it went?”

“I don’t know,” Anna said with a frown. “Maybe it only has limited magic? And it ran out or something and had to go and recharge?”

“Maybe…” Elsa shook her head, mystified. “We definitely need to find out more about these creatures. So we’ll know what to do if we run into one again.” She gave a half smile. “Not that you didn’t make a great stand against it. You were so brave, yelling at it like that! It was like you weren’t even scared at all.”

Elsa thought back to the scene. Speaking of scared, for a moment, when the trees had come down between them, she’d been terrified she wouldn’t be able to rescue her sister. That after all they’d been through, this…horrible creature…would be the end of Anna (or the both of them). She shuddered. It was too awful of a thought to dwell on.

“Please. I’m not about to let Sinister Sissel get the best of me!” Anna declared, puffing out her chest.

“So you really think it was Sissel?” Elsa asked, scratching her head. “That Kristoff’s story has come to life?” It seemed so impossible to her, even after all they had just witnessed.

“I know it sounds crazy, but look at the facts,” Anna replied, her tone and look ultraserious. “You heard Sorenson—draugrs can control the weather, and the minute Kristoff told that story, boom! We have scary dark skies, violent storms…now a monster come to life. I mean, I’m putting two and two together, and I’m not getting five.”

Elsa glanced at the storm outside. It had picked up again, the rain battering at the windows. Another drop landed on her forehead. “Maybe you’re right. Kristoff did say if you told a draugr’s story, you could bring it back….”

Anna swallowed hard. “There’s something more. When I fell, my satchel spilled open with the copy of my article in the Village Crown. You know, the one where Wael interviewed me about taking your place as queen?” Her frown deepened. “The creature picked it up and started freaking out. Like the article upset it or something.”

“Why?” Elsa shot her a puzzled look. “What would a draugr care about a newspaper? Can they even read?”

“If they were once human, maybe. And I mean, think about it!” Anna exclaimed. “I’m the younger sister! I’m just like Inger! And I have the crown. Sissel probably thinks I stole it from you—just like Inger tried to steal it from her! And now she’s trying to get her revenge on me, since Inger’s long gone!”

Elsa raised an eyebrow. “Okay, that’s a bit of a stretch.”

“And yet a story-time monster literally attacking us in real life in the woods and controlling the weather isn’t?” Anna answered. Her whole body was trembling now. Elsa put a comforting hand on her shoulder.

“Anna, you’re upsetting yourself,” she scolded gently. “It’s not going to help. Whatever is going on, we’ll figure it out. But I promise you, I’m not going to let some draugr get you, okay? No matter what.”

“I need to get back to Arendelle,” Anna declared, trying to rise to her feet. “Kristoff is there. If the draugr knows he’s the one who told its story on the anniversary, it could be after him, and everyone in Arendelle. We need to warn people they could be in danger!” She winced in pain as she put weight on her ankle.

“You’re not going anywhere,” Elsa told her sternly. “Not on that ankle. And not in this storm.”

“But Arendelle—”

“Can take care of itself. You left Kristoff and Mattias in charge. They can deal with one little monster.”

Anna raised an eyebrow. “You call that little?”

“You know what I mean,” Elsa chided. “I promise, the second the storm stops, I’ll go out and look for Havski. Or find someone with a wagon. But right now, we both need to stay put.”

Anna nodded glumly, not looking happy about the prospect of staying put. Elsa felt a pang of guilt. Maybe she should have protested harder when Anna said she wanted to come along. Of course, at the time, she hadn’t known there was an actual monster in the woods. Another wave of unease seemed to waft through her stomach. Her magic had been almost useless against that thing. And at the end, it had all but sputtered out. She knew her magic wasn’t limitless—no magic was, according to the Northuldra. But if it wasn’t even enough to save her sister, what were they going to do if the draugr did attack the kingdom?

“Ugh. I hate feeling so useless,” Anna said, glaring down at her hurt ankle.

Elsa knew exactly how she felt. “At least we got our sister time!” she said, trying to cheer her up. “And this time no one can interrupt us!”

Anna made a face. “Yeah, except for our friendly neighborhood draugr…”

Elsa rose to her feet and wandered over to the window. She peered outside. The storm was still raging, but fortunately there was no creature in sight. She walked over to the door and bolted it, just in case.

“The draugr—if that’s what it really was—is gone,” Elsa said. “And we’re safe here in the hut for now.” She dug into her pack. “And look!” Elsa pulled out a bag.

Anna’s eyes widened. “Marshmallows? You brought marshmallows?”

Elsa shrugged. “Well, we never got a chance to roast them over our campfire. So I thought I’d bring them along….” She let out a call and suddenly Bruni appeared, pushing its way through a crack in the front door, slurping the air with its tongue. Elsa led it over to the small stone hearth in the kitchen area of the hut and instructed the Fire Spirit to do its thing. A moment later there was a small blaze that gave off a warm glow.

“Oh my gosh. Best. Sister. Ever!” Anna exclaimed, her upset demeanor pushed aside. She pulled her stool closer to the fire. Elsa handed her a cooking skewer from the side of the fireplace, and Anna stabbed the marshmallow with it, holding it over the small flame. Elsa followed with her own, and soon they had two gooey golden brown marshmallows at the ends of their sticks.

“Sorry we don’t have any chocolate,” Elsa apologized.

“Oh, but we do!” Anna exclaimed, reaching into her own pack. She pulled out a wrapped square of paper. Elsa laughed as her sister revealed the dark-brown treasure inside. “A queen has to be prepared for all kinds of emergencies,” she joked, breaking the bar in two and handing the larger piece to her sister.

“Definitely!” Elsa agreed, watching Anna pull her marshmallow from the fire and set the chocolate on top of it. Elsa did the same, breathing in the warm scent as the chocolate melted on her marshmallow. She looked up at her sister.

“Mmm. Chocolate,” they said in sync. Then they giggled.

“Okay, you’re making me feel a little better,” Anna admitted after savoring her treat. “I’m hardly thinking at all about the monster lurking in the woods.” She glanced out the window. “Hardly…”

Elsa sighed. She was pretty sure neither one of them was going to sleep a wink tonight. But maybe that was for the best. They didn’t know when, or if, the draugr would be back. And Elsa didn’t want it to catch them off guard again. Especially if her powers were really drained.

“Oops!” Anna squeaked as her second marshmallow caught fire. She yanked it out of the hearth. Elsa instinctively lifted a finger and flung a small blast of ice in the marshmallow’s direction, easily quenching the flame.

Anna shot her an appreciative look. “Thanks,” she said.

Elsa smiled, feeling better knowing her powers had returned—at least enough for a marshmallow emergency. It was funny; once upon a time, all she’d wanted was to rid herself of her powers. But now, even the thought of losing them terrified her. As Anna had said, they were a part of her now, for better or worse. Not a curse, like she’d once believed. But a gift that could help people. One that could literally save lives. Make the world a better place. The spirits had trusted her with this gift, and now she wanted nothing more than to prove worthy of that trust.

A thought suddenly struck Elsa. “I may have another way to distract you,” she told her sister.

“Yeah?” Anna queried, looking up. Her mouth was covered in sticky white fluff. “How’s that?”

“I can try the memory thing again. Like I was trying to do in the tent last night.”

“I’d love that!” Anna said encouragingly. “Do you have one of Mother and Father? Maybe one of them when they were growing up?”

“I think so,” Elsa said, closing her eyes for a moment to try to draw up something for her sister. Then she opened her eyes again and smiled. “Yes! I’ve got just the memory! I pulled it up in Ahtohallan the other day. Mother and Father were in a ballroom. Spinning around to this ridiculous dance they made up. I think they called it ‘The Reindeer Who Has to Pee Really Badly but Is Stuck in a Ballroom.’”

Anna raised an eyebrow. “That sounds like quite the dance.”

“I know, right? It’s crazy how silly they used to be. They were so cute together. I sometimes spend hours pulling up their memories.”

“You are so lucky,” Anna said with a sigh. “I wish I could see it all, too.”

Elsa felt a small twinge of guilt at the wistfulness she heard in her sister’s voice. It wasn’t fair that Anna should be locked out of these memories—after all, Iduna and Agnarr were her parents, too. But Elsa was the only one who could access Ahtohallan and its treasure trove of memories. Which meant she was going to have to get creative.

“Well, that’s why I’m working on this,” Elsa said. “My goal is to learn how to re-create the memories I see in Ahtohallan and bring them home to you. So you don’t have to miss out on anything.”

“Did I ever mention you’re amazing?” Anna asked. “Because you are. Amazing.”

Elsa felt her cheeks heat at the praise from her sister. Anna had always loved her magic, even when they were children, and hearing the excitement in her voice now took Elsa back to that innocent time.

Do the magic! Anna would beg, and Elsa could never deny her.

She drew in a deep breath, trying to channel the power inside of her. Then she lifted her index finger, pointing it toward the little puddle of water from the leak in the roof. She’d learned it was easier to pull things from water, because as Olaf liked to remind them, water had memory. As she closed her eyes, she tried to picture the flowing image of her parents in her mind as she’d seen them in Ahtohallan. In the ballroom. In each other’s arms. Twirling and laughing and—

Suddenly her mind went blank. Completely blank—as if someone had smothered a candle. The memory she’d had in her head ceased entirely, and for a moment, she couldn’t even remember what memory she’d been trying to conjure up to begin with. Something about their parents? Was that right?

Her eyes opened. She glanced apologetically at her sister. “Argh. I had it. For a second…” She sighed. “I’m sorry. Maybe it isn’t the best night for this.”

“The best night for what?” Anna asked through a mouthful of burnt marshmallow. She waved her hand in front of her face. “I know I should wait for them to cool down, but they’re just so yummy. I burn the roof of my mouth every time!”

Elsa frowned, confused. Was Anna trying to make her feel better by ignoring what had just happened? That didn’t seem like something her sister would do. She’d at least ask if Elsa was okay. Wouldn’t she? Instead, she was acting like nothing had happened at all.

Or as if she’d forgotten it altogether.

The same way Elsa had forgotten the memory she was trying to pull.

Concern churned in Elsa’s gut. Something was wrong here. Something was very wrong. She thought back to how Anna and Kristoff had acted at the campsite last night. They’d been strangely forgetful then, too. Was it all related? Could it have something to do with the monster?

Only Ahtohallan knows…Her mother’s voice seemed to whisper in her ears.

She drew in a breath. “Look, Anna, here’s what I’m thinking. Tomorrow we’ll get you back to Arendelle to make sure everyone’s okay. And you can do some research on draugrs in our parents’ library. Find out everything you can about the monster. Meanwhile, I’ll go back to Ahtohallan and see what I can learn there. Maybe the white river can tell me something useful.”

Anna swallowed her marshmallow. “Good idea,” she said. “And then we’ll meet back in Arendelle and compare notes. Together, I’m sure we can figure out what this draugr is doing here.”

Elsa smiled at the confidence she heard in her sister’s voice. Anna truly wasn’t scared of anything—even when maybe she should be. Elsa admired her for that and wished she could feel the same.

But as the wind howled outside, the branches of nearby trees rapping angrily against the windowpanes, she realized she was afraid. For herself. For her sister.

And for Arendelle.
chapters.zh:
"来吧，安娜。

再走几步就好。"艾莎扶着妹妹走到小屋门口，用脚踢开了门。

安娜踉跄着进了屋。"你怎么在荒郊野外找到一间放羊人小屋的？"安娜喘过气后环顾四周问道。"我们走的时候我瞥见了它，希望它还完好，"艾莎点亮屋里几支蜡烛后答道。"真高兴它在这儿，今晚能给我们用。"多年前，她们的父母曾下令在阿伦黛尔各地修建这些小屋，好让牧羊人在天气恶劣时能带着牲畜避一避。

（也就是说，这些小屋通常虽干爽，却也常有一股湿羊味儿。）"看起来还好。

不过好像很久没人用过这间了，"安娜注意到，用手指沿桌一划，留下一道灰尘印。

她打了个喷嚏。"看来确实没用过，"艾莎表示同意，在妹妹对面的凳子上坐下。

当她意识到安娜的脚踝伤得那么重，更别提还头痛欲裂，她就明白不该试着让安娜骑上水马，把她匆匆送回阿伦黛尔。

安娜需要先休息恢复，才能长途骑马。"至少这里干爽，"艾莎补充道。

这时，一滴屋顶的漏水落在她肩上。

她皱起眉。"嗯，还算半干吧。""它完美极了。

你也是，"安娜说着，在自己凳上坐定，抬手揉了揉头。"你还好吗？"艾莎担忧地问，注意到妹妹头发里结着血痂。

她心想，安娜的头撞那石头，得有多重？

安娜点点头，把手缩回。"看着大概比实际严重，"她安慰她。"我现在几乎感觉不到疼了。"她伸手去摸脚踝。"可这个嘛……"她做了个苦脸。"真不敢相信，亡灵追着我们的时候，我居然卡在树上、缠在那根蠢树根上！

要不是你回来，那东西早杀了我。""它本可能把我们都杀了，"艾莎若有所思，半是自言自语。"可它却只是消失了。

你觉得它去哪儿了？""不知道，"安娜皱着眉说。"也许它的魔力有限？

用完光了之类的，得去充个电？""也许……"艾莎困惑地摇摇头。"我们确实得进一步弄清这些生物。

这样下次再撞上才知道该怎么办。"她露出半抹微笑。"虽说你刚才对抗它时表现得可圈可点。

你那么勇敢，冲它大喊大叫！

简直像你一点都不害怕。"艾莎回想起了那一幕。

说到害怕，有一刻，当树木倒在他们之间，她曾惊恐地以为自己救不了妹妹。

以为在历经万难之后，这个……可怖的怪物……竟会是安娜（或她们俩）的终结。

她打了个寒颤。

这念头太可怕，不忍细想。"拜托。

我才不会让"阴森的西塞尔"占了上风！"安娜鼓起胸膛宣布。"所以你真觉得那是西塞尔？"艾莎挠着头问。"克斯托夫的故事成真了？"尽管刚亲眼所见，这对她而言仍像天方夜谭。"我知道听着疯狂，但看事实啊，"安娜答道，语气和神情都极度认真。"你听索伦森说了——亡灵能操控天气，而克斯托夫一讲完那故事，砰！

我们就有了吓人的黑天、狂暴的暴风雨……现在还有了活过来的怪物。

我是说，我把二加二放在一起，得出的可不是五。"艾莎瞥了眼外面的暴风雨。

雨势又起，拍打着窗户。

又一滴水落在她额头。"也许你是对的。

克斯托夫确实说过，讲出亡灵的故事，就能把它唤回来……"安娜使劲咽了口唾沫。"还有别的事。

我摔下去时，挎包散开了，里面那份《村庄之冠》上登着我的文章。

就是韦尔采访我、说我接替你成为女王的那篇？"她眉头皱得更紧了。"那怪物捡起报纸，开始发疯。

好像那篇文章把它惹到了。""为什么？"艾莎困惑地瞥了她一眼。"亡灵会在乎一份报纸什么？

它们认字吗？""如果它们曾经是人，也许吧。

而且我是说，你想想看！"安娜喊道。"我是妹妹！

我就跟英格一样！

而且我戴着王冠。

西塞尔大概以为我是偷了你的——就像英格当年想从她那儿抢走一样！

如今英格早就不在了，她就冲我来复仇！"艾莎挑起眉毛。"嗯，这有点牵强了。""可故事里的怪物在森林里真刀真枪地袭击我们、还能操控天气，就不牵强？"安娜反问。

她此刻浑身发抖。

艾莎安慰地把一只手搭在她肩上。"安娜，你在自己吓自己，"她温柔地责备道。"这没用的。

不管怎么回事，我们都会弄清楚的。

但我向你保证，我不会让什么亡灵伤到你，好吗？

无论如何。""我得回阿伦黛尔，"安娜坚定地说，试图站起来。"克斯托夫在那儿。

如果亡灵知道是他在这个周年日讲出了它的故事，它可能会去追他，还有阿伦黛尔的每一个人。

我们得警告大家，他们可能有危险！"她把重量压在脚踝上，疼得缩了一下。"你哪儿也不许去，"艾莎严厉地对她说。"脚踝这样不行。

而且这暴风雨里也不行。""可阿伦黛尔——""它能照顾好自己。

你留下了克斯托夫和马蒂亚斯主持大局。

他们对付一只小怪物绰绰有余。"安娜挑起眉毛。"你管那叫小？""你明白我的意思，"艾莎嗔怪道。"我保证，暴风雨一停，我就出去找哈夫斯基。

或者找辆马车来。

但现在，我们俩都得待着别动。"安娜闷闷不乐地点头，对"待着别动"的前景并不开心。

艾莎感到一阵愧疚。

也许当初安娜说要跟来时，她该更强烈地反对。

当然，那时她还不知道林子里真有怪物。

又一阵不安仿佛从她胃里飘过。

她的魔力对付那东西几乎没用。

而到最后，它几乎彻底泄了气。

她知道自己的魔力并非无限——按北地人的说法，没有哪种魔力是无限的。

可如果连救妹妹都不够，万一亡灵真的攻击王国，她们该怎么办？"唉。

我最恨这种无能为力的感觉，"安娜说，瞪着自己受伤的脚踝。

艾莎太懂她的感受了。"至少我们享受了姐妹时光！"她说着，想给她打气。"而且这回没人能打断我们！"安娜做了个鬼脸。"是啊，除了我们那友好的邻居亡灵……"艾莎站起身，漫步走到窗边。

她朝外面望去。

暴风雨仍在肆虐，但所幸看不见任何怪物。

她走到门边，闩上门栓，以防万一。"亡灵——如果那真是它的话——已经走了，"艾莎说。"眼下我们在小屋里是安全的。"她翻了翻自己的背包。"看！"艾莎掏出一个袋子。

安娜睁大眼睛。"棉花糖？

你带了棉花糖？"艾莎耸耸肩。"嗯，我们一直没机会在营火上烤它们。

所以我想干脆带在身上……"她唤了一声，火灵忽然出现，从门缝里挤进来，用舌头舔着空气。

艾莎把它领到小屋厨房区的小石炉边，命令火灵施展本事。

片刻后便燃起一小簇火苗，散发出温暖的光。"天哪。

最棒了。

姐姐。

永——远——最棒！"安娜惊叹，先前的烦闷一扫而空。

她把凳子往火边挪了挪。

艾莎从壁炉边递给她一根烧烤签，安娜把棉花糖戳上去，举在小火苗上方。

艾莎也如法炮制，很快她们签子末端各有一团金黄黏软的棉花糖。"抱歉我们没有巧克力，"艾莎道歉。"哦，可我们有！"安娜喊道，伸手去翻自己的背包。

她掏出一包用纸裹着的方块。

艾莎笑起来，妹妹亮出了里面深棕色的宝贝。"女王得为各种突发状况做好准备，"她开玩笑说，把巧克力掰成两半，较大的那块递给妹妹。"绝对！"艾莎赞同，看着安娜把棉花糖从火上移开，把巧克力放在上面。

艾莎也照做，巧克力在棉花糖上融化，她深吸着那温暖香气。

她抬头看着妹妹。"嗯。

巧克力，"她们异口同声。

接着她们咯咯笑起来。"好吧，你让我感觉好点了，"安娜细细品味后承认。"我几乎一点都没在想林子里潜伏的怪物了。"她瞥了眼窗外。"几乎……"艾莎叹了口气。

她相当确信，她们今晚谁都别想合眼。

但也许这样最好。

她们不知道亡灵何时会回来，甚至不知它会不会回来。

而艾莎不想再让它打得她们措手不及。

尤其如果她的魔力真的耗尽了。"哎呀！"安娜的第二颗棉花糖着了火，她尖叫一声。

她猛地把签子从炉里抽出来。

艾莎本能地抬起一根手指，朝棉花糖方向射出一小股冰，轻而易举地灭了火。

安娜感激地瞥了她一眼。"谢了，"她说。

艾莎微笑，得知魔力已恢复——至少够应付一颗棉花糖着火的紧急状况——她心情好了些。

说来好笑；曾几何时，她唯一的愿望就是摆脱自己的魔力。

可如今，光是想到失去它们，都让她害怕。

正如安娜所说，它们现在是她的一部分了，无论好坏。

不再是她曾以为的诅咒。

而是一份能帮助人的礼物。

一份真能救命的礼物。

让世界变得更美好。

精灵们把这礼物托付给她，如今她最大的心愿，就是证明自己配得上这份信任。

艾莎忽然灵光一闪。"我也许还有别的法子分散你的注意力，"她对妹妹说。"哦？"安娜抬起头问。

她嘴上沾着黏糊糊的白色绒絮。"怎么个法子？""我可以再试试那个记忆的法子。

就像昨晚在帐篷里我想做的那样。""我太愿意了！"安娜鼓励地说。"你有没有关于爸爸妈妈的？

也许是他们成长中的一段？""我想有，"艾莎说，闭上眼片刻，想为妹妹调出些画面。

然后她又睁眼微笑。"有！

我正好有一段记忆！

前两天我在阿托哈兰重温过它。

爸爸妈妈在舞厅里。

正转着圈跳他们自编的滑稽舞步。

我想他们管它叫"急得想上厕所却被困在舞厅里的驯鹿"。"安娜挑起眉毛。"听起来是个挺了不得的舞。""可不是嘛。

他们以前那么傻，简直疯狂。

俩人在一起时可真可爱。

我有时一调出他们的记忆就是好几个小时。""你真幸运，"安娜叹了口气说。"我也希望能全都看到。"听出妹妹语气里的向往，艾莎心里泛起一丝愧疚。

让安娜被挡在这些记忆之外，实在不公平——毕竟，伊杜娜和安格瑞也是她的父母。

但艾莎是唯一能进入阿托哈兰、触及那记忆宝藏的人。

这意味着她得想点新办法。"嗯，这正是我在钻研这个的原因，"艾莎说。"我的目标是学会如何重现我在阿托哈兰看到的记忆，把它们带回家给你。

这样你就不必错过任何东西了。""我说过你很了不起吗？"安娜问。"因为你就是。

了不起。"听着妹妹的夸奖，艾莎感到脸颊发烫。

安娜从她们还是孩子起就爱她的魔力，此刻听到她声音里的兴奋，艾莎仿佛回到了那段纯真岁月。

变魔法吧！

安娜曾这样央求，而艾莎从没拒绝过她。

她深吸一口气，试图调动体内的力量。

然后她抬起食指，指向屋顶漏水形成的小水洼。

她发现从水中提取画面更容易，因为正如奥拉夫爱提醒她们的，水有记忆。

她闭上眼，努力在脑中勾勒父母流动的影像，就像她在阿托哈兰所见那样。

在舞厅里。

在彼此的臂弯中。

旋转、欢笑，然后——忽然，她的脑中一片空白。

完全空白——仿佛有人掐灭了一支蜡烛。

她脑中原有的那段记忆彻底消失，有那么一会儿，她甚至想不起自己起初想召唤的究竟是哪段记忆。

关于父母的什么？

是这样吗？

她睁开眼。

她歉疚地瞥了妹妹一眼。"哎。

我刚才还有的。

就一瞬间……"她叹了口气。"对不起。

也许今晚不是做这个的好时机。""做什么的好时机？"安娜嘴里塞满烤焦的棉花糖问道。

她把手在面前扇了扇。"我知道该等它们凉了再吃，可它们实在太好吃了。

我每次都把口腔上膛烫到！"艾莎困惑地皱起眉。

安娜是想装作没发生刚才的事，好让她安心吗？

这可不像妹妹的作风。

她至少会问问艾莎没事吧。

不是吗？

可她却表现得像什么都没发生过。

或者说，像把整件事都忘了。

就像艾莎忘了自己正想调出的那段记忆。

艾莎的胃里翻涌起不安。

这里不对劲。

很不对劲。

她回想昨晚安娜和克斯托夫在营地里的表现。

那时他们也怪异地健忘。

这一切都有关联吗？

会不会和那怪物有关？

只有阿托哈兰知道……母亲的声音仿佛在耳边低语。

她深吸一口气。"听着，安娜，我是这么想的。

明天我们送你回阿伦黛尔，确保大家都平安。

你可以去父母的藏书室做些关于亡灵的研究。

尽可能弄清这怪物的底底细。

同时，我回阿托哈兰，看看能学到什么。

也许那条白河能告诉我些有用的。"安娜咽下棉花糖。"好主意，"她说。"然后我们在阿伦黛尔碰头，对一对笔记。

一起，我确信我们能弄清这亡灵来这儿干什么。"听着妹妹声音里的自信，艾莎微微笑了。

安娜当真什么都不怕——哪怕有时她本该害怕。

艾莎钦佩她这一点，也希望自己能有同感。

可当外面风声呼啸，近旁树枝愤怒地敲打窗玻璃，她意识到自己害怕了。

为她自己。

为她的妹妹。

也为阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: We have scary dark skies, violent storms…now a monster come to life.
sentences.zh: 我们就有了吓人的黑天、狂暴的暴风雨……现在还有了活过来的怪物。

sentences.en: I mean, I’m putting two and two together, and I’m not getting five.” Elsa glanced at the storm outside.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我把二加二放在一起，得出的可不是五。"艾莎瞥了眼外面的暴风雨。

sentences.en: It had picked up again, the rain battering at the windows.
sentences.zh: 雨势又起，拍打着窗户。

sentences.en: Another drop landed on her forehead. “Maybe you’re right.
sentences.zh: 又一滴水落在她额头。"也许你是对的。

sentences.en: Kristoff did say if you told a draugr’s story, you could bring it back….” Anna swallowed hard. “There’s something more.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫确实说过，讲出亡灵的故事，就能把它唤回来……"安娜使劲咽了口唾沫。"还有别的事。

sentences.en: When I fell, my satchel spilled open with the copy of my article in the Village Crown .
sentences.zh: 我摔下去时，挎包散开了，里面那份《村庄之冠》上登着我的文章。

sentences.en: You know, the one where Wael interviewed me about taking your place as queen?” Her frown deepened. “The creature picked it up and started freaking out.
sentences.zh: 就是韦尔采访我、说我接替你成为女王的那篇？"她眉头皱得更紧了。"那怪物捡起报纸，开始发疯。

sentences.en: Like the article upset it or something.” “Why?” Elsa shot her a puzzled look. “What would a draugr care about a newspaper?
sentences.zh: 好像那篇文章把它惹到了。""为什么？"艾莎困惑地瞥了她一眼。"亡灵会在乎一份报纸什么？

sentences.en: Can they even read?” “If they were once human, maybe.
sentences.zh: 它们认字吗？""如果它们曾经是人，也许吧。

sentences.en: And I mean, think about it!” Anna exclaimed. “I’m the younger sister!
sentences.zh: 而且我是说，你想想看！"安娜喊道。"我是妹妹！

sentences.en: I’m just like Inger!
sentences.zh: 我就跟英格一样！

sentences.en: And I have the crown.
sentences.zh: 而且我戴着王冠。

sentences.en: Sissel probably thinks I stole it from you—just like Inger tried to steal it from her!
sentences.zh: 西塞尔大概以为我是偷了你的——就像英格当年想从她那儿抢走一样！

sentences.en: And now she’s trying to get her revenge on me, since Inger’s long gone!” Elsa raised an eyebrow. “Okay, that’s a bit of a stretch.” “And yet a story-time monster literally attacking us in real life in the woods and controlling the weather isn’t?” Anna answered.
sentences.zh: 如今英格早就不在了，她就冲我来复仇！"艾莎挑起眉毛。"嗯，这有点牵强了。""可故事里的怪物在森林里真刀真枪地袭击我们、还能操控天气，就不牵强？"安娜反问。

sentences.en: Her whole body was trembling now.
sentences.zh: 她此刻浑身发抖。

sentences.en: Elsa put a comforting hand on her shoulder. “Anna, you’re upsetting yourself,” she scolded gently. “It’s not going to help.
sentences.zh: 艾莎安慰地把一只手搭在她肩上。"安娜，你在自己吓自己，"她温柔地责备道。"这没用的。

sentences.en: Whatever is going on, we’ll figure it out.
sentences.zh: 不管怎么回事，我们都会弄清楚的。

sentences.en: But I promise you, I’m not going to let some draugr get you, okay?
sentences.zh: 但我向你保证，我不会让什么亡灵伤到你，好吗？

sentences.en: No matter what.” “I need to get back to Arendelle,” Anna declared, trying to rise to her feet. “Kristoff is there.
sentences.zh: 无论如何。""我得回阿伦黛尔，"安娜坚定地说，试图站起来。"克斯托夫在那儿。

sentences.en: If the draugr knows he’s the one who told its story on the anniversary, it could be after him, and everyone in Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 如果亡灵知道是他在这个周年日讲出了它的故事，它可能会去追他，还有阿伦黛尔的每一个人。

sentences.en: We need to warn people they could be in danger!” She winced in pain as she put weight on her ankle. “You’re not going anywhere,” Elsa told her sternly. “Not on that ankle.
sentences.zh: 我们得警告大家，他们可能有危险！"她把重量压在脚踝上，疼得缩了一下。"你哪儿也不许去，"艾莎严厉地对她说。"脚踝这样不行。

sentences.en: And not in this storm.” “But Arendelle—” “Can take care of itself.
sentences.zh: 而且这暴风雨里也不行。""可阿伦黛尔——""它能照顾好自己。

sentences.en: You left Kristoff and Mattias in charge.
sentences.zh: 你留下了克斯托夫和马蒂亚斯主持大局。

sentences.en: They can deal with one little monster.” Anna raised an eyebrow. “You call that little?” “You know what I mean,” Elsa chided. “I promise, the second the storm stops, I’ll go out and look for Havski.
sentences.zh: 他们对付一只小怪物绰绰有余。"安娜挑起眉毛。"你管那叫小？""你明白我的意思，"艾莎嗔怪道。"我保证，暴风雨一停，我就出去找哈夫斯基。

sentences.en: Or find someone with a wagon.
sentences.zh: 或者找辆马车来。

sentences.en: But right now, we both need to stay put.” Anna nodded glumly, not looking happy about the prospect of staying put.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们俩都得待着别动。"安娜闷闷不乐地点头，对"待着别动"的前景并不开心。

sentences.en: Elsa felt a pang of guilt.
sentences.zh: 艾莎感到一阵愧疚。

sentences.en: Maybe she should have protested harder when Anna said she wanted to come along.
sentences.zh: 也许当初安娜说要跟来时，她该更强烈地反对。

sentences.en: Of course, at the time, she hadn’t known there was an actual monster in the woods.
sentences.zh: 当然，那时她还不知道林子里真有怪物。

sentences.en: Another wave of unease seemed to waft through her stomach.
sentences.zh: 又一阵不安仿佛从她胃里飘过。

sentences.en: Her magic had been almost useless against that thing.
sentences.zh: 她的魔力对付那东西几乎没用。

sentences.en: And at the end, it had all but sputtered out.
sentences.zh: 而到最后，它几乎彻底泄了气。

sentences.en: She knew her magic wasn’t limitless—no magic was, according to the Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己的魔力并非无限——按北地人的说法，没有哪种魔力是无限的。

sentences.en: But if it wasn’t even enough to save her sister, what were they going to do if the draugr did attack the kingdom? “Ugh.
sentences.zh: 可如果连救妹妹都不够，万一亡灵真的攻击王国，她们该怎么办？"唉。

sentences.en: I hate feeling so useless,” Anna said, glaring down at her hurt ankle.
sentences.zh: 我最恨这种无能为力的感觉，"安娜说，瞪着自己受伤的脚踝。

sentences.en: Elsa knew exactly how she felt. “At least we got our sister time!” she said, trying to cheer her up. “And this time no one can interrupt us!” Anna made a face. “Yeah, except for our friendly neighborhood draugr…” Elsa rose to her feet and wandered over to the window.
sentences.zh: 艾莎太懂她的感受了。"至少我们享受了姐妹时光！"她说着，想给她打气。"而且这回没人能打断我们！"安娜做了个鬼脸。"是啊，除了我们那友好的邻居亡灵……"艾莎站起身，漫步走到窗边。

sentences.en: She peered outside.
sentences.zh: 她朝外面望去。

sentences.en: The storm was still raging, but fortunately there was no creature in sight.
sentences.zh: 暴风雨仍在肆虐，但所幸看不见任何怪物。

sentences.en: She walked over to the door and bolted it, just in case. “The draugr—if that’s what it really was—is gone,” Elsa said. “And we’re safe here in the hut for now.” She dug into her pack. “And look!” Elsa pulled out a bag.
sentences.zh: 她走到门边，闩上门栓，以防万一。"亡灵——如果那真是它的话——已经走了，"艾莎说。"眼下我们在小屋里是安全的。"她翻了翻自己的背包。"看！"艾莎掏出一个袋子。

sentences.en: Anna’s eyes widened. “Marshmallows?
sentences.zh: 安娜睁大眼睛。"棉花糖？

sentences.en: You brought marshmallows?” Elsa shrugged. “Well, we never got a chance to roast them over our campfire.
sentences.zh: 你带了棉花糖？"艾莎耸耸肩。"嗯，我们一直没机会在营火上烤它们。

sentences.en: So I thought I’d bring them along….” She let out a call and suddenly Bruni appeared, pushing its way through a crack in the front door, slurping the air with its tongue.
sentences.zh: 所以我想干脆带在身上……"她唤了一声，火灵忽然出现，从门缝里挤进来，用舌头舔着空气。

sentences.en: Elsa led it over to the small stone hearth in the kitchen area of the hut and instructed the Fire Spirit to do its thing.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把它领到小屋厨房区的小石炉边，命令火灵施展本事。

sentences.en: A moment later there was a small blaze that gave off a warm glow. “Oh my gosh.
sentences.zh: 片刻后便燃起一小簇火苗，散发出温暖的光。"天哪。

sentences.en: Best.
sentences.zh: 最棒了。

sentences.en: Sister.
sentences.zh: 姐姐。

sentences.en: Ever!” Anna exclaimed, her upset demeanor pushed aside.
sentences.zh: 永——远——最棒！"安娜惊叹，先前的烦闷一扫而空。

sentences.en: She pulled her stool closer to the fire.
sentences.zh: 她把凳子往火边挪了挪。

sentences.en: Elsa handed her a cooking skewer from the side of the fireplace, and Anna stabbed the marshmallow with it, holding it over the small flame.
sentences.zh: 艾莎从壁炉边递给她一根烧烤签，安娜把棉花糖戳上去，举在小火苗上方。

sentences.en: Elsa followed with her own, and soon they had two gooey golden brown marshmallows at the ends of their sticks. “Sorry we don’t have any chocolate,” Elsa apologized. “Oh, but we do!” Anna exclaimed, reaching into her own pack.
sentences.zh: 艾莎也如法炮制，很快她们签子末端各有一团金黄黏软的棉花糖。"抱歉我们没有巧克力，"艾莎道歉。"哦，可我们有！"安娜喊道，伸手去翻自己的背包。

sentences.en: She pulled out a wrapped square of paper.
sentences.zh: 她掏出一包用纸裹着的方块。

sentences.en: Elsa laughed as her sister revealed the dark-brown treasure inside. “A queen has to be prepared for all kinds of emergencies,” she joked, breaking the bar in two and handing the larger piece to her sister. “Definitely!” Elsa agreed, watching Anna pull her marshmallow from the fire and set the chocolate on top of it.
sentences.zh: 艾莎笑起来，妹妹亮出了里面深棕色的宝贝。"女王得为各种突发状况做好准备，"她开玩笑说，把巧克力掰成两半，较大的那块递给妹妹。"绝对！"艾莎赞同，看着安娜把棉花糖从火上移开，把巧克力放在上面。

sentences.en: Elsa did the same, breathing in the warm scent as the chocolate melted on her marshmallow.
sentences.zh: 艾莎也照做，巧克力在棉花糖上融化，她深吸着那温暖香气。

sentences.en: She looked up at her sister. “Mmm.
sentences.zh: 她抬头看着妹妹。"嗯。

sentences.en: Chocolate,” they said in sync.
sentences.zh: 巧克力，"她们异口同声。

sentences.en: Then they giggled. “Okay, you’re making me feel a little better,” Anna admitted after savoring her treat. “I’m hardly thinking at all about the monster lurking in the woods.” She glanced out the window. “Hardly…” Elsa sighed.
sentences.zh: 接着她们咯咯笑起来。"好吧，你让我感觉好点了，"安娜细细品味后承认。"我几乎一点都没在想林子里潜伏的怪物了。"她瞥了眼窗外。"几乎……"艾莎叹了口气。

sentences.en: She was pretty sure neither one of them was going to sleep a wink tonight.
sentences.zh: 她相当确信，她们今晚谁都别想合眼。

sentences.en: But maybe that was for the best.
sentences.zh: 但也许这样最好。

sentences.en: They didn’t know when, or if, the draugr would be back.
sentences.zh: 她们不知道亡灵何时会回来，甚至不知它会不会回来。

sentences.en: And Elsa didn’t want it to catch them off guard again.
sentences.zh: 而艾莎不想再让它打得她们措手不及。

sentences.en: Especially if her powers were really drained. “Oops!” Anna squeaked as her second marshmallow caught fire.
sentences.zh: 尤其如果她的魔力真的耗尽了。"哎呀！"安娜的第二颗棉花糖着了火，她尖叫一声。

sentences.en: She yanked it out of the hearth.
sentences.zh: 她猛地把签子从炉里抽出来。

sentences.en: Elsa instinctively lifted a finger and flung a small blast of ice in the marshmallow’s direction, easily quenching the flame.
sentences.zh: 艾莎本能地抬起一根手指，朝棉花糖方向射出一小股冰，轻而易举地灭了火。

sentences.en: Anna shot her an appreciative look. “Thanks,” she said.
sentences.zh: 安娜感激地瞥了她一眼。"谢了，"她说。
