sentences.en: Elsa smiled, feeling better knowing her powers had returned—at least enough for a marshmallow emergency.
sentences.zh: 艾莎微笑，得知魔力已恢复——至少够应付一颗棉花糖着火的紧急状况——她心情好了些。

sentences.en: It was funny; once upon a time, all she’d wanted was to rid herself of her powers.
sentences.zh: 说来好笑；曾几何时，她唯一的愿望就是摆脱自己的魔力。

sentences.en: But now, even the thought of losing them terrified her.
sentences.zh: 可如今，光是想到失去它们，都让她害怕。

sentences.en: As Anna had said, they were a part of her now, for better or worse.
sentences.zh: 正如安娜所说，它们现在是她的一部分了，无论好坏。

sentences.en: Not a curse, like she’d once believed.
sentences.zh: 不再是她曾以为的诅咒。

sentences.en: But a gift that could help people.
sentences.zh: 而是一份能帮助人的礼物。

sentences.en: One that could literally save lives.
sentences.zh: 一份真能救命的礼物。

sentences.en: Make the world a better place.
sentences.zh: 让世界变得更美好。

sentences.en: The spirits had trusted her with this gift, and now she wanted nothing more than to prove worthy of that trust.
sentences.zh: 精灵们把这礼物托付给她，如今她最大的心愿，就是证明自己配得上这份信任。

sentences.en: A thought suddenly struck Elsa. “I may have another way to distract you,” she told her sister. “Yeah?” Anna queried, looking up.
sentences.zh: 艾莎忽然灵光一闪。"我也许还有别的法子分散你的注意力，"她对妹妹说。"哦？"安娜抬起头问。

sentences.en: Her mouth was covered in sticky white fluff. “How’s that?” “I can try the memory thing again.
sentences.zh: 她嘴上沾着黏糊糊的白色绒絮。"怎么个法子？""我可以再试试那个记忆的法子。

sentences.en: Like I was trying to do in the tent last night.” “I’d love that!” Anna said encouragingly. “Do you have one of Mother and Father?
sentences.zh: 就像昨晚在帐篷里我想做的那样。""我太愿意了！"安娜鼓励地说。"你有没有关于爸爸妈妈的？

sentences.en: Maybe one of them when they were growing up?” “I think so,” Elsa said, closing her eyes for a moment to try to draw up something for her sister.
sentences.zh: 也许是他们成长中的一段？""我想有，"艾莎说，闭上眼片刻，想为妹妹调出些画面。

sentences.en: Then she opened her eyes again and smiled. “Yes!
sentences.zh: 然后她又睁眼微笑。"有！

sentences.en: I’ve got just the memory!
sentences.zh: 我正好有一段记忆！

sentences.en: I pulled it up in Ahtohallan the other day.
sentences.zh: 前两天我在阿托哈兰重温过它。

sentences.en: Mother and Father were in a ballroom.
sentences.zh: 爸爸妈妈在舞厅里。

sentences.en: Spinning around to this ridiculous dance they made up.
sentences.zh: 正转着圈跳他们自编的滑稽舞步。

sentences.en: I think they called it ‘The Reindeer Who Has to Pee Really Badly but Is Stuck in a Ballroom.’” Anna raised an eyebrow. “That sounds like quite the dance.” “I know, right?
sentences.zh: 我想他们管它叫"急得想上厕所却被困在舞厅里的驯鹿"。"安娜挑起眉毛。"听起来是个挺了不得的舞。""可不是嘛。

sentences.en: It’s crazy how silly they used to be.
sentences.zh: 他们以前那么傻，简直疯狂。

sentences.en: They were so cute together.
sentences.zh: 俩人在一起时可真可爱。

sentences.en: I sometimes spend hours pulling up their memories.” “You are so lucky,” Anna said with a sigh. “I wish I could see it all, too.” Elsa felt a small twinge of guilt at the wistfulness she heard in her sister’s voice.
sentences.zh: 我有时一调出他们的记忆就是好几个小时。""你真幸运，"安娜叹了口气说。"我也希望能全都看到。"听出妹妹语气里的向往，艾莎心里泛起一丝愧疚。

sentences.en: It wasn’t fair that Anna should be locked out of these memories—after all, Iduna and Agnarr were her parents, too.
sentences.zh: 让安娜被挡在这些记忆之外，实在不公平——毕竟，伊杜娜和安格瑞也是她的父母。

sentences.en: But Elsa was the only one who could access Ahtohallan and its treasure trove of memories.
sentences.zh: 但艾莎是唯一能进入阿托哈兰、触及那记忆宝藏的人。

sentences.en: Which meant she was going to have to get creative. “Well, that’s why I’m working on this,” Elsa said. “My goal is to learn how to re-create the memories I see in Ahtohallan and bring them home to you.
sentences.zh: 这意味着她得想点新办法。"嗯，这正是我在钻研这个的原因，"艾莎说。"我的目标是学会如何重现我在阿托哈兰看到的记忆，把它们带回家给你。

sentences.en: So you don’t have to miss out on anything.” “Did I ever mention you’re amazing?” Anna asked. “Because you are.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不必错过任何东西了。""我说过你很了不起吗？"安娜问。"因为你就是。

sentences.en: Amazing.” Elsa felt her cheeks heat at the praise from her sister.
sentences.zh: 了不起。"听着妹妹的夸奖，艾莎感到脸颊发烫。

sentences.en: Anna had always loved her magic, even when they were children, and hearing the excitement in her voice now took Elsa back to that innocent time.
sentences.zh: 安娜从她们还是孩子起就爱她的魔力，此刻听到她声音里的兴奋，艾莎仿佛回到了那段纯真岁月。

sentences.en: Do the magic!
sentences.zh: 变魔法吧！

sentences.en: Anna would beg, and Elsa could never deny her.
sentences.zh: 安娜曾这样央求，而艾莎从没拒绝过她。

sentences.en: She drew in a deep breath, trying to channel the power inside of her.
sentences.zh: 她深吸一口气，试图调动体内的力量。

sentences.en: Then she lifted her index finger, pointing it toward the little puddle of water from the leak in the roof.
sentences.zh: 然后她抬起食指，指向屋顶漏水形成的小水洼。

sentences.en: She’d learned it was easier to pull things from water, because as Olaf liked to remind them, water had memory.
sentences.zh: 她发现从水中提取画面更容易，因为正如奥拉夫爱提醒她们的，水有记忆。

sentences.en: As she closed her eyes, she tried to picture the flowing image of her parents in her mind as she’d seen them in Ahtohallan.
sentences.zh: 她闭上眼，努力在脑中勾勒父母流动的影像，就像她在阿托哈兰所见那样。

sentences.en: In the ballroom.
sentences.zh: 在舞厅里。

sentences.en: In each other’s arms.
sentences.zh: 在彼此的臂弯中。

sentences.en: Twirling and laughing and— Suddenly her mind went blank.
sentences.zh: 旋转、欢笑，然后——忽然，她的脑中一片空白。

sentences.en: Completely blank—as if someone had smothered a candle.
sentences.zh: 完全空白——仿佛有人掐灭了一支蜡烛。

sentences.en: The memory she’d had in her head ceased entirely, and for a moment, she couldn’t even remember what memory she’d been trying to conjure up to begin with.
sentences.zh: 她脑中原有的那段记忆彻底消失，有那么一会儿，她甚至想不起自己起初想召唤的究竟是哪段记忆。

sentences.en: Something about their parents?
sentences.zh: 关于父母的什么？

sentences.en: Was that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Her eyes opened.
sentences.zh: 她睁开眼。

sentences.en: She glanced apologetically at her sister. “Argh.
sentences.zh: 她歉疚地瞥了妹妹一眼。"哎。

sentences.en: I had it.
sentences.zh: 我刚才还有的。

sentences.en: For a second…” She sighed. “I’m sorry.
sentences.zh: 就一瞬间……"她叹了口气。"对不起。

sentences.en: Maybe it isn’t the best night for this.” “The best night for what?” Anna asked through a mouthful of burnt marshmallow.
sentences.zh: 也许今晚不是做这个的好时机。""做什么的好时机？"安娜嘴里塞满烤焦的棉花糖问道。

sentences.en: She waved her hand in front of her face. “I know I should wait for them to cool down, but they’re just so yummy.
sentences.zh: 她把手在面前扇了扇。"我知道该等它们凉了再吃，可它们实在太好吃了。

sentences.en: I burn the roof of my mouth every time!” Elsa frowned, confused.
sentences.zh: 我每次都把口腔上膛烫到！"艾莎困惑地皱起眉。

sentences.en: Was Anna trying to make her feel better by ignoring what had just happened?
sentences.zh: 安娜是想装作没发生刚才的事，好让她安心吗？

sentences.en: That didn’t seem like something her sister would do.
sentences.zh: 这可不像妹妹的作风。

sentences.en: She’d at least ask if Elsa was okay.
sentences.zh: 她至少会问问艾莎没事吧。

sentences.en: Wouldn’t she?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Instead, she was acting like nothing had happened at all.
sentences.zh: 可她却表现得像什么都没发生过。

sentences.en: Or as if she’d forgotten it altogether.
sentences.zh: 或者说，像把整件事都忘了。

sentences.en: The same way Elsa had forgotten the memory she was trying to pull.
sentences.zh: 就像艾莎忘了自己正想调出的那段记忆。

sentences.en: Concern churned in Elsa’s gut.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的胃里翻涌起不安。

sentences.en: Something was wrong here.
sentences.zh: 这里不对劲。

sentences.en: Something was very wrong.
sentences.zh: 很不对劲。

sentences.en: She thought back to how Anna and Kristoff had acted at the campsite last night.
sentences.zh: 她回想昨晚安娜和克斯托夫在营地里的表现。

sentences.en: They’d been strangely forgetful then, too.
sentences.zh: 那时他们也怪异地健忘。

sentences.en: Was it all related?
sentences.zh: 这一切都有关联吗？

sentences.en: Could it have something to do with the monster?
sentences.zh: 会不会和那怪物有关？

sentences.en: Only Ahtohallan knows… Her mother’s voice seemed to whisper in her ears.
sentences.zh: 只有阿托哈兰知道……母亲的声音仿佛在耳边低语。

sentences.en: She drew in a breath. “Look, Anna, here’s what I’m thinking.
sentences.zh: 她深吸一口气。"听着，安娜，我是这么想的。

sentences.en: Tomorrow we’ll get you back to Arendelle to make sure everyone’s okay.
sentences.zh: 明天我们送你回阿伦黛尔，确保大家都平安。

sentences.en: And you can do some research on draugrs in our parents’ library.
sentences.zh: 你可以去父母的藏书室做些关于亡灵的研究。

sentences.en: Find out everything you can about the monster.
sentences.zh: 尽可能弄清这怪物的底底细。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, I’ll go back to Ahtohallan and see what I can learn there.
sentences.zh: 同时，我回阿托哈兰，看看能学到什么。

sentences.en: Maybe the white river can tell me something useful.” Anna swallowed her marshmallow. “Good idea,” she said. “And then we’ll meet back in Arendelle and compare notes.
sentences.zh: 也许那条白河能告诉我些有用的。"安娜咽下棉花糖。"好主意，"她说。"然后我们在阿伦黛尔碰头，对一对笔记。

sentences.en: Together, I’m sure we can figure out what this draugr is doing here.” Elsa smiled at the confidence she heard in her sister’s voice.
sentences.zh: 一起，我确信我们能弄清这亡灵来这儿干什么。"听着妹妹声音里的自信，艾莎微微笑了。

sentences.en: Anna truly wasn’t scared of anything—even when maybe she should be.
sentences.zh: 安娜当真什么都不怕——哪怕有时她本该害怕。

sentences.en: Elsa admired her for that and wished she could feel the same.
sentences.zh: 艾莎钦佩她这一点，也希望自己能有同感。

sentences.en: But as the wind howled outside, the branches of nearby trees rapping angrily against the windowpanes, she realized she was afraid.
sentences.zh: 可当外面风声呼啸，近旁树枝愤怒地敲打窗玻璃，她意识到自己害怕了。

sentences.en: For herself.
sentences.zh: 为她自己。

sentences.en: For her sister.
sentences.zh: 为她的妹妹。

sentences.en: And for Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 也为阿伦黛尔。

chapters.title: Chapter Eight: Anna
chapters.en:
HORSES ARE LOYAL CREATURES, Anna thought as Elsa returned to the hut the next morning with Anna’s beloved horse at her side.

“Havski!” Anna cried, hobbling toward him.

Her ankle felt much better than it had the day before, but there was no way she could have walked all the way back to Arendelle on it. If Elsa hadn’t located Havski, what would she have done? She imagined her sister creating a toboggan out of ice for her or calling on the ice creature Marshmallow to leave his cozy castle at the top of the North Mountain to carry her back. Wouldn’t that have been a sight—her sitting in Marshmallow’s palm as she approached the village? Talk about making an entrance!

“I’m so glad Elsa found you, boy,” said Anna as she moved to touch Havski’s head, and he twitched. That was odd, but now that she looked at the horse closer, she realized his whole body was shaking.

“Is he okay?” Anna asked.

“I found him wandering around the pasture trying to find you,” Elsa said. “He’s dry, though, so he must have found shelter overnight.” Elsa stroked his long black mane. “Poor guy. He must have been so scared when he saw the draugr.”

“It’s okay, Havski,” Anna said soothingly, petting his pale gray hide. “We’re safe now, and we’re going home to Arendelle to…”

That was funny. There was something she had to do in the village, but for the life of her, she suddenly couldn’t remember what it was. Anna looked at Elsa, who was watching her closely and frowning.

“To check on the people and see what you can find out about the draugr before it returns,” Elsa prompted her. She placed a cool hand on her sister’s cheek. “Anna, you do remember that’s what we discussed last night, don’t you?”

As soon as Elsa touched her, Anna felt what resembled a whooshing sensation through her brain. The memory was back! Anna was headed home to do research on draugrs in their parents’ library, and Elsa was going to Ahtohallan. “Of course!” she declared with a shake of her head. Her copper-colored locks waved side to side. “Sorry! You know my brain after a bad night’s sleep!”

“Speaking of night…” Elsa looked up at the sky, her brow creasing in worry. While they both knew it was morning, the dawn hadn’t come. Instead, for the second day in a row, the world was awash in a darkness that didn’t feel like night or day. There was no sun or moon in sight. The air was thick and the world quiet, as if it were just waiting for disaster to strike. Even the birds and woodland creatures seemed to have gone into hiding.

Anna suddenly found herself longing for the beautiful twilight of the Polar Nights. Maybe this was why Havski seemed unnerved, too. Something was clearly wrong. Days were always shorter leading up to the Polar Nights, and snow was common, but this weather was…different. Anna just wished she knew for certain whether this was the draugr’s doing, and longed to know how to make it go away.

“The sooner we figure out what’s really going on, the better,” Elsa said, seeming to hear her sister’s thoughts as she guided Anna to Havski before helping her up. “I’ll be back from Ahtohallan as soon as I can. Then we can decide the best way to handle this.”

“Handle this,” Anna repeated. Handle what? she wondered, and then she remembered. The draugr! The books in the library! Whether the draugr is Sissel! Right! Why was she suddenly so forgetful? She didn’t want to worry Elsa any more than she had already, so she said nothing about having another foggy moment. Instead, she pulled on Havski’s reins. “I’ll see you soon. Be careful.”

Elsa smiled at her, then whistled for her own steed. The Water Nokk burst through the trees, its crystallized mane casting an array of rainbows across the ground as it raced toward them. Anna watched as Elsa threw her leg over the Water Nokk’s back, hoisting herself up. Anna wondered, not for the first time, what it must be like to ride bareback on such a wild creature. Elsa always made it look magical and super comfy, of course.

“Love you!” Elsa smiled at her sister. “See you soon!”

“Love you, too!” Anna called after her as the Water Nokk turned and headed into the forest. Anna watched her sister go, sending out a silent wish for her safety. She hadn’t wanted to admit it to Elsa, but she was still shaken by their encounter with the monster the night before. If Elsa hadn’t freed her, what would the “D-word” (Anna had decided not to take any chances by saying the creature’s full name anymore, just in case!) have done to her?

She shook her head, urging Havski on. No use thinking about what could have happened, she scolded herself. She needed to get back to Arendelle—before something actually did happen.

Once she reached the village, it took all of Anna’s strength not to start screaming and waving people down yelling, “Draugr danger!” But she didn’t want to terrify everyone. She had to act like a queen, and a queen would remain calm and sound rational. So Anna took a deep breath, deciding she would act firm and direct, and not out of sorts—like she actually was.

It was then she spotted Kristoff, wandering through the town square. “I’m so glad you’re here,” she said, out of breath.

“What’s going on?” Kristoff asked as he reached up to lift Anna off the horse. He helped her down and wrapped his strong arms tightly around her. “Everything okay?”

“We have a situation. I don’t want you to panic.” Even if I’m panicking, she thought. She glanced around at the square, half expecting to see the draugr lurking in the shadows or behind her parents’ statue. But no, everything seemed calm. Normal.

“I’ve learned not to panic till Elsa sends up snow signals,” Kristoff joked.

“This is serious,” she said, lowering her voice. “We need to warn the village about an impending attack…from a draugr.” She held her breath, half thinking Kristoff would laugh at her and say she was being as ridiculous as Olaf.

Instead, Kristoff’s eyes widened, and she felt his body tighten. “A draugr? Are you serious?”

“Unfortunately, yes. It came out of nowhere when Elsa and I were coming back from Sorenson’s. Let’s just say we’re lucky to be alive.” She shivered a little, her mind flashing back to the night before, being trapped by those tree roots. The draugr coming closer and closer…

“You saw Sinister Sissel?” Olaf cried out, bounding up beside them. “Did she try to eat you? Did she try to turn you into a draugr, too?” He narrowed his eyes at her, as if trying to determine if she’d been draugrized somehow. “Are you okay, Anna? You can tell me if you’re feeling at all monster-y. I won’t judge, I swear!”

“I’m fine,” Anna insisted. For now, she thought. “Look, Olaf, I’m sorry I didn’t believe you at first, but I think you might be right. The draugr has to be Sissel—and I think it’s behind all the weird weather we’ve been having.”

“I knew it!” Olaf cried, pacing from side to side. “She heard us talking about her at the campfire and now she’s come to attack us all. Or at least steal our cheese. And slippers. And possibly our souls.” He stared up at the dark sky, opening his mouth and wailing, “Why, Sissel, why?”

“Okay, wait a second. Who is this Sissel again? And why does she want to harm us?” Kristoff asked, looking oddly confused.

Anna did a double take. Had Kristoff just asked who Sissel was? He was the one who had told them about her to begin with! And now he was acting like he didn’t remember her at all! Which was beyond bizarre, considering Kristoff never forgot a thing—even if at times, she wished he would. (Telling him she liked his fish soup was a decision that still haunted her.) This didn’t make any sense. Unless…

She inhaled sharply as a horrible thought suddenly crossed her mind: could this, too, have something to do with the draugr? Could the draugr—or Sissel—be making them both suddenly so forgetful? There was only one way to find out.

“Quick question,” she said to Kristoff. “What very important date for us is coming up?”

Kristoff looked baffled. “Date?”

Olaf slid in next to him. “Just to be clear: there’s several.”

“Several?” Kristoff parroted.

Anna felt her hands turn clammy. “Having to do with chocolate?” she prompted.

“And the fact you’re getting married,” Olaf added. “But no one actually knows when yet. You’ve only been engaged for like a minute.”

“Engaged?” Kristoff, looking lost, blinked rapidly.

Anna felt her heart drop. Forgetting their Choco-versary was one thing, but their engagement was implausible.

“Are you feeling okay?” she asked, feeling her anxiety increase.

“Um, Anna?” Olaf tugged on her sleeve. “I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but he’s not the only one acting forgetful today. In fact, it’s kind of spread to the whole town.”

Anna felt her stomach begin to turn. Looking around, it suddenly occurred to her that things were unusually quiet. Everyone was supposed to be working on the Polar Nights festival, yet people seemed to be moving around in a daze. As if they’d forgotten what they were supposed to be doing. Gretchen, the village painter who was meant to be designing the festival banner, was standing in front of a blank canvas with a brush that had no paint on it. Helmut the ice carver was sitting on a solid block of ice, using his ice pick on his teeth!

Anna spotted the baker and hurried over to her. “Hi, Mrs. Blodget!” She sensed she had greeted the older woman with maybe just a little too much cheeriness in her voice. “Just checking in!” she whispered. “How is Kristoff’s anniversary chocolate mold coming?”

Mrs. Blodget blinked. “Kristoff’s what?”

“Chocolate anniversary gift,” Anna said, her uneasy feeling worsening. “You were doing a special order just for me.”

“I don’t remember any special orders,” Mrs. Blodget responded. “But I’m happy to help you with whatever you need.”

Anna’s heart beat fast in her chest. She turned from Mrs. Blodget to see the two Waffle Brothers standing nearby, not arguing for once. Which was weird in and of itself.

“Hi, guys!” she greeted, her voice now a bit shrill. “What about you? Are you ready for your famous bake-off?”

The brothers looked at one another blankly. “Bake-off? I don’t remember signing up for a bake-off,” said Bjorn.

“You were going to compete with each other to see who made the better waffle,” Anna prompted.

“You make waffles?” Bjarne asked his brother. Bjorn shrugged, taking a bite of a waffle. Anna groaned in frustration.

“It’s been like this all morning,” Olaf said nervously. “The choir couldn’t remember the lyrics to their songs, the pie maker forgot to bake his piecrusts, and the candle shop couldn’t find their wax.”

“Are you serious?” Anna asked. This was getting worse and worse. She leaned against a lamppost, feeling like the world was spinning out of control. “The draugr,” she whispered. “This all has to be from the draugr.” She closed her eyes for a moment, hearing the creature’s moan in her mind.

Sissssttterrrr.

“It must have come here last night and stolen everyone’s memories.” She squeezed her eyes shut even tighter. “What am I going to do?”

“You could try to stop it?” Olaf suggested brightly. “I mean, just a thought!”

“But how?”

“At the campfire, you mentioned a book about draugrs you found in your parents’ secret library,” Olaf reminded her. Clearly, he wasn’t suffering from the same memory loss the rest of them were experiencing. “You might start there.”

Of course! Anna smacked her forehead with her hand. That was why she’d come back to Arendelle to begin with! To research draugrs! She’d totally forgotten.

Again.

Oh, dear.

“Olaf, we need to find that book right away!” Anna cried, grabbing both his hand and Kristoff’s for safekeeping.

She started to pull them toward the castle, then stopped.

There was one thing she had to do first. Anna let go of Kristoff’s hand temporarily, grabbed a piece of paper and a pencil off a nearby table, and scribbled a quick note. Then she held it up in the air.

“Gale?” she called out, and then waited. No matter where the Wind Spirit was when she called, it always seemed to respond quickly, and this time was no different. Gale whisked through the street, blowing unhung decorations for the festival along with it. Anna let the note ride on the wind. “Find my sister and get her back to Arendelle as fast as you can!”
chapters.zh:
马真是忠诚的动物，安娜想。第二天清晨，艾莎回到小屋，身边正是安娜心爱的马。"哈夫斯基！"安娜喊着，一瘸一拐地朝它走去。

她的脚踝比昨天好多了，但靠它一路走回阿伦黛尔是绝无可能的。

如果艾莎没找到哈夫斯基，她可怎么办？

她想象妹妹用冰给她做了个雪橇，或者召唤那个叫"棉花糖"的冰怪，离开北山顶上温暖的城堡来驮她回去。

那场面一定很壮观——她坐在棉花糖的手掌里，朝村庄走去？

那才叫隆重登场！"我真高兴艾莎找到了你，伙计，"安娜说着伸手去摸哈夫斯基的头，它抖了一下。

真奇怪，可当她再仔细打量这匹马，才发现它全身都在发抖。"它没事吧？"安娜问。"我发现它在牧场里转悠，想找你，"艾莎说。"不过它是干的，所以昨晚一定找到了避身之处。"艾莎抚摸着它长长的黑鬃。"可怜的家伙。

它看见亡灵时一定吓坏了。""没事的，哈夫斯基，"安娜温柔地安抚，轻拍它浅灰色的皮毛。"我们现在安全了，要回阿伦黛尔家了，去……"真有意思。

村子里有件事她必须去做，可她死活忽然想不起那是什么了。

安娜望向艾莎，艾莎正紧盯着她，皱着眉。"去探望大家，趁着亡灵回来前，看看能查出关于它的什么，"艾莎提示她。

她把一只冰凉的手贴在妹妹脸颊上。"安娜，你记得这是我们昨晚商量好的吧，对不对？"艾莎一碰到她，安娜脑中便感到一阵类似嗖然掠过的感觉。

记忆回来了！

安娜正要回家，去父母的藏书室研究亡灵，而艾莎要去阿托哈兰。"当然！"她摇着头宣称。

她铜色的发丝左右晃动。"抱歉！

你又不是不知道，我睡不好觉时脑子就……！""说到夜晚……"艾莎抬头望天，眉头担忧地皱起。

她们明知已是清晨，黎明却没到来。

相反，连续第二天，世界浸在一片不分昼夜的黑暗里。

看不见太阳，也看不见月亮。

空气凝重，世界寂静，仿佛只是在等待灾难降临。

连鸟儿和林中走兽似乎都躲了起来。

安娜忽然发现自己想念极夜那美丽的暮光了。

也许这正是哈夫斯基也显得不安的原因。

显然有什么不对劲。

极夜将至时白昼总会变短，下雪也常见，但这天气……不一样。

安娜只希望自己能确定这是不是亡灵的杰作，也渴望知道怎么让它消失。"我们越早弄清到底怎么回事越好，"艾莎说，仿佛听见了妹妹的心声，她扶安娜到哈夫斯基身边，帮她上马。"我会尽快从阿托哈兰回来。

然后我们就能决定对付它的最佳办法。""对付它，"安娜重复道。

对付什么？她纳闷，接着想起来了。

亡灵！

藏书室里的书！

亡灵到底是不是西塞尔！

对！

她怎么突然这么健忘了？

她不想让艾莎比现在更担心，所以对自己的又一次神思恍惚只字未提。

相反，她拉起哈夫斯基的缰绳。"我们很快见。

保重。"艾莎对她笑笑，然后为自己坐骑吹了声口哨。

水马从林间冲出，晶化的鬃毛在地上投下一串彩虹，朝她们疾驰而来。

安娜看着艾莎把腿跨上水马背，纵身坐稳。

安娜不止一次地猜想，骑在这样野性的生灵上、毫无鞍具，会是何种滋味。

当然，艾莎总让它看起来既神奇又超级舒服。"爱你！"艾莎冲妹妹微笑。"很快见！""我也爱你！"水马转身朝森林而去，安娜在身后喊道。

安娜目送妹妹离去，在心中默默为她祈愿平安。

她不愿向艾莎承认，可昨晚与那怪物的遭遇仍让她心有余悸。

若不是艾莎把她救出，那个"D字怪物"（安娜决定为防万一，再也不冒风险说出那怪物的全名了！）会对她做什么？

她摇摇头，催哈夫斯基前行。

想那些可能发生的万一毫无用处，她责怪自己。

她得赶回阿伦黛尔——趁真正出事之前。

一到村庄，安娜使出浑身力气才忍住不扯开嗓子、拦住路人喊"亡灵危险！"可她不想吓坏所有人。

她得像个女王，而女王会保持冷静、言语理性。

于是安娜深吸一口气，决定表现得坚定而直接，而不是像她实际那样、六神无主。

就在这时，她瞥见克斯托夫在城镇广场上游荡。"真高兴你在这儿，"她上气不接下气地说。"怎么回事？"克斯托夫伸手把安娜从马上抱下时问道。

他扶她下来，用健壮的双臂紧紧搂住她。"都好吗？""我们有状况了。

我不想你惊慌。"尽管我自己就在慌，她想。

她环顾广场，半以为会看见亡灵潜伏在暗处或父母雕像背后。

但是没有，一切似乎平静。

正常。"我学乖了，在艾莎发出雪信号前绝不惊慌，"克斯托夫开玩笑。"这很严重，"她压低声音说。"我们得警告全村，一场袭击即将来临……来自一个亡灵。"她屏住呼吸，半以为克斯托夫会笑她，说她跟奥拉夫一样荒唐。

谁知克斯托夫眼睛瞪大，她感到他身体绷紧了。"一个亡灵？

你是说真的？""不幸的是，真的。

它从天而降，当时我和艾莎正从索伦森那儿回来。

咱们能活下来算是走运。"她微微一颤，脑中闪回前一晚被那些树根困住的情景。

亡灵越逼越近……"你们见到"阴森的西塞尔"了？"奥拉夫蹦到他们身旁喊道。"她想吃掉你们吗？

她也想把你们变成亡灵吗？"他眯起眼睛盯着她，像在判断她是否被"亡灵化"了。"你还好吗，安娜？

你要是觉得自己有半点像怪物，可以告诉我。

我绝不评判，我发誓！""我没事，"安娜坚持说。

眼下没事，她想。"听着，奥拉夫，抱歉我起初不信你，但我想你也许是对的。

这亡灵一定是西塞尔——而且我想，我们这段怪天气都是它搞的鬼。""我就知道！"奥拉夫喊着，来回踱步。"她在营火边听见我们谈论她，现在就来袭击我们所有人了。

或者至少偷我们的奶酪。

还有拖鞋。

可能还有我们的灵魂。"他抬头盯着黑漆漆的天空，张嘴哀嚎："为什么啊，西塞尔，为什么？""好了，等一下。

这个西塞尔到底是谁？

她为什么要害我们？"克斯托夫问，神情诡异地困惑。

安娜愣了一下，又看了一眼。

克斯托夫刚才是在问西塞尔是谁？

可最初把她的故事讲给他们听的，正是他啊！

而现在他却表现得像完全不记得她了！

这太离谱了，毕竟克斯托夫从不忘事——哪怕有时她倒希望他忘。

（告诉他喜欢他的鱼汤，这个决定至今让她后悔。）这根本说不通。

除非……她猛吸一口气，一个可怕的念头突然闪过脑海：这会不会也和亡灵有关？

亡灵——或者说西塞尔——会不会让他们俩都突然变得这么健忘？

只有一个办法能弄清。"问个问题，"她对克斯托夫说。"对我们来说，即将到来的一个非常重要的日子是什么？"克斯托夫一脸茫然。"日子？"奥拉夫溜到他身旁。"说清楚点：有好几个呢。""好几个？"克斯托夫鹦鹉学舌。

安娜感到手心冒汗。"和巧克力有关的？"她提示。"还有你们要结婚这件事，"奥拉夫补充。"但还没人真知道具体日子呢。

你们才订婚了一小会儿。""订婚？"克斯托夫一脸茫然，飞快地眨着眼。

安娜的心一沉。

忘了他们的"巧克力纪念日"是一回事，可忘掉订婚就太离谱了。"你感觉还好吗？"她问，焦虑感不断攀升。"呃，安娜？"奥拉夫拽了拽她的袖子。"我不大情愿报忧，可今天健忘的不止他一个。

事实上，这好像扩散到了全镇。"安娜感到胃里一阵翻腾。

环顾四周，她忽然意识到四周异样地安静。

大家本该都在筹备极夜节，可人们却像梦游般晃荡。

仿佛忘了自己该干什么。

本该设计节庆横幅的村庄画师格雷琴，正站在一块空白画布前，手里的笔上却没蘸颜料。

冰雕师赫尔穆特坐在实心冰块上，居然用冰镐剔牙！

安娜瞅见面包师，急忙上前。"嗨，布……

洛杰特太太！"她察觉自己跟这位老妇打招呼时，声音里也许多了一丁点过分的热情。"只是来问问情况！"她压低声音说。"克斯托夫的周年纪念巧克力模具做得怎么样了？"布……

洛杰特太太眨眨眼。"克斯托夫的什么？""巧克力周年礼物，"安娜说，不安感更重了。"你接了我的特别订单啊。""我不记得有什么特别订单，"布……

洛杰特太太答道。"不过你有什么需要，我都很乐意帮忙。"安娜的心在胸腔里狂跳。

她转身离开布……

洛杰特太太，看到旁边的华夫兄弟俩站着，这一回竟没吵架。

这本身就很怪。"嗨，伙计们！"她打招呼，声音这会儿有点尖了。"你们呢？

你们那有名的烘焙大赛准备好了吗？"兄弟俩茫然地对视。"烘焙大赛？

我不记得报名参加过烘焙大赛，"比约恩说。"你们本来要互相比赛，看谁做的华夫饼更好，"安娜提示。"你们做华夫饼？"比亚内问弟弟。

比约恩耸耸肩，咬了一口华夫饼。

安娜懊恼地哼了一声。"整个早上都这样，"奥拉夫紧张地说。"唱诗班记不住歌词，做派的人忘了烤派皮，蜡烛店找不到蜡了。""你是说真的？"安娜问。

这情况越来越糟了。

她靠在灯柱上，觉得世界正失控旋转。"亡灵，"她低声说。"这一切一定都是亡灵搞的。"她闭眼片刻，脑中响起那怪物的呻吟。

妹——妹——啊。"它昨晚一定来过这里，偷走了所有人的记忆。"她把眼睛闭得更紧。"我该怎么办？""你可以试着阻止它？"奥拉夫兴致勃勃地建议。"我是说，随便想想！""可怎么阻止？""在营火边，你提过在父母秘密藏书室里找到一本关于亡灵的书，"奥拉夫提醒她。

显然，他没像其他人那样记忆丧失。"你可以从那儿着手。"当然！

安娜用手拍了下额头。

这才是她当初回阿伦黛尔的原因！

来研究亡灵！

她全忘了。

又忘了。

哦，天哪。"奥拉夫，我们得马上找到那本书！"安娜喊道，一把抓住奥拉夫和克斯托夫的手，生怕弄丢。

她拉着他俩朝城堡走，又停住了。

有件事她得先办。

安娜暂时松开克斯托夫的手，从旁边的桌上抓过一张纸和一支铅笔，匆匆写了张便条。

然后她把纸举向空中。"风灵？"她唤道，然后等待。

无论她召唤时风灵在何处，它似乎总回应得很快，这次也不例外。

风灵呼啸着穿过街道，连同还没挂起的节庆装饰一起吹得飞扬。

安娜让便条随风飘去。"找到我妹妹，尽快把她带回阿伦黛尔！"

sentences.en: HORSES ARE LOYAL CREATURES, Anna thought as Elsa returned to the hut the next morning with Anna’s beloved horse at her side. “Havski!” Anna cried, hobbling toward him.
sentences.zh: 马真是忠诚的动物，安娜想。第二天清晨，艾莎回到小屋，身边正是安娜心爱的马。"哈夫斯基！"安娜喊着，一瘸一拐地朝它走去。

sentences.en: Her ankle felt much better than it had the day before, but there was no way she could have walked all the way back to Arendelle on it.
sentences.zh: 她的脚踝比昨天好多了，但靠它一路走回阿伦黛尔是绝无可能的。

sentences.en: If Elsa hadn’t located Havski, what would she have done?
sentences.zh: 如果艾莎没找到哈夫斯基，她可怎么办？

sentences.en: She imagined her sister creating a toboggan out of ice for her or calling on the ice creature Marshmallow to leave his cozy castle at the top of the North Mountain to carry her back.
sentences.zh: 她想象妹妹用冰给她做了个雪橇，或者召唤那个叫"棉花糖"的冰怪，离开北山顶上温暖的城堡来驮她回去。

sentences.en: Wouldn’t that have been a sight—her sitting in Marshmallow’s palm as she approached the village?
sentences.zh: 那场面一定很壮观——她坐在棉花糖的手掌里，朝村庄走去？

sentences.en: Talk about making an entrance! “I’m so glad Elsa found you, boy,” said Anna as she moved to touch Havski’s head, and he twitched.
sentences.zh: 那才叫隆重登场！"我真高兴艾莎找到了你，伙计，"安娜说着伸手去摸哈夫斯基的头，它抖了一下。

sentences.en: That was odd, but now that she looked at the horse closer, she realized his whole body was shaking. “Is he okay?” Anna asked. “I found him wandering around the pasture trying to find you,” Elsa said. “He’s dry, though, so he must have found shelter overnight.” Elsa stroked his long black mane. “Poor guy.
sentences.zh: 真奇怪，可当她再仔细打量这匹马，才发现它全身都在发抖。"它没事吧？"安娜问。"我发现它在牧场里转悠，想找你，"艾莎说。"不过它是干的，所以昨晚一定找到了避身之处。"艾莎抚摸着它长长的黑鬃。"可怜的家伙。

sentences.en: He must have been so scared when he saw the draugr.” “It’s okay, Havski,” Anna said soothingly, petting his pale gray hide. “We’re safe now, and we’re going home to Arendelle to…” That was funny.
sentences.zh: 它看见亡灵时一定吓坏了。""没事的，哈夫斯基，"安娜温柔地安抚，轻拍它浅灰色的皮毛。"我们现在安全了，要回阿伦黛尔家了，去……"真有意思。

sentences.en: There was something she had to do in the village, but for the life of her, she suddenly couldn’t remember what it was.
sentences.zh: 村子里有件事她必须去做，可她死活忽然想不起那是什么了。

sentences.en: Anna looked at Elsa, who was watching her closely and frowning. “To check on the people and see what you can find out about the draugr before it returns,” Elsa prompted her.
sentences.zh: 安娜望向艾莎，艾莎正紧盯着她，皱着眉。"去探望大家，趁着亡灵回来前，看看能查出关于它的什么，"艾莎提示她。

sentences.en: She placed a cool hand on her sister’s cheek. “Anna, you do remember that’s what we discussed last night, don’t you?” As soon as Elsa touched her, Anna felt what resembled a whooshing sensation through her brain.
sentences.zh: 她把一只冰凉的手贴在妹妹脸颊上。"安娜，你记得这是我们昨晚商量好的吧，对不对？"艾莎一碰到她，安娜脑中便感到一阵类似嗖然掠过的感觉。

sentences.en: The memory was back!
sentences.zh: 记忆回来了！

sentences.en: Anna was headed home to do research on draugrs in their parents’ library, and Elsa was going to Ahtohallan. “Of course!” she declared with a shake of her head.
sentences.zh: 安娜正要回家，去父母的藏书室研究亡灵，而艾莎要去阿托哈兰。"当然！"她摇着头宣称。

sentences.en: Her copper-colored locks waved side to side. “Sorry!
sentences.zh: 她铜色的发丝左右晃动。"抱歉！

sentences.en: You know my brain after a bad night’s sleep!” “Speaking of night…” Elsa looked up at the sky, her brow creasing in worry.
sentences.zh: 你又不是不知道，我睡不好觉时脑子就……！""说到夜晚……"艾莎抬头望天，眉头担忧地皱起。

sentences.en: While they both knew it was morning, the dawn hadn’t come.
sentences.zh: 她们明知已是清晨，黎明却没到来。

sentences.en: Instead, for the second day in a row, the world was awash in a darkness that didn’t feel like night or day.
sentences.zh: 相反，连续第二天，世界浸在一片不分昼夜的黑暗里。

sentences.en: There was no sun or moon in sight.
sentences.zh: 看不见太阳，也看不见月亮。

sentences.en: The air was thick and the world quiet, as if it were just waiting for disaster to strike.
sentences.zh: 空气凝重，世界寂静，仿佛只是在等待灾难降临。

sentences.en: Even the birds and woodland creatures seemed to have gone into hiding.
sentences.zh: 连鸟儿和林中走兽似乎都躲了起来。

sentences.en: Anna suddenly found herself longing for the beautiful twilight of the Polar Nights.
sentences.zh: 安娜忽然发现自己想念极夜那美丽的暮光了。

sentences.en: Maybe this was why Havski seemed unnerved, too.
sentences.zh: 也许这正是哈夫斯基也显得不安的原因。

sentences.en: Something was clearly wrong.
sentences.zh: 显然有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: Days were always shorter leading up to the Polar Nights, and snow was common, but this weather was…different.
sentences.zh: 极夜将至时白昼总会变短，下雪也常见，但这天气……不一样。

sentences.en: Anna just wished she knew for certain whether this was the draugr’s doing, and longed to know how to make it go away. “The sooner we figure out what’s really going on, the better,” Elsa said, seeming to hear her sister’s thoughts as she guided Anna to Havski before helping her up. “I’ll be back from Ahtohallan as soon as I can.
sentences.zh: 安娜只希望自己能确定这是不是亡灵的杰作，也渴望知道怎么让它消失。"我们越早弄清到底怎么回事越好，"艾莎说，仿佛听见了妹妹的心声，她扶安娜到哈夫斯基身边，帮她上马。"我会尽快从阿托哈兰回来。

sentences.en: Then we can decide the best way to handle this.” “Handle this,” Anna repeated.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就能决定对付它的最佳办法。""对付它，"安娜重复道。

sentences.en: Handle what? she wondered, and then she remembered.
sentences.zh: 对付什么？她纳闷，接着想起来了。

sentences.en: The draugr!
sentences.zh: 亡灵！

sentences.en: The books in the library!
sentences.zh: 藏书室里的书！

sentences.en: Whether the draugr is Sissel!
sentences.zh: 亡灵到底是不是西塞尔！

sentences.en: Right!
sentences.zh: 对！

sentences.en: Why was she suddenly so forgetful?
sentences.zh: 她怎么突然这么健忘了？

sentences.en: She didn’t want to worry Elsa any more than she had already, so she said nothing about having another foggy moment.
sentences.zh: 她不想让艾莎比现在更担心，所以对自己的又一次神思恍惚只字未提。

sentences.en: Instead, she pulled on Havski’s reins. “I’ll see you soon.
sentences.zh: 相反，她拉起哈夫斯基的缰绳。"我们很快见。

sentences.en: Be careful.” Elsa smiled at her, then whistled for her own steed.
sentences.zh: 保重。"艾莎对她笑笑，然后为自己坐骑吹了声口哨。

sentences.en: The Water Nokk burst through the trees, its crystallized mane casting an array of rainbows across the ground as it raced toward them.
sentences.zh: 水马从林间冲出，晶化的鬃毛在地上投下一串彩虹，朝她们疾驰而来。

sentences.en: Anna watched as Elsa threw her leg over the Water Nokk’s back, hoisting herself up.
sentences.zh: 安娜看着艾莎把腿跨上水马背，纵身坐稳。

sentences.en: Anna wondered, not for the first time, what it must be like to ride bareback on such a wild creature.
sentences.zh: 安娜不止一次地猜想，骑在这样野性的生灵上、毫无鞍具，会是何种滋味。

sentences.en: Elsa always made it look magical and super comfy, of course. “Love you!” Elsa smiled at her sister. “See you soon!” “Love you, too!” Anna called after her as the Water Nokk turned and headed into the forest.
sentences.zh: 当然，艾莎总让它看起来既神奇又超级舒服。"爱你！"艾莎冲妹妹微笑。"很快见！""我也爱你！"水马转身朝森林而去，安娜在身后喊道。

sentences.en: Anna watched her sister go, sending out a silent wish for her safety.
sentences.zh: 安娜目送妹妹离去，在心中默默为她祈愿平安。

sentences.en: She hadn’t wanted to admit it to Elsa, but she was still shaken by their encounter with the monster the night before.
sentences.zh: 她不愿向艾莎承认，可昨晚与那怪物的遭遇仍让她心有余悸。

sentences.en: If Elsa hadn’t freed her, what would the “D-word” (Anna had decided not to take any chances by saying the creature’s full name anymore, just in case!) have done to her?
sentences.zh: 若不是艾莎把她救出，那个"D字怪物"（安娜决定为防万一，再也不冒风险说出那怪物的全名了！）会对她做什么？

sentences.en: She shook her head, urging Havski on.
sentences.zh: 她摇摇头，催哈夫斯基前行。

sentences.en: No use thinking about what could have happened, she scolded herself.
sentences.zh: 想那些可能发生的万一毫无用处，她责怪自己。

sentences.en: She needed to get back to Arendelle—before something actually did happen.
sentences.zh: 她得赶回阿伦黛尔——趁真正出事之前。

sentences.en: Once she reached the village, it took all of Anna’s strength not to start screaming and waving people down yelling, “Draugr danger!” But she didn’t want to terrify everyone.
sentences.zh: 一到村庄，安娜使出浑身力气才忍住不扯开嗓子、拦住路人喊"亡灵危险！"可她不想吓坏所有人。

sentences.en: She had to act like a queen, and a queen would remain calm and sound rational.
sentences.zh: 她得像个女王，而女王会保持冷静、言语理性。

sentences.en: So Anna took a deep breath, deciding she would act firm and direct, and not out of sorts—like she actually was.
sentences.zh: 于是安娜深吸一口气，决定表现得坚定而直接，而不是像她实际那样、六神无主。

sentences.en: It was then she spotted Kristoff, wandering through the town square. “I’m so glad you’re here,” she said, out of breath. “What’s going on?” Kristoff asked as he reached up to lift Anna off the horse.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，她瞥见克斯托夫在城镇广场上游荡。"真高兴你在这儿，"她上气不接下气地说。"怎么回事？"克斯托夫伸手把安娜从马上抱下时问道。

sentences.en: He helped her down and wrapped his strong arms tightly around her. “Everything okay?” “We have a situation.
sentences.zh: 他扶她下来，用健壮的双臂紧紧搂住她。"都好吗？""我们有状况了。

sentences.en: I don’t want you to panic.” Even if I’m panicking, she thought.
sentences.zh: 我不想你惊慌。"尽管我自己就在慌，她想。

sentences.en: She glanced around at the square, half expecting to see the draugr lurking in the shadows or behind her parents’ statue.
sentences.zh: 她环顾广场，半以为会看见亡灵潜伏在暗处或父母雕像背后。

sentences.en: But no, everything seemed calm.
sentences.zh: 但是没有，一切似乎平静。

sentences.en: Normal. “I’ve learned not to panic till Elsa sends up snow signals,” Kristoff joked. “This is serious,” she said, lowering her voice. “We need to warn the village about an impending attack…from a draugr.” She held her breath, half thinking Kristoff would laugh at her and say she was being as ridiculous as Olaf.
sentences.zh: 正常。"我学乖了，在艾莎发出雪信号前绝不惊慌，"克斯托夫开玩笑。"这很严重，"她压低声音说。"我们得警告全村，一场袭击即将来临……来自一个亡灵。"她屏住呼吸，半以为克斯托夫会笑她，说她跟奥拉夫一样荒唐。

sentences.en: Instead, Kristoff’s eyes widened, and she felt his body tighten. “A draugr?
sentences.zh: 谁知克斯托夫眼睛瞪大，她感到他身体绷紧了。"一个亡灵？

sentences.en: Are you serious?” “Unfortunately, yes.
sentences.zh: 你是说真的？""不幸的是，真的。

sentences.en: It came out of nowhere when Elsa and I were coming back from Sorenson’s.
sentences.zh: 它从天而降，当时我和艾莎正从索伦森那儿回来。

sentences.en: Let’s just say we’re lucky to be alive.” She shivered a little, her mind flashing back to the night before, being trapped by those tree roots.
sentences.zh: 咱们能活下来算是走运。"她微微一颤，脑中闪回前一晚被那些树根困住的情景。

sentences.en: The draugr coming closer and closer… “You saw Sinister Sissel?” Olaf cried out, bounding up beside them. “Did she try to eat you?
sentences.zh: 亡灵越逼越近……"你们见到"阴森的西塞尔"了？"奥拉夫蹦到他们身旁喊道。"她想吃掉你们吗？

sentences.en: Did she try to turn you into a draugr, too?” He narrowed his eyes at her, as if trying to determine if she’d been draugrized somehow. “Are you okay, Anna?
sentences.zh: 她也想把你们变成亡灵吗？"他眯起眼睛盯着她，像在判断她是否被"亡灵化"了。"你还好吗，安娜？

sentences.en: You can tell me if you’re feeling at all monster-y.
sentences.zh: 你要是觉得自己有半点像怪物，可以告诉我。

sentences.en: I won’t judge, I swear!” “I’m fine,” Anna insisted.
sentences.zh: 我绝不评判，我发誓！""我没事，"安娜坚持说。

sentences.en: For now, she thought. “Look, Olaf, I’m sorry I didn’t believe you at first, but I think you might be right.
sentences.zh: 眼下没事，她想。"听着，奥拉夫，抱歉我起初不信你，但我想你也许是对的。

sentences.en: The draugr has to be Sissel—and I think it’s behind all the weird weather we’ve been having.” “I knew it!” Olaf cried, pacing from side to side. “She heard us talking about her at the campfire and now she’s come to attack us all.
sentences.zh: 这亡灵一定是西塞尔——而且我想，我们这段怪天气都是它搞的鬼。""我就知道！"奥拉夫喊着，来回踱步。"她在营火边听见我们谈论她，现在就来袭击我们所有人了。

sentences.en: Or at least steal our cheese.
sentences.zh: 或者至少偷我们的奶酪。

sentences.en: And slippers.
sentences.zh: 还有拖鞋。

sentences.en: And possibly our souls.” He stared up at the dark sky, opening his mouth and wailing, “Why, Sissel, why?” “Okay, wait a second.
sentences.zh: 可能还有我们的灵魂。"他抬头盯着黑漆漆的天空，张嘴哀嚎："为什么啊，西塞尔，为什么？""好了，等一下。

sentences.en: Who is this Sissel again?
sentences.zh: 这个西塞尔到底是谁？

sentences.en: And why does she want to harm us?” Kristoff asked, looking oddly confused.
sentences.zh: 她为什么要害我们？"克斯托夫问，神情诡异地困惑。

sentences.en: Anna did a double take.
sentences.zh: 安娜愣了一下，又看了一眼。

sentences.en: Had Kristoff just asked who Sissel was?
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫刚才是在问西塞尔是谁？

sentences.en: He was the one who had told them about her to begin with!
sentences.zh: 可最初把她的故事讲给他们听的，正是他啊！

sentences.en: And now he was acting like he didn’t remember her at all!
sentences.zh: 而现在他却表现得像完全不记得她了！

sentences.en: Which was beyond bizarre, considering Kristoff never forgot a thing—even if at times, she wished he would.
sentences.zh: 这太离谱了，毕竟克斯托夫从不忘事——哪怕有时她倒希望他忘。

sentences.en: (Telling him she liked his fish soup was a decision that still haunted her.) This didn’t make any sense.
sentences.zh: （告诉他喜欢他的鱼汤，这个决定至今让她后悔。）这根本说不通。

sentences.en: Unless… She inhaled sharply as a horrible thought suddenly crossed her mind: could this, too, have something to do with the draugr?
sentences.zh: 除非……她猛吸一口气，一个可怕的念头突然闪过脑海：这会不会也和亡灵有关？

sentences.en: Could the draugr—or Sissel—be making them both suddenly so forgetful?
sentences.zh: 亡灵——或者说西塞尔——会不会让他们俩都突然变得这么健忘？

sentences.en: There was only one way to find out. “Quick question,” she said to Kristoff. “What very important date for us is coming up?” Kristoff looked baffled. “Date?” Olaf slid in next to him. “Just to be clear: there’s several.” “Several?” Kristoff parroted.
sentences.zh: 只有一个办法能弄清。"问个问题，"她对克斯托夫说。"对我们来说，即将到来的一个非常重要的日子是什么？"克斯托夫一脸茫然。"日子？"奥拉夫溜到他身旁。"说清楚点：有好几个呢。""好几个？"克斯托夫鹦鹉学舌。

sentences.en: Anna felt her hands turn clammy. “Having to do with chocolate?” she prompted. “And the fact you’re getting married,” Olaf added. “But no one actually knows when yet.
sentences.zh: 安娜感到手心冒汗。"和巧克力有关的？"她提示。"还有你们要结婚这件事，"奥拉夫补充。"但还没人真知道具体日子呢。

sentences.en: You’ve only been engaged for like a minute.” “Engaged?” Kristoff, looking lost, blinked rapidly.
sentences.zh: 你们才订婚了一小会儿。""订婚？"克斯托夫一脸茫然，飞快地眨着眼。

sentences.en: Anna felt her heart drop.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心一沉。

sentences.en: Forgetting their Choco-versary was one thing, but their engagement was implausible. “Are you feeling okay?” she asked, feeling her anxiety increase. “Um, Anna?” Olaf tugged on her sleeve. “I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but he’s not the only one acting forgetful today.
sentences.zh: 忘了他们的"巧克力纪念日"是一回事，可忘掉订婚就太离谱了。"你感觉还好吗？"她问，焦虑感不断攀升。"呃，安娜？"奥拉夫拽了拽她的袖子。"我不大情愿报忧，可今天健忘的不止他一个。

sentences.en: In fact, it’s kind of spread to the whole town.” Anna felt her stomach begin to turn.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这好像扩散到了全镇。"安娜感到胃里一阵翻腾。

sentences.en: Looking around, it suddenly occurred to her that things were unusually quiet.
sentences.zh: 环顾四周，她忽然意识到四周异样地安静。

sentences.en: Everyone was supposed to be working on the Polar Nights festival, yet people seemed to be moving around in a daze.
sentences.zh: 大家本该都在筹备极夜节，可人们却像梦游般晃荡。

sentences.en: As if they’d forgotten what they were supposed to be doing.
sentences.zh: 仿佛忘了自己该干什么。

sentences.en: Gretchen, the village painter who was meant to be designing the festival banner, was standing in front of a blank canvas with a brush that had no paint on it.
sentences.zh: 本该设计节庆横幅的村庄画师格雷琴，正站在一块空白画布前，手里的笔上却没蘸颜料。

sentences.en: Helmut the ice carver was sitting on a solid block of ice, using his ice pick on his teeth!
sentences.zh: 冰雕师赫尔穆特坐在实心冰块上，居然用冰镐剔牙！

sentences.en: Anna spotted the baker and hurried over to her. “Hi, Mrs.
sentences.zh: 安娜瞅见面包师，急忙上前。"嗨，布……

sentences.en: Blodget!” She sensed she had greeted the older woman with maybe just a little too much cheeriness in her voice. “Just checking in!” she whispered. “How is Kristoff’s anniversary chocolate mold coming?” Mrs.
sentences.zh: 洛杰特太太！"她察觉自己跟这位老妇打招呼时，声音里也许多了一丁点过分的热情。"只是来问问情况！"她压低声音说。"克斯托夫的周年纪念巧克力模具做得怎么样了？"布……

sentences.en: Blodget blinked. “Kristoff’s what?” “Chocolate anniversary gift,” Anna said, her uneasy feeling worsening. “You were doing a special order just for me.” “I don’t remember any special orders,” Mrs.
sentences.zh: 洛杰特太太眨眨眼。"克斯托夫的什么？""巧克力周年礼物，"安娜说，不安感更重了。"你接了我的特别订单啊。""我不记得有什么特别订单，"布……

sentences.en: Blodget responded. “But I’m happy to help you with whatever you need.” Anna’s heart beat fast in her chest.
sentences.zh: 洛杰特太太答道。"不过你有什么需要，我都很乐意帮忙。"安娜的心在胸腔里狂跳。

sentences.en: She turned from Mrs.
sentences.zh: 她转身离开布……

sentences.en: Blodget to see the two Waffle Brothers standing nearby, not arguing for once.
sentences.zh: 洛杰特太太，看到旁边的华夫兄弟俩站着，这一回竟没吵架。

sentences.en: Which was weird in and of itself. “Hi, guys!” she greeted, her voice now a bit shrill. “What about you?
sentences.zh: 这本身就很怪。"嗨，伙计们！"她打招呼，声音这会儿有点尖了。"你们呢？

sentences.en: Are you ready for your famous bake-off?” The brothers looked at one another blankly. “Bake-off?
sentences.zh: 你们那有名的烘焙大赛准备好了吗？"兄弟俩茫然地对视。"烘焙大赛？

sentences.en: I don’t remember signing up for a bake-off,” said Bjorn. “You were going to compete with each other to see who made the better waffle,” Anna prompted. “You make waffles?” Bjarne asked his brother.
sentences.zh: 我不记得报名参加过烘焙大赛，"比约恩说。"你们本来要互相比赛，看谁做的华夫饼更好，"安娜提示。"你们做华夫饼？"比亚内问弟弟。

sentences.en: Bjorn shrugged, taking a bite of a waffle.
sentences.zh: 比约恩耸耸肩，咬了一口华夫饼。

sentences.en: Anna groaned in frustration. “It’s been like this all morning,” Olaf said nervously. “The choir couldn’t remember the lyrics to their songs, the pie maker forgot to bake his piecrusts, and the candle shop couldn’t find their wax.” “Are you serious?” Anna asked.
sentences.zh: 安娜懊恼地哼了一声。"整个早上都这样，"奥拉夫紧张地说。"唱诗班记不住歌词，做派的人忘了烤派皮，蜡烛店找不到蜡了。""你是说真的？"安娜问。

sentences.en: This was getting worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 这情况越来越糟了。

sentences.en: She leaned against a lamppost, feeling like the world was spinning out of control. “The draugr,” she whispered. “This all has to be from the draugr.” She closed her eyes for a moment, hearing the creature’s moan in her mind.
sentences.zh: 她靠在灯柱上，觉得世界正失控旋转。"亡灵，"她低声说。"这一切一定都是亡灵搞的。"她闭眼片刻，脑中响起那怪物的呻吟。

sentences.en: Sissssttterrrr. “It must have come here last night and stolen everyone’s memories.” She squeezed her eyes shut even tighter. “What am I going to do?” “You could try to stop it?” Olaf suggested brightly. “I mean, just a thought!” “But how?” “At the campfire, you mentioned a book about draugrs you found in your parents’ secret library,” Olaf reminded her.
sentences.zh: 妹——妹——啊。"它昨晚一定来过这里，偷走了所有人的记忆。"她把眼睛闭得更紧。"我该怎么办？""你可以试着阻止它？"奥拉夫兴致勃勃地建议。"我是说，随便想想！""可怎么阻止？""在营火边，你提过在父母秘密藏书室里找到一本关于亡灵的书，"奥拉夫提醒她。

sentences.en: Clearly, he wasn’t suffering from the same memory loss the rest of them were experiencing. “You might start there.” Of course!
sentences.zh: 显然，他没像其他人那样记忆丧失。"你可以从那儿着手。"当然！

sentences.en: Anna smacked her forehead with her hand.
sentences.zh: 安娜用手拍了下额头。

sentences.en: That was why she’d come back to Arendelle to begin with!
sentences.zh: 这才是她当初回阿伦黛尔的原因！

sentences.en: To research draugrs!
sentences.zh: 来研究亡灵！

sentences.en: She’d totally forgotten.
sentences.zh: 她全忘了。

sentences.en: Again.
sentences.zh: 又忘了。

sentences.en: Oh, dear. “Olaf, we need to find that book right away!” Anna cried, grabbing both his hand and Kristoff’s for safekeeping.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。"奥拉夫，我们得马上找到那本书！"安娜喊道，一把抓住奥拉夫和克斯托夫的手，生怕弄丢。

sentences.en: She started to pull them toward the castle, then stopped.
sentences.zh: 她拉着他俩朝城堡走，又停住了。

sentences.en: There was one thing she had to do first.
sentences.zh: 有件事她得先办。

sentences.en: Anna let go of Kristoff’s hand temporarily, grabbed a piece of paper and a pencil off a nearby table, and scribbled a quick note.
sentences.zh: 安娜暂时松开克斯托夫的手，从旁边的桌上抓过一张纸和一支铅笔，匆匆写了张便条。

sentences.en: Then she held it up in the air. “Gale?” she called out, and then waited.
sentences.zh: 然后她把纸举向空中。"风灵？"她唤道，然后等待。

sentences.en: No matter where the Wind Spirit was when she called, it always seemed to respond quickly, and this time was no different.
sentences.zh: 无论她召唤时风灵在何处，它似乎总回应得很快，这次也不例外。

sentences.en: Gale whisked through the street, blowing unhung decorations for the festival along with it.
sentences.zh: 风灵呼啸着穿过街道，连同还没挂起的节庆装饰一起吹得飞扬。

sentences.en: Anna let the note ride on the wind. “Find my sister and get her back to Arendelle as fast as you can!”
sentences.zh: 安娜让便条随风飘去。"找到我妹妹，尽快把她带回阿伦黛尔！"

chapters.title: Chapter Nine: Elsa
chapters.en:
“AH, AH, AH, AH…”

Elsa couldn’t help singing as she and the Water Nokk approached Ahtohallan. It was her version of greeting the Mother Spirit embodied in the glacier. Ahtohallan had become like a second home to her over the last two months. Well, not a home, exactly. But a place of peace. Just being there centered her somehow. She found the icy surroundings comforting. It didn’t really make any sense when she tried to explain it to her sister. But Anna was always so supportive and understanding—even when she didn’t quite get it. It was a sister thing, she surmised.

She wished she could take Anna here. But there was no way to cross the Dark Sea without the Water Nokk, and the spirit had a mind of its own. Which was why Elsa was working so hard to bring the memories home to share with her sister. So Anna could catch just a glimpse of the mysteries revealed here in this fortress of ice.

Because, oh, she’d seen so much in her short time here. She’d gone deep, as deep as she dared, watching her family’s history unfold in front of her eyes. Seeing her mother save her father’s life in the Enchanted Forest. Watching them grow up together, become friends, fall in love. Witness the pain her mother had gone through keeping the secret that she was Northuldra. Elsa knew all too well about keeping secrets.

And then there were the moments that were harder to watch. The fear in her father’s eyes as he witnessed young Elsa’s magic grow. He loved her so much—he tried his best—but he had also grown up with secrets. And he, too, had learned to adhere to the horrific mantra, “Conceal, don’t feel.” He’d passed that on to her, thinking he was doing the best thing he could to help her keep the kingdom. Would he have approved if he knew she’d given it all to Anna in the end after all? Deep down, she believed he would. He would have done anything to keep his girls safe and happy.

And she was happy, she thought, as she slid off the Water Spirit and stepped up to the icy entrance. She was living free in the Enchanted Forest, no longer imprisoned by her guilt and fear. She now had everything she had never known she wanted—needed. She had peace. She had power.

And yet she still had her sister. And Arendelle.

Elsa was blown away by how gracious the kingdom had been the day she gave up her throne. She thought they’d be furious with her. She thought they’d believe she was abandoning them. But no—they understood that she needed this. That she had given them everything she could over the past three years. And now it was time for her to give herself something, too. Something she desperately needed to become the best version of herself. And so, when she had stood on that dais in front of all of Arendelle—and the cheers and shouts of encouragement rose to her ears—she felt tears of gratitude slip down her cheeks. They truly loved her; not just as their queen, but as a person—a citizen of Arendelle!

They were willing to let her go, and because of that she would never truly leave them.

Elsa’s steps quickened as she raced down the icy path, deeper into Ahtohallan. The walls shimmered in their greeting to her, flickering with images of her mother smiling down at her as she ran. Ahtohallan was a mother herself—the mother of all the other spirits. And she often embodied echoes of Elsa’s own mother, Queen Iduna, to give Elsa a friendly face to come home to. And while Elsa knew it was not really her mother in those icy ripples on the wall—her mother was long gone—she still couldn’t keep her heart from swelling with love as she gazed upon the vision of the woman who had given birth to her. Who had loved her unconditionally. Who had believed her powers to be a gift, not a curse. Who had sacrificed her life to try to save her.

At last Elsa stepped into the cavernous heart of the glacier. The icy walls stretched tall above her, as far as her eyes could see, reflecting memories that danced on their surfaces. Ahtohallan was the keeper of memories. And memories were knowledge. There was so much knowledge bursting within these walls—more than any mere library could possibly hold. Surely, she could find something to help with their current situation. The strange darkness, the storms, the draugr that had attacked Anna. And then there were her powers, which had seemed to fizzle out for no reason as she’d attempted to pull a memory up for her sister.

No. Elsa shook her head, her white-blond hair shimmering under the icy lights. No, it wasn’t just that they fizzled out.

It was as if she’d forgotten the memory altogether.

Just like everyone else had been forgetting things. She thought back to the night by the campfire. Kristoff had watched his tent go down—and then seemed to forget all about it a moment later. And then there was the next night in the shepherd’s hut, right after the draugr encounter. Anna had been so excited about seeing Elsa’s memory—but then seemed to lose all interest. And the next morning she hadn’t remembered anything they’d talked about doing.

But was it simply forgetfulness? Or was the loss of memory connected to the draugr somehow? Was Anna’s hunch correct? Was the draugr Sissel, reawakened by Kristoff’s story on the anniversary of her death?

Elsa pressed a hand against the cold wall of ice, trying to concentrate. Trying again to find that memory she’d wanted to share with Anna, of her father and mother laughing and dancing in the ballroom. She’d pulled it up a hundred times before—it was one of her favorites.

But this time, it didn’t materialize.

“What’s wrong?” she whispered, though she knew the glacier couldn’t answer. “Where’s the memory? Why can’t I access it?”

A taste of dread rose in her throat. What was going on here? And was it connected somehow to everything else? After all, it was one thing for Kristoff or Anna to start forgetting things. But quite another for the very literal glacier of memories. Heart beating fast, Elsa pressed her other hand against the icy wall, drawing in a deep but shaky breath.

“Just try something else,” she told herself. “Father under his favorite tree. Mother popping down from the branches, upside down and surprising him.” Another favorite. One she’d pulled up many times before.

For a moment, she thought she saw something. A flicker in the ice, the beginnings of a memory forming. But then it fizzled out as it had in the shepherd’s hut. The ice swirled, then grew dark again.

The memory was gone. As if it had been stolen away from her.

But just as she began to despair, the walls of Ahtohallan suddenly seemed to brighten and shimmer. A gray mist began to rise into the air. A moment later, sculptures made of ice solidified in front of her. But they were not of her mother or her father and their favorite tree. Rather, they were two girls—around Anna and Elsa’s age—wearing clothing that looked old-fashioned. As Elsa watched, the ice began to shift, expand, revealing their location. They were standing on a riverbank.

And they were arguing bitterly.

Elsa gaped. Could it be…? Her mind flashed back to Kristoff’s story of the Vesterland sisters.

One day, Inger got her wish. While on a trip to Arendelle, she caught her sister standing by the rushing river—alone.

“What is this?” she whispered, fear crawling down her spine. Half of her wanted to look away. To turn and flee the glacier altogether and never look back. But instead, something compelled her to stay as the memory swirled and the ice sculptures seemed to come to life. The river rising. Raging. One of the girls being swept away in its vicious current, thrashing in the water, screaming for help.

“INGER!” The words seemed to echo through the icy walls. “Inger—help me!” The vision swirled again, now focusing on the second girl. She was on her knees by the riverbank, her eyes flowing with tears.

“Sissel,” she croaked. “I’m so sorry, Sissel!”

The vision froze; the moving figures were now just statues in the ice. Elsa dropped to her own knees, overwhelmed by what she’d just seen. It was one thing to hear about what happened long ago. But it was quite another to see Sissel thrashing in the rough waters, begging her sister for help while Inger was motionless on the riverbank, clearly filled with remorse for her evil deed.

Elsa didn’t feel sorry for her, though. She deserved all she had gotten and more. But poor Sissel! Elsa couldn’t imagine what must have gone through her mind in those last seconds. The realization that her own sister had hated her enough—had been jealous enough—to do such a thing.

Suddenly she felt a gust of wind behind her. She whirled around, surprised to find Gale swooping into the glacier, a piece of mail in its breeze. She plucked the letter from the Wind Spirit and opened it, her hands still trembling from all she’d seen.

It was from Anna.

Something is very wrong in Arendelle. You need to come back—as soon as possible—before it’s too late!
chapters.zh:
“啊，啊，啊，啊……”艾莎忍不住唱了起来，她和“水马”正逼近阿托哈兰。

这是她向这座冰川中蕴含的“母亲之灵”致意的方式。

在过去的两个月里，阿托哈兰对她来说已经像个第二个家了。

嗯，严格来说，也不算家。

但它是个安宁的地方。

只要待在那里，她莫名就感到心定。

她觉得冰天雪地的环境让人安心。

当她试着向妹妹解释时，这其实说不太通。

但安娜总是那么支持她、理解她——即便她并不是完全懂。

她琢磨着，这大概就是姐妹之间的事吧。

她真希望能带安娜来这里。

但若没有“水马”，根本无法穿越暗海，而那灵性自有主张。

所以艾莎才这么努力地把记忆带回去，和妹妹分享。

好让安娜也能瞥见这座冰之堡垒中显现的奥秘。

因为，噢，她在这短暂时光里看到的太多了。

她潜得很深，深到敢去的极限，亲眼看着家族的历史在眼前展开。

看着母亲在魔法森林里救下父亲的性命。

看着他们一起长大、成为朋友、坠入爱河。

目睹母亲守着自己是北地人的秘密时所经历的痛苦。

艾莎太清楚保守秘密是什么滋味了。

还有那些更难直视的时刻。

父亲看着年幼的艾莎魔力滋长时，眼中的恐惧。

他那么爱她——已尽了全力——可他也是在秘密中长大的。

他也学会了恪守那可怕的箴言：“藏起来，别去感受。”他把它传给了她，以为这是在用最好的办法帮她守住王国。

如果他知道她最终还是把一切都交给了安娜，他会赞同吗？

在内心深处，她相信他会。

为了保护两个女儿平安喜乐，他什么都愿意做。

而她是快乐的，她想着，一边从“水之灵”背上滑下，踏上冰封的入口。

她自由地生活在魔法森林里，不再被愧疚与恐惧囚禁。

她如今拥有了从未知道自己渴望——需要——的一切。

她拥有安宁。

她拥有力量。

而她依然拥有妹妹。

还有阿伦黛尔。

让艾莎震惊的是，在她退位那天，王国竟是如此宽厚。

她原以为他们会愤怒。

她原以为他们会觉得她抛弃了他们。

可没有——他们理解，她需要这样。

理解她过去三年已倾尽所有给了他们。

而如今，也该轮到她为自己做点什么了。

做点她极度需要、以成就最好自己的事。

于是，当她站在阿伦黛尔众人面前的高台上——欢呼声与鼓励的呐喊传入耳中——她感到感激的泪水滑落脸颊。

他们真的爱她；不只是爱她作为女王，更爱她这个人——阿伦黛尔的一位子民！

他们愿意放她走，正因如此，她永远不会真正离开他们。

艾莎脚步加快，沿着冰路奔向阿托哈兰的更深处。

冰壁闪烁着向她致意，映出母亲奔跑时含笑俯视她的画面。

阿托哈兰本身就是一位母亲——所有其他精灵的母亲。

她常常化身出艾莎生母伊杜娜王后的回响，给艾莎一个可以归来的亲切面孔。

艾莎明知冰壁上的涟漪并非真的是母亲——母亲早已远去——可当她凝望这位赋予她生命的女子的幻影时，心仍不禁因爱而涨满。

那位无条件爱过她的人。

那位相信她的力量是礼物而非诅咒的人。

那位为救她而献出生命的人。

终于，艾莎步入冰川空阔的心脏地带。

冰壁高高地向她头顶延展，望不到尽头，上面倒映着在表面舞动的记忆。

阿托哈兰是记忆的守护者。

而记忆即是知识。

这些冰壁间迸涌的知识如此浩瀚——任何凡间图书馆都装不下。

她一定能找到些什么，帮他们应对眼下的处境。

那诡异的黑暗、风暴，还有袭击了安娜的亡灵。

还有她的魔力，当她试图为妹妹提取一段记忆时，竟无缘无故仿佛熄火了。

不。

艾莎摇了摇头，她白金色的长发在冰光下熠熠生辉。

不，不只是熄火那么简单。

更像是她把那段记忆整个忘了。

就像其他人也都在遗忘一样。

她回想起营火旁的那个夜晚。

克斯托夫眼看着自己的帐篷塌了——片刻之后却似乎全忘了这回事。

再到亡灵现身后，牧人小屋里那个翌夜。

安娜方才还因看到艾莎的记忆而兴奋不已——转眼却好像失了全部兴致。

第二天早晨，她已不记得他们谈过要去做的事。

可这单纯是健忘吗？

还是记忆的丧失与亡灵有什么关联？

安娜的直觉是对的吗？

那亡灵真是茜塞尔，在忌日之际被克斯托夫的故事唤醒？

艾莎把手按在冰冷的墙壁上，努力集中精神。

再次尝试寻找那段她想与安娜分享的记忆——父亲与母亲在舞厅里欢笑共舞。

这画面她曾调出过上百次——是她最钟爱的片段之一。

可这一次，它没有浮现。“怎么回事？”她低声问，尽管她知道冰川无法回答。“记忆去哪了？

为什么我取不到？”一阵恐惧涌上她的喉咙。

这里到底发生了什么？

而它又是否和其余一切有关？

毕竟，克斯托夫或安娜开始忘事是一回事。

但这座字面上由记忆构成的冰川忘事，就完全是另一回事了。

艾莎心跳加速，把另一只手也按上冰壁，深吸一口气，却仍微微发颤。“试试别的吧，”她对自己说。“父亲在他最爱的树下。

母亲从树枝上倒挂下来，出其不意地吓他一跳。”又是一段心头好。

一段她曾调出过许多次的画面。

有那么一瞬，她觉得自己看见了什么。

冰中闪过微光，一段记忆正要成形。

可随即它就像在牧人小屋里那样熄灭了。

冰流转着，旋即又暗了下去。

记忆消失了。

仿佛被人从她手里偷走。

可就在她开始绝望之际，阿托哈兰的冰壁忽然亮了起来，闪烁微光。

一团灰雾升入空中。

片刻之后，一座座冰雕在她面前凝实。

可那不是她的母亲或父亲，也不是他们最爱的树。

而是两个女孩——年纪约与安娜和艾莎相仿——穿着看似老式的衣裙。

艾莎望着，冰面开始推移、延展，显出她们所在之处。

她们站在河岸边。

正激烈地争吵着。

艾莎目瞪口呆。

难道会是……？

她的思绪闪回克斯托夫讲过的维斯特兰姐妹的故事。

有一天，英格如愿以偿。

在去阿伦黛尔的途中，她撞见妹妹独自站在奔腾的河边。“这是什么？”她低声道，恐惧顺着脊背爬下。

她一半想移开目光。

想转身逃离冰川，再不回头。

可另一种力量却让她留了下来，看着记忆流转、冰雕仿佛活了过来。

河水上涨。

咆哮。

其中一个女孩被凶猛的水流卷走，在水中拼命挣扎，尖叫求救。“英格！”这喊声仿佛穿透冰壁回荡。“英格——救我！”幻影再度旋转，此刻聚焦于第二个女孩。

她跪在河岸上，泪水夺眶而出。“茜塞尔，”她嘶哑地喊。“对不起，茜塞尔！”幻影定格；活动的人影成了冰中的雕像。

艾莎跪倒在地，被方才所见淹没。

听闻久远的往事是一回事。

可亲眼看见茜塞尔在湍急的水中挣扎、向妹妹求救，而英格一动不动跪在岸边，显然为自己恶行满怀悔恨，就完全是另一回事了。

不过艾莎并不同情她。

她所受的，乃至更多，都是她应得的。

可可怜的茜塞尔啊！

艾莎无法想象，她在最后几秒里心里该是什么滋味。

意识到自己的亲妹妹竟恨她至此——嫉妒她至此——做出这种事。

忽然，她感到身后一阵风。

她猛地转身，惊讶地发现风灵盖尔正俯冲进冰川，风中夹着一封信。

她从风之灵手中取下信，打开，双手仍因所见而微微颤抖。

是安娜寄来的。

阿伦黛尔出大事了。

你得快回来——赶在一切都太晚之前！

sentences.en: “AH, AH, AH, AH…” Elsa couldn’t help singing as she and the Water Nokk approached Ahtohallan.
sentences.zh: “啊，啊，啊，啊……”艾莎忍不住唱了起来，她和“水马”正逼近阿托哈兰。

sentences.en: It was her version of greeting the Mother Spirit embodied in the glacier.
sentences.zh: 这是她向这座冰川中蕴含的“母亲之灵”致意的方式。

sentences.en: Ahtohallan had become like a second home to her over the last two months.
sentences.zh: 在过去的两个月里，阿托哈兰对她来说已经像个第二个家了。

sentences.en: Well, not a home, exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，严格来说，也不算家。

sentences.en: But a place of peace.
sentences.zh: 但它是个安宁的地方。

sentences.en: Just being there centered her somehow.
sentences.zh: 只要待在那里，她莫名就感到心定。

sentences.en: She found the icy surroundings comforting.
sentences.zh: 她觉得冰天雪地的环境让人安心。

sentences.en: It didn’t really make any sense when she tried to explain it to her sister.
sentences.zh: 当她试着向妹妹解释时，这其实说不太通。

sentences.en: But Anna was always so supportive and understanding—even when she didn’t quite get it.
sentences.zh: 但安娜总是那么支持她、理解她——即便她并不是完全懂。

sentences.en: It was a sister thing, she surmised.
sentences.zh: 她琢磨着，这大概就是姐妹之间的事吧。

sentences.en: She wished she could take Anna here.
sentences.zh: 她真希望能带安娜来这里。

sentences.en: But there was no way to cross the Dark Sea without the Water Nokk, and the spirit had a mind of its own.
sentences.zh: 但若没有“水马”，根本无法穿越暗海，而那灵性自有主张。

sentences.en: Which was why Elsa was working so hard to bring the memories home to share with her sister.
sentences.zh: 所以艾莎才这么努力地把记忆带回去，和妹妹分享。

sentences.en: So Anna could catch just a glimpse of the mysteries revealed here in this fortress of ice.
sentences.zh: 好让安娜也能瞥见这座冰之堡垒中显现的奥秘。

sentences.en: Because, oh, she’d seen so much in her short time here.
sentences.zh: 因为，噢，她在这短暂时光里看到的太多了。

sentences.en: She’d gone deep, as deep as she dared, watching her family’s history unfold in front of her eyes.
sentences.zh: 她潜得很深，深到敢去的极限，亲眼看着家族的历史在眼前展开。

sentences.en: Seeing her mother save her father’s life in the Enchanted Forest.
sentences.zh: 看着母亲在魔法森林里救下父亲的性命。

sentences.en: Watching them grow up together, become friends, fall in love.
sentences.zh: 看着他们一起长大、成为朋友、坠入爱河。

sentences.en: Witness the pain her mother had gone through keeping the secret that she was Northuldra.
sentences.zh: 目睹母亲守着自己是北地人的秘密时所经历的痛苦。

sentences.en: Elsa knew all too well about keeping secrets.
sentences.zh: 艾莎太清楚保守秘密是什么滋味了。

sentences.en: And then there were the moments that were harder to watch.
sentences.zh: 还有那些更难直视的时刻。

sentences.en: The fear in her father’s eyes as he witnessed young Elsa’s magic grow.
sentences.zh: 父亲看着年幼的艾莎魔力滋长时，眼中的恐惧。

sentences.en: He loved her so much—he tried his best—but he had also grown up with secrets.
sentences.zh: 他那么爱她——已尽了全力——可他也是在秘密中长大的。

sentences.en: And he, too, had learned to adhere to the horrific mantra, “Conceal, don’t feel.” He’d passed that on to her, thinking he was doing the best thing he could to help her keep the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 他也学会了恪守那可怕的箴言：“藏起来，别去感受。”他把它传给了她，以为这是在用最好的办法帮她守住王国。

sentences.en: Would he have approved if he knew she’d given it all to Anna in the end after all?
sentences.zh: 如果他知道她最终还是把一切都交给了安娜，他会赞同吗？

sentences.en: Deep down, she believed he would.
sentences.zh: 在内心深处，她相信他会。

sentences.en: He would have done anything to keep his girls safe and happy.
sentences.zh: 为了保护两个女儿平安喜乐，他什么都愿意做。

sentences.en: And she was happy, she thought, as she slid off the Water Spirit and stepped up to the icy entrance.
sentences.zh: 而她是快乐的，她想着，一边从“水之灵”背上滑下，踏上冰封的入口。

sentences.en: She was living free in the Enchanted Forest, no longer imprisoned by her guilt and fear.
sentences.zh: 她自由地生活在魔法森林里，不再被愧疚与恐惧囚禁。

sentences.en: She now had everything she had never known she wanted— needed .
sentences.zh: 她如今拥有了从未知道自己渴望——需要——的一切。

sentences.en: She had peace.
sentences.zh: 她拥有安宁。

sentences.en: She had power.
sentences.zh: 她拥有力量。

sentences.en: And yet she still had her sister.
sentences.zh: 而她依然拥有妹妹。

sentences.en: And Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 还有阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: Elsa was blown away by how gracious the kingdom had been the day she gave up her throne.
sentences.zh: 让艾莎震惊的是，在她退位那天，王国竟是如此宽厚。

sentences.en: She thought they’d be furious with her.
sentences.zh: 她原以为他们会愤怒。

sentences.en: She thought they’d believe she was abandoning them.
sentences.zh: 她原以为他们会觉得她抛弃了他们。

sentences.en: But no—they understood that she needed this.
sentences.zh: 可没有——他们理解，她需要这样。

sentences.en: That she had given them everything she could over the past three years.
sentences.zh: 理解她过去三年已倾尽所有给了他们。

sentences.en: And now it was time for her to give herself something, too.
sentences.zh: 而如今，也该轮到她为自己做点什么了。

sentences.en: Something she desperately needed to become the best version of herself.
sentences.zh: 做点她极度需要、以成就最好自己的事。

sentences.en: And so, when she had stood on that dais in front of all of Arendelle—and the cheers and shouts of encouragement rose to her ears—she felt tears of gratitude slip down her cheeks.
sentences.zh: 于是，当她站在阿伦黛尔众人面前的高台上——欢呼声与鼓励的呐喊传入耳中——她感到感激的泪水滑落脸颊。

sentences.en: They truly loved her; not just as their queen, but as a person—a citizen of Arendelle!
sentences.zh: 他们真的爱她；不只是爱她作为女王，更爱她这个人——阿伦黛尔的一位子民！

sentences.en: They were willing to let her go, and because of that she would never truly leave them.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意放她走，正因如此，她永远不会真正离开他们。

sentences.en: Elsa’s steps quickened as she raced down the icy path, deeper into Ahtohallan.
sentences.zh: 艾莎脚步加快，沿着冰路奔向阿托哈兰的更深处。

sentences.en: The walls shimmered in their greeting to her, flickering with images of her mother smiling down at her as she ran.
sentences.zh: 冰壁闪烁着向她致意，映出母亲奔跑时含笑俯视她的画面。

sentences.en: Ahtohallan was a mother herself—the mother of all the other spirits.
sentences.zh: 阿托哈兰本身就是一位母亲——所有其他精灵的母亲。

sentences.en: And she often embodied echoes of Elsa’s own mother, Queen Iduna, to give Elsa a friendly face to come home to.
sentences.zh: 她常常化身出艾莎生母伊杜娜王后的回响，给艾莎一个可以归来的亲切面孔。

sentences.en: And while Elsa knew it was not really her mother in those icy ripples on the wall—her mother was long gone—she still couldn’t keep her heart from swelling with love as she gazed upon the vision of the woman who had given birth to her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎明知冰壁上的涟漪并非真的是母亲——母亲早已远去——可当她凝望这位赋予她生命的女子的幻影时，心仍不禁因爱而涨满。

sentences.en: Who had loved her unconditionally.
sentences.zh: 那位无条件爱过她的人。

sentences.en: Who had believed her powers to be a gift, not a curse.
sentences.zh: 那位相信她的力量是礼物而非诅咒的人。

sentences.en: Who had sacrificed her life to try to save her.
sentences.zh: 那位为救她而献出生命的人。

sentences.en: At last Elsa stepped into the cavernous heart of the glacier.
sentences.zh: 终于，艾莎步入冰川空阔的心脏地带。

sentences.en: The icy walls stretched tall above her, as far as her eyes could see, reflecting memories that danced on their surfaces.
sentences.zh: 冰壁高高地向她头顶延展，望不到尽头，上面倒映着在表面舞动的记忆。

sentences.en: Ahtohallan was the keeper of memories.
sentences.zh: 阿托哈兰是记忆的守护者。

sentences.en: And memories were knowledge.
sentences.zh: 而记忆即是知识。

sentences.en: There was so much knowledge bursting within these walls—more than any mere library could possibly hold.
sentences.zh: 这些冰壁间迸涌的知识如此浩瀚——任何凡间图书馆都装不下。

sentences.en: Surely, she could find something to help with their current situation.
sentences.zh: 她一定能找到些什么，帮他们应对眼下的处境。

sentences.en: The strange darkness, the storms, the draugr that had attacked Anna.
sentences.zh: 那诡异的黑暗、风暴，还有袭击了安娜的亡灵。

sentences.en: And then there were her powers, which had seemed to fizzle out for no reason as she’d attempted to pull a memory up for her sister.
sentences.zh: 还有她的魔力，当她试图为妹妹提取一段记忆时，竟无缘无故仿佛熄火了。

sentences.en: No .
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Elsa shook her head, her white-blond hair shimmering under the icy lights.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摇了摇头，她白金色的长发在冰光下熠熠生辉。

sentences.en: No, it wasn’t just that they fizzled out.
sentences.zh: 不，不只是熄火那么简单。

sentences.en: It was as if she’d forgotten the memory altogether.
sentences.zh: 更像是她把那段记忆整个忘了。

sentences.en: Just like everyone else had been forgetting things.
sentences.zh: 就像其他人也都在遗忘一样。

sentences.en: She thought back to the night by the campfire.
sentences.zh: 她回想起营火旁的那个夜晚。

sentences.en: Kristoff had watched his tent go down—and then seemed to forget all about it a moment later.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫眼看着自己的帐篷塌了——片刻之后却似乎全忘了这回事。

sentences.en: And then there was the next night in the shepherd’s hut, right after the draugr encounter.
sentences.zh: 再到亡灵现身后，牧人小屋里那个翌夜。

sentences.en: Anna had been so excited about seeing Elsa’s memory—but then seemed to lose all interest.
sentences.zh: 安娜方才还因看到艾莎的记忆而兴奋不已——转眼却好像失了全部兴致。

sentences.en: And the next morning she hadn’t remembered anything they’d talked about doing.
sentences.zh: 第二天早晨，她已不记得他们谈过要去做的事。

sentences.en: But was it simply forgetfulness?
sentences.zh: 可这单纯是健忘吗？

sentences.en: Or was the loss of memory connected to the draugr somehow?
sentences.zh: 还是记忆的丧失与亡灵有什么关联？

sentences.en: Was Anna’s hunch correct?
sentences.zh: 安娜的直觉是对的吗？

sentences.en: Was the draugr Sissel, reawakened by Kristoff’s story on the anniversary of her death?
sentences.zh: 那亡灵真是茜塞尔，在忌日之际被克斯托夫的故事唤醒？

sentences.en: Elsa pressed a hand against the cold wall of ice, trying to concentrate.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把手按在冰冷的墙壁上，努力集中精神。

sentences.en: Trying again to find that memory she’d wanted to share with Anna, of her father and mother laughing and dancing in the ballroom.
sentences.zh: 再次尝试寻找那段她想与安娜分享的记忆——父亲与母亲在舞厅里欢笑共舞。

sentences.en: She’d pulled it up a hundred times before—it was one of her favorites.
sentences.zh: 这画面她曾调出过上百次——是她最钟爱的片段之一。

sentences.en: But this time, it didn’t materialize. “What’s wrong?” she whispered, though she knew the glacier couldn’t answer. “Where’s the memory?
sentences.zh: 可这一次，它没有浮现。“怎么回事？”她低声问，尽管她知道冰川无法回答。“记忆去哪了？

sentences.en: Why can’t I access it?” A taste of dread rose in her throat.
sentences.zh: 为什么我取不到？”一阵恐惧涌上她的喉咙。

sentences.en: What was going on here?
sentences.zh: 这里到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And was it connected somehow to everything else?
sentences.zh: 而它又是否和其余一切有关？

sentences.en: After all, it was one thing for Kristoff or Anna to start forgetting things.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，克斯托夫或安娜开始忘事是一回事。

sentences.en: But quite another for the very literal glacier of memories.
sentences.zh: 但这座字面上由记忆构成的冰川忘事，就完全是另一回事了。

sentences.en: Heart beating fast, Elsa pressed her other hand against the icy wall, drawing in a deep but shaky breath. “Just try something else,” she told herself. “Father under his favorite tree.
sentences.zh: 艾莎心跳加速，把另一只手也按上冰壁，深吸一口气，却仍微微发颤。“试试别的吧，”她对自己说。“父亲在他最爱的树下。

sentences.en: Mother popping down from the branches, upside down and surprising him.” Another favorite.
sentences.zh: 母亲从树枝上倒挂下来，出其不意地吓他一跳。”又是一段心头好。

sentences.en: One she’d pulled up many times before.
sentences.zh: 一段她曾调出过许多次的画面。

sentences.en: For a moment, she thought she saw something.
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬，她觉得自己看见了什么。

sentences.en: A flicker in the ice, the beginnings of a memory forming.
sentences.zh: 冰中闪过微光，一段记忆正要成形。

sentences.en: But then it fizzled out as it had in the shepherd’s hut.
sentences.zh: 可随即它就像在牧人小屋里那样熄灭了。

sentences.en: The ice swirled, then grew dark again.
sentences.zh: 冰流转着，旋即又暗了下去。

sentences.en: The memory was gone.
sentences.zh: 记忆消失了。

sentences.en: As if it had been stolen away from her.
sentences.zh: 仿佛被人从她手里偷走。

sentences.en: But just as she began to despair, the walls of Ahtohallan suddenly seemed to brighten and shimmer.
sentences.zh: 可就在她开始绝望之际，阿托哈兰的冰壁忽然亮了起来，闪烁微光。

sentences.en: A gray mist began to rise into the air.
sentences.zh: 一团灰雾升入空中。

sentences.en: A moment later, sculptures made of ice solidified in front of her.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，一座座冰雕在她面前凝实。

sentences.en: But they were not of her mother or her father and their favorite tree.
sentences.zh: 可那不是她的母亲或父亲，也不是他们最爱的树。

sentences.en: Rather, they were two girls—around Anna and Elsa’s age—wearing clothing that looked old-fashioned.
sentences.zh: 而是两个女孩——年纪约与安娜和艾莎相仿——穿着看似老式的衣裙。

sentences.en: As Elsa watched, the ice began to shift, expand, revealing their location.
sentences.zh: 艾莎望着，冰面开始推移、延展，显出她们所在之处。

sentences.en: They were standing on a riverbank.
sentences.zh: 她们站在河岸边。

sentences.en: And they were arguing bitterly.
sentences.zh: 正激烈地争吵着。

sentences.en: Elsa gaped.
sentences.zh: 艾莎目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: Could it be…?
sentences.zh: 难道会是……？

sentences.en: Her mind flashed back to Kristoff’s story of the Vesterland sisters.
sentences.zh: 她的思绪闪回克斯托夫讲过的维斯特兰姐妹的故事。

sentences.en: One day, Inger got her wish.
sentences.zh: 有一天，英格如愿以偿。

sentences.en: While on a trip to Arendelle, she caught her sister standing by the rushing river—alone. “What is this?” she whispered, fear crawling down her spine.
sentences.zh: 在去阿伦黛尔的途中，她撞见妹妹独自站在奔腾的河边。“这是什么？”她低声道，恐惧顺着脊背爬下。

sentences.en: Half of her wanted to look away.
sentences.zh: 她一半想移开目光。

sentences.en: To turn and flee the glacier altogether and never look back.
sentences.zh: 想转身逃离冰川，再不回头。

sentences.en: But instead, something compelled her to stay as the memory swirled and the ice sculptures seemed to come to life.
sentences.zh: 可另一种力量却让她留了下来，看着记忆流转、冰雕仿佛活了过来。

sentences.en: The river rising.
sentences.zh: 河水上涨。

sentences.en: Raging.
sentences.zh: 咆哮。

sentences.en: One of the girls being swept away in its vicious current, thrashing in the water, screaming for help. “INGER!” The words seemed to echo through the icy walls. “Inger—help me!” The vision swirled again, now focusing on the second girl.
sentences.zh: 其中一个女孩被凶猛的水流卷走，在水中拼命挣扎，尖叫求救。“英格！”这喊声仿佛穿透冰壁回荡。“英格——救我！”幻影再度旋转，此刻聚焦于第二个女孩。

sentences.en: She was on her knees by the riverbank, her eyes flowing with tears. “Sissel,” she croaked. “I’m so sorry, Sissel!” The vision froze; the moving figures were now just statues in the ice.
sentences.zh: 她跪在河岸上，泪水夺眶而出。“茜塞尔，”她嘶哑地喊。“对不起，茜塞尔！”幻影定格；活动的人影成了冰中的雕像。

sentences.en: Elsa dropped to her own knees, overwhelmed by what she’d just seen.
sentences.zh: 艾莎跪倒在地，被方才所见淹没。

sentences.en: It was one thing to hear about what happened long ago.
sentences.zh: 听闻久远的往事是一回事。

sentences.en: But it was quite another to see Sissel thrashing in the rough waters, begging her sister for help while Inger was motionless on the riverbank, clearly filled with remorse for her evil deed.
sentences.zh: 可亲眼看见茜塞尔在湍急的水中挣扎、向妹妹求救，而英格一动不动跪在岸边，显然为自己恶行满怀悔恨，就完全是另一回事了。

sentences.en: Elsa didn’t feel sorry for her, though.
sentences.zh: 不过艾莎并不同情她。

sentences.en: She deserved all she had gotten and more.
sentences.zh: 她所受的，乃至更多，都是她应得的。

sentences.en: But poor Sissel!
sentences.zh: 可可怜的茜塞尔啊！

sentences.en: Elsa couldn’t imagine what must have gone through her mind in those last seconds.
sentences.zh: 艾莎无法想象，她在最后几秒里心里该是什么滋味。

sentences.en: The realization that her own sister had hated her enough—had been jealous enough—to do such a thing.
sentences.zh: 意识到自己的亲妹妹竟恨她至此——嫉妒她至此——做出这种事。

sentences.en: Suddenly she felt a gust of wind behind her.
sentences.zh: 忽然，她感到身后一阵风。

sentences.en: She whirled around, surprised to find Gale swooping into the glacier, a piece of mail in its breeze.
sentences.zh: 她猛地转身，惊讶地发现风灵盖尔正俯冲进冰川，风中夹着一封信。

sentences.en: She plucked the letter from the Wind Spirit and opened it, her hands still trembling from all she’d seen.
sentences.zh: 她从风之灵手中取下信，打开，双手仍因所见而微微颤抖。

sentences.en: It was from Anna.
sentences.zh: 是安娜寄来的。

sentences.en: Something is very wrong in Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔出大事了。

sentences.en: You need to come back—as soon as possible—before it’s too late!
sentences.zh: 你得快回来——赶在一切都太晚之前！

chapters.title: Chapter Ten: Anna
chapters.en:
KRISTOFF MIGHT HAVE BEEN CONFUSED about a few things, but one thing he remembered was his love of lingonberry pie. Leaving him and Sven in the capable hands of Olina, the castle cook, who had a fresh pie hot out of the oven, Anna and Olaf trudged up to the secret room that led to her parents’ private library.

Anna pulled on the Water Nokk statue that guarded the space and the bookcase swung open, revealing the arched passageway beyond. She and Olaf stepped inside. Anna stifled a sneeze as they headed down the passageway into the windowless secret room. It was still a bit dusty, though she had tried to clear out all the cobwebs that had draped the bookcases. Before she’d discovered the room, it had been years since anyone had used it, making it a perfect home for spiders and other small creatures of the castle that Anna didn’t really want to run into. But she’d shooed them all away, knowing her mother would have approved of a clean home—everywhere.

She paused at the entrance to the room, taking in the high shelves filled with books and scrolls and other curios—glass beakers, silver scales. A portrait of Aren of Arendelle, the legendary ruler of Arendelle of old, hung from a far wall. The place probably didn’t look much different now from how it had when her parents had first stumbled upon it in their teens. According to Elsa’s Ahtohallan memories, this room had been a special place for Iduna and Agnarr. A secret hideaway where they could spend time together without anyone else watching. A perfect place to fall in love.

Anna sighed dreamily over her parents’ romance, then got back to the task at hand, heading straight to the bookshelves. Her fingers flew over the leather spines, looking for the book she remembered reading one time, about mythical creatures that went bump in the night. Or bump in the day that resembled the night. But where was it?

“Come out, come out, wherever you are, book,” Anna muttered, staring at all the tomes in front of her. Their spines boasted tales of the history of Arendelle and information about the science of soil, and there were even some fun mysteries thrown in for good measure. But nothing about draugrs. She sighed and moved to another shelf. Surely, it had to be here somewhere.

“I think I found it!” Olaf exclaimed at last, from the top of the ladder. He pulled an old, cracked leather book from the very top shelf and tossed it to the floor. It landed with a loud thump, stirring up a large cloud of dust, which made him sneeze. “It was stuck behind a book on the history of cheese.” He giggled. “How cheesy is that?” He jumped off the ladder to retrieve the book, then shuffled over to the table.

“That’s it!” Anna said, feeling relieved when she saw the title: Of Nightmares and Nixies. She stepped up to the table and cracked open the spine, causing more dust to float into the air in the low-lit space. She skimmed through it until she found a page titled “Draugrs.” A sketch of a creepy-looking creature in tattered clothing, skin practically peeling off its body, stared back at them. Anna shuddered at the sight. “That’s what I ran into, all right.”

“‘A draugr,’” Olaf read, “‘is sometimes thought of as a ghost or spirit but is in fact a reanimated, decayed corpse that rose from the dead because it didn’t receive a proper burial.’”

The two looked at one another and said, “Eww,” at the same time.

“Also,” Olaf observed, “that fits Sinister Sissel! She drowned, remember?”

Anna felt a prickling at the back of her neck, thinking back to the creature towering over her in the woods while she lay on the ground, its blackened teeth bared. Princess Sissel—come back from the dead. “Let’s keep reading,” she said, pushing her fears aside. “It says here that draugrs can have magical abilities and can control the weather and turn day into night.” She grimaced. “Well, we know that part already!”

Olaf pointed to another passage. “And here’s where it talks about memories. Draugrs have the power to slip in and steal people’s memories while they sleep.” He flipped the page. “But where’s the part about stealing slippers? That seems important.”

Anna’s heartbeat quickened. “So the draugr did come to Arendelle while Elsa and I were gone. And it stole everyone’s memories!”

“But why?” Olaf asked, looking up from the book.

Anna scowled, squeezing her hands into fists. “I know why. Sissel is mad at me for becoming queen in place of Elsa. She doesn’t know the whole story, and now she’s taking it out on the kingdom!” She shook her head. “What we need to find out is whether the memories the draugr stole are gone for good or if there’s a way to get them back. Does the book say anything about that?” She flipped the pages anxiously, but the words seemed to blur. It was then that she became aware that she was crying.

“Anna, are you okay?” Olaf asked, concerned.

She wasn’t, Anna realized. She wasn’t okay at all. “What if their memory loss gets worse?” she said worriedly. “Right now, Kristoff can’t even remember our engagement. If we don’t get rid of this draugr, he could end up forgetting everything…including me.” Her voice caught on the last part. She couldn’t imagine a world where Kristoff didn’t know her. Didn’t love her.

Olaf patted her hand. “Don’t worry, Anna. We won’t let that happen. I’m sure if we can just get rid of the draugr, everything will go back to normal. And look!” He pointed at the next page in the book. “They even list ways to do it.”

“They do?” Anna asked, a glimmer of hope rising inside her. She scanned the passage Olaf had pointed to quickly. Then she frowned. “Uh, it says we can chop off its head…”

The snowman shrugged. “Brutal. But likely effective.”

“And likely impossible,” Anna muttered. She thought back to the encounter the night before and tried to imagine even getting close enough to the corpse to remove its head. “There’s got to be something else.” She turned back to the book, her eyes focusing on a paragraph on the next page. “Okay, what about this? It says if you can lead the draugr back into its grave, it will find peace and fade away.”

“Well, that does seem much less violent,” Olaf agreed, looking a little relieved.

“Except…Sissel doesn’t have a grave. She was swept out to sea.” Anna tried not to panic. This was proving to be harder than she’d thought.

“I wonder if Elsa could freeze the draugr and then shatter it into a thousand pieces,” Olaf mused. “Ice powers…swoosh!”

Hmm. Anna consulted the book again. A moment later, she shook her head. “I don’t think that’ll work, either. It says here draugrs are immune to acts of strength. In fact, it says that when angered, they can curse their enemies and prevent them from growing stronger.” She pursed her lips. “Back in the forest, Elsa made it really mad by making this wall of ice. And immediately afterward, her powers started fizzling out.”

“That doesn’t seem good,” Olaf murmured.

“No.” Anna sighed, closing the book. “This is not good at all.”

“What isn’t?” called out a new voice.

Anna looked up just in time to see Elsa burst into the room. Her sister leaned on her hands and knees, trying to catch her breath. “I got your note and came as fast as I could.”

Anna ran around the table, throwing her arms around her sister. “I’m so glad to see you. We’re too late to stop the draugr. It’s already been here and stolen people’s memories!”

Elsa’s face was pained. “No. Oh, Anna…are you sure?”

Anna grimaced. “Unfortunately, yes. Even Kristoff’s…” She trailed off, miserable as her mind flashed to her handsome ice harvester. “And that’s not all—the book says draugrs can curse their enemies and prevent them from growing stronger.” She looked at Elsa. “Do you think that’s why your powers started to fizzle after we saw the draugr?”

Elsa sat down on one of the velvet chairs, looking drained. “Maybe. I was having trouble pulling up memories from Ahtohallan, too. I didn’t understand why. But now…” She closed her eyes.
