安娜惊得说不出话。

她不敢相信自己听到的话。

永恒的黑夜？

王国坠入无尽的黑暗？

更别提永不停歇的风暴了！

真到了那一步，他们该怎么办？

没有太阳，阿伦黛尔的庄稼会枯死。

船只会在狂暴的海浪中沉没，而非装载药品与补给平安靠港。

她不愿相信皮比说的话，但这种事他从未出错。

可还有一个可怕的问题在心里刺着她，逼她要个答案。

一个她并不确定自己真想问出口的问题。

因为风暴虽糟、永夜更糟……记忆……人们的记忆……“皮比？”她试探着，语气软了下来。“如果我们无法除去阿伦黛尔这个威胁——”“我们会除掉的，”艾莎坚定地打断。“可如果我们除不掉，”安娜温和地继续，“那是不是意味着……会不会也意味着……”她的声音哽住，目光越过山谷，望向那魁梧的采冰人和他的驯鹿。

克斯托夫正惊叹地望着那些会说话、会滚动、会蹦跳的地精，仿佛从未见过他们。

连斯文都怪异地盯着他。“人们会……克斯托夫会……””皮比用同样轻柔的声音答道：“我很抱歉，安娜。”

他不必再说下去。

安娜强迫自己盯着地精们颈间的晶体，盼着那些发光的颜色能让她平静。

她只想放声尖叫。

为什么克斯托夫非讲那个鬼故事不可？

为什么？“但你一定懂什么咒语或药方，能帮人找回丢失的记忆，”她坚持道，音量越来越高。“你们以前取走过记忆。

你们一定也知道怎么放回去！”可她又悻悻地想，地精们从未找回她被抹去的全部记忆——那是她儿时为保护她免受姐姐魔力所害，被他们取走的。

时至今日，她的脑中仍有空洞，那些与姐姐共度、再也回不来的珍贵时光。

皮比的目光掠过山谷，落在克斯托夫身上。“我很抱歉，陛下。

我们自己的法子都够难控制了。

要去驾驭他人的，几乎不可能。

我无法抹去亡灵所行之事。”“可那意味着……克斯托夫，”安娜念到这个名字，声音哽住了。

她想起那个用对冰的爱、用替驯鹿代言的模样、用对古怪食谱的热忱偷走她心的山里人。

克斯托夫。

她的克斯托夫。

记忆在她脑中闪过。

她送他新雪橇后两人的初吻，还有第一次玩比手画脚。

他单膝跪地、向她求婚的那一刻。

克斯托夫——她的克斯托夫！

如今却几乎记不得她是谁。

安娜觉得双腿发软。

地精和艾莎伸手扶她，安娜却退开一步，不愿被人搀扶。

不。

她不愿接受，克斯托夫对她的爱会因某个怪物而消失。

她也绝不让她的子民承受永夜或无尽风暴。

她是阿伦黛尔的女王。

平息此事是她的职责。

总会有办法的。

她思绪飞转，努力回想皮比仰望星空时说的话。

地精说话总像谜语。

但谜底往往藏在其中。

“曾逃逸者，今启航……欲了此局，须述她事……她的事。”

可他们早已讲过茜塞尔的故事！

在营火旁。

后来在阿伦黛尔又讲过……忽然，安娜的思绪闪回奥肯的桑拿房，那时他们正看着两位公主的画像。

那时奥肯坚称英格和茜塞尔是朋友，而非克斯托夫等人所说的水火不容。

他还赌咒说英格想当科学家，而非像她姐姐那样当女王。

当时安娜还纳闷，她们的故事会不会另有隐情。

如今她确信一定如此。

她转向艾莎，脸上写满决心。“答案在茜塞尔身上，”她朗声道。“我们得弄清她和英格之间到底发生了什么。

你听到奥肯说的了。

他知道一些我们不知道的英格的事。

故事里一定有我们漏掉的一块。

也许那缺失的片段，能帮我们理解茜塞尔、理解她想要什么。”艾莎点头。“这主意不坏，”她赞同。“可我们怎么才能弄清真相？

似乎人人记得的版本都不一样。

而阿伦黛尔大半的人根本什么都不记得了。”“没错。

可当年总该有文字记载，”安娜提醒她。“我是说，那准是个大新闻，对吧？

两位公主造访阿伦黛尔，其中一个还谋害了另一个？

说真的，我打赌它上了头版。”姐姐眼睛一亮。“当然！

《村庄之冠》。

他们的档案能追溯多年。”“也许我们可以从那儿入手，”安娜说。“我是说，值得一试，对吧？”“绝对。

我们得尽快赶回阿伦黛尔。”艾莎转向皮比。“多谢相助，”她说。“接下来的交给我们。”皮比清了清嗓子。“陛下们，愿你们寻得所求，”他说。“而且要快。”他忧心忡忡地瞥了眼克斯托夫——那人正漫无目的地游荡，兴高采烈地和看似真石头的石头聊天，而非地精。“这期间，何不把克斯托夫留在我们这儿？

我们替你们照看他，直到你们……了结……此事。”“什么？

留下克斯托夫？”安娜惊呼，满脸骇然。

顷刻间，她方才解开谜团的新信心与兴奋仿佛碎了一地。

他们竟要她丢下未婚夫？“他在这儿，亡灵伤不到他，”艾莎温柔地提醒她。

安娜低下头。

她知道妹妹是对的。

可一想到要留下他……“好吧。

但你们也得留下斯文，”她脱口而出。“就算克斯托夫不记得它，他俩也从不分开。”布尔达把手搭在她膝上。“当然！

斯文永远受欢迎……。”安娜茫然地点头，目光锁在未婚夫身上，胃里又是一阵翻腾。“就让我道个别。

我是说，暂别，”她纠正自己。“当然，”艾莎说，眼里满是同情。“我们给你点空间。”尽管安娜想要独处，她却一点不期待这场告别。

她走到克斯托夫和斯文身边，这会儿他们至少是在和一位真地精聊天，而非死石头。“你说你在这次庆典上要赢水晶？”克斯托夫正说着。“这些水晶有什么用？”小石笑了。“噢，克斯托夫！”他看见安娜，笑起来。“嘿，你新娘来了。”说完便蹦跳着找别人去了。

克斯托夫对着安娜重新打量。“我的新娘？”他脸红了。

她脸也红了。“我不是你新娘，”她飞快地说。

至少现在还不是，她心想。“但我是非常在乎你的人。”她摸了摸他被风吹得冰冷粗糙的脸颊。“所以我才要把你和斯文留在这儿，交给布尔达照顾几天。

布尔达会好好照顾你，直到我回来。”“好，”克斯托夫开心地说。“那你回来是因为……？”安娜的心猛地一缩，连气都透不过来。

可她要勇敢。

她绝不让克斯托夫看见，她为他、为他们的王国有多害怕。

她会扭转一切。

然后她再也不、绝不再让他讲第二个营火故事。

安娜倾身，吻上他的唇。“因为我爱你，”她贴着他的脸说。“而你也爱我，等我回来、你重新记起一切，我们还有整段未来要规划。”她退开一步，心痛得超乎想象。

她声音沙哑地继续：“那就等我回来前乖乖平安，好吗？”“好，”克斯托夫说。“走吧，斯文。

我们去找到那位布尔达女士。”他顿了顿，又转向安娜。“再见，新娘小姐！”安娜望着他若无其事地穿过地精人群，心如刀绞。

他不记得我们了，她想。

他不记得我了。

她想哭，可此刻正需要坚强。

于是她挺直肩膀，远远望着布尔达握住他的手，转眼就飞快念叨起某种听着吓人的汤，发誓能把克斯托夫和斯文治好。

安娜但愿布尔达说得对，可她心里清楚，在亡灵之事彻底了结前，没什么能把她此生挚爱唤回。

他们顺道去奥肯的杂货铺与桑拿房接上奥拉夫，当天晚些时候回到村里时，雪又下了起来。

抵达阿伦黛尔时，每扇窗里都闪着灯，却不见有人在为极夜庆典忙碌。

事实上，他们仿佛根本忘了这场庆典。

走向报社办公室时，他们撞见马蒂亚斯，他正坐在父母纪念像下，低头盯着一张自己和哈丽玛的照片，摇着头，一脸茫然。“我们回来了，”安娜告诉他。“我们走了以后，一切都还好吗？”马蒂亚斯抬头瞥了他们一眼，神情空白。“都好，”他平板地说。“能不好吗？”安娜胸口一紧。“呃，我说不好。

我们海岸边的海盗？

猛烈得离谱的风暴？

阴影里游荡的怪僵尸？”马蒂亚斯耸耸肩：“这些我可都没听说。”安娜的心直沉下去。

马蒂亚斯把手中照片朝他们一递。“你碰巧知道这是谁吗？

她看着好眼熟，可我对不上号了。”“一位特别的人。

我想你在那边能找到她，”艾莎说着，扶他起身，轻轻引他走向哈得逊炉边酒馆——那是由他此生挚爱所开、而他此刻似乎已不记得的酒馆。

马蒂亚斯茫然地点点头，朝那栋建筑走去。

可还没走到一半，他似乎就忘了要去哪。

忽然，他调头往反方向走，荒腔走板地吹起口哨。

艾莎朝安娜投去忧心的一瞥。“这不妙，”她说。“要是马蒂亚斯也失了记忆，就没人照看阿伦黛尔了。”“更该尽快查明英格与茜塞尔故事的真相了，”安娜 declare，努力不让内心的担忧显露。

她的子民指望她。

克斯托夫也指望她——不论他记不记得。

她不能让任何一个人失望。

我绝不会，她坚定地对自己说。

无论如何，我们要阻止这亡灵。

我们要拨乱反正。“走吧，”她对艾莎说。“去找韦尔。”“噢，你好！”韦尔说着，打开《村庄之冠》报社办公室的门——他就住在楼上。

安娜、艾莎和奥拉夫鱼贯而入，嗅着扑面而来的油墨与温纸气味。“有人作伴真好！”安娜吃了一惊。

办公室里乱作一团，纸张到处都是。

这可不像韦尔。“‘有人作伴真好’？

这可真新鲜，”奥拉夫嘟囔。

韦尔平时忙得顾不上说话，除非在做采访，工作起来极其严肃。“韦尔，我们其实是想问你几个关于报纸的问题，”安娜直截了当地开口。

韦尔脸一沉。“恐怕这周没有新刊了。

我好像忘了怎么开印刷机……还找不到我的油墨。

你看见我的铅笔在哪吗？”艾莎伸手，从韦尔耳后抽出那支笔。“噢！”韦尔咯咯笑。“我真傻！

今天真是忘性大。”安娜瞥了姐姐一眼。“这正是我们担心的。”看来和别人一样，韦尔也帮不上忙。

任何查考都得靠他们自己了。“韦尔，”艾莎对他说。“我们想看看你的档案。

旧报纸你都收在哪儿？”韦尔来了精神。“在后屋！

全都有，从创刊号起一期不缺。”他抢在他们前头走，躲开这周忘了发出的那摞报纸。“《村庄之冠》创办有……呃……”“六十年了，”奥拉夫接话。“对！”韦尔又笑起来。“见到我们的读者真高兴。”他打开后屋的门，安娜看见满墙书架，上面摞着报纸。“慢慢看，随便翻，”韦尔说。“我去另一间，嗯……干点活。”他自顾自笑着消失了。“嗯，”艾莎走向第一个书架，“至少忘性的韦尔是个友善的韦尔。”“好，我们分头找，”安娜说着走向第二个书架。“我们找大约五十年前登的一篇报道。”“那范围窄多了，”奥拉夫跳上凳子，对付起第三个书架。

搜寻花了好一阵，安娜的耐心渐失，隔壁韦尔倒是吹得欢。

不久，屋里像遭了飓风，纸堆高高歪在两侧，满地散落。

（结果，奥拉夫式的“查资料”有点……乱。）他们找到往年各种有趣报道：父母的结婚启事、布洛杰特面包店开业、丽塔王后——鲁纳德国王之妻、他们的祖母——的悲剧，以及她在父亲还是幼童时离奇失踪。

却没有一篇讲维斯特兰姐妹。“噢，这儿有篇讲你出生的，安娜！”奥拉夫兴奋地喊，把一张皱巴巴的报纸推给她。

安娜扫了眼头版，皱起眉。“呃，在哪？”她困惑地问。“就那儿！”奥拉夫指向页底。“就在那篇巨幅报道‘蓝眼老太’海盗女王威胁阿伦黛尔海岸的下面！”“果然，”安娜抱怨，目光落到小得多的标题上：阿伦黛尔欢迎二公主降生！

显然《村庄之冠》对海盗的执念深得很……“我好像找到了什么！”艾莎喊着，从顶层架子上跳下，怀里抱着几份报纸。

她把报纸摔在桌上，指着最上面那份。“是篇讲维斯特兰姐妹造访阿伦黛尔的报道。

而且时间对得上。”她把报纸在桌上摊开。

果然，画着两个女孩——一个长发绾成复杂的辫子，一个留着短波波头——回望着他们。

艾莎摸了摸报纸。“就是她们。

奥肯画像里那两个女孩。”她指着长发女孩。“英格，”她说，又把手移到短发女孩。“这是茜塞尔。”“我得说，茜塞尔当真姑娘时，比腐烂僵尸好看多了，”奥拉夫评道。“我是说，长相不重要。

内心美才重要。”安娜盯着茜塞尔的画像。

很难相信，袭击过他们的那个怪物，曾是这样美丽的女孩。

她看起来那么快乐，仿佛从来无忧无虑。

可英格也是——画里她仰望着姐姐，满眼爱慕，像在崇拜茜塞尔踩过的土地。

有一点确凿无疑：她们绝不像不共戴天的仇敌。

艾莎大声念起报道。“‘《村庄之冠》欣悦报道：维斯特兰两位公主，人称维斯特兰姐妹，将赴阿伦黛尔与鲁纳德国王举行重要会晤。’”安娜皱眉。“重要会晤？

谈什么？”艾莎告诉她：“没说。”翻到另一篇报道。“不过这儿有篇讲那场意外的。”三人一齐俯身，同时读起来。“就跟村里人一直说的一样，”安娜说，自知语气失望。“英格和茜塞尔吵了一架，茜塞尔淹死了。

英格被控谋杀，祖父把她送上囚船流放。

船在驶向目的地前，于风暴中沉没。

再没别的了。”“要是英格死了，那茜塞尔现在现身想图什么？”艾莎问。“显然不是复仇。”“我不知道。

可这也没告诉我们新东西。”她把报纸放下。“我们得进一步了解姐妹俩本身。

或是她们吵得那么凶、以至于闹出人命的原因。”“唉，这儿可找不着了，”艾莎说。

安娜缓缓点头，有些气馁。“而且阿伦黛尔显然没人记得任何事，”她开口。

忽然她有了主意。“对了！

我之前怎么没想到？””什么？”艾莎困惑地问。“我们得去维斯特兰！”安娜兴奋地说。“也许乔纳斯国王和玛丽知道，英格和茜塞尔来阿伦黛尔所为何事，又为何争吵。

我是说，那是她们的故国！

若有人知道，必是他们！””好主意，安娜，”艾莎赞同。“拜访乔纳斯国王能解决我们所有问题。”安娜合上书，做着美梦般微笑。

解决所有问题。

找回克斯托夫。

她忽然充满希望。“我们去通知马蒂亚斯，明早一早就动身。”

sentences.en: ANNA WAS TOO STUNNED TO SPEAK.
sentences.zh: 安娜惊得说不出话。

sentences.en: She couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
sentences.zh: 她不敢相信自己听到的话。

sentences.en: Forever night?
sentences.zh: 永恒的黑夜？

sentences.en: The kingdom plunged into eternal darkness?
sentences.zh: 王国坠入无尽的黑暗？

sentences.en: Not to mention never-ending storms!
sentences.zh: 更别提永不停歇的风暴了！

sentences.en: What would they do if that happened?
sentences.zh: 真到了那一步，他们该怎么办？

sentences.en: Without the sun, Arendelle’s crops would wither and die.
sentences.zh: 没有太阳，阿伦黛尔的庄稼会枯死。

sentences.en: Ships would sink in the stormy waters of the sea instead of reaching safe harbor with their medicines and supplies.
sentences.zh: 船只会在狂暴的海浪中沉没，而非装载药品与补给平安靠港。

sentences.en: She didn’t want to believe what Grand Pabbie was saying, but he’d never been wrong about something like this.
sentences.zh: 她不愿相信皮比说的话，但这种事他从未出错。

sentences.en: And then there was another horrifying question needling at her, begging for an answer.
sentences.zh: 可还有一个可怕的问题在心里刺着她，逼她要个答案。

sentences.en: One she wasn’t sure she really wanted to ask.
sentences.zh: 一个她并不确定自己真想问出口的问题。

sentences.en: Because while storms were bad and eternal night was worse… Memories…people’s memories… “Grand Pabbie?” she ventured, her tone softening. “If we can’t rid Arendelle of this threat—” “We will,” Elsa cut in firmly. “But if we can’t ,” Anna continued gently, “does that mean…could it also mean…” Her voice caught as she stared across the valley at the burly ice harvester and his reindeer.
sentences.zh: 因为风暴虽糟、永夜更糟……记忆……人们的记忆……“皮比？”她试探着，语气软了下来。“如果我们无法除去阿伦黛尔这个威胁——”“我们会除掉的，”艾莎坚定地打断。“可如果我们除不掉，”安娜温和地继续，“那是不是意味着……会不会也意味着……”她的声音哽住，目光越过山谷，望向那魁梧的采冰人和他的驯鹿。

sentences.en: Kristoff was taking in the sight of the talking, rolling, jumping trolls in amazement, as if he’d never seen them before.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫正惊叹地望着那些会说话、会滚动、会蹦跳的地精，仿佛从未见过他们。

sentences.en: Even Sven was looking at him strangely. “Will the people…will Kristoff…” “I’m sorry, Anna,” Grand Pabbie replied, his voice equally soft.
sentences.zh: 连斯文都怪异地盯着他。“人们会……克斯托夫会……””皮比用同样轻柔的声音答道：“我很抱歉，安娜。”

sentences.en: He didn’t have to continue.
sentences.zh: 他不必再说下去。

sentences.en: Anna forced herself to focus on the crystals around the trolls’ necks, hoping the illuminating colors would calm her.
sentences.zh: 安娜强迫自己盯着地精们颈间的晶体，盼着那些发光的颜色能让她平静。

sentences.en: All she wanted to do was scream.
sentences.zh: 她只想放声尖叫。

sentences.en: Why did Kristoff have to tell that scary story?
sentences.zh: 为什么克斯托夫非讲那个鬼故事不可？

sentences.en: Why? “But you must know some spell, or remedy, that can help people with their lost memories,” she insisted, her voice escalating in volume. “You’ve removed memories before.
sentences.zh: 为什么？“但你一定懂什么咒语或药方，能帮人找回丢失的记忆，”她坚持道，音量越来越高。“你们以前取走过记忆。

sentences.en: You must know how to put them back in, too!” Then again, she thought begrudgingly, the trolls never did recover all her erased memories, which they’d removed when she was a child to protect her from her sister’s magic.
sentences.zh: 你们一定也知道怎么放回去！”可她又悻悻地想，地精们从未找回她被抹去的全部记忆——那是她儿时为保护她免受姐姐魔力所害，被他们取走的。

sentences.en: To this day, her mind still had holes in it, precious missing moments of time spent with her sister she’d never get back.
sentences.zh: 时至今日，她的脑中仍有空洞，那些与姐姐共度、再也回不来的珍贵时光。

sentences.en: Grand Pabbie’s eyes flitted to Kristoff across the valley. “I am sorry, Your Majesty.
sentences.zh: 皮比的目光掠过山谷，落在克斯托夫身上。“我很抱歉，陛下。

sentences.en: Our own ways are hard enough to control.
sentences.zh: 我们自己的法子都够难控制了。

sentences.en: Trying to master another’s is almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 要去驾驭他人的，几乎不可能。

sentences.en: I cannot undo what the draugr has done.” “But that means…Kristoff,” Anna’s voice caught on the name.
sentences.zh: 我无法抹去亡灵所行之事。”“可那意味着……克斯托夫，”安娜念到这个名字，声音哽住了。

sentences.en: She thought of the mountain man who had stolen her heart with his love of ice, with the way he spoke on his reindeer’s behalf, with his enthusiastic love of unusual recipes.
sentences.zh: 她想起那个用对冰的爱、用替驯鹿代言的模样、用对古怪食谱的热忱偷走她心的山里人。

sentences.en: Kristoff.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫。

sentences.en: Her Kristoff .
sentences.zh: 她的克斯托夫。

sentences.en: Memories flashed through her mind.
sentences.zh: 记忆在她脑中闪过。

sentences.en: The first time they’d kissed after she’d presented him with his new sled, the first time they’d played charades.
sentences.zh: 她送他新雪橇后两人的初吻，还有第一次玩比手画脚。

sentences.en: The moment he had gotten down on one knee and asked her to marry him.
sentences.zh: 他单膝跪地、向她求婚的那一刻。

sentences.en: Kristoff— her Kristoff!
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫——她的克斯托夫！

sentences.en: Who could now barely remember who she was.
sentences.zh: 如今却几乎记不得她是谁。

sentences.en: Anna felt her legs buckle.
sentences.zh: 安娜觉得双腿发软。

sentences.en: The trolls and Elsa reached for her, but Anna stepped back, unwilling to be helped.
sentences.zh: 地精和艾莎伸手扶她，安娜却退开一步，不愿被人搀扶。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: She wasn’t willing to accept that Kristoff’s love for her could disappear because of some creature’s doing.
sentences.zh: 她不愿接受，克斯托夫对她的爱会因某个怪物而消失。

sentences.en: And she wasn’t about to let her people suffer from eternal night or never-ending storms, either.
sentences.zh: 她也绝不让她的子民承受永夜或无尽风暴。

sentences.en: She was queen of Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 她是阿伦黛尔的女王。

sentences.en: It was her job to fix this.
sentences.zh: 平息此事是她的职责。

sentences.en: Somehow.
sentences.zh: 总会有办法的。

sentences.en: Her mind raced, trying to remember Grand Pabbie’s words as he’d consulted with the stars.
sentences.zh: 她思绪飞转，努力回想皮比仰望星空时说的话。

sentences.en: The troll spoke in riddles.
sentences.zh: 地精说话总像谜语。

sentences.en: But there was usually a clue buried within them.
sentences.zh: 但谜底往往藏在其中。

sentences.en: What once did flee, now sets sail… To end this all, you must tell her tale… Her tale .
sentences.zh: “曾逃逸者，今启航……欲了此局，须述她事……她的事。”

sentences.en: But they’d told Sissel’s tale!
sentences.zh: 可他们早已讲过茜塞尔的故事！

sentences.en: At the campfire.
sentences.zh: 在营火旁。

sentences.en: And again in Arendelle… Suddenly, Anna’s mind flashed back to Oaken’s sauna as they were looking at the portraits of the two princesses.
sentences.zh: 后来在阿伦黛尔又讲过……忽然，安娜的思绪闪回奥肯的桑拿房，那时他们正看着两位公主的画像。

sentences.en: How Oaken had insisted Inger and Sissel were friends, not enemies as Kristoff and the others had claimed.
sentences.zh: 那时奥肯坚称英格和茜塞尔是朋友，而非克斯托夫等人所说的水火不容。

sentences.en: He’d also sworn that Inger had wanted to be a scientist, not a queen like her sister.
sentences.zh: 他还赌咒说英格想当科学家，而非像她姐姐那样当女王。

sentences.en: At the time, Anna had wondered if there could be more to their story.
sentences.zh: 当时安娜还纳闷，她们的故事会不会另有隐情。

sentences.en: Now she was convinced there must be.
sentences.zh: 如今她确信一定如此。

sentences.en: She turned to Elsa, her face showing her determination. “The answer is Sissel,” she exclaimed. “We need to figure out exactly what happened between her and Inger.
sentences.zh: 她转向艾莎，脸上写满决心。“答案在茜塞尔身上，”她朗声道。“我们得弄清她和英格之间到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: You heard Oaken.
sentences.zh: 你听到奥肯说的了。

sentences.en: He knew things about Inger we didn’t.
sentences.zh: 他知道一些我们不知道的英格的事。

sentences.en: There’s got to be a piece of the story we’re missing.
sentences.zh: 故事里一定有我们漏掉的一块。

sentences.en: And maybe whatever it is can help us understand Sissel and what she might want.” Elsa nodded. “It’s not a bad idea,” she agreed. “But how can we figure out what really happened?
sentences.zh: 也许那缺失的片段，能帮我们理解茜塞尔、理解她想要什么。”艾莎点头。“这主意不坏，”她赞同。“可我们怎么才能弄清真相？

sentences.en: Everyone seems to remember it differently.
sentences.zh: 似乎人人记得的版本都不一样。

sentences.en: And most of Arendelle doesn’t remember anything at all.” “True.
sentences.zh: 而阿伦黛尔大半的人根本什么都不记得了。”“没错。

sentences.en: But it must have been written down at one point,” Anna reminded her. “I mean, it had to be a big story, right?
sentences.zh: 可当年总该有文字记载，”安娜提醒她。“我是说，那准是个大新闻，对吧？

sentences.en: Two princesses visiting Arendelle, and one of them murdering the other?
sentences.zh: 两位公主造访阿伦黛尔，其中一个还谋害了另一个？

sentences.en: In fact, I bet it was front-page news.” Her sister’s eyes widened. “Of course!
sentences.zh: 说真的，我打赌它上了头版。”姐姐眼睛一亮。“当然！

sentences.en: The Village Crown.
sentences.zh: 《村庄之冠》。

sentences.en: Their archives go back for years.” “Maybe we can start there,” Anna said. “I mean, it’s worth a try, right?” “Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 他们的档案能追溯多年。”“也许我们可以从那儿入手，”安娜说。“我是说，值得一试，对吧？”“绝对。

sentences.en: We should get back to Arendelle as quickly as possible.” Elsa turned to Grand Pabbie. “Thank you for your help,” she said. “We’ll take it from here.” Grand Pabbie cleared his throat. “Your Majesties, I hope you find what you seek,” he said. “And quickly, too.” He glanced worriedly at Kristoff, who was wandering around aimlessly, happily chatting with rocks that appeared to be actual rocks—not trolls. “In the meantime, why don’t you leave Kristoff with us?
sentences.zh: 我们得尽快赶回阿伦黛尔。”艾莎转向皮比。“多谢相助，”她说。“接下来的交给我们。”皮比清了清嗓子。“陛下们，愿你们寻得所求，”他说。“而且要快。”他忧心忡忡地瞥了眼克斯托夫——那人正漫无目的地游荡，兴高采烈地和看似真石头的石头聊天，而非地精。“这期间，何不把克斯托夫留在我们这儿？

sentences.en: We can watch over him until you…resolve…the situation.” “What?
sentences.zh: 我们替你们照看他，直到你们……了结……此事。”“什么？

sentences.en: Leave Kristoff?” Anna cried, horrified.
sentences.zh: 留下克斯托夫？”安娜惊呼，满脸骇然。

sentences.en: Suddenly all her newfound confidence and excitement about solving the mystery seemed to shatter.
sentences.zh: 顷刻间，她方才解开谜团的新信心与兴奋仿佛碎了一地。

sentences.en: They wanted her to leave her fiancé behind? “He’ll be safe from the draugr here,” Elsa reminded her gently.
sentences.zh: 他们竟要她丢下未婚夫？“他在这儿，亡灵伤不到他，”艾莎温柔地提醒她。

sentences.en: Anna bowed her head.
sentences.zh: 安娜低下头。

sentences.en: She knew her sister was right.
sentences.zh: 她知道妹妹是对的。

sentences.en: But still, the thought of leaving him… “Okay.
sentences.zh: 可一想到要留下他……“好吧。

sentences.en: But you’ll have to keep Sven, too,” she blurted out. “Even if Kristoff doesn’t remember him, those two are never apart.” Bulda placed a hand on her knee. “Of course!
sentences.zh: 但你们也得留下斯文，”她脱口而出。“就算克斯托夫不记得它，他俩也从不分开。”布尔达把手搭在她膝上。“当然！

sentences.en: Sven is always welcome here….” Anna nodded, vacantly, her eyes locking on her fiancé, and her stomach did a somersault all over again. “Just give me a moment to say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 斯文永远受欢迎……。”安娜茫然地点头，目光锁在未婚夫身上，胃里又是一阵翻腾。“就让我道个别。

sentences.en: I mean, so long for now,” she corrected herself. “Of course,” said Elsa, her eyes filled with sympathy. “We’ll give you some space.” As much as Anna wanted breathing room, she wasn’t looking forward to this farewell.
sentences.zh: 我是说，暂别，”她纠正自己。“当然，”艾莎说，眼里满是同情。“我们给你点空间。”尽管安娜想要独处，她却一点不期待这场告别。

sentences.en: She made her way over to Kristoff and Sven, who were now at least chatting with an actual troll instead of a lifeless rock. “So you say you’re earning a crystal during this celebration?” Kristoff was saying. “What do these crystals do?” Little Rock laughed. “Oh, Kristoff!” He saw Anna and smiled. “Hey, your bride is here.” He then bounded off to find the others.
sentences.zh: 她走到克斯托夫和斯文身边，这会儿他们至少是在和一位真地精聊天，而非死石头。“你说你在这次庆典上要赢水晶？”克斯托夫正说着。“这些水晶有什么用？”小石笑了。“噢，克斯托夫！”他看见安娜，笑起来。“嘿，你新娘来了。”说完便蹦跳着找别人去了。

sentences.en: Kristoff did a double take at Anna. “My bride?” His cheeks reddened.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫对着安娜重新打量。“我的新娘？”他脸红了。

sentences.en: So did hers. “I’m not your bride,” she said quickly.
sentences.zh: 她脸也红了。“我不是你新娘，”她飞快地说。

sentences.en: Not yet, anyway, she thought. “But I am someone who cares about you very much.” She touched his cheeks, which were windburned and cold. “That’s why I’m going to leave you and Sven here with Bulda for a few days.
sentences.zh: 至少现在还不是，她心想。“但我是非常在乎你的人。”她摸了摸他被风吹得冰冷粗糙的脸颊。“所以我才要把你和斯文留在这儿，交给布尔达照顾几天。

sentences.en: Bulda will take good care of you till I get back.” “Okay,” Kristoff said happily. “And you’re coming back because…?” Anna felt her heart squeeze so tightly that she lost her breath.
sentences.zh: 布尔达会好好照顾你，直到我回来。”“好，”克斯托夫开心地说。“那你回来是因为……？”安娜的心猛地一缩，连气都透不过来。

sentences.en: But she would be brave.
sentences.zh: 可她要勇敢。

sentences.en: She would not let Kristoff see how scared she was for him and their kingdom.
sentences.zh: 她绝不让克斯托夫看见，她为他、为他们的王国有多害怕。

sentences.en: She would make things right.
sentences.zh: 她会扭转一切。

sentences.en: And then she’d never, ever let him tell another campfire story again.
sentences.zh: 然后她再也不、绝不再让他讲第二个营火故事。

sentences.en: Anna leaned in and kissed him on the lips. “Because I love you,” she said, holding his face close. “And you love me, and we’ve got a whole future to plan when I get back and you start remembering things again.” She stepped away, her heart hurting more than she thought was possible.
sentences.zh: 安娜倾身，吻上他的唇。“因为我爱你，”她贴着他的脸说。“而你也爱我，等我回来、你重新记起一切，我们还有整段未来要规划。”她退开一步，心痛得超乎想象。

sentences.en: Her voice was hoarse as she continued, “So stay safe till I do, okay?” “Okay,” said Kristoff. “Come along, Sven.
sentences.zh: 她声音沙哑地继续：“那就等我回来前乖乖平安，好吗？”“好，”克斯托夫说。“走吧，斯文。

sentences.en: Let’s go find this Bulda lady.” He paused, then turned to Anna. “Goodbye, Miss Bride!” Anna ached as she watched him wander through the crowd of trolls without a care in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们去找到那位布尔达女士。”他顿了顿，又转向安娜。“再见，新娘小姐！”安娜望着他若无其事地穿过地精人群，心如刀绞。

sentences.en: He doesn’t remember us, she thought.
sentences.zh: 他不记得我们了，她想。

sentences.en: He doesn’t remember me .
sentences.zh: 他不记得我了。

sentences.en: She wanted to cry, but now was when she needed to be strong.
sentences.zh: 她想哭，可此刻正需要坚强。

sentences.en: So instead, she squared her shoulders and watched from a growing distance as Bulda took his hands and within seconds was talking fast about some terrible-sounding soup that she swore would fix Kristoff and Sven right up.
sentences.zh: 于是她挺直肩膀，远远望着布尔达握住他的手，转眼就飞快念叨起某种听着吓人的汤，发誓能把克斯托夫和斯文治好。

sentences.en: Anna hoped Bulda was right, but she knew in her heart nothing would bring the love of her life back to her till this draugr business was finished once and for all.
sentences.zh: 安娜但愿布尔达说得对，可她心里清楚，在亡灵之事彻底了结前，没什么能把她此生挚爱唤回。

sentences.en: Snow had started falling again as they stopped to pick up Olaf at Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna and then made their way back into the village later in the day.
sentences.zh: 他们顺道去奥肯的杂货铺与桑拿房接上奥拉夫，当天晚些时候回到村里时，雪又下了起来。

sentences.en: When they arrived in Arendelle, lights were flickering in every window, but it didn’t appear as if anyone was working on the Polar Nights festivities.
sentences.zh: 抵达阿伦黛尔时，每扇窗里都闪着灯，却不见有人在为极夜庆典忙碌。

sentences.en: In fact, it was as if they didn’t remember the celebration at all.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们仿佛根本忘了这场庆典。

sentences.en: As they walked toward the newspaper office, they ran into Mattias, who was sitting beneath their parents’ tribute statue, staring down at a photo of himself and Halima, shaking his head, looking puzzled. “We’re back,” Anna told him. “How has everything been since we were gone?” Mattias glanced up at the two of them, a blank look on his face. “Everything is fine,” he said flatly. “Why wouldn’t it be?” Anna’s chest tightened. “Uh, I don’t know.
sentences.zh: 走向报社办公室时，他们撞见马蒂亚斯，他正坐在父母纪念像下，低头盯着一张自己和哈丽玛的照片，摇着头，一脸茫然。“我们回来了，”安娜告诉他。“我们走了以后，一切都还好吗？”马蒂亚斯抬头瞥了他们一眼，神情空白。“都好，”他平板地说。“能不好吗？”安娜胸口一紧。“呃，我说不好。

sentences.en: Pirates off our shores?
sentences.zh: 我们海岸边的海盗？

sentences.en: Crazy strong storms?
sentences.zh: 猛烈得离谱的风暴？

sentences.en: Weird zombies lurking in the shadows?” “I haven’t heard any of that,” Mattias said with a shrug; Anna’s stomach plummeted.
sentences.zh: 阴影里游荡的怪僵尸？”马蒂亚斯耸耸肩：“这些我可都没听说。”安娜的心直沉下去。

sentences.en: Mattias pushed the photo in his hands in their direction. “Do you happen to know who this is?
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯把手中照片朝他们一递。“你碰巧知道这是谁吗？

sentences.en: She looks so familiar, but I can’t place her.” “Someone special.
sentences.zh: 她看着好眼熟，可我对不上号了。”“一位特别的人。

sentences.en: I think you’ll find her over there,” Elsa said, helping him up from his seat and gently directing him toward Hudson’s Hearth—the tavern owned by the love of his life, whom he currently didn’t seem to remember.
sentences.zh: 我想你在那边能找到她，”艾莎说着，扶他起身，轻轻引他走向哈得逊炉边酒馆——那是由他此生挚爱所开、而他此刻似乎已不记得的酒馆。

sentences.en: Mattias nodded vacantly, then started toward the building.
sentences.zh: 马蒂亚斯茫然地点点头，朝那栋建筑走去。

sentences.en: But he seemed to forget where he was going before he was halfway there.
sentences.zh: 可还没走到一半，他似乎就忘了要去哪。

sentences.en: Suddenly he began walking in the other direction, whistling tunelessly.
sentences.zh: 忽然，他调头往反方向走，荒腔走板地吹起口哨。

sentences.en: Elsa shot Anna a concerned look. “This isn’t good,” she said. “If Mattias has lost his memories, too, there’s no one to look out for Arendelle.” “All the more reason we need to get to the bottom of Inger and Sissel’s story fast,” Anna declared, trying not to show how worried she was inside.
sentences.zh: 艾莎朝安娜投去忧心的一瞥。“这不妙，”她说。“要是马蒂亚斯也失了记忆，就没人照看阿伦黛尔了。”“更该尽快查明英格与茜塞尔故事的真相了，”安娜 declare，努力不让内心的担忧显露。

sentences.en: Her people were counting on her.
sentences.zh: 她的子民指望她。

sentences.en: Kristoff was counting on her—whether he remembered it or not.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫也指望她——不论他记不记得。

sentences.en: She couldn’t let any of them down.
sentences.zh: 她不能让任何一个人失望。

sentences.en: And I won’t, she told herself firmly.
sentences.zh: 我绝不会，她坚定地对自己说。

sentences.en: One way or another, we’re going to stop this draugr.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们要阻止这亡灵。

sentences.en: We’re going to make things right. “Come on,” she said to Elsa. “Let’s go find Wael.” “Oh, hello!” Wael said as he opened the door to the office of the Village Crown , which he lived above.
sentences.zh: 我们要拨乱反正。“走吧，”她对艾莎说。“去找韦尔。”“噢，你好！”韦尔说着，打开《村庄之冠》报社办公室的门——他就住在楼上。

sentences.en: Anna, Elsa, and Olaf filed in, taking in the smell of ink and warm paper that greeted them. “It’s so nice to have company!” Anna was startled.
sentences.zh: 安娜、艾莎和奥拉夫鱼贯而入，嗅着扑面而来的油墨与温纸气味。“有人作伴真好！”安娜吃了一惊。

sentences.en: The office was a mess, and papers were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 办公室里乱作一团，纸张到处都是。

sentences.en: That was not like Wael. “‘Nice to have company’?
sentences.zh: 这可不像韦尔。“‘有人作伴真好’？

sentences.en: This is new,” Olaf mumbled.
sentences.zh: 这可真新鲜，”奥拉夫嘟囔。

sentences.en: Wael was usually too busy to talk unless he was doing an interview, and when he was working, he was super serious. “Wael, we were actually hoping to ask you some questions about the paper,” Anna started right in.
sentences.zh: 韦尔平时忙得顾不上说话，除非在做采访，工作起来极其严肃。“韦尔，我们其实是想问你几个关于报纸的问题，”安娜直截了当地开口。

sentences.en: Wael’s face fell. “I’m afraid there is no new issue this week.
sentences.zh: 韦尔脸一沉。“恐怕这周没有新刊了。

sentences.en: I seem to have forgotten how to work my printing press…and I can’t find my ink.
sentences.zh: 我好像忘了怎么开印刷机……还找不到我的油墨。

sentences.en: Have you seen my pencil anywhere?” Elsa reached up and pulled it out from where it was tucked behind Wael’s ear. “Oh!” Wael chuckled. “Silly me!
sentences.zh: 你看见我的铅笔在哪吗？”艾莎伸手，从韦尔耳后抽出那支笔。“噢！”韦尔咯咯笑。“我真傻！

sentences.en: So forgetful today.” Anna glanced at her sister. “That’s what we were afraid of.” It appeared, like everyone else, Wael would be no help.
sentences.zh: 今天真是忘性大。”安娜瞥了姐姐一眼。“这正是我们担心的。”看来和别人一样，韦尔也帮不上忙。

sentences.en: Any research would have to be done on their own. “Wael,” Elsa addressed him. “We’re hoping to look at your archives.
sentences.zh: 任何查考都得靠他们自己了。“韦尔，”艾莎对他说。“我们想看看你的档案。

sentences.en: Where do you keep all the old issues of the paper?” Wael brightened. “In the back room!
sentences.zh: 旧报纸你都收在哪儿？”韦尔来了精神。“在后屋！

sentences.en: I have all of them, dating back to the paper’s first issue.” He hurried ahead of them, dodging stacks of this week’s forgotten issue. “The Village Crown has been around for…uh…” “Sixty years,” Olaf offered. “Right!” Wael said, smiling again. “Nice to meet fans of our work.” He opened the door to the back room, and Anna saw walls of bookshelves with papers stacked on them. “Take your time and look at anything you want,” Wael said. “I’ll be in the other room, um…working on something.” He chuckled to himself and disappeared. “Well,” Elsa said as she went to the first bookshelf. “At least a forgetful Wael is a friendly Wael.” “Okay, let’s divide and conquer,” Anna said, heading to the second bookshelf. “We’re looking for a story that ran about fifty years ago.” “That narrows it down,” said Olaf, hopping up on a stool and tackling the third bookcase.
sentences.zh: 全都有，从创刊号起一期不缺。”他抢在他们前头走，躲开这周忘了发出的那摞报纸。“《村庄之冠》创办有……呃……”“六十年了，”奥拉夫接话。“对！”韦尔又笑起来。“见到我们的读者真高兴。”他打开后屋的门，安娜看见满墙书架，上面摞着报纸。“慢慢看，随便翻，”韦尔说。“我去另一间，嗯……干点活。”他自顾自笑着消失了。“嗯，”艾莎走向第一个书架，“至少忘性的韦尔是个友善的韦尔。”“好，我们分头找，”安娜说着走向第二个书架。“我们找大约五十年前登的一篇报道。”“那范围窄多了，”奥拉夫跳上凳子，对付起第三个书架。

sentences.en: The search took a while, Anna’s patience wearing thin as Wael whistled happily in the next room.
sentences.zh: 搜寻花了好一阵，安娜的耐心渐失，隔壁韦尔倒是吹得欢。

sentences.en: Before long, the place looked like a hurricane had hit it, with stacks of papers now piled in disarray high on either side of them and scattered all over the floor.
sentences.zh: 不久，屋里像遭了飓风，纸堆高高歪在两侧，满地散落。

sentences.en: (Turned out, Olaf’s version of researching was a bit…messy.) They’d found all sorts of interesting stories from years past: their parents’ wedding announcement, the grand opening of Blodget’s Bakery, the tragic story of Queen Rita—King Runeard’s wife and their grandmother—and her strange disappearance when their father was just a small child.
sentences.zh: （结果，奥拉夫式的“查资料”有点……乱。）他们找到往年各种有趣报道：父母的结婚启事、布洛杰特面包店开业、丽塔王后——鲁纳德国王之妻、他们的祖母——的悲剧，以及她在父亲还是幼童时离奇失踪。

sentences.en: But nothing about the Vesterland sisters. “Ooh, here’s a story about your birth, Anna!” Olaf announced excitedly, pushing a crumpled paper in her direction.
sentences.zh: 却没有一篇讲维斯特兰姐妹。“噢，这儿有篇讲你出生的，安娜！”奥拉夫兴奋地喊，把一张皱巴巴的报纸推给她。

sentences.en: Anna scanned the front page, then frowned. “Uh, where?” she asked, confused. “It’s right there!” Olaf pointed to the bottom of the page. “Right under that really big article about ‘Old Blue Eyes’ the Pirate Queen threatening Arendelle’s shores!” “Of course it is,” Anna grumbled, her eyes falling to the much smaller headline, ARENDELLE WELCOMES THEIR SECOND PRINCESS!
sentences.zh: 安娜扫了眼头版，皱起眉。“呃，在哪？”她困惑地问。“就那儿！”奥拉夫指向页底。“就在那篇巨幅报道‘蓝眼老太’海盗女王威胁阿伦黛尔海岸的下面！”“果然，”安娜抱怨，目光落到小得多的标题上：阿伦黛尔欢迎二公主降生！

sentences.en: Clearly the Village Crown ’s obsession with pirates ran deep…. “I think I found something!” Elsa shouted, jumping down from a top shelf with several papers in her arms.
sentences.zh: 显然《村庄之冠》对海盗的执念深得很……“我好像找到了什么！”艾莎喊着，从顶层架子上跳下，怀里抱着几份报纸。

sentences.en: She dropped them on the table and pointed to the paper on top. “It’s an article about the Vesterland sisters visiting Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 她把报纸摔在桌上，指着最上面那份。“是篇讲维斯特兰姐妹造访阿伦黛尔的报道。

sentences.en: And the timing is right.” She laid out the newspaper on the table.
sentences.zh: 而且时间对得上。”她把报纸在桌上摊开。

sentences.en: Sure enough, there was a drawing of two girls—one with long hair tied up in complicated braids and one with a short bob—staring back at them.
sentences.zh: 果然，画着两个女孩——一个长发绾成复杂的辫子，一个留着短波波头——回望着他们。

sentences.en: Elsa touched the newspaper. “That’s them.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摸了摸报纸。“就是她们。

sentences.en: The same girls in Oaken’s portrait.” She pointed to the long-haired girl. “Inger,” she said, then moved her hand to the girl with the bob. “And Sissel.” “I have to say, Sissel’s a lot prettier as a real girl than a rotting zombie,” Olaf observed. “I mean, not that looks matter.
sentences.zh: 奥肯画像里那两个女孩。”她指着长发女孩。“英格，”她说，又把手移到短发女孩。“这是茜塞尔。”“我得说，茜塞尔当真姑娘时，比腐烂僵尸好看多了，”奥拉夫评道。“我是说，长相不重要。

sentences.en: It’s what’s in your heart that counts.” Anna stared at the picture of Sissel.
sentences.zh: 内心美才重要。”安娜盯着茜塞尔的画像。

sentences.en: It was hard to believe the creature that had attacked them had once been this beautiful girl.
sentences.zh: 很难相信，袭击过他们的那个怪物，曾是这样美丽的女孩。

sentences.en: She looked so happy, as if she hadn’t had a care in the world.
sentences.zh: 她看起来那么快乐，仿佛从来无忧无虑。

sentences.en: But then, so did Inger, who was smiling adoringly up at her sister in the picture, like she worshipped the ground Sissel walked on.
sentences.zh: 可英格也是——画里她仰望着姐姐，满眼爱慕，像在崇拜茜塞尔踩过的土地。

sentences.en: One thing was for sure: they definitely didn’t look like mortal enemies.
sentences.zh: 有一点确凿无疑：她们绝不像不共戴天的仇敌。

sentences.en: Elsa started reading the story aloud. “‘The Village Crown is pleased to report that the princesses of Vesterland, known as the Vesterland sisters, are coming to Arendelle for an important meeting with King Runeard.’” Anna frowned. “An important meeting?
sentences.zh: 艾莎大声念起报道。“‘《村庄之冠》欣悦报道：维斯特兰两位公主，人称维斯特兰姐妹，将赴阿伦黛尔与鲁纳德国王举行重要会晤。’”安娜皱眉。“重要会晤？

sentences.en: About what?” “It doesn’t say,” Elsa told her, flipping ahead to another story. “Here’s one about the accident, though.” The three of them leaned over the paper and read the article at the same time. “It’s just like everyone in the village has already been saying,” Anna said, knowing she sounded disappointed. “Inger and Sissel had an argument, and Sissel drowned.
sentences.zh: 谈什么？”艾莎告诉她：“没说。”翻到另一篇报道。“不过这儿有篇讲那场意外的。”三人一齐俯身，同时读起来。“就跟村里人一直说的一样，”安娜说，自知语气失望。“英格和茜塞尔吵了一架，茜塞尔淹死了。

sentences.en: Inger was charged with her murder, and Grandfather had her sent away on a prison ship to be banished.
sentences.zh: 英格被控谋杀，祖父把她送上囚船流放。

sentences.en: It went down at sea in a storm before it made it to its destination.
sentences.zh: 船在驶向目的地前，于风暴中沉没。

sentences.en: There’s nothing else to report.” “If Inger is dead, then what could Sissel be after by appearing now?” Elsa asked. “Not revenge, clearly.” “I don’t know.
sentences.zh: 再没别的了。”“要是英格死了，那茜塞尔现在现身想图什么？”艾莎问。“显然不是复仇。”“我不知道。

sentences.en: But this isn’t telling us anything new.” She put the paper back down. “We need to find out more about the sisters themselves.
sentences.zh: 可这也没告诉我们新东西。”她把报纸放下。“我们得进一步了解姐妹俩本身。

sentences.en: Or what they were arguing about that was so bad it led to murder.” “Well, we won’t find that here,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 或是她们吵得那么凶、以至于闹出人命的原因。”“唉，这儿可找不着了，”艾莎说。

sentences.en: Anna nodded slowly, feeling discouraged. “And clearly no one in Arendelle remembers anything,” she began.
sentences.zh: 安娜缓缓点头，有些气馁。“而且阿伦黛尔显然没人记得任何事，”她开口。

sentences.en: Then a thought came to her. “That’s it!
sentences.zh: 忽然她有了主意。“对了！

sentences.en: Why didn’t I think of this before?” “What?” Elsa asked, looking puzzled. “We need to go to Vesterland!” Anna said, getting excited. “Maybe King Jonas and Mari know why Inger and Sissel were here in Arendelle or what they were arguing about.
sentences.zh: 我之前怎么没想到？””什么？”艾莎困惑地问。“我们得去维斯特兰！”安娜兴奋地说。“也许乔纳斯国王和玛丽知道，英格和茜塞尔来阿伦黛尔所为何事，又为何争吵。
