sentences.en: In fact, they got lost in the dark woods three times before finally stumbling their way to the small, crude wooden statue honoring the two Vesterland princesses plopped down on a stone pedestal at a bend in the river.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们在漆黑的树林里迷路了三次，才终于跌跌撞撞地走到那座简陋的小木像前——那是立在河湾石座上、纪念维斯特兰两位公主的雕像。

sentences.en: Elsa pointed to it with a cheer and Anna let out a sigh of relief, dropping off Havski and rushing over to it.
sentences.zh: 艾莎欢快地指了指它，安娜长舒一口气，翻身跳下哈夫斯基，冲了过去。

sentences.en: She placed her hands on her hips, examining the carved wood. “You know, maybe Sissel just wants a new memorial,” she remarked, poking at the spot where Sissel’s arm should have been.
sentences.zh: 她双手叉腰，打量着雕刻的木头。"你看，说不定西塞尔只是想要一座新纪念碑呢，"她戳着本该是西塞尔手臂的位置说道。

sentences.en: It had clearly broken off at some point over the years, and some of the wood was rotted clear through. “I mean, this one’s kind of falling apart.” “Imagine if it were that simple.” Elsa smiled as she slipped off the Water Nokk and stepped up to Anna.
sentences.zh: 显然这些年里它某处断裂过，有些木头已经烂透了。"我是说，这座都快散架了。""要是真有那么简单就好了。"艾莎笑着从水马背上滑下，走到安娜身边。

sentences.en: She squinted at the wooden memorial, which had clearly seen better days.
sentences.zh: 她眯起眼睛看着那座木碑，它显然已风光不再。

sentences.en: She supposed fifty years of exposure to the elements would do that to any piece of wood.
sentences.zh: 她想，任凭风吹雨打五十年，再结实的木头也免不了这样。

sentences.en: Still, the lettering at the bottom was clear enough to read.
sentences.zh: 不过，底部的刻字还算清晰，能看得清。

sentences.en: BELOVED PRINCESSES.
sentences.zh: "至爱公主。"

sentences.en: MAY YOU REST IN PEACE.
sentences.zh: "愿你们安息。"

sentences.en: Hopefully they could make that happen—and soon, too. “This is definitely the same spot I saw in my vision,” Elsa mused, her eyes rising to the rapidly flowing water. “I remember that boulder just offshore.
sentences.zh: 但愿她们能如愿——而且越快越好。"这绝对就是我在幻象里看到的地方，"艾莎若有所思地说，目光投向湍急的水流。"我记得离岸边那块大石头。

sentences.en: And that tree is much larger now, but it was definitely there,” she added, pointing to a large oak with branches that hung over the river.
sentences.zh: "那棵树现在大多了，但当时肯定就在那儿，"她补充道，指着河上方垂着枝条的一棵大橡树。

sentences.en: She nodded. “Yes, this is definitely the spot where Sissel drowned.” “But did Inger do it?” Anna asked. “That’s the question we need answered.
sentences.zh: 她点点头。"对，这里就是西塞尔溺亡的确切地点。""可那是英格干的吗？"安娜问。"这才是我们需要解答的问题。

sentences.en: And if she did—why?
sentences.zh: "如果真是她——又为什么要这么做？"

sentences.en: Everything we’ve learned about the sisters so far makes it seem like they were close.
sentences.zh: "到目前为止，我们了解到的一切都表明姐妹俩感情很好。"

sentences.en: That they loved each other.” “Right.
sentences.zh: "她们彼此相爱。""没错。

sentences.en: I mean, sure, they disagreed on a few things, but so what?” Elsa asked. “I mean, we disagree all the time.” “Usually about you putting yourself in danger,” Anna pointed out.
sentences.zh: "我是说，她们固然在一些事上有分歧，但那又怎样呢？"艾莎反问。"咱们不也整天意见不合吗。""通常都是因为你让自己陷进危险，"安娜指出。

sentences.en: Elsa snorted.
sentences.zh: 艾莎嗤笑一声。

sentences.en: She turned back to the memorial. “In my Ahtohallan vision, I saw Sissel struggling in the water.
sentences.zh: 她转回身对着纪念碑。"在阿托哈兰的幻象里，我看见西塞尔在水中挣扎。

sentences.en: But we need to go back further.
sentences.zh: "但我们需要回溯到更早之前。

sentences.en: To hear what they were fighting about and what happened.
sentences.zh: "去听清她们当时在争执什么，又发生了什么。

sentences.en: That’s the only way to know for sure.” She turned to the river.
sentences.zh: "只有这样才能确凿地知道真相。"她转向河流。

sentences.en: It was rushing past them pretty hard, tossing around large chunks of ice in the current.
sentences.zh: 河水湍急地从他们身边奔涌而过，激流卷起大块的浮冰。

sentences.en: Very unlike the slow, serene section they were familiar with that ran by Arendelle’s town center.
sentences.zh: 和流经阿伦黛尔镇中心那段他们熟悉的平缓宁静的水面大不相同。

sentences.en: Elsa guessed there might be a glacier nearby, feeding the river with melted snow.
sentences.zh: 艾莎猜测附近或许有座冰川，用融雪为河流补给水量。

sentences.en: Even a good swimmer would have a tough time keeping their head above water there.
sentences.zh: 即便水性再好的人，在那里也难把头露出水面。

sentences.en: She dropped her hand into the river and felt the current through her fingers. “Do you sense anything?” Anna asked eagerly.
sentences.zh: 她把手探进河里，用手指感受着水流。"你感觉到什么了吗？"安娜急切地问。

sentences.en: Elsa shook her head. “Just freezing cold water,” she replied, frowning.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摇摇头。"只有刺骨的冰水，"她皱着眉回答。

sentences.en: She closed her eyes, thinking of Sissel and Inger.
sentences.zh: 她闭上眼睛，想着西塞尔和英格。

sentences.en: Trying to imagine them on this shore.
sentences.zh: 努力想象她们在这岸边的模样。

sentences.en: Arguing.
sentences.zh: 争吵着。

sentences.en: What were they arguing about?
sentences.zh: 她们在吵些什么？

sentences.en: But nothing came to her.
sentences.zh: 可她什么也没感觉到。

sentences.en: It was then that she realized the problem.
sentences.zh: 直到这时她才意识到问题所在。

sentences.en: Water had memory.
sentences.zh: 水是有记忆的。

sentences.en: But this particular current wasn’t the same water that had been here when Sissel had drowned.
sentences.zh: 但这股特别的水流，已不是西塞尔溺亡时停留在这里的那片水了。

sentences.en: River water was constantly moving, always changing.
sentences.zh: 河水始终在流动，永远在变化。

sentences.en: If Elsa were in Ahtohallan, maybe she could manage to pull something up with the help of the spirit of memories.
sentences.zh: 如果艾莎身在阿托哈兰，或许能借助记忆之灵的力量，翻找出些什么。

sentences.en: But here—she was on her own, and she wasn’t sure it was going to work.
sentences.zh: 但在这里——只能靠她自己，她没把握能成功。

sentences.en: Elsa slumped onto the riverbank, feeling discouraged.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一屁股坐在河岸边，满心沮丧。

sentences.en: What good were her powers if she couldn’t use them to help anyone?
sentences.zh: 如果她的魔力帮不上任何人的忙，那又有什么用？

sentences.en: Had this all been a dead end?
sentences.zh: 难道这一切都是死路一条？

sentences.en: Frustration began to rise inside of her.
sentences.zh: 一股挫败感在她心底升起。

sentences.en: She squeezed her hands into fists. “Hey!
sentences.zh: 她攥紧双手成拳。"喂！

sentences.en: Elsa!
sentences.zh: "艾莎！

sentences.en: Relax.” She felt Anna by her side, putting her arms around her. “It’s okay.” “It’s not okay!” Elsa snapped. “I need to figure this out!” She squirmed free of Anna’s grasp and dunked her hands in the freezing cold water again.
sentences.zh: "放松点。"她感到安娜来到身边，用双臂搂住她。"没事的。""这根本不好！"艾莎厉声说。"我得把这件事查清楚！"她挣脱安娜的怀抱，再次把双手浸入刺骨的冰水中。

sentences.en: Maybe if she could go deeper, she could find something.
sentences.zh: 也许潜得更深些，她就能找到些什么。

sentences.en: She squeezed her eyes shut.
sentences.zh: 她紧紧闭上眼睛。

sentences.en: Trying, trying.
sentences.zh: 努力着，努力着。

sentences.en: SPLASH!
sentences.zh: "扑通！"

sentences.en: Elsa screamed as she lost her balance, tumbling headfirst into the icy river.
sentences.zh: 艾莎失去平衡，一头栽进冰冷的河里，惊声尖叫。

sentences.en: She thrashed around, trying to lodge her feet against the slippery stones, while choking on a mouthful of dirty water.
sentences.zh: 她拼命扑腾，想用脚抵住滑溜的石头，却被一口脏水呛得喘不过气。

sentences.en: The current was strong, dragging her downstream fast. “Anna!” she cried, trying to use her magic to freeze the rushing water.
sentences.zh: 水流湍急，飞快把她往下游拖。"安娜！"她喊道，试图用魔力冻结奔涌的河水。

sentences.en: But nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 可什么事也没发生。

sentences.en: It was as if she were wearing gloves, even though she wasn’t.
sentences.zh: 就好像她戴着手套似的——尽管她并没有戴。

sentences.en: She’d probably drained her powers reaching so deep, and now they were fizzling out again.
sentences.zh: 大概是探得太深耗尽了魔力，如今它们又快要熄灭了。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: "哦，不。

sentences.en: No, no, no! “Anna!
sentences.zh: "不，不，不！"安娜！

sentences.en: Help!” she cried again, knowing she sounded scared.
sentences.zh: "救命！"她又喊了一声，知道自己听起来很惊恐。

sentences.en: Desperate.
sentences.zh: 绝望极了。

sentences.en: She fought to keep her head above water, to suck in air in the moments she could.
sentences.zh: 她拼命把头露出水面，抓住空当拼命吸气。

sentences.en: But instead, she was gulping river water too fast, choking and sputtering as she tried again to find the river’s bottom.
sentences.zh: 可恰恰相反，她大口吞着河水，呛得连连咳嗽，又再次想探到河底。

sentences.en: But it was deep here and her feet only kicked uselessly as the current dragged her further down.
sentences.zh: 可这里水很深，她的脚只是徒劳地乱蹬，水流把她往更深处拽。

sentences.en: Her body began to weaken.
sentences.zh: 她的身体开始发软。

sentences.en: The riverbank seemed miles away. “Elsa!
sentences.zh: 河岸仿佛远在数英里之外。"艾莎！

sentences.en: I’ve got you!” Suddenly, she felt strong arms grab her, dragging her to the shore.
sentences.zh: "我抓住你了！"突然，她感到一双有力的手臂抓住她，把她拖上岸。

sentences.en: Anna heaved her onto dry land, then rolled her over, slapping her hard on the back until she hacked up all the dirty water.
sentences.zh: 安娜把她拖到干地上，翻过身来，用力拍打她的后背，直到她把脏水全咳出来。

sentences.en: Elsa’s heart pumped madly in her chest as she sucked in breath after breath of clean air. “Are you okay?” Anna’s voice sounded very concerned. “Elsa!
sentences.zh: 艾莎的心在胸口狂跳，一口接一口地吸着干净的空气。"你没事吧？"安娜的声音里满是担忧。"艾莎！

sentences.en: Talk to me!” She struggled to sit up. “I think so.” She swallowed hard, trying to stop her body from shaking in a mixture of terror and cold. “I just leaned in too far.” “Yeah, I saw.” Anna pursed her lips together. “You scared me half to death.
sentences.zh: "跟我说说话！"她挣扎着坐起来。"我想没事。"她艰难地咽了口唾沫，想止住因恐惧和寒冷而颤抖的身体。"我只是探得太往前了。""嗯，我看见了。"安娜抿紧嘴唇。"你差点把我吓死。

sentences.en: I thought…” She trailed off, unable to continue.
sentences.zh: "我还以为……"她话音渐弱，说不下去了。

sentences.en: But Elsa knew exactly what she’d been thinking.
sentences.zh: 但艾莎完全知道她在想什么。

sentences.en: That she’d almost shared Sissel’s fate.
sentences.zh: 她差一点就步了西塞尔的后尘。

sentences.en: Elsa wrung out her white dress, staring at the river ruefully. “I guess now I understand how Sissel drowned,” she said. “That current is rough.” “Lucky for you, you have a strong sister.” Anna gathered up a small pile of wood and leaves. “Bruni?” she called out to the Fire Spirit when she was finished. “Want to help warm up your girl?” The spirit leapt onto the small pile, easily igniting it with its flames.
sentences.zh: 艾莎拧干白色长裙上的水，懊恼地盯着河水。"我想现在我明白西塞尔是怎么淹死的了，"她说。"那水流太猛了。""你走运，有个强壮的妹妹。"安娜捡起一小堆木柴和枯叶。"火灵？"收拾好后她唤来火灵。"想帮忙给你家姑娘暖暖身子吗？"火灵跳上那小堆柴，轻而易举地用火焰把它点燃。

sentences.en: Soon they had a small fire giving off a nice hot glow.
sentences.zh: 很快，一小堆火就散发出了温暖明亮的光。

sentences.en: Elsa sighed gratefully, warming her hands.
sentences.zh: 艾莎感激地叹了口气，暖着手。

sentences.en: Her heart, however, was still beating very fast. “So much for that plan,” she said sorrowfully, giving the river an annoyed look.
sentences.zh: 不过她的心跳仍快得厉害。"那个计划算是泡汤了，"她难过地说，恼火地瞪了河水一眼。

sentences.en: She hugged her chest. “Sorry I dragged you all the way out here,” she said. “It was probably a dumb idea.
sentences.zh: 她抱紧胸口。"抱歉把你一路拖到这儿来，"她说。"这大概是个蠢主意。

sentences.en: I just thought…I mean, I remember pulling the memory from our parents’ ship.
sentences.zh: "我只是想……我是说，我记得从咱父母的船上抽取过记忆。

sentences.en: But that water had been there for years—so the memories were still there, inside of it.
sentences.zh: "可那水是多年积下的——所以记忆还停留在里面，封存在水中。

sentences.en: This water is all new.
sentences.zh: "这里的水全是新的。

sentences.en: There’s nothing to pull from it.
sentences.zh: "没什么可抽取的。

sentences.en: I’m sorry, Anna.
sentences.zh: "对不起，安娜。

sentences.en: I really wanted to figure out Sissel’s story so we could end this.” Her voice broke. “Water has memory,” Anna whispered thoughtfully. “Yes.
sentences.zh: "我真的很想弄清楚西塞尔的故事，好让这一切结束。"她的声音哽咽了。"水是有记忆的，"安娜若有所思地轻声说。"是的。

sentences.en: I just said that.
sentences.zh: "我刚说过。

sentences.en: But—” “But the water here isn’t the same.
sentences.zh: "可——""可这里的水不一样。

sentences.en: You need something that might have remnants of water from back then, right?” “Right.
sentences.zh: "你需要能保留着当年那水的残余的东西，对吗？""对。

sentences.en: But that’s impossible.
sentences.zh: "可那不可能。

sentences.en: It was fifty years ago.” “Maybe not.” Elsa cocked her head in question.
sentences.zh: "那都是五十年前的事了。""未必吧。"艾莎歪着头疑惑地问。

sentences.en: Anna lifted Sissel’s locket from around her neck and held it out to her sister. “Remember how the portraits seemed warped?” she said. “Like they’d been underwater?
sentences.zh: 安娜从脖子上取下西塞尔的吊坠，递给妹妹。"记得画像看起来有点变形吗？"她说。"像是在水下泡过？

sentences.en: Maybe they still have a bit of it in them.” “Anna!
sentences.zh: "说不定里面还留着一点当年的水。""安娜！

sentences.en: You’re a genius!” Elsa plucked the locket from her sister’s fingers, palming it in her hands. “The Figels told us Sissel never went anywhere without her locket.
sentences.zh: "你真是个天才！"艾莎从妹妹指间拈起吊坠，攥在掌心。"菲格尔斯告诉我们，西塞尔去哪儿都戴着她的吊坠。

sentences.en: Which meant she must have been wearing it when she drowned.” Her breath caught in her throat as hope surged through her.
sentences.zh: "也就是说，她溺亡时一定还戴着它。"希望涌上心头，她屏住了呼吸。

sentences.en: She tried to tell herself not to get too excited, but she couldn’t help it.
sentences.zh: 她想让自己别太激动，却控制不住。

sentences.en: She wrapped her fingers around the locket.
sentences.zh: 她用手指握住吊坠。

sentences.en: Then she closed her eyes, searching deep for her powers.
sentences.zh: 然后闭上眼睛，向深处探寻自己的魔力。

sentences.en: For a moment, she felt nothing and worried they had fizzled again.
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬，她什么也感觉不到，担心魔力又熄灭了。

sentences.en: But then, slowly, the familiar feeling began to rise inside of her. “It’s working!
sentences.zh: 可随后，那熟悉的感觉慢慢在身体里升起。"有反应了！

sentences.en: Elsa, it’s working!” Elsa’s eyes flew open.
sentences.zh: "艾莎，有反应了！"艾莎猛地睁开眼睛。

sentences.en: Sure enough, a small mist seemed to be rising from her closed hand.
sentences.zh: 果然，一缕薄雾似乎正从她握紧的手里升起。

sentences.en: She released her fingers, opening them up one by one.
sentences.zh: 她松开手指，一根根张开。

sentences.en: The mist was twining out from the locket.
sentences.zh: 薄雾正从吊坠里缠绕而出。

sentences.en: And suddenly they could see it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 突然间，他们看得一清二楚。

sentences.en: Two girls.
sentences.zh: 两个女孩。

sentences.en: One with long hair tied up in complicated braids.
sentences.zh: 一个头发很长，编成复杂的辫子。

sentences.en: The other with a short bob. “Inger and Sissel,” Elsa breathed.
sentences.zh: 另一个留着齐耳短发。"英格和西塞尔，"艾莎轻声说。

sentences.en: Anna looked as mesmerized as she felt.
sentences.zh: 安娜和她一样看得入了迷。

sentences.en: Even more so when the voices began to rise in the air. “Inger, you need to stop arguing with him!
sentences.zh: 当空中的声音响起时，她更着迷了。"英格，你别再跟他争吵了！

sentences.en: It’s not going to work.” “But, Sissel, we have to try!
sentences.zh: "那没用的。""可是西塞尔，我们得试试啊！

sentences.en: He’s already started clearing land.
sentences.zh: "他已经开始清理土地了。

sentences.en: If he builds that dam, it’s going to destroy the Enchanted Forest and all the Northuldra’s territory.
sentences.zh: "要是他建起那座水坝，就会毁掉魔法森林和北地人的全部领地。

sentences.en: It’ll be an environmental disaster.” Elsa gasped.
sentences.zh: "那会是场环境灾难。"艾莎倒吸一口凉气。

sentences.en: So they had been fighting about the dam that day!
sentences.zh: 原来那天她们争执的就是那座水坝！

sentences.en: And Inger definitely wasn’t in favor of it. “Look, I understand.
sentences.zh: 而且英格显然并不赞成它。"听我说，我明白的。

sentences.en: I really do,” Sissel broke in. “But what are we going to do?
sentences.zh: "我真的明白，"西塞尔插话道。"可我们又能怎么办？

sentences.en: King Runeard is never going to listen to us.
sentences.zh: "鲁内亚国王绝不会听我们的。

sentences.en: And if we try to fight him on this, he’s going to punish Vesterland.
sentences.zh: "要是我们在这件事上跟他作对，他就会惩罚维斯特兰。

sentences.en: Our actual people.
sentences.zh: "我们真正的子民。

sentences.en: I mean, I care about reindeer and bunnies and all that, too, but I also care about our citizens.
sentences.zh: "我是说，我也在乎驯鹿、兔子那些，可我同样在乎我们的百姓。

sentences.en: As their future queen, I need to protect them.
sentences.zh: "作为未来的女王，我必须保护他们。

sentences.en: Arendelle controls the port—all the food and supplies and medicine coming in from other kingdoms.
sentences.zh: "阿伦黛尔掌控着港口——所有从其他王国运进来的食物、物资和药品。

sentences.en: Without that, we will suffer greatly.” “We will also suffer if all the animals die or migrate further north,” Inger argued. “What are we going to hunt for food?
sentences.zh: "没有这些，我们会吃大苦头。""要是动物全死光或往更北迁徙，我们也会遭殃，"英格争辩道。"到时候我们靠什么打猎当口粮？

sentences.en: He has to know the greater impacts his dam will have on our lands.” Sissel sighed. “He already knows.
sentences.zh: "他肯定知道那水坝会给我们的土地带来多大的影响。"西塞尔叹了口气。"他早就知道了。

sentences.en: He just doesn’t care.” “You have to make him care!
sentences.zh: "他只是不在乎罢了。""你得让他上心！

sentences.en: That’s what a queen would do!” The sisters stared at one another, clearly at a standoff.
sentences.zh: "那才是一位女王该做的事！"姐妹俩互相盯着，显然僵持不下。

sentences.en: Elsa glanced over at Anna, who was watching the scene with horrified eyes. “Yeah, well, maybe you should be queen, then!” Sissel shot back. “If you’re such an expert and all!” “You know I don’t want that,” Inger protested, sounding hurt. “And you know I think you’ll be an amazing queen.
sentences.zh: "是啊，那说不定你才该当女王！"西塞尔回嘴道。"既然你这么在行！""你知道我不想要那个，"英格委屈地抗议，"而且你知道，我觉得你会是一位了不起的女王。

sentences.en: You’re already an amazing sister.
sentences.zh: "你已经是一位了不起的姐姐了。

sentences.en: I’m just trying to help.
sentences.zh: "我只是想帮忙。

sentences.en: Don’t shut me out.
sentences.zh: "别把我推开。

sentences.en: Please!” For a moment, Sissel just bristled.
sentences.zh: "求你了！"西塞尔一时语塞。

sentences.en: Then her shoulders began to slump.
sentences.zh: 随后她的肩膀垮了下来。

sentences.en: She sighed deeply, then gave her sister an apologetic look. “I’m sorry.
sentences.zh: 她深深叹了口气，愧疚地看着妹妹。"对不起。

sentences.en: I didn’t mean that.
sentences.zh: "我不是那个意思。

sentences.en: I love you; you know that.” “And I love you.” Inger reached for Sissel’s hand. “We’ll figure this out.
sentences.zh: "我爱你，你知道的。""我也爱你。"英格握住西塞尔的手。"我们会想出办法的。

sentences.en: One way or another.” Elsa watched, entranced, as the two sisters embraced on the side of the river.
sentences.zh: "总会有办法的。"艾莎看得入迷，两个姐妹在河边相拥。

sentences.en: No longer fighting with one another, just hugging each other tightly.
sentences.zh: 不再争执，只是紧紧相拥。

sentences.en: Just like she and Anna did after they argued. “So it’s true.
sentences.zh: 就像她和安娜吵完架后那样。"这么说传说是真的。

sentences.en: Inger didn’t want to be queen.
sentences.zh: "英格并不想当女王。

sentences.en: She was just trying to help Sissel,” Anna whispered, also looking on in awe. “She loved her sister.” “Then what happened between them that could have led to Sissel’s death?” Elsa asked. “I don’t get it.” “Just keep watching!” Anna urged. “There’s got to be more.” But the vision was already fading.
sentences.zh: "她只是想帮西塞尔，"安娜也敬畏地看着，轻声说。"她爱她姐姐。""那她们之间究竟发生了什么，才会导致西塞尔的死？"艾莎问。"我想不通。""接着看下去！"安娜催促道。"肯定还有下文。"可幻象已经开始消散。

sentences.en: The magic drained from her fingers.
sentences.zh: 魔力从她指尖退去。

sentences.en: Elsa gritted her teeth, trying to keep it going, but she could feel it falling away.
sentences.zh: 艾莎咬紧牙关，想维持住它，却感到它在一点点消逝。

sentences.en: The mist began to sputter from the necklace.
sentences.zh: 薄雾从项链里断断续续地冒出。

sentences.en: The vision began to dim.
sentences.zh: 幻象开始暗淡。

sentences.en: She squeezed her eyes shut, straining.
sentences.zh: 她紧闭双眼，全力支撑。

sentences.en: Feeling the ice crackle on her skin.
sentences.zh: 感到冰晶在皮肤上噼啪作响。

sentences.en: No!
After all this, she couldn’t lose it now.
sentences.zh: "折腾了这么久，她现在决不能功亏一篑。

sentences.en: She just couldn’t! “Elsa, look!” Elsa’s eyes shot open.
sentences.zh: "她绝不能！"艾莎，看！"艾莎猛地睁开眼睛。

sentences.en: Her mouth gaped, realizing they were no longer alone.
sentences.zh: 她目瞪口呆——意识到他们不再孤单。

sentences.en: Standing by the memorial statue, seeming to have come out of nowhere, was the draugr itself.
sentences.zh: 立在纪念碑旁、仿佛凭空出现的，正是那亡灵本尊。

sentences.en: Where had it come from?
sentences.zh: 它从哪来的？

sentences.en: Had it followed them here?
sentences.zh: 是跟着他们来的吗？

sentences.en: This was not good.
sentences.zh: 这可不妙。

sentences.en: Not good at all. “Anna, back away slowly.
sentences.zh: "一点都不妙。"安娜，慢慢退后。

sentences.en: Don’t make any sudden moves.
sentences.zh: "别突然动作。

sentences.en: I’ll distract it and then find you later,” Elsa whispered to her sister, her mind racing with a plan.
sentences.zh: "我会引开它，之后再找你，"艾莎压低声音对妹妹说，脑中飞速盘算着计划。

sentences.en: Ice hadn’t stopped the draugr last time.
sentences.zh: 上次冰没能挡住亡灵。

sentences.en: But maybe it could slow the creature down enough for them to get away.
sentences.zh: 但或许能把它拖得够久，让他们脱身。

sentences.en: She glanced at Anna, who hadn’t moved. “What are you waiting for?” she cried, fear pounding in her heart. “Go!” But Anna didn’t go.
sentences.zh: 她瞥了眼安娜，对方却没动。"你还在等什么？"她心怦怦直跳地喊道。"快走！"可安娜没走。

sentences.en: Instead, she stepped between her sister and the draugr. “What are you doing?” Elsa choked out, horrified.
sentences.zh: 相反，她挡在了妹妹和亡灵之间。"你在干什么？"艾莎惊恐得声音发哽。

sentences.en: Her eyes locked onto the draugr, waiting for it to strike.
sentences.zh: 她的眼睛死死盯住亡灵，等着它出手。

sentences.en: Anna was too close.
sentences.zh: 安娜离得太近了。

sentences.en: Far too close.
sentences.zh: 近得过头了。

sentences.en: It would only take one swipe of the creature’s claws, and…“Anna, it’s going to attack you!” Or worse… “No,” Anna said firmly, keeping her eyes glued to it. “I think if it was, it would have done it already.
sentences.zh: 只要那怪物利爪一挥……"安娜，它要攻击你了！"更糟的是……"不会的，"安娜坚定地说，目光始终黏在它身上。"要是会，它早就动手了。

sentences.en: I think it wants us here.
sentences.zh: "我想它正是要我们留在这里。

sentences.en: I think it has something to show us.
sentences.zh: "我想它有东西要给我们看。

sentences.en: The draugr was the one who left us the locket,” she reminded Elsa. “Maybe it hoped you could pull something from it.
sentences.zh: "是那亡灵把吊坠留给我们的，"她提醒艾莎。"也许它希望你能从中翻出些什么。

sentences.en: In fact, maybe that’s why it’s been haunting us all along.
sentences.zh: "其实，也许这正是它一直缠着我们的原因。

sentences.en: Because you’re the only one with the power to see into the past.
sentences.zh: "因为你是唯一有力量窥见过去的人。

sentences.en: To discover the true story behind the sisters.” “Sissssster…” the creature moaned, its eyes seemingly aflame when saying the word. “Sisssssster.
sentences.zh: "去发现姐妹俩背后的真相。""姐……姐……"那怪物低吟，念这个词时眼睛仿佛燃着火。"姐……姐。

sentences.en: Minnnnne.” The draugr raised a rotted finger, pointing it toward the locket in Elsa’s hand.
sentences.zh: "我……的。"亡灵举起一只腐烂的手指，指向艾莎手中的吊坠。

sentences.en: For a moment, nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，什么也没发生。

sentences.en: Then, suddenly, the sputtering stream of mist began to thicken, get stronger. “Yes!” Anna cried out in excitement. “Yes!” Elsa watched in amazement as more mist began to spill from the necklace, onto the riverbank, rebuilding the vision they’d been watching before.
sentences.zh: 接着，突然间，那断断续续的雾流开始变浓、变强。"对了！"安娜兴奋地叫道。"对了！"艾莎惊奇地看着更多薄雾从项链涌出，落向河岸，重建起他们刚才看到的幻象。

sentences.en: Slowly, with their combined magic, the vision grew more solid, real.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，在两者魔力的融合下，幻象变得越来越凝实、真切。

sentences.en: As if the two girls were standing right in front of them. “Now, let’s see what really happened that day,” Anna declared, her voice high-pitched with excitement.
sentences.zh: 仿佛那两个女孩就站在他们面前。"现在，让我们看看那天到底发生了什么，"安娜宣称，声音因兴奋而拔高。

sentences.en: Biting her lower lip, Elsa turned back to the scene playing out in front of them, concentrating hard to keep the magic flowing.
sentences.zh: 艾莎咬着下唇，转回身面对正在眼前上演的场景，全力集中精神让魔力持续流动。

sentences.en: Inger and Sissel were stepping out of their embrace, smiling at each other. “I’m sorry,” Inger said. “I don’t want to fight with you.” “No, I’m sorry!” Sissel exclaimed. “You are right.
sentences.zh: 英格和西塞尔正从相拥中分开，相视而笑。"对不起，"英格说。"我不想跟你吵。""不，是我对不起！"西塞尔喊道。"你是对的。

sentences.en: I’ve been a coward, not wanting to face Runeard.
sentences.zh: "我一直是个懦夫，不敢面对鲁内亚。

sentences.en: He scares me.
sentences.zh: "他让我害怕。

sentences.en: But not as much as the idea of our lands being destroyed.
sentences.zh: "但比起我们的土地被毁掉，那点害怕不算什么。

sentences.en: Our people deserve better.” “So you’re going to talk to him?” Inger asked, her voice rising in hope. “Yes.
sentences.zh: "我们的人民值得更好的。""那你要去跟他谈？"英格问，声音里升起希望。"对。

sentences.en: We’ll go back to Arendelle together, and I’ll request another audience.
sentences.zh: "我们一起回阿伦黛尔，我会请求再次觐见。

sentences.en: I’m going to tell him Vesterland will not contribute to this project.” “And without our funding, he’ll never get it off the ground!” Inger crowed. “Take that, Runeard.” She raised a fist triumphantly, swinging her arm in the air as if punching their grandfather in the nose.
sentences.zh: "我要告诉他，维斯特兰不会为这个项目出资。""没了我们的资金，他根本启动不了！"英格欢呼。"接招吧，鲁内亚。"她胜利地举起拳头，在空中挥舞手臂，仿佛一拳打在她们外祖父的鼻子上。

sentences.en: Elsa started to laugh.
sentences.zh: 艾莎笑了起来。

sentences.en: She liked this girl!
sentences.zh: 她喜欢这姑娘！

sentences.en: But the laughter died in her throat as a noise rose in her ears.
sentences.zh: 可笑声还没出口，耳边就响起一阵声响，噎在了喉咙里。

sentences.en: The roar of approaching water. “A flash flood,” Elsa gasped. “There was a flash flood.” No sooner had she said the words than it came into view.
sentences.zh: 是逼近的水声。"山洪暴发了，"艾莎喘着气说。"当时发了一场山洪。"话音未落，它就出现了。

sentences.en: Rushing water racing down the river at top speed.
sentences.zh: 湍急的水以最快速度顺河而下。

sentences.en: Sissel screamed in horror.
sentences.zh: 西塞尔惊恐地尖叫。

sentences.en: She leapt backward. “Inger!” she cried.
sentences.zh: 她向后跳开。"英格！"她喊道。

sentences.en: Her sister was right in the path of the water.
sentences.zh: 她妹妹正好处在水流必经之路上。

sentences.en: Inger’s face turned white, but she didn’t move.
sentences.zh: 英格脸色惨白，却动弹不得。

sentences.en: It was as if she was frozen by fear. “Inger!” Sissel tried again.
sentences.zh: 仿佛被恐惧冻住了。"英格！"西塞尔又喊。

sentences.en: Her voice was full of panic.
sentences.zh: 声音里满是恐慌。

sentences.en: She dove for her sister, throwing herself at her, knocking her out of the water’s path.
sentences.zh: 她扑向妹妹，整个人撞上去，把妹妹推出了水流。

sentences.en: But her foot caught on a root, and she tripped, falling into the water. “Sissel!” Inger screamed. “No!” Inger scrambled to her feet, dashing to the riverbank.
sentences.zh: 可她的脚绊在树根上，一个趔趄栽进了水里。"西塞尔！"英格尖叫。"不！"英格慌忙爬起，冲向河岸。

sentences.en: Sissel was already far away, thrashing in the water just as Elsa had been doing moments before.
sentences.zh: 西塞尔已被冲出很远，在水里拼命扑腾，正如片刻前的艾莎一般。

sentences.en: With the water rougher because of the flood, waves rose over the shore, forcing Inger to stumble backward and further away. “Inger!” Sissel cried. “Help me, Inger!” She tried to grab hold of a fallen log, then some outstretched branches—anything to stop from being pulled away.
sentences.zh: 因洪水而更猛的水中，浪头打上河岸，逼得英格踉跄后退、离得更远。"英格！"西塞尔喊。"救我，英格！"她想抓住一根倒下的木头，又够向伸出的枝条——任何能阻止自己被冲走的东西。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Inger ran alongside the shore, screaming for help.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，英格沿岸边奔跑，大声呼救。

sentences.en: Elsa glanced at Anna, then started to run down the river, following the vision.
sentences.zh: 艾莎瞥了安娜一眼，便顺着河往下跑，跟着幻象而去。

sentences.en: Suddenly, she stopped short, her eyes bulging from her head as she realized what Sissel was headed for.
sentences.zh: 突然，她猛地停住，瞪大了眼睛——意识到西塞尔正冲向什么。

sentences.en: A giant waterfall. “Look out, Sissel!” Inger cried, her face streaming with tears as she ran helplessly along the shore. “Look out!” Sissel glanced behind her, her jaw dropping as she realized what was coming.
sentences.zh: 一道巨大的瀑布。"小心，西塞尔！"英格哭喊，脸上淌着泪，沿岸无助地奔跑。"小心！"西塞尔回头瞥了一眼，看清逼近之物，惊得合不拢嘴。

sentences.en: She lunged for the shore again, this time managing to grab on to a small branch.
sentences.zh: 她再一次扑向岸边，这次总算抓住了一根小树枝。

sentences.en: She struggled to use it as a rope to pull herself to shore.
sentences.zh: 她拼命把它当绳子，想把自己拉回岸上。

sentences.en: But the current was too strong and the branch began to crack.
sentences.zh: 可水流太猛，树枝开始断裂。

sentences.en: At that moment the vision froze, crystallizing into solid ice.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，幻象凝固了，结晶成坚冰。

sentences.en: Elsa frowned, trying to push more magic into it, to get it moving again.
sentences.zh: 艾莎皱起眉，想把更多魔力注入其中，让它重新动起来。

sentences.en: But it was stuck fast as if paused on purpose.
sentences.zh: 可它卡得死死的，像被人故意按了暂停。

sentences.en: She looked back at the draugr, who was still standing there by its statue.
sentences.zh: 她回头看亡灵，它还立在雕像旁。

sentences.en: But this time the creature’s eyes weren’t on the two sisters by the river.
sentences.zh: 但这次，那怪物的眼睛没盯着河边两姐妹。

sentences.en: It was looking at something behind them.
sentences.zh: 它望着她们身后的某样东西。

sentences.en: Or make that…someone. “Look!” Anna cried, pointing. “Who’s that?” Elsa squinted at the figure, standing motionless, encased in ice.
sentences.zh: 或者说……某个人。"看！"安娜指着喊道。"那是谁？"艾莎眯眼看向那个人影——他一动不动，被封在冰里。

sentences.en: It appeared to be a young boy—around fourteen or fifteen years of age.
sentences.zh: 看起来是个少年——约莫十四五岁的样子。

sentences.en: He had shaggy hair and big eyes and was carrying a shepherd’s crook.
sentences.zh: 他头发蓬乱，眼睛大大的，手里拿着一根牧羊杖。

sentences.en: In fact, she realized, as her eyes dropped lower, there was a lamb at his feet. “Whoa,” she whispered. “It’s the witness!” Anna cried. “From Kristoff’s story!
sentences.zh: 她目光下移，才发觉他脚边有只羊羔。"哇，"她轻声说。"是那个目击者！"安娜喊道。"克斯托夫故事里那个！

sentences.en: I totally forgot until now, but he said there was a witness!
sentences.zh: "我之前全忘了，可他说过有个目击者！

sentences.en: That’s how they were able to prove Inger’s crime!” She turned back to Elsa. “Make the memory move again.
sentences.zh: "他们就是靠这个证明英格有罪的！"她转回身对艾莎说。"让记忆再动起来。

sentences.en: Let’s see if he says anything.” Elsa bit her lower lip. “Um, I didn’t stop it to begin with.” She glanced over at the draugr. “Can you show us more?” The creature seemed to nod.
sentences.zh: "看看他会不会说什么。"艾莎咬着下唇。"呃，其实不是我停的。"她瞥了眼亡灵。"能让我们看更多吗？"那怪物似乎点了点头。

sentences.en: The vision leapt back to life.
sentences.zh: 幻象重新活了过来。

sentences.en: Inger’s screams once again reached their ears. “Help me!” she was crying to the boy. “Help me save my sister!
sentences.zh: 英格的尖叫再次传入他们耳中。"救救我！"她对那少年哭喊。"帮我救我姐姐！

sentences.en: Please!” “Stay where you are,” the boy shouted. “You’ll be swept away, too!” He ran to the shore, leaning over the water, wrapping his hand around a tree to anchor himself.
sentences.zh: "求你了！""你待在原地别动，"少年喊道。"你也会被卷走的！"他跑到岸边，探身向水，一只手抱住树稳住自己。

sentences.en: He tried to grab the other end of the branch Sissel was clinging to, but it was just out of his reach.
sentences.zh: 他想抓住西塞尔紧抓的树枝另一端，可就差那么一点够不到。

sentences.en: Inger stood watching, helpless and scared. “Come on, Sissel,” she whispered. “Just hold on.” Sissel looked up at her younger sister.
sentences.zh: 英格站在一旁看着，无助又害怕。"撑住啊，西塞尔，"她轻声说。"千万抓牢。"西塞尔抬头望着妹妹。

sentences.en: Her brown eyes no longer reflected her fear, but rather a strange sense of resolve.
sentences.zh: 她棕色的眼睛里不再有恐惧，而是一种奇异的决然。

sentences.en: Elsa cringed, realizing the truth.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一颤，明白了真相。

sentences.en: At that very moment, Sissel had known she was going to die.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，西塞尔已知道自己必死无疑。

sentences.en: And she had accepted her fate. “I love you, Inger,” Sissel said. “And I believe in you.
sentences.zh: 她接受了命运的安排。"我爱你，英格，"西塞尔说。"我也相信你。

sentences.en: I know you will do me proud.” “NO!” Inger begged, her face twisted with horror. “Don’t leave me, Sissel!” Her voice cracked on the words. “I can’t do this without you!” But her sister only shook her head. “Yes, you can,” she said solemnly.
sentences.zh: "我知道你不会让我失望。""不！"英格央求，脸因恐惧而扭曲。"别丢下我，西塞尔！"声音说到这里裂了。"没有你我做不到！"可妹妹只是摇头。"你做得到，"她郑重地说。

sentences.en: Her voice no longer sounded afraid, but determined. “You can do anything.” She paused, then added, “You’re my sister.
sentences.zh: "声音不再害怕，而是坚定。"你什么都能做到。"她顿了顿，又道，"你是我的妹妹。

sentences.en: And you’re stronger than you know.” And with that, the branch broke free.
sentences.zh: "也比你以为的更坚强。"话音未落，树枝断了。

sentences.en: Sissel’s body was tossed like a rag doll over the falls.
sentences.zh: 西塞尔的身体像布娃娃一样被甩下瀑布。

sentences.en: Inger screamed in agony, collapsing to the ground, sobs wracking her body. “Sissel,” she cried out. “Oh, my sweet Sissel.” A moment later the shepherd boy was by her side.
sentences.zh: 英格痛苦地尖叫，瘫倒在地，浑身被抽泣颤抖占满。"西塞尔，"她哭喊。"哦，我亲爱的西塞尔。"片刻后，牧羊少年来到她身边。

sentences.en: He tried to help her get up, but Inger’s legs refused to work.
sentences.zh: 他想扶她起来，可英格的腿软得使不上劲。

sentences.en: She kept staring at the raging river, her whole body trembling with grief.
sentences.zh: 她一直盯着咆哮的河，整个人因悲伤而颤抖。

sentences.en: The boy reached down, gently swiping a lock of hair from her face, meeting her eyes with his own. “What’s your name?” he said gently. “Inger,” she whispered, clinging to his hand.
sentences.zh: 少年俯下身，轻轻拨开她脸上的发丝，与她对视。"你叫什么名字？"他温柔地说。"英格，"她轻声答，紧紧抓着他的手。

sentences.en: He nodded. “Inger, I’m Stig.
sentences.zh: 他点点头。"英格，我是斯蒂格。

sentences.en: I’m going to help you,” he said.
sentences.zh: "我会帮你的，"他说。

sentences.en: And just like that, the vision faded.
sentences.zh: 话音落下，幻象消散。

sentences.en: The raging river went quiet again.
sentences.zh: 咆哮的河重归平静。

sentences.en: Elsa turned slowly back to the draugr.
sentences.zh: 艾莎缓缓转回身，面向亡灵。

sentences.en: It was still standing by the shore, staring at the water.
sentences.zh: 它还立在岸边，盯着水面。

sentences.en: It took Elsa a moment to realize the creature’s cheeks were wet.
sentences.zh: 艾莎过了一会儿才察觉，那怪物脸颊上是湿的。

sentences.en: It was crying.
sentences.zh: 它在流泪。

sentences.en: She was crying. “Your sister didn’t murder you,” Anna whispered. “That’s what you’ve been trying to tell us, isn’t it?
sentences.zh: 她在哭。"你姐姐没有害死你，"安娜轻声说。"这就是你一直想告诉我们的，对吗？

sentences.en: Everyone’s been spreading a false story!
sentences.zh: "大家一直在传一个假故事！

sentences.en: You want them to know the truth.
sentences.zh: "你想让大家知道真相。

sentences.en: It was an accident.
sentences.zh: "那是个意外。

sentences.en: Your sister was innocent all along.
sentences.zh: "你姐姐自始至终都是清白的。

sentences.en: She loved you.
sentences.zh: "她爱你。

sentences.en: And you loved her.” Sissel nodded, staring forlornly at the river.
sentences.zh: "你也爱她。"西塞尔点点头，怅然若失地望着河。

sentences.en: Elsa felt her heart go out to the creature, and suddenly she half wanted to run over and give her a warm hug.
sentences.zh: 艾莎对那怪物心生怜意，突然有点想跑过去给她一个温暖的拥抱。

sentences.en: They’d been afraid of the draugr for so long.
sentences.zh: 他们怕这亡灵怕了这么久。

sentences.en: But now she felt only pity as she gazed on the grotesque creature.
sentences.zh: 可此刻望着这狰狞的怪物，她只觉怜悯。

sentences.en: For Inger, too, who had been accused of a crime she hadn’t committed.
sentences.zh: 对英格也是如此——她被指控犯下自己没做过的罪行。

sentences.en: To lose your sister like that had to feel like you’d lost one of your own limbs.
sentences.zh: 那样失去姐姐，想必就像失去自己的一肢。

sentences.en: Elsa could only hope this was a pain she’d never have to go through herself.
sentences.zh: 艾莎只盼自己永远不必承受这种痛。

sentences.en: Because to lose Anna…her Anna… She shook her head.
sentences.zh: 因为失去安娜……她的安娜……她摇摇头。

sentences.en: No.
She wouldn’t even think of it.
sentences.zh: "她连想都不会去想。

sentences.en: She couldn’t.
sentences.zh: "她不能。

sentences.en: Elsa looked up at the draugr again. “You were trying to share this memory with me earlier, weren’t you?” she asked, realization washing over her. “When we met you in the forest.
sentences.zh: 艾莎再次抬头看亡灵。"你之前就想把这记忆分享给我，对吧？"她恍然大悟地问。"我们那次在森林里遇见你时。

sentences.en: You grabbed my hand.
sentences.zh: "你抓住了我的手。

sentences.en: I thought you were trying to erase my memories.
sentences.zh: "我以为你想抹去我的记忆。

sentences.en: But you were trying to share your own.” She gave an apologetic shrug. “I’m sorry I didn’t understand.” The draugr shuffled from foot to foot, moaning softly.
sentences.zh: "可你其实想分享你自己的记忆。"她略带歉意地耸耸肩。"抱歉我没懂。"亡灵来回挪着脚，低低呻吟。

sentences.en: Elsa decided to take that as forgiveness.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把这当作原谅。

sentences.en: She turned back to Anna. “At least now we know the whole story,” she said. “What really happened.” “Do we, though?” Anna asked, scratching her head as she looked from the draugr to the memorial upstream. “Why did Inger get blamed for it all?
sentences.zh: 她转回身对安娜。"至少现在我们知道整个故事了，"她说。"真正发生了什么。""可我们真的知道了吗？"安娜问，一边挠头，目光在亡灵和上游的纪念碑间游移。"为什么英格要为这一切背锅？

sentences.en: I mean, there was a witness!
sentences.zh: "我是说，明明有目击者啊！

sentences.en: Why didn’t she and that boy, Stig, just go back and tell people what really happened?
sentences.zh: "她和那少年斯蒂格为什么不回去告诉大家真相？

sentences.en: Her name would have been cleared!” Sissel moaned, shaking her head.
sentences.zh: "她的罪名早就该洗清了！"西塞尔呻吟着摇头。

sentences.en: She clearly didn’t know why—she had died before that part of the story happened.
sentences.zh: 她显然不知道原因——那段情节发生前她就已经死了。

sentences.en: Leaving yet another mystery to solve, Elsa realized.
sentences.zh: 艾莎意识到，这又留下一个待解的谜团。

sentences.en: Just one more mystery in this whole thing. “Don’t worry,” she told Sissel. “We’re going to figure this out.
sentences.zh: "整件事里的又一道谜题而已。"别担心，"她对西塞尔说。"我们会弄清楚的。

sentences.en: Somehow.
sentences.zh: "总会有办法。

sentences.en: And then we’ll tell everyone the truth.
sentences.zh: "然后我们告诉大家真相。

sentences.en: What really happened.
sentences.zh: "真正发生了什么。

sentences.en: Clear your sister’s name once and for all.” The draugr’s eyes seemed to brighten. “Sissssster,” she moaned, seeming to agree. “Sissssster mine…” And with that, she began to shuffle off into the woods.
sentences.zh: "彻底洗清你姐姐的名声。"亡灵的眼睛似乎亮了起来。"姐……姐，"她呻吟着，像在表示同意。"我……的姐姐……"说完，她慢慢挪步，走进树林。

sentences.en: Elsa and Anna watched her go, amazed. “Guess we know what the draugr wants now,” Anna said. “ And we know where to go next,” Elsa agreed. “To find the one person who might still be alive.
sentences.zh: 艾莎和安娜惊奇地看她离去。"看来我们知道亡灵想要什么了，"安娜说。"而且知道下一步去哪了，"艾莎赞同。"去找那个或许还活着的人。

sentences.en: The one person who was really there.” “Stig,” Anna said. “And I know just how to track him down.”
sentences.zh: "那个真正在场的人。""斯蒂格，"安娜说。"而我知道该怎么找到他。"

chapters.title: Chapter Sixteen: Anna
chapters.en:
ANNA AND ELSA RODE LIKE the Wind Spirit—fast, without stopping—not talking till they reached a stormy Arendelle. Rain and snow were mixing as sleet pooled on the cobblestone streets and thunder continued to boom overhead. But there was no time to focus on the weather. The pair didn’t stop till they were safely inside the darkened castle.

“You’re back!” Olaf cried, hurrying down the staircase to meet them. “Good morning! Or should I say, ‘good night’? It’s getting really dark here,” he added, worry written all over his face. “But the good news is there have been no draugr sightings since you left. And we have the pirate situation completely under control!”

Anna slapped her head and groaned. “That’s right! The pirates!” She hesitated, wanting to go back down the stairs, out of the castle, and straight to the port. “Are they actually here? In Arendelle? What’s going on? Are they stopping our ships from coming in and out of port?” A flash of lightning lit up the room.

“The storms are stopping our ships, actually.” Olaf touched her hand. “But thankfully they’re keeping the pirates at bay, too. At least for now.”

Well, thank you, Sissel, Anna said to herself. At least that gave them some time to help Sissel before dealing with the pirates. Got it.

Being a queen was exhausting sometimes.

“Your Majesty!” Mattias appeared at the foot of the stairs and stood at attention. “I have stationed our guards around the port. Any pirate dares approach and they’ll live to regret it.” He cleared his throat. “And we will send word to their captain that we would like a meeting as soon as the storms let up, as you requested.”

“Well, that’s good,” Anna reasoned. Though she hadn’t actually requested anything, obviously. Mattias’s memory was clearly as bad as the others. But at least he was now acting like a general again. “Please send word if anything changes.”

Mattias looked at her strangely, then glanced at Olaf.

“You can go do your general stuff,” Olaf said. Mattias nodded and disappeared around a corner. Anna shot a look at Elsa. They really needed to clear this Sissel thing up—and fast!

Olaf’s eyes lit up. “So where are you going? Can I come? And…not be left alone for Sinister Sissel to find?”

Elsa picked Olaf up. “First, let’s stop calling Sissel sinister. We’re pretty sure she’s not trying to harm us. She actually needs our help.”

“Oh, and her sister didn’t murder her, either, turns out,” Anna added. When Olaf’s eyes widened, she shrugged. “We’ll fill you in, but it’s a long story. First, we need to find Stig.”

“Stig?” Olaf asked. “I don’t remember any Stig.” He stopped short. “Oh no! Is my memory going, too?”

“No, no! You don’t know him. None of us do. But he was there the day Sissel drowned, and he might have some answers as to why Inger was blamed.”

“We’re hoping we can find him listed in the census and figure out where he lives.” Anna bit her lower lip. “If he’s still alive…”

“Then what are we waiting for?” Olaf asked, jumping down and toddling away. “Let’s go find this sentence! I mean, census! That’s a book, right?”

The trio headed to Anna’s private study, which had belonged to Elsa and their father before them. Probably Runeard as well, once upon a time, though Anna didn’t like to think about their grandfather seated in the same old, cracked leather chair that she used now. She hadn’t mentioned this to Elsa yet, but she was getting a sneaking suspicion something about this whole mess was at least partially their grandfather’s doing. After all, he was why Sissel and Inger had come to Arendelle to begin with.

“Luckily, they only do a census every ten or more years,” Elsa said as she opened one of the books and went to the most recent record. Her finger slid along each listing, which cataloged people by the farms or properties they lived on, their jobs, and their ages and marital status, along with birth and death dates and lists of the other members of the household. “Let’s see how many people named Stig used to be shepherds and are around sixty-five years old.” She shook her head. “This could take a bit, since everything’s listed by last name.”

“Which is why we also need to look in these court records,” said Anna as she pulled out a thick bound book. “Since we know when the sisters visited Arendelle, I can narrow it down.” She flipped through the pages, looking for the correct year, and soon found the Vesterland sisters’ names. “This is it! Inger’s hearing!” Elsa and Olaf came over to look.

“‘Witness, Stig Petter,’” Elsa read. “Perfect. I’ll just—”

“Whoa,” Anna interrupted, her eyes skimming the page. “No way.”

“What is it?” Elsa asked.

Anna sat back. “He lied. Stig lied!”

“What?” Elsa stared down at the record in disbelief.

“According to this, Stig reported seeing Inger push Sissel into the water and watch her drown,” Anna summarized. “Inger denied the claim, but as Stig was the lone witness, the court sided with him.” She closed the book, stunned. “Why would he lie? He was right there! He saw the whole thing!”

“Stig Petter, what are you hiding?” Elsa murmured, going back to the census and scanning the listings with her fingers. “Here he is! He’s still alive,” she said, relieved. “But it looks like he doesn’t live in Arendelle anymore.”

“Where does he live?” Anna asked, her heart sinking a little. Hopefully it wasn’t too far.

“In the mountains. Just outside the village of Harmon.”

Okay, that wasn’t far. And also? Maybe since he was outside of Arendelle, Stig wouldn’t have lost his memory like everyone here had.

It was a long shot. But it was the only one they had.

Please, Stig, Anna thought when they finally arrived at his cottage after battling more wind and rain. Help us get to the bottom of this mystery. Unfortunately, she wasn’t hopeful he was going to be a very cooperative witness. After all, he’d lied years ago. What if he continued to stick to his story now? He was their last hope; the one person who had been there—seen everything. Somehow they had to convince him to help them. Or Sissel might never find peace.

And Arendelle would be cast into stormy darkness forever.

Anna slid off her horse while Elsa quickly dismounted the Water Nokk and the two of them hurried to the door, rapping hard to be heard over the thunder. A moment later, the door flew open. An older man with wire-rim spectacles and a bald head, tufts of white hair over his ears, stared at them angrily.

“What are you doing out in weather like this?” he demanded in a gruff voice.

“Mr. Petter?” Anna asked eagerly as water dripped off her nose. “Stig Petter?”

“Yes,” he said, sounding cranky. “That’s my name, and yours is Queen Anna, and hers is Queen Elsa. What I don’t know is why you’re at my door.”

“Something is happening in Arendelle that we could use your help with,” Elsa informed him, giving him a hopeful smile. “Can we come in?”

“Sorry,” Stig said, looking suddenly nervous. “I can’t help you.” He made a move to shut his door.

“Please?” Anna begged as a crack of thunder made the group jump. “Just let us in for a moment. We’re soaked to the bone.”

Stig sighed. “Fine. Get in here, then. But don’t expect anything further from me. I left Arendelle fifty years ago. And I have no interest in the kingdom’s affairs.”

That didn’t sound promising. But at least he was letting them in. Maybe Anna could work on him a little more once he heard how dire the situation was. And at least it would get them out of the rain. The two girls quickly moved into the cottage, and Stig shut the door behind them. It was a humble space with a fire roaring and a pot over the hearth that was bubbling with some sort of soup. Unlike at the Figels’ house, this soup smelled delicious.

“Thank you,” Elsa said, wringing out the bottom of her dress. “We don’t mean to impose.”

“We just had a few questions for you about something that happened when you were a young man,” Anna told him as she wiped her wet hands on her skirt. She was so tired of being wet all the time.

Stig’s expression darkened. “If you’re asking how I got the funds for this cottage when I stopped herding sheep, that’s none of your business! It’s like I told everyone else—I don’t owe you any explanations! I inherited this cottage fair and…square.” His voice trailed off.

“This isn’t about the cottage,” Elsa told him.

“Oh,” Stig said, still sounding uncomfortable. “Then what is it you want to know?”

Anna decided to go for broke. “We want to know about Princess Inger. We know you were there the day she and her sister argued at the riverbank and Sissel was swept away.” Anna tried to sound calm. Rational. Like she was asking a simple question about the weather. But inside, she was angry—Stig had lied, and his lie had destroyed a young girl’s life! Why had he done it? And would he admit to it now—fifty years later?

Stig stiffened. “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” he muttered. But his cheeks were quite red. Another lie, Anna presumed.

“Come on. We saw the whole thing in a memory I created,” Elsa broke in. “We know that Sissel fell in while trying to save Inger, and that you were there and tried to help save her. When you couldn’t, you went back and comforted Inger.”

“You told her you were going to help her!” Anna added indignantly. “And then you went and accused her of murder! Publicly! Because of you, she was sentenced to death! For something you know she didn’t do!”

Stig’s face hardened. “You have to leave. Now,” he said, guiding Anna by the arm to the door. “I’m sorry, Your Majesties, but I have made my peace with this matter.” His voice caught. “I never want to hear the Vesterland sisters’ names again.”

Anna was so close she could see the deep wrinkles in his forehead and the windburn on his chapped cheeks. His blue eyes were almost gray with age and held so much fear. Something had happened that day that haunted him. But what? Why would he lie about Inger? Why did he live up here alone, hidden away from the world, and bristle at talk of how he paid for his cottage, unless…

Suddenly she remembered her hunch back at the castle. She turned to face Stig and tried to take a different approach. “Someone asked you to lie about Inger, didn’t they?” she said gently, not really making it a question.

Stig looked away, not answering her, which told her she was probably right.

“But who would do that?” Elsa asked, turning to her sister in confusion.

“Isn’t it obvious? Our grandfather,” Anna pronounced. “With Sissel dead and Inger being held for her murder, the Vesterland sisters couldn’t oppose the dam,” she explained. “You heard them in that memory—they wanted to go back and stand up to Grandfather. Inger convinced Sissel not to help fund the dam, and they could have rallied other nearby kingdoms, too, which would have meant Arendelle wouldn’t have the funding to build.” She drew in a breath. “Grandfather couldn’t allow that to happen.”

“That’s horrible,” Elsa whispered. “And yet, it makes sense. Even with Sissel gone, Inger never would have stopped fighting Grandfather on the dam.” She glanced at Stig. “If he had a witness willing to say Inger pushed Sissel in the river, neither sister would ever be a problem for him again.”

Stig placed his face in his hands. A single tear slipped down his cheek. When he finally looked up, the hurt in his face was visible. “You’re right. I lied then. And now, fifty years later, those lies are still haunting me.” He grabbed a handkerchief and blew into it loudly. “Trust me, I’ll never forgive myself for what I did to that poor, sweet girl, but it’s too late to do anything about it now.”

“Actually, that might not be true,” said Anna as she took his hand and led him to a chair. “Let’s talk. So, King Runeard told you to lie?”

“Yes,” Stig said, his voice shaking. It took him a moment before he spoke again. Anna waited patiently. “I wasn’t planning to lie at first. I told the king exactly what happened. Inger was beside herself when Sissel was swept away. She and I ran back to the village for help, but of course there was nothing we could do.” Anna squeezed his hand. “It was only after the king met with Inger that something changed…” His voice trailed off.

“Go on, “Elsa urged gently. “It’s okay.”

“Runeard called for me again and told me that I was wrong about Inger—that I was to tell the world I saw her murder her sister.” He covered his face with his hands again. “He told me if I said otherwise, he’d inform people I helped Inger do it and have me sent to prison for life.” His voice cracked. “I said I’d speak out and tell everyone how he threatened me, but the king just laughed.” He glanced into the distance, his eyes glazing over. “I remember he said, ‘Who is going to believe you? You’re nothing but a poor shepherd.’”

“That’s despicable!” Anna said angrily. “Your king shouldn’t have threatened you.”

“I know, but what could I do?” Stig said hoarsely. “I could either lie or face jail—or worse. So I did what I was told, and the king rewarded me for my lie. I no longer had to be a sheepherder. I had enough money to buy this place and hide away here.”

He motioned to the cottage around him, and Elsa and Anna were quiet, listening to the rain pound the cottage’s roof.

“I was too ashamed to be part of village life after that,” Stig said. “I was afraid someone would ask me about the Vesterland sisters and I’d slip, so I’ve stayed away all these years while the guilt has eaten at me from the inside out. Those two sisters have haunted my dreams for years.” He closed his eyes. “Sometimes, I feel like I can still hear Inger calling out to Sissel on that riverbank so long ago.” The old man broke down in tears.

Anna felt anger rise inside of her all over again. But this time it was not directed at Stig. He had been a victim as much as the two sisters, she realized. And though he hadn’t done the right thing at the time, it was pretty understandable why. She put her arm around the shepherd, trying to comfort him as best she could as she looked up to her sister, who appeared deep in thought. “It all makes sense,” she said softly. “Why everyone has the story wrong. Our grandfather made sure of it.”

“And now Sissel wants the story set straight,” Elsa agreed. “And she wants us to do it.”

Stig looked up, surprised. “Wait. Are you saying Sissel is still alive? But I saw her drown! There’s no way she could have survived that waterfall!”

Anna hesitated. She wasn’t sure how much more Stig could take, but…

“Yes and no. Sissel has become a draugr, and she’s haunting Arendelle and stealing memories to try to make people stop thinking Inger murdered her. She’s what’s causing this weather and the darkness.”

Stig’s jaw fell. “A draugr?” he whispered.

“Yes, but if you come forward, Sissel might finally rest,” Elsa told him. “Like Grand Pabbie said, ‘To end this all, you must tell her tale.’ You need to tell people the truth about Inger.”

Stig thought for a moment. “I don’t know if they’ll listen to an old shepherd, but I guess I could try. I owe Inger that much. Maybe she’ll even forgive me. Though I wouldn’t blame her if she didn’t.” He stared down at the cottage floor, looking sad.

Anna shot Elsa a look. “I hate to tell you this,” she said gently, “but Inger can’t forgive you. She’s dead, too.”

Stig’s head jerked. His eyes locked on the sisters. “Yes, that’s what people think,” he said. “But in truth, she’s very much alive. And from what I understand, she’s not far away, either.”
chapters.zh:
安娜和艾莎骑得就像风灵一般——又快又急，一刻不停——直到抵达风雨交加的阿伦黛尔，两人才开口说话。

雨雪交织，冰霰在鹅卵石街道上积成一洼洼水，雷声仍在头顶隆隆作响。

但此刻已无暇顾及天气。

两人一路疾驰，直到安然进入昏暗的城堡才停下脚步。"你们回来了！"奥拉夫喊着，急匆匆跑下楼梯来迎她们。"早上好！

或者我该说，"晚上好"？

"这里越来越黑了，"他补充道，脸上写满担忧。"不过好消息是，你们走后还没人再见到亡灵的踪影。

"而且海盗的事我们也完全控制住了！"安娜一拍脑门，叹起气来。"对哦！

"海盗！"她一愣，恨不得掉头下楼、冲出城堡直奔港口。"他们真的来了？

"在阿伦黛尔？

"到底怎么回事？

"他们是不是封锁了港口，不让我们的船进出？"一道闪电照亮了房间。"其实，眼下是我们自己的风暴挡住了船。"奥拉夫碰了碰她的手。"不过谢天谢地，风暴也把海盗挡在了外面。

"至少暂时是这样。"安娜在心里默默道：好吧，这回谢了，西塞尔。

至少这给了她们一点时间，在应付海盗之前先帮西塞尔解脱。

明白了。

当女王有时真累人。"陛下！"马蒂亚斯出现在楼梯脚下，立正行礼。"我已在港口四周布下卫兵。

"海盗胆敢靠近，定叫他们后悔莫及。"他清了清嗓子。"我们也会按您的吩咐，待风暴一停就传话给他们的船长，请求会面。" "嗯，这还行，"安娜思量着说。

虽说得明白，她其实压根没吩咐过什么。

马蒂亚斯的记性显然和别人一样糟糕。

但至少他现在又像个将军了。"若有任何变化，请传话告知。"马蒂亚斯奇怪地看了她一眼，又瞥了瞥奥拉夫。"你该去忙你的将军事务啦，"奥拉夫说。

马蒂亚斯点点头，拐过墙角不见了。

安娜向艾莎递了个眼神。

她们真得把西塞尔这桩事查个水落石出——而且得快！

奥拉夫眼睛一亮。"那你们要去哪儿？

"我能一起去吗？

"还有……别把我一个人丢下，让'阴森西塞尔'给逮着？"艾莎把奥拉夫抱了起来。"首先，咱们别再叫西塞尔'阴森'了。

"我们相当确定，她并不是要伤害我们。

"她其实是需要我们帮忙。" "哦，而且事实证明，她妹妹也没有谋害她，"安娜补充道。

奥拉夫瞪大了眼睛，她耸耸肩。"我们待会儿跟你细说，不过说来话长。

"首先，我们得找到斯蒂格。" "斯蒂格？"奥拉夫问。"我可不记得有什么斯蒂格。"他猛地停住。"哦不！

"我的记忆也要不行了吗？" "不不不！

"你不认识他。

"我们谁都不认识。

"但他就在西塞尔溺亡那天在场，也许能说明为何英格被冤枉。" "我们希望能在人口普查名册里找到他，弄清他住哪儿。"安娜咬着下唇。"要是他还活着……" "那还等什么？"奥拉夫跳下来，一摇一摆地走开了。"咱们去找这个句——

"我是说，人口——"

"人口名册！那是本书，对吧？"三人朝安娜的私人书房走去，这书房早先是艾莎和她们父亲用的。

很可能鲁内尔德也曾用过，虽说安娜不愿去想祖父就坐在她如今坐着的这把老旧开裂的皮椅上。

她还没跟艾莎提过这事，但她心头渐渐生出一个隐约的怀疑：这团乱麻至少有一部分是她们祖父酿成的。

毕竟，西塞尔和英格当初之所以来到阿伦黛尔，正是因为他。"幸好人口普查每隔十年或更长才做一次，"艾莎边说边翻开其中一本书，翻到最新的记录。

她的手指一行行划过名单——上面按人们居住的农庄或房产登记，写明职业、年龄、婚姻状况，还有出生与死亡日期及同住家庭成员。"咱们看看，名叫斯蒂格、以前当过牧羊人、如今约六十五岁的人有几个。"她摇摇头。"这可得费点工夫，因为全是按姓氏排的。" "所以我们还得查这些法庭记录，"安娜一边抽出一本厚重的装订本一边说。"既然我们知道姐妹俩来访阿伦黛尔的时间，就能缩小范围。"她翻动书页寻找正确的年份，很快找到了维斯特兰德姐妹的名字。"找到了！

"英格的听证会！"艾莎和奥拉夫凑过来看。"'证人，斯蒂格·佩特，'"艾莎念道。"完美。

"我这就——" "哇哦，"安娜打断了她，目光扫过那一页。"不可能。" "怎么了？"艾莎问。

安娜往后一靠。"他撒谎了。

"斯蒂格撒谎了！" "什么？"艾莎难以置信地盯着记录。"据上面所写，斯蒂格报告说，他看见英格把西塞尔推入水中，眼睁睁看她淹死，"安娜概括道。"英格否认了指控，但既然斯蒂格是唯一证人，法庭便采信了他。"她合上书，惊愕不已。"他为何要撒谎？

"他当时就在现场！

"整件事他都看在眼里！" "斯蒂格·佩特，你在隐瞒什么？"艾莎低声道，回到人口普查名册上，用手指一行行搜寻。"他在这儿！

"他还活着，"她松了口气说。"但他似乎已不住在阿伦黛尔了。" "他住哪儿？"安娜问，心里微微一沉。

但愿别太远。"在山里。

"就在哈尔蒙村外。"好吧，那不算远。

"而且呢？

"也许正因为他在阿伦黛尔之外，斯蒂格没有像这里所有人那样失去记忆。

"这希望有点渺茫。

"但这是她们唯一的指望。

"求你了，斯蒂格，安娜在终于顶着风雨抵达他的小屋时心想。

"帮我们揭开这个谜团的真相。

可惜她并不指望他会是个配合的证人。

毕竟，他多年前撒过谎。

若他现在仍咬定原来的说法，可怎么办？

他是她们最后的希望；是唯一当时在场、目睹一切的人。

无论如何，她们得说服他帮忙。

否则西塞尔也许永远无法安息。

阿伦黛尔也将永远陷入风暴与黑暗。

安娜滑下马，艾莎也迅速从水马背上跃下，两人急步奔向门口，在雷声中用力敲门好让人听见。

片刻之后，门猛地开了。

一位戴金属细框眼镜、秃着头顶、耳畔垂着几撮白发的老人，怒气冲冲地瞪着她们。"这种天气你们跑出来干什么？"他用沙哑的嗓音质问。"佩特先生？

"佩特？"安娜急切地问，水珠从鼻尖滴落。"是斯蒂格·佩特吗？" "没错，"他没好气地说。"那是我的名字，而你是安娜女王，她是艾莎女王。

"我只是不知道你们为何找上门来。" "阿伦黛尔正发生一些事，我们需要你帮忙，"艾莎告诉他，露出满怀希望的微笑。"我们能进去吗？" "抱歉，"斯蒂格突然显得紧张起来。"我帮不了你们。"他作势要关门。"求你了？"雷声一炸，众人都吓了一跳，安娜哀求道。"就让我们进去待一会儿。

"我们都湿透了。"斯蒂格叹了口气。"行吧。

"那就进来。

"但别指望我还会做什么。

"我五十年前就离开了阿伦黛尔。

"对王国的事毫无兴趣。"这话听起来不妙。

但至少他肯让她们进去了。

等他听明白情况有多危急，安娜或许能再多劝劝他。

而且至少能让她们躲开雨水。

两个姑娘快步走进小屋，斯蒂格在身后关上了门。

屋里陈设简朴，炉火正旺，壁炉上的锅里咕嘟咕嘟煮着某种汤。

与菲格尔家不同，这汤闻起来香气扑鼻。"谢谢，"艾莎拧着裙摆上的水说。"我们并非有意打扰。" "我们只想问你几个问题，关于你年轻时发生的一件事，"安娜擦着湿手、在裙子上边说。

她真是受够了总是浑身湿透。

斯蒂格脸色一沉。"若是问我不当牧羊人后，是哪来的钱买下这小屋，那不关你们的事！

"就像我跟别人说的——我无需向你们解释！

"这小屋是我……正正当当继承来的。"他声音低了下去。"这和屋子无关，"艾莎告诉他。"哦，"斯蒂格仍显得不安。"那你们究竟想知道什么？"安娜决定豁出去。"我们想知道英格公主的事。

"我们知道，那天她和妹妹在河岸争吵、西塞尔被冲走时，你就在场。"安娜尽量让语气显得平静。

理智。

仿佛只是在问一个关于天气的简单问题。

但内心深处，她怒火中烧——斯蒂格撒了谎，而他的谎言毁了一个年轻女孩的一生！

他为何要这么做？

事隔五十年，他现在会承认吗？

斯蒂格僵住了。"我不知道你在说什么，"他喃喃道。

但他的脸颊涨得通红。

又一句谎话，安娜心想。"得了。

"我们在我创造的一段记忆里，亲眼看到了整件事，"艾莎插话道。"我们知道，西塞尔是为了救英格才掉进水里的，而你在场，还曾试着救她。

"你没能救成，便回去安慰英格。" "你还对她说会帮她的！"安娜愤愤地补了一句。"结果你反倒去指控她谋杀！

"当众！

"就因为你的证词，她被判了死刑！

"为你明知她没做的事！"斯蒂格脸色一沉。"你们得走。

"现在，"他说着，攥着安娜的手臂把她往门口带。"很抱歉，两位陛下，但这件事我已与自己和解了。"他声音哽咽。"我永远不想再听到维斯特兰德姐妹的名字。"安娜离得那样近，能看清他额头深深的皱纹和皲裂脸颊上的冻伤。

他苍老得发灰的蓝眼睛里，盛满了恐惧。

那天发生的某件事，一直缠着他不放。

可那究竟是什么？

他为何要诬陷英格？

他为何独居在此、与世隔绝，又为何一提起买屋的钱就恼火——除非……她忽然记起在城堡里的那个直觉。

她转向斯蒂格，试着换个方式。"是有人让你诬陷英格的，对吧？"她轻声说，这并不像一句真正的问话。

斯蒂格移开目光，没有回答，这让她知道自己多半猜对了。"可谁会这么做呢？"艾莎困惑地转向妹妹问。"这还用说吗？

"我们的祖父，"安娜断言。"西塞尔一死，英格又被当作凶手关押，维斯特兰德姐妹便无法反对大坝了，"她解释道。"你在那段记忆里听见过——她们想回去对抗祖父。

"是英格说服西塞尔别资助大坝，她们还能联合附近其他王国，那样阿伦黛尔就筹不到钱来建造了。"她深吸一口气。"祖父绝不能让这种事发生。" "太可怕了，"艾莎低语。"可这话又说通了。

"即便西塞尔不在了，英格也绝不会停止在大坝上与祖父抗争。"她瞥了斯蒂格一眼。"只要有个愿意指证英格将西塞尔推入河中的证人，两姐妹就再也不会是他的麻烦了。"斯蒂格双手捂住了脸。

一滴泪顺着他的脸颊滑落。

当他终于抬起头，脸上的痛楚清晰可见。"你们说得对。

"那时我撒了谎。

"而如今，五十年过去了，那些谎言仍在缠着我。"他抓起手帕，响亮地擤了擤鼻子。"相信我，我永远无法原谅自己对不起那个可怜又善良的姑娘，但现在做什么都太迟了。" "其实，也许还不至于，"安娜握着他的手，把他领到椅子上坐下。"我们谈谈。

"那么，是鲁内尔德国王让你撒谎的？" "是的，"斯蒂格声音颤抖地说。

他停顿了片刻，才又开口。

安娜耐心地等着。"起初我并不打算撒谎。

"我对国王如实说了发生的一切。

"西塞尔被冲走时，英格几近崩溃。

"她和我跑回村里求救，可当然，我们无能为力。"安娜握紧了他的手。"直到国王见过英格之后，情况才起了变化……"他声音低了下去。"说下去，"艾莎柔声催促。"没关系的。"

"鲁内尔德再次召见我，说我关于英格的记忆是错的——说我得告诉世人，是我亲眼看见她谋害了妹妹。"他再次用双手捂住脸。"他告诉我，若我说别的，他就向众人宣称是我帮英格干的，并让我终身坐牢。"他的声音劈了。"我说我会站出来，告诉所有人他是如何威胁我的，可国王只是大笑。"他望向远处，目光变得迷离。"我记得他说：'谁会相信你？

"你不过是个穷牧羊人。'" "真卑鄙！"安娜愤愤地说。"你们的国王不该那样威胁你。" "我知道，可我能怎么办？"斯蒂格声音沙哑地说。"我要么撒谎，要么坐牢——甚至更糟。

"于是我照他说的做了，而国王奖赏了我的谎言。

"我不必再当牧羊人。

"我有了足够的钱买下这地方，躲在这里。"他指了指四周的小屋，艾莎和安娜静静听着雨点敲打屋顶。"从那以后，我羞于再过村子的生活，"斯蒂格说。"我怕有人问起维斯特兰德姐妹，我会说漏嘴，所以这些年来一直躲开众人，而愧疚却由内而外啃噬着我。

"那两姐妹缠了我多年的梦。"他闭上眼睛。"有时，我仿佛还能听见英格在很久以前那片河岸上呼唤西塞尔。"老人失声痛哭。

安娜感到一股怒火再次从心底涌起。

但这一次，怒火并非指向斯蒂格。

她意识到，他和那两姐妹一样，也是个受害者。

尽管他当时没做对的事，但其中的缘由倒也情有可原。

她搂住牧羊人的肩膀，尽力安慰他，同时抬眼望向若有所思的妹妹。"一切都说得通了，"她轻声说。"大家都把故事记错的原因。

"是我们的祖父一手造成的。" "而如今西塞尔想把真相纠正过来，"艾莎附和。"她要我们去做。"斯蒂格吃惊地抬起头。"等等。

"你是说西塞尔还活着？

"可我亲眼见她淹死的！

"她绝不可能从那个瀑布下活下来！"安娜犹豫了。

她不确定斯蒂格还能承受多少，但……"既算也不算。

"西塞尔已变成亡灵，她缠着阿伦黛尔，盗取人们的记忆，想让大家不再以为英格杀了她。

"这天气和黑暗都是她造成的。"斯蒂格惊得合不拢嘴。"亡灵？"他低语。"是的，但若你站出来，西塞尔也许终于能安息了，"艾莎对他说。"就像皮比长老说的：'要了结这一切，你必须讲述她的故事。

'你得把英格的真相告诉众人。"斯蒂格想了想。"我不知人们会不会听一个老牧羊人的，但我想我可以试试。

"我欠英格这份情。

"也许她甚至会原谅我。

"即便她不原谅，我也不会怪她。"他垂眼盯着小屋的地板，神情哀伤。

安娜向艾莎使了个眼色。"我不忍心告诉你这个，"她温和地说，"但英格无法原谅你了。

"她也死了。"斯蒂格猛地抬起头。

他的目光紧紧锁住姐妹俩。"是的，人们都这么以为，"他说。"但其实，她活得好好的。而且据我所知，她离这儿也不远。

sentences.zh: "我能一起去吗？

sentences.en: And…not be left alone for Sinister Sissel to find?” Elsa picked Olaf up. “First, let’s stop calling Sissel sinister.
sentences.zh: "还有……别把我一个人丢下，让'阴森西塞尔'给逮着？"艾莎把奥拉夫抱了起来。"首先，咱们别再叫西塞尔'阴森'了。

sentences.en: We’re pretty sure she’s not trying to harm us.
sentences.zh: "我们相当确定，她并不是要伤害我们。

sentences.en: She actually needs our help.” “Oh, and her sister didn’t murder her, either, turns out,” Anna added.
sentences.zh: "她其实是需要我们帮忙。" "哦，而且事实证明，她妹妹也没有谋害她，"安娜补充道。

sentences.en: When Olaf’s eyes widened, she shrugged. “We’ll fill you in, but it’s a long story.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫瞪大了眼睛，她耸耸肩。"我们待会儿跟你细说，不过说来话长。

sentences.en: First, we need to find Stig.” “Stig?” Olaf asked. “I don’t remember any Stig.” He stopped short. “Oh no!
sentences.zh: "首先，我们得找到斯蒂格。" "斯蒂格？"奥拉夫问。"我可不记得有什么斯蒂格。"他猛地停住。"哦不！

sentences.en: Is my memory going, too?” “No, no!
sentences.zh: "我的记忆也要不行了吗？" "不不不！

sentences.en: You don’t know him.
sentences.zh: "你不认识他。

sentences.en: None of us do.
sentences.zh: "我们谁都不认识。

sentences.en: But he was there the day Sissel drowned, and he might have some answers as to why Inger was blamed.” “We’re hoping we can find him listed in the census and figure out where he lives.” Anna bit her lower lip. “If he’s still alive…” “Then what are we waiting for?” Olaf asked, jumping down and toddling away. “Let’s go find this sentence !
sentences.zh: "但他就在西塞尔溺亡那天在场，也许能说明为何英格被冤枉。" "我们希望能在人口普查名册里找到他，弄清他住哪儿。"安娜咬着下唇。"要是他还活着……" "那还等什么？"奥拉夫跳下来，一摇一摆地走开了。"咱们去找这个句——

sentences.en: I mean, census!
sentences.zh: "我是说，人口——"

sentences.en: That’s a book, right?” The trio headed to Anna’s private study, which had belonged to Elsa and their father before them.
sentences.zh: "人口名册！那是本书，对吧？"三人朝安娜的私人书房走去，这书房早先是艾莎和她们父亲用的。

sentences.en: Probably Runeard as well, once upon a time, though Anna didn’t like to think about their grandfather seated in the same old, cracked leather chair that she used now.
sentences.zh: 很可能鲁内尔德也曾用过，虽说安娜不愿去想祖父就坐在她如今坐着的这把老旧开裂的皮椅上。

sentences.en: She hadn’t mentioned this to Elsa yet, but she was getting a sneaking suspicion something about this whole mess was at least partially their grandfather’s doing.
sentences.zh: 她还没跟艾莎提过这事，但她心头渐渐生出一个隐约的怀疑：这团乱麻至少有一部分是她们祖父酿成的。

sentences.en: After all, he was why Sissel and Inger had come to Arendelle to begin with. “Luckily, they only do a census every ten or more years,” Elsa said as she opened one of the books and went to the most recent record.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，西塞尔和英格当初之所以来到阿伦黛尔，正是因为他。"幸好人口普查每隔十年或更长才做一次，"艾莎边说边翻开其中一本书，翻到最新的记录。

sentences.en: Her finger slid along each listing, which cataloged people by the farms or properties they lived on, their jobs, and their ages and marital status, along with birth and death dates and lists of the other members of the household. “Let’s see how many people named Stig used to be shepherds and are around sixty-five years old.” She shook her head. “This could take a bit, since everything’s listed by last name.” “Which is why we also need to look in these court records,” said Anna as she pulled out a thick bound book. “Since we know when the sisters visited Arendelle, I can narrow it down.” She flipped through the pages, looking for the correct year, and soon found the Vesterland sisters’ names. “This is it!
sentences.zh: 她的手指一行行划过名单——上面按人们居住的农庄或房产登记，写明职业、年龄、婚姻状况，还有出生与死亡日期及同住家庭成员。"咱们看看，名叫斯蒂格、以前当过牧羊人、如今约六十五岁的人有几个。"她摇摇头。"这可得费点工夫，因为全是按姓氏排的。" "所以我们还得查这些法庭记录，"安娜一边抽出一本厚重的装订本一边说。"既然我们知道姐妹俩来访阿伦黛尔的时间，就能缩小范围。"她翻动书页寻找正确的年份，很快找到了维斯特兰德姐妹的名字。"找到了！

sentences.en: Inger’s hearing!” Elsa and Olaf came over to look. “‘Witness, Stig Petter,’” Elsa read. “Perfect.
sentences.zh: "英格的听证会！"艾莎和奥拉夫凑过来看。"'证人，斯蒂格·佩特，'"艾莎念道。"完美。

sentences.en: I’ll just—” “Whoa,” Anna interrupted, her eyes skimming the page. “No way.” “What is it?” Elsa asked.
sentences.zh: "我这就——" "哇哦，"安娜打断了她，目光扫过那一页。"不可能。" "怎么了？"艾莎问。

sentences.en: Anna sat back. “He lied.
sentences.zh: 安娜往后一靠。"他撒谎了。

sentences.en: Stig lied!” “What?” Elsa stared down at the record in disbelief. “According to this, Stig reported seeing Inger push Sissel into the water and watch her drown,” Anna summarized. “Inger denied the claim, but as Stig was the lone witness, the court sided with him.” She closed the book, stunned. “Why would he lie?
sentences.zh: "斯蒂格撒谎了！" "什么？"艾莎难以置信地盯着记录。"据上面所写，斯蒂格报告说，他看见英格把西塞尔推入水中，眼睁睁看她淹死，"安娜概括道。"英格否认了指控，但既然斯蒂格是唯一证人，法庭便采信了他。"她合上书，惊愕不已。"他为何要撒谎？

sentences.en: He was right there!
sentences.zh: "他当时就在现场！

sentences.en: He saw the whole thing!” “Stig Petter, what are you hiding?” Elsa murmured, going back to the census and scanning the listings with her fingers. “Here he is!
sentences.zh: "整件事他都看在眼里！" "斯蒂格·佩特，你在隐瞒什么？"艾莎低声道，回到人口普查名册上，用手指一行行搜寻。"他在这儿！

sentences.en: He’s still alive,” she said, relieved. “But it looks like he doesn’t live in Arendelle anymore.” “Where does he live?” Anna asked, her heart sinking a little.
sentences.zh: "他还活着，"她松了口气说。"但他似乎已不住在阿伦黛尔了。" "他住哪儿？"安娜问，心里微微一沉。

sentences.en: Hopefully it wasn’t too far. “In the mountains.
sentences.zh: 但愿别太远。"在山里。

sentences.en: Just outside the village of Harmon.” Okay, that wasn’t far.
sentences.zh: "就在哈尔蒙村外。"好吧，那不算远。

sentences.en: And also?
sentences.zh: "而且呢？

sentences.en: Maybe since he was outside of Arendelle, Stig wouldn’t have lost his memory like everyone here had.
sentences.zh: "也许正因为他在阿伦黛尔之外，斯蒂格没有像这里所有人那样失去记忆。

sentences.en: It was a long shot.
sentences.zh: "这希望有点渺茫。

sentences.en: But it was the only one they had.
sentences.zh: "但这是她们唯一的指望。

sentences.en: Please, Stig, Anna thought when they finally arrived at his cottage after battling more wind and rain.
sentences.zh: "求你了，斯蒂格，安娜在终于顶着风雨抵达他的小屋时心想。

sentences.en: Help us get to the bottom of this mystery.
sentences.zh: "帮我们揭开这个谜团的真相。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, she wasn’t hopeful he was going to be a very cooperative witness.
sentences.zh: 可惜她并不指望他会是个配合的证人。

sentences.en: After all, he’d lied years ago.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，他多年前撒过谎。

sentences.en: What if he continued to stick to his story now?
sentences.zh: 若他现在仍咬定原来的说法，可怎么办？

sentences.en: He was their last hope; the one person who had been there—seen everything.
sentences.zh: 他是她们最后的希望；是唯一当时在场、目睹一切的人。

sentences.en: Somehow they had to convince him to help them.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，她们得说服他帮忙。

sentences.en: Or Sissel might never find peace.
sentences.zh: 否则西塞尔也许永远无法安息。

sentences.en: And Arendelle would be cast into stormy darkness forever.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔也将永远陷入风暴与黑暗。

sentences.en: Anna slid off her horse while Elsa quickly dismounted the Water Nokk and the two of them hurried to the door, rapping hard to be heard over the thunder.
sentences.zh: 安娜滑下马，艾莎也迅速从水马背上跃下，两人急步奔向门口，在雷声中用力敲门好让人听见。

sentences.en: A moment later, the door flew open.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，门猛地开了。

sentences.en: An older man with wire-rim spectacles and a bald head, tufts of white hair over his ears, stared at them angrily. “What are you doing out in weather like this?” he demanded in a gruff voice. “Mr.
sentences.zh: 一位戴金属细框眼镜、秃着头顶、耳畔垂着几撮白发的老人，怒气冲冲地瞪着她们。"这种天气你们跑出来干什么？"他用沙哑的嗓音质问。"佩特先生？

sentences.en: Petter?” Anna asked eagerly as water dripped off her nose. “Stig Petter?” “Yes,” he said, sounding cranky. “That’s my name, and yours is Queen Anna, and hers is Queen Elsa.
sentences.zh: "佩特？"安娜急切地问，水珠从鼻尖滴落。"是斯蒂格·佩特吗？" "没错，"他没好气地说。"那是我的名字，而你是安娜女王，她是艾莎女王。

sentences.en: What I don’t know is why you’re at my door.” “Something is happening in Arendelle that we could use your help with,” Elsa informed him, giving him a hopeful smile. “Can we come in?” “Sorry,” Stig said, looking suddenly nervous. “I can’t help you.” He made a move to shut his door. “Please?” Anna begged as a crack of thunder made the group jump. “Just let us in for a moment.
sentences.zh: "我只是不知道你们为何找上门来。" "阿伦黛尔正发生一些事，我们需要你帮忙，"艾莎告诉他，露出满怀希望的微笑。"我们能进去吗？" "抱歉，"斯蒂格突然显得紧张起来。"我帮不了你们。"他作势要关门。"求你了？"雷声一炸，众人都吓了一跳，安娜哀求道。"就让我们进去待一会儿。

sentences.en: We’re soaked to the bone.” Stig sighed. “Fine.
sentences.zh: "我们都湿透了。"斯蒂格叹了口气。"行吧。

sentences.en: Get in here, then.
sentences.zh: "那就进来。

sentences.en: But don’t expect anything further from me.
sentences.zh: "但别指望我还会做什么。

sentences.en: I left Arendelle fifty years ago.
sentences.zh: "我五十年前就离开了阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: And I have no interest in the kingdom’s affairs.” That didn’t sound promising.
sentences.zh: "对王国的事毫无兴趣。"这话听起来不妙。

sentences.en: But at least he was letting them in.
sentences.zh: 但至少他肯让她们进去了。

sentences.en: Maybe Anna could work on him a little more once he heard how dire the situation was.
sentences.zh: 等他听明白情况有多危急，安娜或许能再多劝劝他。

sentences.en: And at least it would get them out of the rain.
sentences.zh: 而且至少能让她们躲开雨水。

sentences.en: The two girls quickly moved into the cottage, and Stig shut the door behind them.
sentences.zh: 两个姑娘快步走进小屋，斯蒂格在身后关上了门。

sentences.en: It was a humble space with a fire roaring and a pot over the hearth that was bubbling with some sort of soup.
sentences.zh: 屋里陈设简朴，炉火正旺，壁炉上的锅里咕嘟咕嘟煮着某种汤。

sentences.en: Unlike at the Figels’ house, this soup smelled delicious. “Thank you,” Elsa said, wringing out the bottom of her dress. “We don’t mean to impose.” “We just had a few questions for you about something that happened when you were a young man,” Anna told him as she wiped her wet hands on her skirt.
sentences.zh: 与菲格尔家不同，这汤闻起来香气扑鼻。"谢谢，"艾莎拧着裙摆上的水说。"我们并非有意打扰。" "我们只想问你几个问题，关于你年轻时发生的一件事，"安娜擦着湿手、在裙子上边说。

sentences.en: She was so tired of being wet all the time.
sentences.zh: 她真是受够了总是浑身湿透。

sentences.en: Stig’s expression darkened. “If you’re asking how I got the funds for this cottage when I stopped herding sheep, that’s none of your business!
sentences.zh: 斯蒂格脸色一沉。"若是问我不当牧羊人后，是哪来的钱买下这小屋，那不关你们的事！

sentences.en: It’s like I told everyone else—I don’t owe you any explanations!
sentences.zh: "就像我跟别人说的——我无需向你们解释！

sentences.en: I inherited this cottage fair and…square.” His voice trailed off. “This isn’t about the cottage,” Elsa told him. “Oh,” Stig said, still sounding uncomfortable. “Then what is it you want to know?” Anna decided to go for broke. “We want to know about Princess Inger.
sentences.zh: "这小屋是我……正正当当继承来的。"他声音低了下去。"这和屋子无关，"艾莎告诉他。"哦，"斯蒂格仍显得不安。"那你们究竟想知道什么？"安娜决定豁出去。"我们想知道英格公主的事。

sentences.en: We know you were there the day she and her sister argued at the riverbank and Sissel was swept away.” Anna tried to sound calm.
sentences.zh: "我们知道，那天她和妹妹在河岸争吵、西塞尔被冲走时，你就在场。"安娜尽量让语气显得平静。

sentences.en: Rational.
sentences.zh: 理智。

sentences.en: Like she was asking a simple question about the weather.
sentences.zh: 仿佛只是在问一个关于天气的简单问题。

sentences.en: But inside, she was angry—Stig had lied, and his lie had destroyed a young girl’s life!
sentences.zh: 但内心深处，她怒火中烧——斯蒂格撒了谎，而他的谎言毁了一个年轻女孩的一生！

sentences.en: Why had he done it?
sentences.zh: 他为何要这么做？

sentences.en: And would he admit to it now—fifty years later?
sentences.zh: 事隔五十年，他现在会承认吗？

sentences.en: Stig stiffened. “I don’t know what you’re talking about,” he muttered.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂格僵住了。"我不知道你在说什么，"他喃喃道。

sentences.en: But his cheeks were quite red.
sentences.zh: 但他的脸颊涨得通红。

sentences.en: Another lie, Anna presumed. “Come on.
sentences.zh: 又一句谎话，安娜心想。"得了。

sentences.en: We saw the whole thing in a memory I created,” Elsa broke in. “We know that Sissel fell in while trying to save Inger, and that you were there and tried to help save her.
sentences.zh: "我们在我创造的一段记忆里，亲眼看到了整件事，"艾莎插话道。"我们知道，西塞尔是为了救英格才掉进水里的，而你在场，还曾试着救她。

sentences.en: When you couldn’t, you went back and comforted Inger.” “You told her you were going to help her!” Anna added indignantly. “And then you went and accused her of murder!
sentences.zh: "你没能救成，便回去安慰英格。" "你还对她说会帮她的！"安娜愤愤地补了一句。"结果你反倒去指控她谋杀！

sentences.en: Publicly!
sentences.zh: "当众！

sentences.en: Because of you, she was sentenced to death!
sentences.zh: "就因为你的证词，她被判了死刑！

sentences.en: For something you know she didn’t do!” Stig’s face hardened. “You have to leave.
sentences.zh: "为你明知她没做的事！"斯蒂格脸色一沉。"你们得走。

sentences.en: Now,” he said, guiding Anna by the arm to the door. “I’m sorry, Your Majesties, but I have made my peace with this matter.” His voice caught. “I never want to hear the Vesterland sisters’ names again.” Anna was so close she could see the deep wrinkles in his forehead and the windburn on his chapped cheeks.
sentences.zh: "现在，"他说着，攥着安娜的手臂把她往门口带。"很抱歉，两位陛下，但这件事我已与自己和解了。"他声音哽咽。"我永远不想再听到维斯特兰德姐妹的名字。"安娜离得那样近，能看清他额头深深的皱纹和皲裂脸颊上的冻伤。

sentences.en: His blue eyes were almost gray with age and held so much fear.
sentences.zh: 他苍老得发灰的蓝眼睛里，盛满了恐惧。

sentences.en: Something had happened that day that haunted him.
sentences.zh: 那天发生的某件事，一直缠着他不放。

sentences.en: But what?
sentences.zh: 可那究竟是什么？

sentences.en: Why would he lie about Inger?
sentences.zh: 他为何要诬陷英格？

sentences.en: Why did he live up here alone, hidden away from the world, and bristle at talk of how he paid for his cottage, unless… Suddenly she remembered her hunch back at the castle.
sentences.zh: 他为何独居在此、与世隔绝，又为何一提起买屋的钱就恼火——除非……她忽然记起在城堡里的那个直觉。

sentences.en: She turned to face Stig and tried to take a different approach. “Someone asked you to lie about Inger, didn’t they?” she said gently, not really making it a question.
sentences.zh: 她转向斯蒂格，试着换个方式。"是有人让你诬陷英格的，对吧？"她轻声说，这并不像一句真正的问话。

sentences.en: Stig looked away, not answering her, which told her she was probably right. “But who would do that?” Elsa asked, turning to her sister in confusion. “Isn’t it obvious?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂格移开目光，没有回答，这让她知道自己多半猜对了。"可谁会这么做呢？"艾莎困惑地转向妹妹问。"这还用说吗？

sentences.en: Our grandfather,” Anna pronounced. “With Sissel dead and Inger being held for her murder, the Vesterland sisters couldn’t oppose the dam,” she explained. “You heard them in that memory—they wanted to go back and stand up to Grandfather.
sentences.zh: "我们的祖父，"安娜断言。"西塞尔一死，英格又被当作凶手关押，维斯特兰德姐妹便无法反对大坝了，"她解释道。"你在那段记忆里听见过——她们想回去对抗祖父。

sentences.en: Inger convinced Sissel not to help fund the dam, and they could have rallied other nearby kingdoms, too, which would have meant Arendelle wouldn’t have the funding to build.” She drew in a breath. “Grandfather couldn’t allow that to happen.” “That’s horrible,” Elsa whispered. “And yet, it makes sense.
sentences.zh: "是英格说服西塞尔别资助大坝，她们还能联合附近其他王国，那样阿伦黛尔就筹不到钱来建造了。"她深吸一口气。"祖父绝不能让这种事发生。" "太可怕了，"艾莎低语。"可这话又说通了。

sentences.en: Even with Sissel gone, Inger never would have stopped fighting Grandfather on the dam.” She glanced at Stig. “If he had a witness willing to say Inger pushed Sissel in the river, neither sister would ever be a problem for him again.” Stig placed his face in his hands.
sentences.zh: "即便西塞尔不在了，英格也绝不会停止在大坝上与祖父抗争。"她瞥了斯蒂格一眼。"只要有个愿意指证英格将西塞尔推入河中的证人，两姐妹就再也不会是他的麻烦了。"斯蒂格双手捂住了脸。

sentences.en: A single tear slipped down his cheek.
sentences.zh: 一滴泪顺着他的脸颊滑落。

sentences.en: When he finally looked up, the hurt in his face was visible. “You’re right.
sentences.zh: 当他终于抬起头，脸上的痛楚清晰可见。"你们说得对。

sentences.en: I lied then.
sentences.zh: "那时我撒了谎。

sentences.en: And now, fifty years later, those lies are still haunting me.” He grabbed a handkerchief and blew into it loudly. “Trust me, I’ll never forgive myself for what I did to that poor, sweet girl, but it’s too late to do anything about it now.” “Actually, that might not be true,” said Anna as she took his hand and led him to a chair. “Let’s talk.
sentences.zh: "而如今，五十年过去了，那些谎言仍在缠着我。"他抓起手帕，响亮地擤了擤鼻子。"相信我，我永远无法原谅自己对不起那个可怜又善良的姑娘，但现在做什么都太迟了。" "其实，也许还不至于，"安娜握着他的手，把他领到椅子上坐下。"我们谈谈。

sentences.en: So, King Runeard told you to lie?” “Yes,” Stig said, his voice shaking.
sentences.zh: "那么，是鲁内尔德国王让你撒谎的？" "是的，"斯蒂格声音颤抖地说。

sentences.en: It took him a moment before he spoke again.
sentences.zh: 他停顿了片刻，才又开口。

sentences.en: Anna waited patiently. “I wasn’t planning to lie at first.
