“快啊，风灵！

“快点！”艾莎紧张地抬头望向漆黑阴沉的天空，狂风卷起她的头发，让她恨不得把头发重新编成辫子。

至少雨和雪都停了。

尽管如此，他们已经在这波涛汹涌的海面上挣扎着返回阿伦黛尔好几个小时了，可风却丝毫不肯配合。

相反，风把船像玩具小船一样抛来甩去，害得她胃里翻江倒海。

风灵已经使出了全力推动小船前进，可就连风之精灵也难以在风暴中逆风而行。

而水马在汹涌的海面上也寸步难行，似乎对风灵的努力不屑一顾。“你该和其他人一起到甲板下去，”埃里克船长不得不扯着嗓子盖过风声下令，“外面不安全。”船员们来回奔跑，互相喊叫；就连他们那经过海浪考验的稳当脚步也显得踉跄起来。

艾莎生硬地点了点头。“我没事，”她向他保证，“我得确认风灵和水马不需要任何帮助。”虽说在这种情形下，冰魔法其实没什么大用。

有那么一瞬，她想象着父母也曾身处相似的风暴、相似的船上，就在船沉没之前。

而他们当时并没有魔法精灵帮他们浮在水面。

他们是在哪一刻意识到自己撑不下去的？

一想到父母是为了去暗海试图救她才出海的，艾莎心里仍有一丝愧疚。

但她心里明白，如果换作自己处在他们的位置，也会做出同样的选择去救他们。

他们已经尽了一切努力去救她。

而现在，她和妹妹将去拯救阿伦黛尔。

只要他们能及时赶到。“陆地，前方有陆地！”突然，一个声音从上方桅杆上的瞭望台穿过风声传来。

艾莎踉跄着跑到甲板前端，使劲眯眼想看清瞭望员所见。

果然，她瞥见岸边闪烁着点点微光。

那是家家户户的灯笼。

来自阿伦黛尔。

她长舒了一口气。

她觉得自己从没这么高兴见到家乡——这可说明了很多。

（不过考虑到船越靠越近时岸边一片漆黑，“看见”这个词或许并不贴切。）此时的艾莎已经完全没了时间概念，根本不知道他们是在深夜航行，还是正当中午。“阿伦黛尔，”一个声音在她身旁轻声说，王国已映入眼帘，“我从未想过还能再亲眼看到它。”艾莎转头，发现英格已经来到船头，站在她身边。

和她的孙女一样，这位老妇人站稳了脚跟，不用扶着船舷也能立稳。

她选择乘他们的船同行，而孙女则指挥着那艘主海盗船。“我敢说这地方带给你的不是什么好回忆，”艾莎对这位前公主歉疚地说。“是没有——可某种意义上，也有，”英格坦言，明亮的蓝眼睛里蒙上一层泪雾。“那是我和茜塞尔共度最后时光的地方。

我们小时候常来这里。

在阿伦黛尔，我们总是玩得很开心。

那里的人那么热情、好客。

还有巧克力！”她舔了舔干裂的嘴唇，“我一直都最爱巧克力！”“听起来你和我有许多共同点，”安娜温柔地说，走上前来站在她们身边。

她被风暴折腾得还有点脸色发青，但看到海岸越来越近，神情也放松了许多。

英格朝她温暖地笑了笑。“也许吧。

可你比我当年勇敢多了，”她对安娜说，“听大家说，你有勇气采取行动。

去炸毁水坝、解放森林。

你为我们的世界所做的善事，怎么夸赞都不为过。”安娜脸红了。“那是该做的事。”“有时候，做对的事恰恰是最难的事，”英格回答。

她凝望着阿伦黛尔的海岸，神情恍惚而怅然。

艾莎打心底里怜惜她。

英格大半生都在逃亡中度过。

远离家乡、远离家人，也失去了妹妹。

若不是安娜不肯放弃她，这本来也很容易成为艾莎的命运。

她无法想象没有妹妹在身边，自己该如何面对这个世界。

水手们一边靠港，一边互相吆喝。

虽然风暴终于渐渐平息，但在如此起伏的海面上靠岸并不容易，他们头几次尝试，船都重重撞上码头，把所有人都晃得踉跄。

风灵接手，轻柔地将船送向岸边，水手们终于能跳下船去把它们系好。

等船发出“一切就绪”的信号，艾莎便朝跳板走去。“来吧，”她对妹妹和英格说，“我们这就去。”她们顺着跳板走下船。

可就在这时——“站住！

以阿伦黛尔之名！”一个高大的身影挡在他们面前，拦住去路，艾莎吃了一惊。

那是马提亚斯，身边还围着一队卫兵。

他“唰”地抽出剑，剑尖直指她的咽喉。“你们是什么人，为何侵犯我们的海岸？

你们是海盗吗？

因为我们这座庄严的城镇，绝不容海盗放肆。”艾莎震惊地盯着他。

随即她恍然大悟。

他不记得她了。

他谁都不记得了！“马提亚斯！”她惊恐地喊道，“是我！

艾莎！”“艾莎？”他的嘴唇念着她的名字，可眼里毫无认出的神色。“我不认识什么艾莎。”他转向卫兵，“这有人认识一个叫艾莎的吗？”他们面面相觑，完全摸不着头脑。

噢，不！

他们的记忆都没了！

所有人都是！“借过！

借过一下！”艾莎越过马提亚斯身后，看到奥拉夫正费力地从士兵的人群中挤过来。

令艾莎惊讶的是，他戴着一个十分考究的领结，还穿着绣花马甲。“奥拉夫！

这到底是怎么回事？”安娜开口道。

但奥拉夫把一根手指抵在嘴唇上。“嘘，”他小声说，“配合我就行，好吗？”他跳上旁边一块大石头，转身面对困惑的民众和士兵。“没事了！”他喊道，“这两位是我的朋友，艾莎和安娜。

他们是来帮我们的！”艾莎松了口气，马提亚斯点了点头。“抱歉，陛下，”他说，“我方才没认出来。”他收剑入鞘，恭恭敬敬地向……奥拉夫鞠了一躬？

雪人咯咯笑起来，有点难为情。“说来话长，”趁着人群散去，他小声对艾莎说，“这么说吧，他们的记忆比以前更糟了。

事实上，他们把你们两个全忘光了。”“我看出来了，”艾莎干巴巴地说，“事情开始变得真的很疯狂。

大家都在打架。

没人记得律法是什么。

我得想个法子维持秩序。

所以……我可能编了个小故事。”“说你是他们的统治者？”安娜挑起眉毛问。“这么说吧，管用了！！”他得意地咧嘴一笑，“他们听我的，城堡和村庄都还在。”“这其实真的很聪明，”艾莎说着拍了拍奥拉夫的头，“谢谢你。”“愿为您效劳！”他郑重宣布，“不过现在我希望你们已经想出办法摆脱这团乱麻，因为现在大家连怎么拥抱都忘了！

真让人难过！”“我们也这么觉得。

但我们需要大家集中注意力，”安娜说，“你能确保在接下来十分钟内，把他们全都召集到镇广场父母的雕像前吗？

我们得给他们讲讲我们自己的故事。”“奥拉夫国王听候差遣！”他郑重宣布。

接着他不好意思地耸了耸肩。“我是说，交给我就行！”奥拉夫一溜烟跑开了，一边跑一边发号施令。

艾莎瞥了安娜一眼，安娜迟疑地朝她笑了笑。

她知道妹妹在想什么——这招最好管用！

不然在可预见的将来，安娜就得在幕后当统治者了！

艾莎转回身面对英格，她还站在跳板上，突然显得十分紧张。“你没事吧？”她问。“我只是……我想我是害怕，”英格缓缓说道，“已经过去这么多年了。

要是他们不相信我怎么办？

要是他们说该把我关起来呢？”“我们相信你，”安娜向她保证，“等他们听完整个故事，也会信的。”“我们还有斯蒂格为你作证，”艾莎补充道，目光在广场上搜寻。

斯蒂格到达阿伦黛尔了吗？

她还没看到他的踪影。

但愿他没有因为害怕而临阵退缩。

英格犹豫着，仍是一副将信将疑的样子。

但她的孙女从身后走上前，搂住她的肩膀。“来吧，奶奶，”她温柔地说，“时候到了。”“我想你是对的，”英格说，“无论发生什么，至少我死也能瞑目了，因为我讲了实话。”她们一起朝镇广场走去。

奥拉夫尽职了，一大群人已经聚在乐队的舞台周围。

瑞德扶着祖母登上台阶，艾莎和安娜也走上台，转身面向人群。“阿伦黛尔的人民，”安娜对众人说道。

艾莎沮丧地发现，根本没人在听。

他们都在彼此闲聊，完全没把台上的人放在心上。

安娜无奈地叹了口气。“奥拉夫？”她喊道，“帮帮忙好吗？”奥拉夫从人群中挤过来，走上了舞台。

他蹦上舞台，转身面向人群，把树枝手放进嘴里，吹了一声响亮的口哨。

人群立刻安静下来。

所有人都转向舞台。

安娜翻了个白眼。“女士们，先生们，”奥拉夫庄重地说，“请允许我向各位介绍今天的说书人！

他们有一个精彩绝伦的故事要讲，定能让您和孩子们听得入迷。

惊险、刺激、跌宕起伏，应有尽有！

所以请大家全神贯注地听。

他们是我最最亲爱的朋友，理应得到所有人的敬重。”说罢，他一蹦下了舞台，留下安娜、艾莎、英格和瑞德站在台上。

安娜咬着下唇，望向台下——此刻人们正好奇地抬头盯着她们。“要我开始吗？”她小声问。

艾莎皱了皱眉。“我想是的。

不过我本希望斯蒂格能在这儿。

你看到他在哪儿了吗？”安娜扫视人群。“没有。

你觉得他临阵退缩了？”“要是这样，我们可就很难证明我们的故事了。”“你觉得我们该多等他一会儿吗？”艾莎抬头望向天空。

云层已经厚了起来。

看样子马上又要下雨了。

一旦下起倾盆大雨，他们就会失去听众。

这是他们唯一的机会。“不行。

开始吧。

就算他没出现，我们也能想出别的办法，”她对安娜说。

安娜清了清嗓子，转向人群。“大家听好了！”她用一种十分威严的声调说道，尽管台下没人认得出这声音。“正如奥拉夫所说，今天我们要给大家讲一个故事。

英格和茜塞尔的真实故事。

也就是众所周知的维斯特兰姐妹。”人群礼貌地鼓起掌来。

几个小孩子在前排盘腿坐在地上。

艾莎突然想到，既然大家几乎把其他一切都忘了，不知道还有没有人记得维斯特兰姐妹最初的故事。

不过话说回来，也许他们不记得那个虚假的故事反倒更好。

这样，只要把真相告诉他们就好。

也许，从一开始这就是茜塞尔的计划……

于是安娜开始讲述她的故事。

人群静静听着，随着故事推进越发投入。

讲到茜塞尔跌落瀑布时，许多听众倒吸一口凉气；瑞德紧紧抱住祖母，把脸埋进孙女的肩膀，显然正重温着她自己记忆中的过往。“英格已经竭尽全力去救妹妹了，”安娜讲完时对在场上的人说，“那是个意外。

简单，却真实。

若不是我们的外祖父鲁内尔德国王从中作梗，这件事本该被如实记录——他看准了诬陷一个无辜之人能带来政治好处。”她继续讲述国王的贪婪与欺骗——以及他执意要建水坝，哪怕以他人的生命和名誉为代价。“可大家为什么会相信他呢？”画家格雷琴在安娜停下来喘口气时问道，“他当时根本不在场！

他不可能知道到底发生了什么。”“他们相信他，是因为我替他的说辞作了证。”听到一个突如其来、出乎意料的声音，所有人都转过身去。

艾莎瞥见人群后方的那个身影，在心里暗暗欢呼。

斯蒂格！

他终究还是来了！

而且来得正是时候。“我就是那个证人，”他一瘸一拐地朝舞台走来，说道。

人们向后退去，给他让出空间。

他呼吸急促，一瘸一拐地走着，但终究还是走到了台前。

他看到英格，羞愧地低下头。“我非常抱歉，公主殿下，”他说，“没错，他威胁过我，可那不能成为我所作所为的借口。

也不能成为我这些年来隐瞒真相的理由。

我那样对你，你根本不该承受。

我这辈子都在为那个决定后悔。”有片刻，英格严厉地俯视着他，蓝色的眼睛仿佛要刺穿他的灵魂。

随后，她布满皱纹的脸庞柔和下来。

她伸出手，搭在他的肩上。“我理解，”她缓缓说道，“你和我一样，都是受害者。

那时我们都还只是孩子。

是那场致命政治博弈中的棋子。

假如你不肯就范，鲁内尔德国王很可能会杀了你，再找别人替你撒谎。

他想让我消失，为此会不择手段。”“真是个大坏蛋！”安娜嘟囔道，“真不敢相信我和他有血缘关系！”“那么您……”斯蒂格使劲咽了口唾沫，“您……原谅我了吗？”英格郑重地点了点头。“我原谅你。

也希望有一天你能原谅自己。”两人紧紧握住彼此的手。

人群中爆发出兴奋的欢呼。

他们也许并不知道全部真相，但显然已被深深吸引。

艾莎叹了口气。

唉，有总比没有强。“所以现在你们都知道了，”安娜转身回到阿伦黛尔人民面前，郑重宣布，“维斯特兰姐妹的真实故事。

以及为何在我们的王国里，贪婪、谎言与私利绝不能再被容忍。

从今往后，她们的故事将被如实写进史册，传遍四面八方。

英格不是杀人犯。

她是一名战士。

一位环境的守护者。

一个深爱着妹妹的女孩。”全场观众都鼓掌欢呼起来。

英格低头望着他们，难以置信地摇着头。“这么多年了，”她轻声说，“我从没想过……”“噢，奶奶！”瑞德紧紧抱住她。

艾莎扫视人群，咬着下唇。

成功了吗？

他们已经讲出了真相。

这难道意味着大家的记忆都恢复了？“马提亚斯？”她试着朝将军喊了一声。

可他正忙着向奥拉夫鞠躬。

艾莎转向安娜，脸色惨白。“没用！”她喊道，“为什么没用？”“我不知道！”安娜和艾莎一样慌乱，“难道还缺了什么？

茜塞尔还想要什么？”她的话被一声刺耳的非人尖叫打断。

闪电划过天空，紧接着是隆隆的雷声。

一声尖叫从港口方向传来。

所有人都转头望去，被眼前的景象吓得倒吸凉气。

那具亡灵从深海浮现。

她缓缓爬出水面，满身缠着黑色海藻，畸形的双脚在泥里发出咯吱咯吱的声响。

到了岸边，她直起身来，布满血丝的眼睛里燃烧着怒火。

她举起双臂。

一声低沉的呻吟从她唇间逸出。“噢，天哪！”英格声音沙哑地低语，紧紧抓着孙女。“那是？

那不可能是她！

她……她是——”“怪物！”赫尔穆特抓起冰镐，护在身前喊道，“大家快跑！

快躲起来！”人群尖叫起来，四散奔逃。

茜塞尔咆哮着，踉跄地追在后面。“妹——妹，”她呻吟着，“妹——妹——妹。”“等等！

住手！”安娜喊道，可没人听她的。

他们都忙着逃命。

突然，马提亚斯跃到亡灵面前，猛地抽出剑。

他向前迈了一步，目光死死锁定那怪物。

他紧抿着嘴，神情凶悍。“以阿伦黛尔之名，停下！”他命令道，“否则我就在你站立之处将你劈倒！”“不要！”英格惊恐地喊道，“求你别伤害她！”“马提亚斯！”安娜试图阻止。

可他连头都没回。

他不再听命于她了。

还有奥拉夫——奥拉夫去哪儿了？

她的目光在广场上四处搜寻，看到雪人正在对面安抚一个小男孩。

他离得太远——根本来不及赶到。

马提亚斯冲了上去。

艾莎反应极快，抬手朝他射出一堵冰墙。

他被冰墙弹开，向后摔倒，重重跌在地上。

艾莎皱起了眉。

她待会儿得向他道歉，可她绝不能让马提亚斯伤害英格的妹妹。“妹——妹。

我——的——”艾莎抓住英格的胳膊。“跟她说话，”她催促道，“她是你的妹妹。

只有你能阻止这一切！”英格缓缓点头，深吸一口气。

那一刻，她不再像个老妇人，而像传说中的海盗女王。

她向前迈了一步，从孙女的怀抱中挣脱出来。

她挺直肩膀，艾莎感到脊背一阵发凉。“茜塞尔！”那具亡灵停住脚步，歪着头转向一侧。

她转向声音传来的方向，腐烂的脸上浮现出突如其来的困惑。“妹——妹？”亡灵喃喃道。

英格走下讲台，来到那怪物正前方。“是的，”她说，声音此刻微微发颤，“我是你妹妹。

英格。

而你该停下这一切。

现在。”茜塞尔发出一声轻微的呻吟。

她盯着英格，眯起眼睛，仿佛在判断自己是不是受了骗。

显然，英格和茜塞尔上次见到她时的那个女孩已毫无相似之处。

已经过去了那么多年。

亡灵会认出她吗？“没事了，茜塞尔，”英格轻声说，“你找到我了。

你终于可以安息了。”茜塞尔又发出一声呻吟，可这一声听起来不一样。

这次不是悲伤。

不是愤怒。

不是困惑。

而是满含喜悦。“妹——妹？”她疑惑地问，“我的妹妹？”“是的，”英格应道，声音因激动而哽咽，“是的！

你是我的妹妹。

我亲爱的妹妹。

我好想你。”突然，令艾莎震惊的是，那具亡灵似乎渐渐淡去。

怪物消失时，人群中响起一片惊呼。

取而代之的，是一位年轻女子的幽灵幻影，她穿着旧式衣裙，留着齐耳短发。

那是茜塞尔生前的模样。

此刻就站在他们面前。“英格！”茜塞尔喊道，“噢，英格！”英格向前奔去，仿佛自己也回到了二十岁。

艾莎明白，她是要张开双臂拥抱妹妹。

艾莎心一紧，急速思索，朝那幻影射出一束冰，尽可能将她的身体凝实，好让姐妹俩至少能重逢片刻。

英格扑向茜塞尔，紧紧抱住她，把脸埋进她冰冷的肩头，全村人都惊叹地看着。“噢，茜塞尔。

我终于找到你了。

我好想你！”“我也想你。

他们说了你许多坏话。”茜塞尔本来的声音回来了，听起来又和艾莎幻象中一样。“他们说是你杀了我。

说你把我推下了河。

我想告诉他们——你绝不会伤害我！

我们毕竟是姐妹啊！”“我知道，”英格说着，从拥抱中退开。

她脸上泪痕斑斑。“不过我们不必再为那件事担心了。

多亏了这两位勇敢的姑娘。”她朝艾莎和安娜示意，“这两位姐妹。

多亏了她们，再不会有人把我们的故事讲错了。”茜塞尔的目光落到两姐妹身上。“谢谢你们，”她轻声说，“谢谢你们纠正了这一切。

还让我和妹妹重逢。

你们不会明白这对我有多重要。”“噢，我想我大概能体会，”艾莎微微一笑。

她抬手摸向脸颊，发现已被幸福的泪水打湿。

安娜伸手搂住她的腰。

她没有说话，但艾莎完全知道她在想什么。

这世上没有什么能比得上两姐妹之间的爱。“好了，”姐妹俩含泪再次相拥时，安娜转向艾莎宣布，“我想我们终于弄清楚茜塞尔想要什么了。

说实话，我们一开始其实就该猜到的。

我的意思是，谁不想要回自己的妹妹呢？”艾莎冲她笑了笑。“可不是嘛，”她表示赞同。“嘿！”奥拉夫突然挤到她们中间。“看！

太阳回来了！”等等，什么？

艾莎的目光猛地投向天空。

她方才太沉浸在团聚的喜悦中，竟没注意到外面的天已经亮了不少。

此刻她才看清，暴风云已经散去，露出西沉的落日、朦胧的蓝色暮色，以及一片璀璨的星海。

她屏住了呼吸。

风暴结束了。

这意味着……她转回身面向两姐妹。

可令她意外的是，此刻只有英格还站在那里。

茜塞尔已经消失了。

英格一瘸一拐地走到姑娘们面前，脸上挂着悲伤的微笑。“她走了，”她告诉她们，“云一散、太阳一出来，她就消失了。”“我很遗憾，”艾莎说着，把手搭在老海盗的臂上。“别遗憾。”英格的蓝眼睛湿润却明亮，她看看艾莎、安娜，又看看瑞德。“你们给了我毕生渴望的东西。

一个能好好道别的机会。

而茜塞尔——嗯，多亏了你们，她终于能得到永恒的安息了。”“我真高兴，”安娜说，“而且我现在向你们保证，再不会有人把你们的故事讲错了。

我们要建一座纪念碑！

不，一座纪念堂！

我们甚至可以请威尔为《村庄之冠》写一篇文章！”她兴奋地补充道，“我们要把整个故事讲出来——完完全全按它真实的样子！

我们要把报纸散发到四面八方，让周围所有王国——包括维斯特兰——的人终于都能知道真相。”“听起来太棒了，”英格说，“谢谢你们，好孩子们。

我觉得，你们身上有你们祖母的影子。”她温柔地看了她们一眼。“真希望我们曾认识她，”安娜怅然地说。“总有一天我会回来，把关于她的一切都讲给你们听，”英格承诺道，“不过现在，我得回到我的船员那里了。

他们一定想知道接下来该怎么办。

我们的使命已经持续太久了。

但现在我们终于有机会重新开始。”“你确定不能留下吗？”安娜问，“如果愿意，你们可以和我们一同参加极夜节的庆祝活动。

你和你的船员们。

只要你们需要，阿伦黛尔永远是你们的家。”“我很感激。

但我还有另一件必须先行完成的事。”她咬着下唇，显得有些忐忑。“我终于得回家了。”“回维斯特兰的家？”艾莎惊讶地问。

虽说也许她本不该惊讶。

英格点了点头。“已经五十年了。

我想在死前再看看它。”“这主意太好了，”安娜表示赞同，“我可以事先给乔纳斯国王和他的女儿玛丽捎话，”她热切地说，“既然真相已大白，我确信他们一定会张开双臂欢迎你。”“谢谢你们，”英格说着，向两姐妹深深鞠躬，“现在，如果你们允许，我就告辞了。

你们大概还有很多善后要处理。”她苦笑了一下，“不过我不担心。

毕竟，只要两姐妹同心，就没有什么做不到的事。”艾莎转向安娜。

两人都咧嘴笑了。“这才是一个真实的故事，”她宣布道。

安娜挽住艾莎的手臂，望着英格和孙女登上她们的海盗船，准备起航。

此刻海面平静，天空是一片美丽的湛蓝。

茜塞尔对阿伦黛尔的束缚终于消散了。“噢，不！”身后有人喊道，“不，不，不！”

sentences.en: Gale was doing its best to move the boat along, but even the Wind Spirit was having trouble making headway against the storm.
sentences.zh: 风灵已经使出了全力推动小船前进，可就连风之精灵也难以在风暴中逆风而行。

sentences.en: And the Water Nokk was having no luck navigating the rough seas, which seemed to be unimpressed by the spirit’s attempts. “You should go belowdecks with the others,” Captain Erik commanded, having to shout over the wind. “It’s not safe out here.” The crew was running from side to side, yelling at one another; even their sea legs were looking unsure.
sentences.zh: 而水马在汹涌的海面上也寸步难行，似乎对风灵的努力不屑一顾。“你该和其他人一起到甲板下去，”埃里克船长不得不扯着嗓子盖过风声下令，“外面不安全。”船员们来回奔跑，互相喊叫；就连他们那经过海浪考验的稳当脚步也显得踉跄起来。

sentences.en: Elsa nodded stiffly. “I’m all right,” she assured him. “I need to make sure Gale and the Water Nokk don’t need any help.” Not that ice powers were all that useful in a situation like this.
sentences.zh: 艾莎生硬地点了点头。“我没事，”她向他保证，“我得确认风灵和水马不需要任何帮助。”虽说在这种情形下，冰魔法其实没什么大用。

sentences.en: For a moment she imagined her parents, in a similar storm, on a similar ship, just before it went down.
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬，她想象着父母也曾身处相似的风暴、相似的船上，就在船沉没之前。

sentences.en: And they hadn’t had magical spirits to help them stay afloat.
sentences.zh: 而他们当时并没有魔法精灵帮他们浮在水面。

sentences.en: At what moment had they realized they weren’t going to make it?
sentences.zh: 他们是在哪一刻意识到自己撑不下去的？

sentences.en: Elsa still felt a little guilty about the fact that they’d gone out to the Dark Sea to try to help her.
sentences.zh: 一想到父母是为了去暗海试图救她才出海的，艾莎心里仍有一丝愧疚。

sentences.en: But she knew, in her heart, if she’d been in their shoes, she would have made the same choice to help them.
sentences.zh: 但她心里明白，如果换作自己处在他们的位置，也会做出同样的选择去救他们。

sentences.en: They had done their best to save her.
sentences.zh: 他们已经尽了一切努力去救她。

sentences.en: And now she and her sister would save Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 而现在，她和妹妹将去拯救阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: If they could reach it in time. “Land ho!” Suddenly a voice cut through the wind from the ship’s crow’s nest above.
sentences.zh: 只要他们能及时赶到。“陆地，前方有陆地！”突然，一个声音从上方桅杆上的瞭望台穿过风声传来。

sentences.en: Elsa stumbled to the front of the deck, straining to see what the lookout saw.
sentences.zh: 艾莎踉跄着跑到甲板前端，使劲眯眼想看清瞭望员所见。

sentences.en: Sure enough, she could catch glimpses of small flickering lights at the shore.
sentences.zh: 果然，她瞥见岸边闪烁着点点微光。

sentences.en: Lanterns from houses.
sentences.zh: 那是家家户户的灯笼。

sentences.en: From Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 来自阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: She breathed a sigh of relief.
sentences.zh: 她长舒了一口气。

sentences.en: She didn’t think she’d ever been so glad to see her hometown—and that was saying something.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己从没这么高兴见到家乡——这可说明了很多。

sentences.en: (Though “see” might not have been the right word in this case, considering how dark the shore was as the ships pulled closer.) Elsa had lost track of time at this point and had no idea whether they were traveling in the dead of night—or the middle of the day. “Arendelle,” a voice whispered beside her as the kingdom came into view. “I never thought I’d lay eyes on it again.” Elsa turned to see that Inger had joined her at the front of the boat.
sentences.zh: （不过考虑到船越靠越近时岸边一片漆黑，“看见”这个词或许并不贴切。）此时的艾莎已经完全没了时间概念，根本不知道他们是在深夜航行，还是正当中午。“阿伦黛尔，”一个声音在她身旁轻声说，王国已映入眼帘，“我从未想过还能再亲眼看到它。”艾莎转头，发现英格已经来到船头，站在她身边。

sentences.en: Like her granddaughter, the woman had her sea legs and stood without holding on to the sides.
sentences.zh: 和她的孙女一样，这位老妇人站稳了脚跟，不用扶着船舷也能立稳。

sentences.en: She’d chosen to travel with them on their ship, while her granddaughter helmed the main pirate ship. “I’m sure it doesn’t bring back good memories for you,” Elsa said apologetically to the former princess. “It doesn’t—and yet, in a way it does,” Inger confessed, tears misting her bright blue eyes. “It was the last place I spent time with Sissel.
sentences.zh: 她选择乘他们的船同行，而孙女则指挥着那艘主海盗船。“我敢说这地方带给你的不是什么好回忆，”艾莎对这位前公主歉疚地说。“是没有——可某种意义上，也有，”英格坦言，明亮的蓝眼睛里蒙上一层泪雾。“那是我和茜塞尔共度最后时光的地方。

sentences.en: We’d come here a lot as children.
sentences.zh: 我们小时候常来这里。

sentences.en: And we always had a good time in Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 在阿伦黛尔，我们总是玩得很开心。

sentences.en: The people were so warm and welcoming.
sentences.zh: 那里的人那么热情、好客。

sentences.en: And the chocolate!” She licked her cracked lips. “I always loved the chocolate!” “Sounds like you and I have a lot in common,” Anna said gently, coming up beside them.
sentences.zh: 还有巧克力！”她舔了舔干裂的嘴唇，“我一直都最爱巧克力！”“听起来你和我有许多共同点，”安娜温柔地说，走上前来站在她们身边。

sentences.en: She still looked a little green from the storm, but she also looked very relieved to see the shore coming closer.
sentences.zh: 她被风暴折腾得还有点脸色发青，但看到海岸越来越近，神情也放松了许多。

sentences.en: Inger smiled warmly at her. “Perhaps.
sentences.zh: 英格朝她温暖地笑了笑。“也许吧。

sentences.en: But you are much braver than I ever was,” she told Anna. “From what I’ve heard, you had the courage to act.
sentences.zh: 可你比我当年勇敢多了，”她对安娜说，“听大家说，你有勇气采取行动。

sentences.en: To break the dam and free the forest.
sentences.zh: 去炸毁水坝、解放森林。

sentences.en: The good you have done for our world cannot be overstated.” Anna blushed. “It was the right thing to do.” “Sometimes doing the right thing is the hardest thing of all,” Inger replied.
sentences.zh: 你为我们的世界所做的善事，怎么夸赞都不为过。”安娜脸红了。“那是该做的事。”“有时候，做对的事恰恰是最难的事，”英格回答。

sentences.en: She stared at Arendelle’s shores, looking wistful.
sentences.zh: 她凝望着阿伦黛尔的海岸，神情恍惚而怅然。

sentences.en: Elsa’s heart went out to her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎打心底里怜惜她。

sentences.en: Most of Inger’s life had been spent on the run.
sentences.zh: 英格大半生都在逃亡中度过。

sentences.en: Away from her home and her family, and without her sister.
sentences.zh: 远离家乡、远离家人，也失去了妹妹。

sentences.en: That could have easily been Elsa’s fate, too, had Anna not refused to give up on her.
sentences.zh: 若不是安娜不肯放弃她，这本来也很容易成为艾莎的命运。

sentences.en: She couldn’t imagine facing the world without her sister by her side.
sentences.zh: 她无法想象没有妹妹在身边，自己该如何面对这个世界。

sentences.en: The sailors shouted to one another as they pulled into port.
sentences.zh: 水手们一边靠港，一边互相吆喝。

sentences.en: Though the storm was finally easing, it wasn’t easy docking in such choppy waters, and their first tries had the ships slamming hard against the docks, causing everyone to stumble.
sentences.zh: 虽然风暴终于渐渐平息，但在如此起伏的海面上靠岸并不容易，他们头几次尝试，船都重重撞上码头，把所有人都晃得踉跄。

sentences.en: Gale took over, easing the ships toward the land, and at last the sailors were able to jump out and tie them off.
sentences.zh: 风灵接手，轻柔地将船送向岸边，水手们终于能跳下船去把它们系好。

sentences.en: Elsa stepped toward the gangplank once they’d given the all clear. “Come on,” she said to her sister and Inger. “Let’s do this.” They started down the gangplank and off the ship.
sentences.zh: 等船发出“一切就绪”的信号，艾莎便朝跳板走去。“来吧，”她对妹妹和英格说，“我们这就去。”她们顺着跳板走下船。

sentences.en: But then— “Stop!
sentences.zh: 可就在这时——“站住！

sentences.en: In the name of Arendelle!” Elsa startled as a tall figure stepped before them, blocking their path.
sentences.zh: 以阿伦黛尔之名！”一个高大的身影挡在他们面前，拦住去路，艾莎吃了一惊。

sentences.en: It was Mattias, and he was surrounded by guards.
sentences.zh: 那是马提亚斯，身边还围着一队卫兵。

sentences.en: He pulled his sword from its sheath and pointed it at her throat. “Who are you and why do you breach our shores?
sentences.zh: 他“唰”地抽出剑，剑尖直指她的咽喉。“你们是什么人，为何侵犯我们的海岸？

sentences.en: Are you pirates?
sentences.zh: 你们是海盗吗？

sentences.en: For we do not suffer pirates lightly in this noble town.” Elsa stared at him in shock.
sentences.zh: 因为我们这座庄严的城镇，绝不容海盗放肆。”艾莎震惊地盯着他。

sentences.en: Then realization fell over her.
sentences.zh: 随即她恍然大悟。

sentences.en: He didn’t remember her.
sentences.zh: 他不记得她了。

sentences.en: He didn’t remember any of them! “Mattias!” she cried in horror. “It’s me!
sentences.zh: 他谁都不记得了！“马提亚斯！”她惊恐地喊道，“是我！

sentences.en: Elsa!” “Elsa?” His lips formed her name, but there was no recognition in his eyes. “I don’t know an Elsa.” He turned to the guards. “Anyone here know an Elsa?” They looked at one another, completely confused.
sentences.zh: 艾莎！”“艾莎？”他的嘴唇念着她的名字，可眼里毫无认出的神色。“我不认识什么艾莎。”他转向卫兵，“这有人认识一个叫艾莎的吗？”他们面面相觑，完全摸不着头脑。

sentences.en: Oh no!
sentences.zh: 噢，不！

sentences.en: Their memories were gone!
sentences.zh: 他们的记忆都没了！

sentences.en: All of them! “Excuse me!
sentences.zh: 所有人都是！“借过！

sentences.en: Coming through!” Elsa looked behind Mattias to find Olaf trying to make his way through the crowd of soldiers.
sentences.zh: 借过一下！”艾莎越过马提亚斯身后，看到奥拉夫正费力地从士兵的人群中挤过来。

sentences.en: To Elsa’s surprise, he was wearing a very fancy cravat and embroidered vest. “Olaf!
sentences.zh: 令艾莎惊讶的是，他戴着一个十分考究的领结，还穿着绣花马甲。“奥拉夫！

sentences.en: What on earth?” Anna started.
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？”安娜开口道。

sentences.en: But Olaf put a finger to his lips. “Shh,” he whispered. “Just go with it, okay?” He leapt onto a nearby boulder and turned to face the confused citizens and soldiers. “It’s all right!” he cried. “These are my friends, Elsa and Anna.
sentences.zh: 但奥拉夫把一根手指抵在嘴唇上。“嘘，”他小声说，“配合我就行，好吗？”他跳上旁边一块大石头，转身面对困惑的民众和士兵。“没事了！”他喊道，“这两位是我的朋友，艾莎和安娜。

sentences.en: They’re here to help us!” To Elsa’s relief, Mattias nodded. “I’m sorry, Your Majesty,” he said. “I didn’t realize.” He sheathed his sword and bowed reverently to…Olaf?
sentences.zh: 他们是来帮我们的！”艾莎松了口气，马提亚斯点了点头。“抱歉，陛下，”他说，“我方才没认出来。”他收剑入鞘，恭恭敬敬地向……奥拉夫鞠了一躬？

sentences.en: The snowman giggled, as if embarrassed. “It’s a long story,” he whispered to Elsa as the crowd began to wander away. “Let’s just say their memories have gotten way worse.
sentences.zh: 雪人咯咯笑起来，有点难为情。“说来话长，”趁着人群散去，他小声对艾莎说，“这么说吧，他们的记忆比以前更糟了。

sentences.en: In fact, they forgot all about you two.” “I noticed,” Elsa said dryly. “It started getting really crazy.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们把你们两个全忘光了。”“我看出来了，”艾莎干巴巴地说，“事情开始变得真的很疯狂。

sentences.en: People were fighting.
sentences.zh: 大家都在打架。

sentences.en: No one remembered what laws were.
sentences.zh: 没人记得律法是什么。

sentences.en: I needed to figure out a way to keep the peace.
sentences.zh: 我得想个法子维持秩序。

sentences.en: So…I might have told a little story.” “That you were their ruler?” Anna asked, raising an eyebrow. “Let’s just say it worked!!” He grinned proudly. “They listened to me, and the castle and village are still standing.” “That was actually really smart,” Elsa said, patting Olaf’s head. “Thank you.” “I live to serve!” he declared. “But now I’m hoping you figured out a way to get out of this mess, because no one even remembers how to hug anymore!
sentences.zh: 所以……我可能编了个小故事。”“说你是他们的统治者？”安娜挑起眉毛问。“这么说吧，管用了！！”他得意地咧嘴一笑，“他们听我的，城堡和村庄都还在。”“这其实真的很聪明，”艾莎说着拍了拍奥拉夫的头，“谢谢你。”“愿为您效劳！”他郑重宣布，“不过现在我希望你们已经想出办法摆脱这团乱麻，因为现在大家连怎么拥抱都忘了！

sentences.en: It’s so sad!” “We think so.
sentences.zh: 真让人难过！”“我们也这么觉得。

sentences.en: But we need everyone’s attention,” Anna said. “Can you make sure they all gather at our parents’ statue in the town square in the next ten minutes?
sentences.zh: 但我们需要大家集中注意力，”安娜说，“你能确保在接下来十分钟内，把他们全都召集到镇广场父母的雕像前吗？

sentences.en: We need to tell them a little story of our own.” “King Olaf at your service!” he declared.
sentences.zh: 我们得给他们讲讲我们自己的故事。”“奥拉夫国王听候差遣！”他郑重宣布。

sentences.en: Then he shrugged sheepishly. “I mean, just leave it to me!” Olaf scurried off, calling out orders as he went.
sentences.zh: 接着他不好意思地耸了耸肩。“我是说，交给我就行！”奥拉夫一溜烟跑开了，一边跑一边发号施令。

sentences.en: Elsa glanced at Anna, who smiled hesitantly back at her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎瞥了安娜一眼，安娜迟疑地朝她笑了笑。

sentences.en: She knew what her sister was thinking—this had better work!
sentences.zh: 她知道妹妹在想什么——这招最好管用！

sentences.en: Or Anna’d be ruling behind the scenes for the foreseeable future!
sentences.zh: 不然在可预见的将来，安娜就得在幕后当统治者了！

sentences.en: Elsa turned back to Inger, who was still standing on the gangplank, suddenly looking very nervous. “Are you all right?” she asked. “I just…I guess I’m scared,” Inger said slowly. “It’s been so many years.
sentences.zh: 艾莎转回身面对英格，她还站在跳板上，突然显得十分紧张。“你没事吧？”她问。“我只是……我想我是害怕，”英格缓缓说道，“已经过去这么多年了。

sentences.en: What if they don’t believe me?
sentences.zh: 要是他们不相信我怎么办？

sentences.en: What if they say I should be locked up?” “ We believe you,” Anna assured her. “And they will, too, once they hear the whole story.” “We also have Stig to back you up,” Elsa added, her eyes searching the square.
sentences.zh: 要是他们说该把我关起来呢？”“我们相信你，”安娜向她保证，“等他们听完整个故事，也会信的。”“我们还有斯蒂格为你作证，”艾莎补充道，目光在广场上搜寻。

sentences.en: Had Stig made it to Arendelle?
sentences.zh: 斯蒂格到达阿伦黛尔了吗？

sentences.en: She didn’t see any sign of him yet.
sentences.zh: 她还没看到他的踪影。

sentences.en: Hopefully he hadn’t gotten scared and backed out.
sentences.zh: 但愿他没有因为害怕而临阵退缩。

sentences.en: Inger hesitated, still looking doubtful.
sentences.zh: 英格犹豫着，仍是一副将信将疑的样子。

sentences.en: But her granddaughter came up behind her, putting an arm around her shoulder. “Come on, Gammy,” she said gently. “It’s time.” “I suppose you’re right,” Inger said. “Whatever happens, at least I can die knowing I told the truth.” Together they walked toward the town square.
sentences.zh: 但她的孙女从身后走上前，搂住她的肩膀。“来吧，奶奶，”她温柔地说，“时候到了。”“我想你是对的，”英格说，“无论发生什么，至少我死也能瞑目了，因为我讲了实话。”她们一起朝镇广场走去。

sentences.en: Olaf had done his job, and a crowd had gathered around the band’s stage.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫尽职了，一大群人已经聚在乐队的舞台周围。

sentences.en: Red helped her grandmother climb up the steps, and Elsa and Anna joined them, turning to the crowd. “People of Arendelle,” Anna addressed the group.
sentences.zh: 瑞德扶着祖母登上台阶，艾莎和安娜也走上台，转身面向人群。“阿伦黛尔的人民，”安娜对众人说道。

sentences.en: Elsa realized in dismay that no one was listening.
sentences.zh: 艾莎沮丧地发现，根本没人在听。

sentences.en: They were all chatting with one another, not paying any attention to the people on the stage.
sentences.zh: 他们都在彼此闲聊，完全没把台上的人放在心上。

sentences.en: Anna sighed, exasperated. “Olaf?” she called out. “A little help here?” Olaf pushed through the crowd, making his way to the stage.
sentences.zh: 安娜无奈地叹了口气。“奥拉夫？”她喊道，“帮帮忙好吗？”奥拉夫从人群中挤过来，走上了舞台。

sentences.en: He hopped up onto it and turned to face the crowd, putting his stick hand in his mouth and giving a loud whistle.
sentences.zh: 他蹦上舞台，转身面向人群，把树枝手放进嘴里，吹了一声响亮的口哨。

sentences.en: The crowd went silent immediately.
sentences.zh: 人群立刻安静下来。

sentences.en: Everyone turned to the stage.
sentences.zh: 所有人都转向舞台。

sentences.en: Anna rolled her eyes. “Ladies and gentlemen,” Olaf said grandly. “Allow me to introduce you to your storytellers of the day!
sentences.zh: 安娜翻了个白眼。“女士们，先生们，”奥拉夫庄重地说，“请允许我向各位介绍今天的说书人！

sentences.en: They have a fabulous tale to tell, sure to entertain you and your children.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个精彩绝伦的故事要讲，定能让您和孩子们听得入迷。

sentences.en: Thrills, chills, and spills galore!
sentences.zh: 惊险、刺激、跌宕起伏，应有尽有！

sentences.en: So please give them your undivided attention.
sentences.zh: 所以请大家全神贯注地听。

sentences.en: They are my dear, dear friends, and deserve every respect.” And with that, he popped off the stage, leaving Anna, Elsa, Inger, and Red alone.
sentences.zh: 他们是我最最亲爱的朋友，理应得到所有人的敬重。”说罢，他一蹦下了舞台，留下安娜、艾莎、英格和瑞德站在台上。

sentences.en: Anna bit her lower lip, looking over the crowd, which was now staring up at them curiously. “Should I start?” she whispered.
sentences.zh: 安娜咬着下唇，望向台下——此刻人们正好奇地抬头盯着她们。“要我开始吗？”她小声问。

sentences.en: Elsa frowned. “I guess so.
sentences.zh: 艾莎皱了皱眉。“我想是的。

sentences.en: Though I was hoping Stig would be here.
sentences.zh: 不过我本希望斯蒂格能在这儿。

sentences.en: Do you see him anywhere?” Anna scanned the crowd. “No.
sentences.zh: 你看到他在哪儿了吗？”安娜扫视人群。“没有。

sentences.en: Do you think he backed out?” “If he did, we’re going to have a tough time proving our story.” “Do you think we should give him more time to show?” Elsa looked up at the sky.
sentences.zh: 你觉得他临阵退缩了？”“要是这样，我们可就很难证明我们的故事了。”“你觉得我们该多等他一会儿吗？”艾莎抬头望向天空。

sentences.en: The clouds had thickened.
sentences.zh: 云层已经厚了起来。

sentences.en: It looked moments away from beginning to rain again.
sentences.zh: 看样子马上又要下雨了。

sentences.en: If it started pouring, they’d lose their audience.

sentences.zh: 多亏了这两位勇敢的姑娘。”她朝艾莎和安娜示意，“这两位姐妹。

sentences.en: Thanks to them, no one will ever tell our story wrong again.” Sissel’s gaze traveled to the two sisters. “Thank you,” she whispered. “Thank you for setting things right.
sentences.zh: 多亏了她们，再不会有人把我们的故事讲错了。”茜塞尔的目光落到两姐妹身上。“谢谢你们，”她轻声说，“谢谢你们纠正了这一切。

sentences.en: And for reuniting me with my sister.
sentences.zh: 还让我和妹妹重逢。

sentences.en: You can’t know how much that means to me.” “Oh, I think I have an idea,” Elsa said with a small smile.
sentences.zh: 你们不会明白这对我有多重要。”“噢，我想我大概能体会，”艾莎微微一笑。

sentences.en: She lifted her hand to her cheek, realizing it was wet with happy tears.
sentences.zh: 她抬手摸向脸颊，发现已被幸福的泪水打湿。

sentences.en: Anna put an arm around her waist.
sentences.zh: 安娜伸手搂住她的腰。

sentences.en: She didn’t speak, but Elsa knew exactly what she was thinking.
sentences.zh: 她没有说话，但艾莎完全知道她在想什么。

sentences.en: There was nothing in the world like the love of two sisters. “Well,” Anna declared, turning to Elsa as the sisters tearfully embraced again. “Guess we finally figured out what Sissel wanted.
sentences.zh: 这世上没有什么能比得上两姐妹之间的爱。“好了，”姐妹俩含泪再次相拥时，安娜转向艾莎宣布，“我想我们终于弄清楚茜塞尔想要什么了。

sentences.en: You know, we probably should have guessed from the start.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我们一开始其实就该猜到的。

sentences.en: I mean, who doesn’t want their sister back?” Elsa smiled at her. “Who indeed,” she agreed. “Hey!” Olaf suddenly butted between them. “Look!
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁不想要回自己的妹妹呢？”艾莎冲她笑了笑。“可不是嘛，”她表示赞同。“嘿！”奥拉夫突然挤到她们中间。“看！

sentences.en: The sun is back!” Wait, what?
sentences.zh: 太阳回来了！”等等，什么？

sentences.en: Elsa’s eyes shot toward the sky.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的目光猛地投向天空。

sentences.en: She’d been so wrapped up in the happy reunion she hadn’t noticed how much it had lightened outside.
sentences.zh: 她方才太沉浸在团聚的喜悦中，竟没注意到外面的天已经亮了不少。

sentences.en: Now she could see that the storm clouds had rolled away, revealing a setting sun, a hazy blue twilight, and a sea of shining stars.
sentences.zh: 此刻她才看清，暴风云已经散去，露出西沉的落日、朦胧的蓝色暮色，以及一片璀璨的星海。

sentences.en: Her breath caught in her throat.
sentences.zh: 她屏住了呼吸。

sentences.en: The storm was over.
sentences.zh: 风暴结束了。

sentences.en: Which meant… She turned back to the two sisters.
sentences.zh: 这意味着……她转回身面向两姐妹。

sentences.en: But to her surprise, only Inger stood there now.
sentences.zh: 可令她意外的是，此刻只有英格还站在那里。

sentences.en: Sissel had vanished.
sentences.zh: 茜塞尔已经消失了。

sentences.en: Inger hobbled over to the girls, a sad smile on her face. “She’s gone,” she told them. “She vanished the second the clouds went away and the sun came out.” “I’m sorry,” Elsa said, laying a hand on the old pirate’s arm. “Don’t be.” Inger’s blue eyes were wet but bright as she looked from Elsa and Anna to Red. “You gave me something I longed for all my life.
sentences.zh: 英格一瘸一拐地走到姑娘们面前，脸上挂着悲伤的微笑。“她走了，”她告诉她们，“云一散、太阳一出来，她就消失了。”“我很遗憾，”艾莎说着，把手搭在老海盗的臂上。“别遗憾。”英格的蓝眼睛湿润却明亮，她看看艾莎、安娜，又看看瑞德。“你们给了我毕生渴望的东西。

sentences.en: A chance to say a real goodbye.
sentences.zh: 一个能好好道别的机会。

sentences.en: And Sissel—well, thanks to you, she’s finally able to find eternal peace.” “I’m so glad,” Anna said. “And I promise you now, no one will ever tell your story wrong again.
sentences.zh: 而茜塞尔——嗯，多亏了你们，她终于能得到永恒的安息了。”“我真高兴，”安娜说，“而且我现在向你们保证，再不会有人把你们的故事讲错了。

sentences.en: We will create a monument!
sentences.zh: 我们要建一座纪念碑！

sentences.en: No, a memorial!
sentences.zh: 不，一座纪念堂！

sentences.en: And we can even have Wael write an article for the Village Crown !” she added excitedly “We will tell the whole story—exactly how it really happened!
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以请威尔为《村庄之冠》写一篇文章！”她兴奋地补充道，“我们要把整个故事讲出来——完完全全按它真实的样子！

sentences.en: And we can spread the papers far and wide so everyone from all the surrounding kingdoms—including Vesterland—will know the truth at last.” “That sounds wonderful,” Inger said. “Thank you, sweet ones.
sentences.zh: 我们要把报纸散发到四面八方，让周围所有王国——包括维斯特兰——的人终于都能知道真相。”“听起来太棒了，”英格说，“谢谢你们，好孩子们。

sentences.en: You have something of your grandmother in you, I think.” She gave them a loving look. “I wish we had known her,” Anna said wistfully. “Someday I will return and tell you all about her,” Inger promised. “But for now, I must get back to my crew.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你们身上有你们祖母的影子。”她温柔地看了她们一眼。“真希望我们曾认识她，”安娜怅然地说。“总有一天我会回来，把关于她的一切都讲给你们听，”英格承诺道，“不过现在，我得回到我的船员那里了。

sentences.en: They’re going to want to know what’s next.
sentences.zh: 他们一定想知道接下来该怎么办。

sentences.en: We’ve been on our mission for so long.
sentences.zh: 我们的使命已经持续太久了。

sentences.en: But now we have a chance for a new beginning.” “Are you sure you can’t stay?” Anna asked. “You could join us for the Polar Nights festivities if you like.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们终于有机会重新开始。”“你确定不能留下吗？”安娜问，“如果愿意，你们可以和我们一同参加极夜节的庆祝活动。

sentences.en: You and your crew.
sentences.zh: 你和你的船员们。

sentences.en: Arendelle will always be a home for you, if you need it.” “I appreciate that.
sentences.zh: 只要你们需要，阿伦黛尔永远是你们的家。”“我很感激。

sentences.en: But I have another task that must be done first.” She bit her lower lip, looking a little apprehensive. “I must finally go home.” “Home to Vesterland?” Elsa asked, surprised.
sentences.zh: 但我还有另一件必须先行完成的事。”她咬着下唇，显得有些忐忑。“我终于得回家了。”“回维斯特兰的家？”艾莎惊讶地问。

sentences.en: Though maybe she shouldn’t have been.
sentences.zh: 虽说也许她本不该惊讶。

sentences.en: Inger nodded. “It’s been fifty years.
sentences.zh: 英格点了点头。“已经五十年了。

sentences.en: I’d like to see it again before I die.” “That’s a great idea,” Anna agreed. “I can send advance word to King Jonas and his daughter, Mari,” she said eagerly. “I’m sure they’d welcome you with open arms, now that the true story is known.” “Thank you,” Inger said, bowing low to the two sisters. “And now, with your permission, I’ll take my leave.
sentences.zh: 我想在死前再看看它。”“这主意太好了，”安娜表示赞同，“我可以事先给乔纳斯国王和他的女儿玛丽捎话，”她热切地说，“既然真相已大白，我确信他们一定会张开双臂欢迎你。”“谢谢你们，”英格说着，向两姐妹深深鞠躬，“现在，如果你们允许，我就告辞了。

sentences.en: You probably have a lot to do to clean up this whole mess.” She gave a wry grin. “But I’m not worried.
sentences.zh: 你们大概还有很多善后要处理。”她苦笑了一下，“不过我不担心。

sentences.en: After all, there’s nothing two sisters can’t do if they put their minds to it.” Elsa turned to Anna.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，只要两姐妹同心，就没有什么做不到的事。”艾莎转向安娜。

sentences.en: They both grinned. “Now that’s a true story,” she declared.
sentences.zh: 两人都咧嘴笑了。“这才是一个真实的故事，”她宣布道。

sentences.en: Anna linked arms with Elsa and watched as Inger and her granddaughter boarded their pirate ship and prepared to set sail.
sentences.zh: 安娜挽住艾莎的手臂，望着英格和孙女登上她们的海盗船，准备起航。

sentences.en: The sea was now calm and the sky a beautiful blue.
sentences.zh: 此刻海面平静，天空是一片美丽的湛蓝。

sentences.en: Sissel’s hold on Arendelle was no more. “Oh, no!” cried someone behind them. “No, no, no!”
sentences.zh: 茜塞尔对阿伦黛尔的束缚终于消散了。“噢，不！”身后有人喊道，“不，不，不！”

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty: Anna
chapters.en:
ELSA AND ANNA EXCHANGED LOOKS. What now? They turned around, surprised to see Helmut standing in front of his block of ice, looking upset.

“What’s wrong?” Elsa asked.

“My ice sculptures! I haven’t even started them yet!” he cried in dismay. “How am I going to get them carved in time for the Polar Nights festival?”

“And my banner!” Gretchen burst in then, looking up at the half-blank canvas hanging haphazardly over the town square. “It’s not even close to being finished.”

“My waffle batter better be okay!” grumbled Bjorn. “There’s no way I’m letting Bjarne win this year!”

“Oh, I’m going to win!” Bjarne broke in. “If I can find any eggs, that is. How did I forget to get eggs?” He smacked his hand to his forehead in dismay.

“It’s okay!” Anna cried, leaping back onto the stage and addressing the crowd. She was shaking, she was so happy—everyone’s memories were being restored! “It’s all okay. We had a little setback on the Polar Nights celebration, but it doesn’t matter.”

“But we’re not going to be ready in time!” Mrs. Blodget protested. “The party will be ruined!”

“We really wanted it to be special for you,” added Halima, wringing her hands together. “We know how much it means to you. We didn’t want to let our queen down.”

Anna shook her head, a smile crossing her face. “You didn’t let me down. Don’t you understand? None of this matters! Not the ice sculptures or banners or waffles—or even chocolate. The only thing we need for a Polar Nights party is…” She paused dramatically. “Each other.”

The crowd cheered. The Waffle Brothers hugged each other. The band grabbed their instruments and began to play a cheery tune, and the children began to dance up and down the streets. Anna threw a smile at Elsa, who smiled back even wider. Anna could tell her sister approved of her message.

Soon the village was bustling with activity. Even as the sun slipped below the horizon, people moved tables in preparation of the upcoming celebration. They hung decorations. The smell of waffle batter began to permeate the air. A farmer started to roast corn while the fishmonger started grilling thick cuts of cod. Street vendors set up stands overflowing with their wares. And was that Oaken rolling into town on a shiny new sleigh, dressed in a festive red coat and matching hat and loaded up with Polar Nights party kits?

“Hope I’m not too late!” he cried, slipping off his sleigh and hugging his family. They jumped up and down in joy to see him. “Big winter blowout!” he called out, handing a kit to an eager young child. “Free of charge!”

As the people worked, Anna could hear snippets of conversation as they busily moved around her. “Remember the story of the Vesterland sisters? Inger’s innocent! Did you hear?” said one. “That awful King Runeard! How dare he force that poor shepherd to lie!” said another. “Our dear Queen Rita was Inger’s savior. Can you believe it?” said a third. The true story spread far and wide.

There was just one thing missing. One thing to make this a truly happily ever after. Anna turned to Elsa. “Can I send Gale on a little mission?” she asked hesitantly. “Would you mind?”

“Already done,” Elsa assured her. “And Gale’s fast. I bet it’s already reached the trolls. And a certain ice harvester.” She winked at her sister.

Anna’s heart leapt in her chest as she thought of Kristoff. Her Kristoff. She couldn’t wait to throw her arms around him and squeeze him so tight he’d squeak. She’d have to decide later whether she’d ever let him go.

“Queen Anna?”

She turned to see Wael approaching her, quill and paper in hand. “Do you have a moment? I’d love to interview you for the Village Crown. A front-page story above the fold this time. With a big picture! All about how you saved Arendelle from Sinister Sissel and—”

“Actually? Sissel wasn’t sinister,” Olaf broke in, waddling up behind the reporter. He had taken off his cravat and looked much more comfortable au natural. “In fact, she was actually kind of sweet.”

“You’re right! I saw it with my own eyes. I should have known better than to call her that. I’m sorry, she’s Sweet Sissel.” Wael wrote it down in his notebook. “See, this is why I need the interview. I want to make sure I get it exactly right.”

“I can help with that,” Olaf assured him, giving Anna a knowing look. “Let’s let our queen do her job and you can interview me instead. After all, I’m the only one around this place who never forgot a thing. I’m the true witness!”

“As am I,” Stig chimed in, walking up to the snowman and reporter. “And it’s time I tell my tale, officially. Once and for all.”

Wael rubbed his hands together excitedly. “Well, this is great!” he exclaimed. “You two can tell me everything! But we must hurry. The paper must go to press within the hour so I can get the issue out in time for the festivities.”

“Wael?” Anna said suddenly. “I might need a bonus edition of the paper after the festival is done.” She looked at her sister. “I need to reach out to King Jonas of Vesterland about this, but I feel like Inger and Sissel need a proper memorial, too. Not that overgrown run-down one. We will want everyone’s help getting it ready. Maybe even before Inger sets sail again?”

Elsa smiled. “That sounds like a wonderful idea.”

“Bonus issue! Of the Village Crown!” Wael repeated. “Yes, my queen! So much to do! I’m on it!”

He hurried Olaf and Stig off. Anna watched them go, amused. Olaf was already talking Wael’s ear off.

“I wonder if Stig will manage to get a word in edgewise,” she remarked to Elsa. Her sister snorted.

“Poor Stig,” she said.

“Poor Wael,” Anna added.

They started to laugh. It felt good to laugh again after such a harrowing few days of thinking she’d lost everything. Including her own memories. She closed her eyes and started cataloging her thoughts, searching for any holes. But everything seemed intact.

“That’s it, then,” she sighed happily. “We did it. We saved Arendelle.”

“Once more with feeling,” Elsa said. “You know, this is getting to be a bit of a habit.”

“This has got to be the last time,” Anna declared. She frowned. “You think it’s the last time, right?”

“Oh, yes. Definitely.” Elsa gave her a teasing grin.

Anna poked her playfully. “I do hope Inger decides to come visit someday,” she said. “I’d love to hear more about her and Sissel. And our grandmother, too.”

Before Elsa could answer, there was a rumble, so loud it almost sounded like an earthquake. Everyone in the village stopped what they were doing and turned to see what looked like a dozen or more boulders rolling and bouncing down the village street. They tumbled to a stop in front of Anna and Elsa and sprang into the air, transforming into the trolls Anna knew so well. The largest boulder rolled forward, stopping at the front of the group. The rock flipped over to reveal Grand Pabbie.

“Your Majesties,” Grand Pabbie said in that deep voice of his. This time there was a smile on his rocky face. “You succeeded in saving the Polar Nights and helping a draugr find eternal rest. Well done! Arendelle’s future is secure once more.”

A cheer rose up around the trolls, but Anna still felt restless. She wouldn’t feel complete until…“Kristoff?” she asked hurriedly, searching behind all the trolls. It was the longest they’d been apart since…well, ever. She missed him so much. Had he gotten his memories back, too?

“ANNA!”

And suddenly there he was. Speeding over the bridge and into the village, on the back of Sven, who was going so fast that for a moment she mistook him for the Water Nokk.

Her eyes welled with tears. He was not only here, but he had said her name. He had said her name because he remembered her name.

“KRISTOFF!” she cried, taking off running.

Whisk! Anna felt the wind at her back and realized Gale was there, helping her reach her fiancé quicker. Within seconds, they were together. Finally!

“Anna,” Kristoff said, practically jumping off Sven’s back. Sven greeted Anna with a lick on her cheek, but that was nothing compared to Kristoff’s greeting. He pulled her straight into his arms and up into the air, spinning her around before finally placing her back on the ground and kissing her deeply. He cupped her face. “Are you all right? I feel like I haven’t seen you in days! No, weeks!” He shook his head. “I feel like my head was in a fog, but now it’s lifting, and the minute it did, I looked at Sven and said—‘Anna! We have to get to Anna and see what she needs!’ So? Are you all right?”

“Am I all right?” Anna cried, laughing through her tears. “Are you? Who am I?” she demanded. “Tell me quickly!”

Kristoff blinked at her before his face broke into a huge smile. “You’re my feisty, fearless, ginger-sweet fiancée.”

She threw her arms around him again. “You’re back!”

“I’m back,” he said, holding her tightly. “And if I’m not mistaken, I believe today is our Choco-versary.”

“YES!” Anna practically shouted with relief. Then she blushed and added, “But it’s been a rough few days. All that matters is we’re together again.”

“Please. Do you think I’d forget our Choco-versary?” Kristoff scoffed. “What kind of fiancé do you think I am?”

He whistled, and Sven, who had wandered off without Anna’s knowledge, returned, balancing a large box on his back. Kristoff ran over and grabbed the top of the box. “Happy Choco-versary, my love! Ta-da!”

The witnessing trolls all cheered.

Anna’s heart felt as if it would burst out of her chest as she pulled the box cover off, revealing a giant…wait, what was that?

“Um, is that a chocolate Flemmingrad the fungus troll?” she asked, her eyes bulging.

“Oh my,” Mattias said, loud enough for everyone to hear.

“Yes! I quickly made him out of mushroom-flavored chocolate and edible plants!” Kristoff said excitedly, plucking a strange-looking purple leaf out of the troll’s ear and popping it into his mouth. “Yum! Delicious! Should I break off a piece for you?”

“Uh, that’s okay,” Anna said, backing up slightly. “We should probably…um…wait until my gift for you is ready!” she finished brightly.

“Oh, my dear, but it is!” said Mrs. Blodget as she popped out of her shop, carrying the large reindeer-shaped chocolate Anna had commissioned weeks before. She couldn’t believe Mrs. Blodget even had it done after all that had happened.

Anna smiled sheepishly at Kristoff. “Happy Choco-versary?” she said.

“Amazing!” Kristoff declared, looking right at her. And she was pretty sure he wasn’t just talking about the chocolate. A warm, gooey feeling fell over her, and she reached for his hand.

“I love you,” she whispered.

“I love you, too,” he said. “And don’t you forget it.”

She snorted. “To be fair, I’m not the one who—”

Her words were interrupted by a low ooh. Followed by a group ahh. She turned from Kristoff to see what it was.

“Look!” said Mattias. “It’s the Northern Lights!”

A hush came over the village. Everyone looked up into the sky, murmuring excitedly at the shafts of greens and golds whisking across the horizon like a nighttime rainbow. The aurora borealis. Here at last. Anna felt a shiver trip down her spine. She cuddled a little closer to Kristoff, putting her head on his shoulder.

“It’s so beautiful,” she whispered. “So perfect.”

Kristoff put an arm around her, and Olaf jumped into Elsa’s arms. Sven came up alongside them, and Anna scratched him behind the ears. All around them, the Arendellians looked up in awe at the spectacular show in the sky.

“You wanted the best Polar Nights ever,” Elsa said, leaning in to whisper in Anna’s ear. “I’m pretty sure you got it.”

“Yes,” Anna agreed. “This is definitely a night I won’t soon forget.”
chapters.zh:
艾莎和安娜交换了一个眼神。

又怎么了？

她们转过身，惊讶地看见赫尔穆特站在他的冰块前，一脸沮丧。“怎么了？”艾莎问。“我的冰雕！

我连一个都还没开始刻呢！”他沮丧地喊道，“我怎么赶在极夜节前把它们雕好？”“还有我的横幅！”这时格雷琴插话进来，抬头望着那块歪歪斜斜挂在镇广场上空、还没画完的画布。“它连一半都没完成呢。”“我的华夫饼面糊可千万别出问题！”比约恩嘟囔着，“今年我绝不会让比亚内赢！”“噢，赢的会是我！”比亚内插嘴道，“只要我能找到鸡蛋的话。

我怎么就忘了买鸡蛋？”他懊恼地一拍额头。“没事的！”安娜喊道，跳回舞台对人群说道。

她激动得发抖——大家的记忆正在恢复！“一切都好。

极夜节的筹备是出了点小岔子，但没关系。”“可我们赶不及准备好了！”布拉吉特夫人抗议道。

“这场聚会要被毁了！”“我们真的很想为你办得特别一点，”哈丽玛双手绞在一起补充道，“我们知道这对你有多重要。

我们不想让我们的女王失望。”安娜摇了摇头，脸上浮现出微笑。“你们没有让我失望。

你还不明白吗？

这些都不重要！

不论是冰雕、横幅、华夫饼——还是巧克力，都不重要。

极夜节聚会唯一需要的东西是……”她戏剧性地顿了顿，“彼此。”人群欢呼起来。

华夫兄弟俩互相拥抱。

乐队抓起乐器，奏起欢快的曲调，孩子们开始在街上蹦蹦跳跳地跳舞。

安娜朝艾莎投去一个微笑，艾莎回以更灿烂的笑容。

安娜看得出，妹妹很赞同她的话。

不久，村庄便热闹忙碌起来。

即便太阳已沉入地平线，人们仍搬动桌子，为即将到来的庆典做准备。

他们挂起装饰。

华夫饼面糊的香味开始弥漫在空气中。

一位农夫开始烤玉米，鱼贩则支起炉子烤起厚切鳕鱼。

街头小贩支起摊位，上面堆满了货物。

那是不是奥肯驾着崭新发亮的小雪橇进了城？他身穿喜庆的红外套，戴着配套的帽子，车上装满了极夜节聚会套装。“希望我还不算太晚！”他喊道，跳下雪橇拥抱家人。

见到他，家人高兴得蹦了起来。“冬季大甩卖！”他喊着，把一个套装递给一个迫不及待的孩子。“免费赠送！”人们忙碌着，安娜能听到身旁飘过的只言片语。“还记得维斯特兰姐妹的故事吗？

英格是无辜的！

你听说了吗？”一个人说。“那个糟糕的鲁内尔德国王！

他竟敢逼那个可怜的牧羊人撒谎！”另一个人说。“我们亲爱的丽塔王后是英格的救命恩人。

你能相信吗？”第三个人说。

真实的故事传遍了四面八方。

只差一件事还没圆满。

一件事，能让这成为一个真正的大团圆结局。

安娜转向艾莎。“我能派风灵去办件小事吗？”她犹豫地问，“你介意吗？”“已经办好了，”艾莎向她保证，“而且风灵跑得很快。

我打赌它已经到地精那儿了。

还有某位采冰人。”她朝妹妹眨了眨眼。

一想到克斯托夫，安娜的心就在胸口怦然跳动。

她的克斯托夫。

她恨不得马上张开双臂紧紧抱住他，勒得他直叫唤。

至于要不要放开他，她得以后再做决定。“安娜女王？”她转头，看见威尔手持羽毛笔和纸向她走来。“您有空吗？

我想为《村庄之冠》采访您。

这次要登在头版头条。

还要配一张大照片！

全讲您如何把阿伦黛尔从阴森茜塞尔手中拯救出来，还有——”“其实？

茜塞尔并不阴森，”奥拉夫插话道，摇摇摆摆地走到记者身后。

他已经摘下了领结，这副自然模样看上去自在多了。“其实，她还挺可爱的。”“你说得对！

我亲眼所见。

我早该想到不该那么叫她。

抱歉，她是可爱茜塞尔。”威尔把这句话记在笔记本上。“看吧，这就是为什么我需要采访。

我想确保把每件事都写得准确无误。”“这事我能帮上忙，”奥拉夫向他保证，朝安娜使了个眼色，“让我们的女王去忙她的正事，你改采访我好了。

毕竟，这地方只有我一个人从没忘记过任何事。

我才是真正的目击者！”“我也是，”斯蒂格插话道，走到雪人和记者面前，“是时候由我正式讲述我的故事了。

一次说个清楚。”威尔兴奋地搓着手。“哇，这太好了！”他叫道，“你们两个可以把一切都告诉我！

但我们得抓紧。

报纸必须在一小时内付印，我才能在节前把这一期发出去。”“威尔？”安娜突然说，“节庆结束后我可能需要报纸出一期增刊。”她看了看妹妹，“我得就这件事联系维斯特兰的乔纳斯国王，不过我觉得英格和茜塞尔也需要一座像样的纪念堂。

不要那座荒废失修的旧纪念物。

我们会需要大家帮忙把它建好。

也许在英格再次起航前就建好？”艾莎笑了。“这主意听起来很棒。”“增刊！

《村庄之冠》的增刊！”威尔重复道，“是，我的女王！

要做的事太多了！

这事交给我！”他催着奥拉夫和斯蒂格离开了。

安娜好笑地看着他们离去。

奥拉夫已经唠唠叨叨说个没完。“我怀疑斯蒂格能不能插得进一句话，”她对艾莎说道。

妹妹哼了一声。“可怜的斯蒂格，”她说。“可怜的威尔，”安娜补了一句。

两人笑了起来。

在以为失去一切的惊魂数日之后，能再次开怀大笑，感觉真好。

包括她自己的记忆。

她闭上眼睛，开始梳理自己的思绪，查找任何遗漏。

但一切似乎都完好无缺。“那就没问题了，”她幸福地叹道，“我们做到了。

我们拯救了阿伦黛尔。”“再说一遍，带点感情，”艾莎说，“你知道，这都快成习惯了。”“这绝对是最后一次了，”安娜郑重宣布。

她皱起眉。“你觉得这是最后一次，对吧？”“噢，当然。

绝对是。”艾莎朝她调皮地咧嘴一笑。

安娜顽皮地戳了她一下。“我真希望英格哪天能来决定来拜访，”她说，“我想多听听她和茜塞尔的事。

还有我们的祖母。”艾莎还没来得及回答，一阵隆隆声传来，响得简直像地震。

村里所有人都停下手中的活，转头望向看似十几个或更多的巨石，正沿着村中街道翻滚蹦跳而来。

它们在安娜和艾莎面前翻滚着停下，随即腾空而起，变成了安娜再熟悉不过的地精。

那块最大的石头向前滚了滚，停在人堆前面。

石头翻过来，露出了皮比。“两位陛下，”皮比用他那低沉的嗓音说道。

这一次，他岩石般的脸上带着笑容。“你们成功拯救了极夜节，并帮助一具亡灵得到了永恒的安息。

干得好！

阿伦黛尔的未来再度安稳了。”地精们中间响起一片欢呼，可安娜仍感到不安。

她总觉得还缺了点什么，直到……“克斯托夫呢？”她急切地问，在地精们身后寻找。

这是他们自……嗯，自有记忆以来分开最久的一次。

她太想他了。

他的记忆也恢复了吗？“安娜！”突然，他出现了。

他骑着斯文飞驰过桥、冲进村庄，斯文跑得飞快，有一瞬间她竟把他错认成了水马。

她的眼眶涌上泪水。

他不仅在这里，还喊出了她的名字。

他喊出她的名字，是因为他记起了她的名字。“克斯托夫！”她喊着，拔腿就跑。

嗖！

安娜感到背后一阵风，才意识到风灵来了，正帮她更快奔向未婚夫。

几秒钟内，他们就相拥在一起。

终于！“安娜，”克斯托夫说着，几乎是从斯文背上跳了下来。

斯文舔了舔安娜的脸颊以示问候，但这和克斯托夫的问候比起来根本不算什么。

他一把将她拥入怀中，腾空抱起，转着圈儿，最后才把她放回地面，深深地吻了她。

他捧起她的脸。“你还好吗？

我觉得好像好几天没见到你了！

不，好几个星期了！”他摇着头，“我觉得自己的脑袋一直像蒙在雾里，可现在雾散了，雾一散，我看着斯文就说——‘安娜！

我们得去找安娜，看看她需要什么！’所以呢？

你还好吗？”“我好不好？”安娜喊道，含泪笑着，“你呢？

我是谁？”她逼问，“快告诉我！”克斯托夫眨了眨眼，随即脸上绽开大大的笑容。“你是我那泼辣、无畏、红发甜心的未婚妻。”她再次张开双臂抱住他。“你回来了！”“我回来了，”他紧紧抱着她说，“而且如果我没记错，今天是我们的巧克力纪念日。”“没错！”安娜如释重负地几乎喊了出来。

接着她红了脸，补充道，“不过这几天真是够呛。

重要的是我们又在一起了。”“拜托。

你以为我会忘了我们的巧克力纪念日吗？”克斯托夫嗤之以鼻，“你把我当什么未婚夫了？”他吹了声口哨，斯文——它刚才趁安娜不注意溜开了——驮着一个大盒子回来了。

克斯托夫跑过去，抓住盒盖。“巧克力纪念日快乐，我的爱人！

当当！”旁观的地精们齐声欢呼。

安娜掀开盒盖，心仿佛要跳出胸膛——里面是一个巨大的……等等，那是什么？“呃，那是巧克力做的蘑菇地精弗莱明格拉德吗？”她瞪大眼睛问。“噢，天哪，”马提亚斯说得足够响，让所有人都听见了。“没错！

我用蘑菇味的巧克力和可食用植物很快做出了它！”克斯托夫兴奋地说，从地精耳朵里摘下一片样子奇怪的紫叶子，塞进嘴里。“好吃！

美味！

要不要我掰一块给你？”“呃，不用了，”安娜说着微微后退，“我们也许该……呃……等我的礼物准备好了再说！”她明朗地补了一句。“噢，我的亲爱的，可它已经好了！”布拉吉特夫人说道。

布拉吉特夫人从店里冲出来，捧着安娜几周前订做的那块驯鹿形大巧克力。

她不敢相信布拉吉特夫人——

在经历这么多变故之后，居然还把它做出来了。

安娜朝克斯托夫不好意思地笑了笑。“巧克力纪念日快乐？”她说。“太棒了！”克斯托夫注视着她宣布。

而且她相当确定，他说的可不只是巧克力。

一阵温暖黏腻的感觉涌上心头，她伸过手去牵住他的手。“我爱你，”她轻声说。“我也爱你，”他说，“你可不许忘了。”她哼了一声。“说句公道话，忘了的人可不是我——”她的话被一声低低的“噢”打断了。

紧接着是一群人的“啊”。

她从克斯托夫身上转过头，想看看是什么。“看！”马提亚斯说，“是北极光！”村庄顿时安静下来。

所有人都抬头望向天空，望着那一道道绿与金的光束如夜空彩虹般掠过地平线，兴奋地低语。

北极光。

终于来了。

安娜感到一阵战栗顺着脊背而下。

她往克斯托夫怀里靠了靠，把头枕在他肩上。“真美，”她轻声说，“太完美了。”克斯托夫搂住她，而奥拉夫跳进了艾莎怀里。

斯文走到他们身边，安娜挠了挠它耳后。

周围所有的阿伦黛尔人都仰望天空，惊叹于那场壮观的演出。“你想要的，是有史以来最棒的极夜节，”艾莎凑近安娜耳边低语，“我敢说你得到了。”“是的，”安娜赞同道，“这绝对是一个我久久不会忘怀的夜晚。”

sentences.zh: 抱歉，她是可爱茜塞尔。”威尔把这句话记在笔记本上。“看吧，这就是为什么我需要采访。

sentences.en: I want to make sure I get it exactly right.” “I can help with that,” Olaf assured him, giving Anna a knowing look. “Let’s let our queen do her job and you can interview me instead.
sentences.zh: 我想确保把每件事都写得准确无误。”“这事我能帮上忙，”奥拉夫向他保证，朝安娜使了个眼色，“让我们的女王去忙她的正事，你改采访我好了。

sentences.en: After all, I’m the only one around this place who never forgot a thing.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这地方只有我一个人从没忘记过任何事。

sentences.en: I’m the true witness!” “As am I,” Stig chimed in, walking up to the snowman and reporter. “And it’s time I tell my tale, officially.
sentences.zh: 我才是真正的目击者！”“我也是，”斯蒂格插话道，走到雪人和记者面前，“是时候由我正式讲述我的故事了。

sentences.en: Once and for all.” Wael rubbed his hands together excitedly. “Well, this is great!” he exclaimed. “You two can tell me everything!
sentences.zh: 一次说个清楚。”威尔兴奋地搓着手。“哇，这太好了！”他叫道，“你们两个可以把一切都告诉我！

sentences.en: But we must hurry.
sentences.zh: 但我们得抓紧。

sentences.en: The paper must go to press within the hour so I can get the issue out in time for the festivities.” “Wael?” Anna said suddenly. “I might need a bonus edition of the paper after the festival is done.” She looked at her sister. “I need to reach out to King Jonas of Vesterland about this, but I feel like Inger and Sissel need a proper memorial, too.
sentences.zh: 报纸必须在一小时内付印，我才能在节前把这一期发出去。”“威尔？”安娜突然说，“节庆结束后我可能需要报纸出一期增刊。”她看了看妹妹，“我得就这件事联系维斯特兰的乔纳斯国王，不过我觉得英格和茜塞尔也需要一座像样的纪念堂。

sentences.en: Not that overgrown run-down one.
sentences.zh: 不要那座荒废失修的旧纪念物。

sentences.en: We will want everyone’s help getting it ready.
sentences.zh: 我们会需要大家帮忙把它建好。

sentences.en: Maybe even before Inger sets sail again?” Elsa smiled. “That sounds like a wonderful idea.” “Bonus issue!
sentences.zh: 也许在英格再次起航前就建好？”艾莎笑了。“这主意听起来很棒。”“增刊！

sentences.en: Of the Village Crown !” Wael repeated. “Yes, my queen!
sentences.zh: 《村庄之冠》的增刊！”威尔重复道，“是，我的女王！

sentences.en: So much to do!
sentences.zh: 要做的事太多了！

sentences.en: I’m on it!” He hurried Olaf and Stig off.
sentences.zh: 这事交给我！”他催着奥拉夫和斯蒂格离开了。

sentences.en: Anna watched them go, amused.
sentences.zh: 安娜好笑地看着他们离去。

sentences.en: Olaf was already talking Wael’s ear off. “I wonder if Stig will manage to get a word in edgewise,” she remarked to Elsa.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫已经唠唠叨叨说个没完。“我怀疑斯蒂格能不能插得进一句话，”她对艾莎说道。

sentences.en: Her sister snorted. “Poor Stig,” she said. “Poor Wael,” Anna added.
sentences.zh: 妹妹哼了一声。“可怜的斯蒂格，”她说。“可怜的威尔，”安娜补了一句。

sentences.en: They started to laugh.
sentences.zh: 两人笑了起来。

sentences.en: It felt good to laugh again after such a harrowing few days of thinking she’d lost everything.
sentences.zh: 在以为失去一切的惊魂数日之后，能再次开怀大笑，感觉真好。

sentences.en: Including her own memories.
sentences.zh: 包括她自己的记忆。

sentences.en: She closed her eyes and started cataloging her thoughts, searching for any holes.
sentences.zh: 她闭上眼睛，开始梳理自己的思绪，查找任何遗漏。

sentences.en: But everything seemed intact. “That’s it, then,” she sighed happily. “We did it.
sentences.zh: 但一切似乎都完好无缺。“那就没问题了，”她幸福地叹道，“我们做到了。

sentences.en: We saved Arendelle.” “Once more with feeling,” Elsa said. “You know, this is getting to be a bit of a habit.” “This has got to be the last time,” Anna declared.
sentences.zh: 我们拯救了阿伦黛尔。”“再说一遍，带点感情，”艾莎说，“你知道，这都快成习惯了。”“这绝对是最后一次了，”安娜郑重宣布。

sentences.en: She frowned. “You think it’s the last time, right?” “Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 她皱起眉。“你觉得这是最后一次，对吧？”“噢，当然。

sentences.en: Definitely.” Elsa gave her a teasing grin.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。”艾莎朝她调皮地咧嘴一笑。

sentences.en: Anna poked her playfully. “I do hope Inger decides to come visit someday,” she said. “I’d love to hear more about her and Sissel.
sentences.zh: 安娜顽皮地戳了她一下。“我真希望英格哪天能来决定来拜访，”她说，“我想多听听她和茜塞尔的事。

sentences.en: And our grandmother, too.” Before Elsa could answer, there was a rumble, so loud it almost sounded like an earthquake.
sentences.zh: 还有我们的祖母。”艾莎还没来得及回答，一阵隆隆声传来，响得简直像地震。

sentences.en: Everyone in the village stopped what they were doing and turned to see what looked like a dozen or more boulders rolling and bouncing down the village street.
sentences.zh: 村里所有人都停下手中的活，转头望向看似十几个或更多的巨石，正沿着村中街道翻滚蹦跳而来。

sentences.en: They tumbled to a stop in front of Anna and Elsa and sprang into the air, transforming into the trolls Anna knew so well.
sentences.zh: 它们在安娜和艾莎面前翻滚着停下，随即腾空而起，变成了安娜再熟悉不过的地精。

sentences.en: The largest boulder rolled forward, stopping at the front of the group.
sentences.zh: 那块最大的石头向前滚了滚，停在人堆前面。

sentences.en: The rock flipped over to reveal Grand Pabbie. “Your Majesties,” Grand Pabbie said in that deep voice of his.
sentences.zh: 石头翻过来，露出了皮比。“两位陛下，”皮比用他那低沉的嗓音说道。

sentences.en: This time there was a smile on his rocky face. “You succeeded in saving the Polar Nights and helping a draugr find eternal rest.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他岩石般的脸上带着笑容。“你们成功拯救了极夜节，并帮助一具亡灵得到了永恒的安息。

sentences.en: Well done!
sentences.zh: 干得好！

sentences.en: Arendelle’s future is secure once more.” A cheer rose up around the trolls, but Anna still felt restless.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔的未来再度安稳了。”地精们中间响起一片欢呼，可安娜仍感到不安。

sentences.en: She wouldn’t feel complete until…“Kristoff?” she asked hurriedly, searching behind all the trolls.
sentences.zh: 她总觉得还缺了点什么，直到……“克斯托夫呢？”她急切地问，在地精们身后寻找。

sentences.en: It was the longest they’d been apart since…well, ever.
sentences.zh: 这是他们自……嗯，自有记忆以来分开最久的一次。

sentences.en: She missed him so much.
sentences.zh: 她太想他了。

sentences.en: Had he gotten his memories back, too? “ANNA!” And suddenly there he was.
sentences.zh: 他的记忆也恢复了吗？“安娜！”突然，他出现了。

sentences.en: Speeding over the bridge and into the village, on the back of Sven, who was going so fast that for a moment she mistook him for the Water Nokk.
sentences.zh: 他骑着斯文飞驰过桥、冲进村庄，斯文跑得飞快，有一瞬间她竟把他错认成了水马。

sentences.en: Her eyes welled with tears.
sentences.zh: 她的眼眶涌上泪水。

sentences.en: He was not only here, but he had said her name.
sentences.zh: 他不仅在这里，还喊出了她的名字。

sentences.en: He had said her name because he remembered her name. “KRISTOFF!” she cried, taking off running.
sentences.zh: 他喊出她的名字，是因为他记起了她的名字。“克斯托夫！”她喊着，拔腿就跑。

sentences.en: Whisk!
sentences.zh: 嗖！

sentences.en: Anna felt the wind at her back and realized Gale was there, helping her reach her fiancé quicker.
sentences.zh: 安娜感到背后一阵风，才意识到风灵来了，正帮她更快奔向未婚夫。

sentences.en: Within seconds, they were together.
sentences.zh: 几秒钟内，他们就相拥在一起。

sentences.en: Finally! “Anna,” Kristoff said, practically jumping off Sven’s back.
sentences.zh: 终于！“安娜，”克斯托夫说着，几乎是从斯文背上跳了下来。

sentences.en: Sven greeted Anna with a lick on her cheek, but that was nothing compared to Kristoff’s greeting.
sentences.zh: 斯文舔了舔安娜的脸颊以示问候，但这和克斯托夫的问候比起来根本不算什么。

sentences.en: He pulled her straight into his arms and up into the air, spinning her around before finally placing her back on the ground and kissing her deeply.
sentences.zh: 他一把将她拥入怀中，腾空抱起，转着圈儿，最后才把她放回地面，深深地吻了她。

sentences.en: He cupped her face. “Are you all right?
sentences.zh: 他捧起她的脸。“你还好吗？

sentences.en: I feel like I haven’t seen you in days!
sentences.zh: 我觉得好像好几天没见到你了！

sentences.en: No, weeks!” He shook his head. “I feel like my head was in a fog, but now it’s lifting, and the minute it did, I looked at Sven and said—‘Anna!
sentences.zh: 不，好几个星期了！”他摇着头，“我觉得自己的脑袋一直像蒙在雾里，可现在雾散了，雾一散，我看着斯文就说——‘安娜！

sentences.en: We have to get to Anna and see what she needs!’ So?
sentences.zh: 我们得去找安娜，看看她需要什么！’所以呢？

sentences.en: Are you all right?” “Am I all right?” Anna cried, laughing through her tears. “Are you?
sentences.zh: 你还好吗？”“我好不好？”安娜喊道，含泪笑着，“你呢？

sentences.en: Who am I?” she demanded. “Tell me quickly!” Kristoff blinked at her before his face broke into a huge smile. “You’re my feisty, fearless, ginger-sweet fiancée.” She threw her arms around him again. “You’re back!” “I’m back,” he said, holding her tightly. “And if I’m not mistaken, I believe today is our Choco-versary.” “YES!” Anna practically shouted with relief.
sentences.zh: 我是谁？”她逼问，“快告诉我！”克斯托夫眨了眨眼，随即脸上绽开大大的笑容。“你是我那泼辣、无畏、红发甜心的未婚妻。”她再次张开双臂抱住他。“你回来了！”“我回来了，”他紧紧抱着她说，“而且如果我没记错，今天是我们的巧克力纪念日。”“没错！”安娜如释重负地几乎喊了出来。

sentences.en: Then she blushed and added, “But it’s been a rough few days.
sentences.zh: 接着她红了脸，补充道，“不过这几天真是够呛。

sentences.en: All that matters is we’re together again.” “Please.
sentences.zh: 重要的是我们又在一起了。”“拜托。

sentences.en: Do you think I’d forget our Choco-versary?” Kristoff scoffed. “What kind of fiancé do you think I am?” He whistled, and Sven, who had wandered off without Anna’s knowledge, returned, balancing a large box on his back.
sentences.zh: 你以为我会忘了我们的巧克力纪念日吗？”克斯托夫嗤之以鼻，“你把我当什么未婚夫了？”他吹了声口哨，斯文——它刚才趁安娜不注意溜开了——驮着一个大盒子回来了。

sentences.en: Kristoff ran over and grabbed the top of the box. “Happy Choco-versary, my love!
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫跑过去，抓住盒盖。“巧克力纪念日快乐，我的爱人！

sentences.en: Ta-da!” The witnessing trolls all cheered.
sentences.zh: 当当！”旁观的地精们齐声欢呼。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart felt as if it would burst out of her chest as she pulled the box cover off, revealing a giant…wait, what was that? “Um, is that a chocolate Flemmingrad the fungus troll?” she asked, her eyes bulging. “Oh my,” Mattias said, loud enough for everyone to hear. “Yes!
sentences.zh: 安娜掀开盒盖，心仿佛要跳出胸膛——里面是一个巨大的……等等，那是什么？“呃，那是巧克力做的蘑菇地精弗莱明格拉德吗？”她瞪大眼睛问。“噢，天哪，”马提亚斯说得足够响，让所有人都听见了。“没错！

sentences.en: I quickly made him out of mushroom-flavored chocolate and edible plants!” Kristoff said excitedly, plucking a strange-looking purple leaf out of the troll’s ear and popping it into his mouth. “Yum!
sentences.zh: 我用蘑菇味的巧克力和可食用植物很快做出了它！”克斯托夫兴奋地说，从地精耳朵里摘下一片样子奇怪的紫叶子，塞进嘴里。“好吃！

sentences.en: Delicious!
sentences.zh: 美味！

sentences.en: Should I break off a piece for you?” “Uh, that’s okay,” Anna said, backing up slightly. “We should probably…um…wait until my gift for you is ready!” she finished brightly. “Oh, my dear, but it is!” said Mrs.
sentences.zh: 要不要我掰一块给你？”“呃，不用了，”安娜说着微微后退，“我们也许该……呃……等我的礼物准备好了再说！”她明朗地补了一句。“噢，我的亲爱的，可它已经好了！”布拉吉特夫人说道。

sentences.en: Blodget as she popped out of her shop, carrying the large reindeer-shaped chocolate Anna had commissioned weeks before.
sentences.zh: 布拉吉特夫人从店里冲出来，捧着安娜几周前订做的那块驯鹿形大巧克力。

sentences.en: She couldn’t believe Mrs.
sentences.zh: 她不敢相信布拉吉特夫人——

sentences.en: Blodget even had it done after all that had happened.
sentences.zh: 在经历这么多变故之后，居然还把它做出来了。

sentences.en: Anna smiled sheepishly at Kristoff. “Happy Choco-versary?” she said. “Amazing!” Kristoff declared, looking right at her.
sentences.zh: 安娜朝克斯托夫不好意思地笑了笑。“巧克力纪念日快乐？”她说。“太棒了！”克斯托夫注视着她宣布。

sentences.en: And she was pretty sure he wasn’t just talking about the chocolate.
sentences.zh: 而且她相当确定，他说的可不只是巧克力。

sentences.en: A warm, gooey feeling fell over her, and she reached for his hand. “I love you,” she whispered. “I love you, too,” he said. “And don’t you forget it.” She snorted. “To be fair, I’m not the one who—” Her words were interrupted by a low ooh .
sentences.zh: 一阵温暖黏腻的感觉涌上心头，她伸过手去牵住他的手。“我爱你，”她轻声说。“我也爱你，”他说，“你可不许忘了。”她哼了一声。“说句公道话，忘了的人可不是我——”她的话被一声低低的“噢”打断了。

sentences.en: Followed by a group ahh .
sentences.zh: 紧接着是一群人的“啊”。

sentences.en: She turned from Kristoff to see what it was. “Look!” said Mattias. “It’s the Northern Lights!” A hush came over the village.
sentences.zh: 她从克斯托夫身上转过头，想看看是什么。“看！”马提亚斯说，“是北极光！”村庄顿时安静下来。

sentences.en: Everyone looked up into the sky, murmuring excitedly at the shafts of greens and golds whisking across the horizon like a nighttime rainbow.
sentences.zh: 所有人都抬头望向天空，望着那一道道绿与金的光束如夜空彩虹般掠过地平线，兴奋地低语。

sentences.en: The aurora borealis.
sentences.zh: 北极光。

sentences.en: Here at last.
sentences.zh: 终于来了。

sentences.en: Anna felt a shiver trip down her spine.
sentences.zh: 安娜感到一阵战栗顺着脊背而下。

sentences.en: She cuddled a little closer to Kristoff, putting her head on his shoulder. “It’s so beautiful,” she whispered. “So perfect.” Kristoff put an arm around her, and Olaf jumped into Elsa’s arms.
sentences.zh: 她往克斯托夫怀里靠了靠，把头枕在他肩上。“真美，”她轻声说，“太完美了。”克斯托夫搂住她，而奥拉夫跳进了艾莎怀里。

sentences.en: Sven came up alongside them, and Anna scratched him behind the ears.
sentences.zh: 斯文走到他们身边，安娜挠了挠它耳后。

sentences.en: All around them, the Arendellians looked up in awe at the spectacular show in the sky. “You wanted the best Polar Nights ever,” Elsa said, leaning in to whisper in Anna’s ear. “I’m pretty sure you got it.” “Yes,” Anna agreed. “This is definitely a night I won’t soon forget.”
sentences.zh: 周围所有的阿伦黛尔人都仰望天空，惊叹于那场壮观的演出。“你想要的，是有史以来最棒的极夜节，”艾莎凑近安娜耳边低语，“我敢说你得到了。”“是的，”安娜赞同道，“这绝对是一个我久久不会忘怀的夜晚。”

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-One: Anna
chapters.en:
Two Weeks Later…

It was amazing how different a place felt when sadness was replaced with hope.

Standing near the river at the border of Vesterland and Arendelle where Sissel had lost her life, Anna marveled at how much had been done in such a short amount of time.

The tiny makeshift memorial area had been cleared of overgrown weeds and shrubs to make way for a larger space with a hand-carved canopy and natural rock seating (Kristoff’s idea), along with hand-carved benches (Olga’s idea) for visitors to sit at and reflect. Snow currently covered the ground, but in the spring Anna could already envision the grassy knoll and canopy filled with wildflowers (Helga said they were Sissel’s favorite).

Underneath the canopy sat a veiled statue that Anna would be christening that morning alongside Elsa, King Jonas, and Princess Mari. Helmut had been working night and day over the last two weeks to complete the statue of the Vesterland sisters, whose true story had finally been told.

And for those who hadn’t heard it yet, there was now a large plaque etched into rock that told the tale of Sissel and Inger and what both had strived to do for their kingdom. It also included the story of what had actually happened between them that fateful December day at the river and all that Inger had endured in the weeks that followed when she was accused of Sissel’s murder.

The little wooden statue that Olga and Helga had made to serve as the original memorial hadn’t been forgotten, either. It would soon reside in the Vesterland History Museum along with a new exhibit about Sissel and Inger that Mari was overseeing with Olga and Helga’s help. Anna couldn’t imagine anyone better suited to tell Sissel and Inger’s story than their loyal stewards. Well, other than Inger herself.

Anna felt a cool hand on her shoulder; she didn’t have to ask who was there. “Do you think she’s going to show?” Anna asked Elsa without turning to look at her.

“I’m not sure,” Elsa said thoughtfully, staring at the rushing river just a few feet away. For safety’s sake, Anna insisted the grounds of the memorial now include a wooden fence to keep others from falling in when they visited the site. “It might be too painful for her to come back here again.”

Anna hadn’t spoken to Inger since that day at the festival. When she had met with the pirates to discuss a new trade agreement, Red was the one who had done the negotiating on Inger’s behalf. And now that a peace deal had been brokered, Red had sent word to Anna that the pirates would be leaving the fjord in a few days’ time. Anna’s invitation to join them today at the memorial ceremony had gone unanswered.

“You don’t think Inger is afraid to meet with the people of Vesterland, do you?” Elsa wondered.

“Red said Inger was hoping to meet privately with Jonas and Mari. I’m sure they assured her she’s welcome in her homeland again.” Anna looked around at all the people putting the finishing touches on things before the ceremony. Arendellians and the people of Vesterland had worked overtime to bring the memorial site together so quickly. Now, people from both kingdoms were tying blue and purple ribbons, which happened to be Sissel and Inger’s favorite colors, around all the chairs at the service and weaving handmade silk flowers into the canopy covering the statue. “I just want her to be here so she can see for herself how much she and Sissel mean to everyone. Today is their celebration.”

“Seriously!” Olaf said, bounding up to them with both a blue silk flower and a purple one. “When was the last time we had two parties to plan in two weeks?” He placed one of his tree-branch arms across his forehead. “I’m exhausted from planning!”

“Party pooper,” Kristoff teased as he and Sven joined the others. “All you had to do was spread the word about the memorial. It’s not like you had to transport heavy rocks to the site and carve a wooden canopy like me and Sven.”

Anna stood on tippy-toes to kiss him. “It all looks great, honey. I can’t imagine a better tribute to the Vesterland sisters.”

“The next party I throw will be your and Kristoff’s engagement party,” Olaf said. “Sven and I already have a theme planned. Right, Sven?” Sven snorted.

“Give me a little time off to rest first,” Kristoff said, speaking on his reindeer’s behalf. “I’m still recovering from the Polar Nights festival.”

“That’s good, because I want a say on that party theme, too,” Elsa teased and looked at Anna. “It’s too bad you can’t plan your own engagement party. You did such a great job with the Polar Nights.”

Anna blushed as Kristoff put his arm around her and pulled her close.

“I second that! It was the best one ever, I’ll have you know.” He blanched. “No offense to our snow queen.”

Elsa laughed. “None taken!”

Anna blushed. “Thanks, everyone. Considering half the village couldn’t remember who they were for most of the planning stage, things came together rather nicely at the end.”

“Only because they have a great leader to help get things done,” Elsa reminded her.

“A leader who is good at delegating!” Anna said with a small fist pump. “Which is what I’m going to do now to make sure this ceremony is perfect.” She looked out at the crowd of people again and prayed she’d spot Inger or the pirates. She didn’t.

Kristoff gave her another squeeze as the gray day gave way to peeks of sun through the clouds. “Cheer up. Even if the pirates don’t come today, I’m sure they appreciate what you’ve done here. And something tells me Sissel is somewhere watching.”

“Just not as a draugr, right?” Olaf looked momentarily alarmed.

“Actually, I like to imagine Sissel almost like Gale—just a lovely afternoon wind gliding by on its way to see the world now that it can,” Elsa offered. Olaf looked appeased.

The sound of horses approaching in the distance announced King Jonas’s arrival. His carriage came to a stop near the clearing and he stepped out, walking straight over to Anna and Elsa.

“Queens Anna and Elsa,” he said, clasping their hands as Mari walked over to join them. “I’m so glad we could do this today, and so quickly! Thank you for all your help the past few weeks.”

“Vesterland and Arendelle are not only allies and neighbors, we’re friends,” Anna reminded the king. “Nothing could mean more to Elsa and me than the chance to make things right.”

“Good. Because we brought a few extra friends along to celebrate.” Mari stepped aside, gesturing with her hands. Anna watched in surprise as the crowd parted to make way for a familiar-looking band of pirates.

“They came!” Olaf said, jumping up and down.

Anna couldn’t believe her eyes. The pirates had come after all, and they were all dressed for the occasion in their finest boots and leather vests, hats with feathers atop their heads, each one wearing a blue ribbon for Sissel woven into their hair or tied to their vest. Red led the way, holding the arm of her grandmother, Inger, whose attendance was the biggest surprise of all. Anna watched as Old Blue Eyes took in the scene around her with wonder. Inger blinked away tears, but she was smiling. In her hands, she held tight to a bouquet of wildflowers—the same flowers that were woven through the two long white braids in her hair. Where Inger had found them in the winter, Anna had no idea.

“Good to see you, both,” Inger said with a small nod. “We hope we’re not too late.”

“Late? Never! We couldn’t start without you,” said Anna as she clasped Inger’s hands and didn’t let go. “We’re glad you’re here. It’s so good to see you again.”

“And you two as well,” Inger said with a soft smile. “This place has been transformed. It looks so peaceful. Sissel would be pleased.”

“She’s…at peace?” Kristoff couldn’t help asking.

“Yes,” Inger said, exhaling softly. “We both are. My sister’s spirit is now free, and so am I. It’s back to the sea I go with my family.” She tightened her grip on Red’s arm.

“We hope you know you’re welcome in Vesterland anytime,” King Jonas told Inger. “It is your homeland, after all.”

“We could find you a place, help you settle back in,” Mari added. “There are so many people here who miss you and want to see you again.” She looked over at Olga and Helga, who were hugging and crying at the same time at the sight of Inger.

Inger took one look at her former stewards and her tears flowed harder. “Thank you. And I do appreciate the generous offer. It’s been so long since I’ve stood on dry land for any amount of time.” She looked at Red. “But the sea is where I want to spend my remaining years. It is truly my home now, but it’s not everyone’s. My granddaughter should have the chance to have a real life in Vesterland.”

King Jonas cleared his throat. “Of course, and as a descendant of the royal family, Red could also lay claim to the—”

“I’ll stop you right there, King Jonas,” interrupted Red. “While I appreciate the offer to reclaim my family’s royal line, I’m truly like my grandmother.” She looked at the older woman. “I am a pirate and I belong at sea, not in a castle.” The two embraced. “But it is good to know there is somewhere I can call home if ever I tire of the water.”

King Jonas nodded. “You will always have a place here.”

“We hope you’ll make this memorial space your own and visit often. Vesterland even has plans for an exhibit about you and Sissel in their museum,” Mari informed her.

“Is that right?” Inger said. “I hope Olga and Helga are helping put that together. They have such wonderful stories about our childhood, and even our nicknames.” She chuckled. “Sissel hated how we all called her ‘Stinky Sissel’ when she ate too much garlic.”

Everyone laughed.

“Noted!” said Elsa.

Olaf giggled loudest of all. “Stinky Sissel is a much better nickname than—”

“Don’t say Sinister Sissel!” Anna cut him off. “Well, if you’re all ready, it’s time.” Anna took Inger’s free arm and led her and Red to the front of the waiting crowd by the bench.

By now, everyone was holding candles that were lit one by one. King Jonas, Mari, and Elsa moved to the front, where Anna joined them, looking out on all the people who had gathered for this important moment in their kingdoms’ shared history. Her eyes were on Inger’s.

“Thank you all for coming today to help us unveil the Vesterland sisters’ memorial,” Anna said.

“Their true story is long overdue,” continued Jonas. “And it is the hope of both Vesterland and Arendelle that people will come to this memorial site often to reflect on both sisters’ lives and what they did for their kingdom.”

Anna moved to the sheet covering the statue. “And now, may we present, this memorial statue—The Love of Two Vesterland Sisters by Master Sculptor Helmut of Arendelle.”

She and Kristoff pulled the sheet away, revealing a hand-carved statue of Sissel and Inger in a tight embrace. They were carved as their younger selves, looking vibrant and hopeful as they stared into one another’s eyes. This is the way the world should remember them, Anna thought, as a united front; two sisters who fought together for the betterment of Vesterland and who loved each other till their dying days; a young woman lost far too soon and the sister who loved her so much that she spent her life searching for her.

Inger let out a small gasp at the sight of her younger self with Sissel, then rose and made her way slowly to the statue. Her granddaughter did the same, both of them touching the smooth stone and looking at it in wonder.

“Do you like it?” Anna asked shyly, her hand moving to find Elsa’s.

Inger looked at both queens with love in her teary eyes. “It’s perfect. Absolutely perfect.”

And just at that moment, a sudden gust of wind rustled through the bare trees, blowing the last of the autumn leaves through the knoll with such force that people held on to their hats and gasped in surprise.

Anna felt a smile come to her lips. She looked at Elsa, remembering her sister’s words from earlier.

Sissel.

She was there, and she was finally at peace.

两周后……当悲伤被希望取代，一个地方给人的感觉竟能如此不同，这真令人惊叹。

站在维斯特兰与阿伦黛尔交界、茜塞尔丧生的那条河边，安娜惊叹于短短时间里竟完成了这么多事。

那处狭小的临时纪念地被清理掉了疯长的杂草和灌木，腾出一块更大的空间：有手工雕刻的顶棚和自然岩石座椅（克斯托夫的主意），还有手工雕刻的长凳（奥尔加的主意），供来访者坐下追思。

此刻地上覆盖着积雪，但到了春天，安娜已经能想象出那片草坡和顶棚开满野花的样子（赫尔加说那是茜塞尔最喜欢的花）。

顶棚下立着一尊蒙着罩布的雕像，那天上午安娜将和艾莎、乔纳斯国王以及玛丽公主一同为它揭幕。

过去两周，赫尔穆特日夜赶工，终于完成了这尊维斯特兰姐妹的雕像——她们的真实故事终于被讲了出来。

而对于还没听过的人，现在有一块刻在岩石上的大匾牌，讲述着茜塞尔和英格的故事，以及她们曾为王国努力做过的一切。

匾牌上还记载了那个命中注定的十二月、在河边真正发生于两人之间的事，以及此后数周里英格被指控谋杀茜塞尔后所承受的一切。

奥尔加和赫尔加制作的那座小木雕——最初的纪念物——也没有被遗忘。

它很快会入驻维斯特兰历史博物馆，与玛丽在奥尔加和赫尔加协助下筹备的、关于茜塞尔和英格的新展览一同展出。

安娜想不出还有谁比她们忠实的管家更适合讲述茜塞尔和英格的故事。

嗯，英格本人除外。

安娜感到一只冰凉的手搭上她的肩；她不用问也知道是谁。“你觉得她会来吗？”安娜没有转头，问艾莎。“我不确定，”艾莎若有所思地说，盯着几步外奔流的河水。

出于安全考虑，安娜坚持纪念园现在要围一道木栅栏，免得访客来访时跌落河中。“对她来说，再回到这里也许太痛苦了。”自那天节庆之后，安娜再没和英格说过话。

当她与海盗会面商讨新的贸易协定时，是瑞德代表英格进行了谈判。

既然和平协议已经达成，瑞德捎话给安娜，说海盗们几天后就要离开峡湾了。

安娜邀请他们今天来参加纪念仪式的信，没有得到回复。“你该不会以为英格是怕见维斯特兰的人吧？”艾莎疑惑道。“瑞德说英格希望能私下见见乔纳斯和玛丽。

我确信他们已向她保证，她在家乡再次受到欢迎。”安娜环顾四周，人们正在仪式前做最后的修饰。

阿伦黛尔人和维斯特兰人加班加点，才这么快把纪念园建好。

此刻，两国的人民正把蓝紫色的丝带——恰是茜塞尔和英格最爱的颜色——系在仪式现场的所有椅子上，并把手工丝绸花编进遮蔽雕像的顶棚里。“我只希望她能来，亲自看看她和茜塞尔对大家有多重要。

今天是她们的庆典。”“说真的！”奥拉夫蹦跳着跑到他们面前，一手举着一朵蓝丝绸花，一手举着一朵紫丝绸花。“上一次我们两周内要筹备两场聚会是什么时候？”他把一条树枝手臂横在额前，“筹备可把我累坏了！”“扫兴鬼，”克斯托夫和他与斯文一同加入众人时调侃道，“你不过就是去传个话、让大家知道纪念园的事。

你又不用像我和斯文那样把重石头运到现场、再雕个木顶棚。”安娜踮起脚尖亲了他一下。“一切都看起来很棒，亲爱的。

我想不出比这更好的、献给维斯特兰姐妹的敬意了。”“下一场我来筹办的聚会，就是你和克斯托夫的订婚派对，”奥拉夫说，“我和斯文已经想好主题了。

对吧，斯文？”斯文哼了一声。“先给我点休息时间，”克斯托夫替他的驯鹿说道，“极夜节过后我还没缓过来呢。”“那正好，因为那个派对的主题我也想说几句，”艾莎调侃着看向安娜，“只可惜你没法自己筹划自己的订婚派对。

你把极夜节办得太棒了。”克斯托夫搂住安娜、把她拉近，安娜红了脸。“我附议！

据我所知，那是有史以来最棒的一次。”他脸色一白，“对我们的雪之女王绝无冒犯之意。”艾莎大笑。“哪有的事！”安娜红了脸。“谢谢大家。

想想看，筹备阶段大半村子的人都不记得自己是谁，最后事情却办得相当漂亮。”“那是因为他们有位好领导帮着把事办成，”艾莎提醒她，“一位善于分派任务的好领导！”安娜小小挥了下拳头。“这正是我现在要做的，好让仪式万无一失。”她再次望向人群，暗暗祈祷能瞥见英格或海盗们。

她没看到。

灰蒙蒙的天渐渐透出云缝间的阳光，克斯托夫又轻轻搂紧了她。“开心点。

就算海盗们今天没来，我也确信他们感激你在这里做的一切。

而且我有种感觉，茜塞尔正在某处看着呢。”“只是不是以亡灵的样子，对吧？”奥拉夫一时有些惊慌。“其实，我倒愿意把茜塞尔想象得近似风灵——如今她终于自由，就像一阵可爱的午后微风，正滑翔着去见识这个世界，”艾莎说道。

奥拉夫安心了。

远处传来的马蹄声宣告了乔纳斯国王的到来。

他的马车在空地旁停下，他走下车，径直走向安娜和艾莎。“安娜女王、艾莎女王，”他说着握住她们的手，玛丽也走上前来加入。“真高兴我们今天就能办成，而且还这么快！

感谢你们过去几周的全力相助。”“维斯特兰和阿伦黛尔不只是盟友和邻居，我们还是朋友，”安娜提醒国王，“对艾莎和我来说，没有什么比纠正过往的机会更有意义了。”“好。

因为我们还带了几位额外的朋友来同庆。”玛丽向旁边让了让，用手势示意。

安娜惊讶地看着人群分开，让出一队眼熟的海盗。“他们来了！”奥拉夫蹦跳着说。

安娜简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

海盗们终究还是来了，而且都为这场场合盛装打扮：最好的靴子、皮马甲，头上戴着插羽毛的帽子，每个人都在头发或马甲上系了一条为茜塞尔而戴的蓝丝带。

瑞德走在最前面，挽着祖母英格的胳膊——英格能来，实在是最大的惊喜。

安娜望着“蓝眼睛老奶奶”惊叹地打量着四周的景象。

英格眨去眼泪，却面带微笑。

她双手紧握一束野花——那花正与她两条白色长辫里编着的鲜花一模一样。

安娜不知道英格在这冬天里从哪儿找来这些花。“很高兴见到你们两位，”英格微微点头说，“希望我们不算太晚。”“晚？

绝不会！

没有你我们没法开始，”安娜说着紧紧握住英格的手不放，“我们很高兴你来了。

能再见到你们真好。”“你们两位也是，”英格温柔地微笑着说，“这地方已经变了样。

看起来这么安宁。

茜塞尔会欣慰的。”“她……安息了？”克斯托夫忍不住问。“是的，”英格轻轻呼了口气说，“我们俩都是。

我妹妹的魂灵如今自由了，我也是。

我要和家人们回大海去了。”她更紧地握住瑞德的胳膊。“我们希望你知道，维斯特兰随时欢迎你，”乔纳斯国王对英格说，“毕竟那是你的故乡。”“我们可以给你找个住处，帮你安顿下来，”玛丽补充道，“这里有那么多人想念你、想再见你一面。”她望向奥尔加和赫尔加——两人一看到英格，就又抱又哭。

英格看了一眼从前的管家，泪水涌得更凶了。“谢谢你们。

我真的很感激这份慷慨的邀请。

我已经很久没有在陆地上待过这么久了。”她看着瑞德，“可是大海，才是我想度过余生之处。

如今它才是我真正的家，但并非每个人都如此。

我的孙女应当有机会在维斯特兰过真正的生活。”乔纳斯国王清了清嗓子。“当然，作为王室的血脉，瑞德也可以主张继承——”“我就在这儿打断您，乔纳斯国王，”瑞德插话道，“虽然我感激您让我重振家族王系的好意，可我真的像我祖母。”“我是个海盗，属于大海，不属于城堡。”两人相拥。“不过知道有处地方可称作家、哪天厌倦了水也能回去，这感觉很好。”乔纳斯国王点了点头。“你在这里永远有个位置。”“我们希望你能把这处纪念园当作自己的地方，常来走走。

维斯特兰甚至打算在博物馆里办一个关于你和茜塞尔的展览，”玛丽告诉她。“是吗？”英格说，“我希望奥尔加和赫尔加在帮忙筹备。

她们有那么多关于我们童年的美好故事，连我们的外号都知道。”她轻声笑了，“茜塞尔最讨厌我们因为她吃太多大蒜而叫她‘臭茜塞尔’。”大家都笑了。“记住了！”艾莎说。

奥拉夫笑得最大声。“‘臭茜塞尔’这外号可比——”“不许说阴森茜塞尔！”安娜截断他的话。“好了，如果大家都准备好了，时候到了。”安娜挽起英格空着的那条胳膊，领着她和瑞德走到长凳旁等候的人群前面。

此时，每个人都手持蜡烛，被一一点亮。

乔纳斯国王、玛丽和艾莎走到前面，安娜也加入他们，望着为这两国共同历史的重要时刻而聚集的所有人。

她的目光落在英格身上。“感谢各位今天前来，帮我们为维斯特兰姐妹纪念园揭幕，”安娜说。“她们的真实故事早该被讲述，”乔纳斯接着说，“维斯特兰和阿伦黛尔都希望人们能常来这处纪念园，追思两姐妹的一生，以及她们为王国所做的贡献。”安娜走到盖着雕像的罩布前。“现在，请允许我们呈献这尊纪念雕像——阿伦黛尔雕塑大师赫尔穆特作品：《两姐妹之爱》。”她和克斯托夫揭开罩布，露出一尊手工雕刻、两姐妹紧紧相拥的雕像。

雕像雕刻的是她们年轻时的模样，两两相望，神采飞扬、充满希望。

世界就该这样记住她们，安娜想，作为一个并肩的整体；两姐妹曾一同为维斯特兰的福祉而奋斗，至死相爱；一个过早逝去的少女，和一个如此爱她、用一生去寻找她的姐姐。

看到年轻的自己和茜塞尔，英格轻轻倒吸一口气，随后起身，缓缓走向雕像。

孙女也照样做了，两人都抚摸着光滑的石头，惊奇地端详。“你们喜欢吗？”安娜羞涩地问，伸手去牵艾莎的手。

英格含泪的眼里满是爱意，望着两位女王。“它太完美了。

绝对完美。”就在此刻，一阵突如其来的风吹过光秃秃的树，把最后几片秋叶猛地卷过草坡，人们只得按住帽子，惊讶地倒吸一口气。

安娜觉得嘴角浮起微笑。

她望向艾莎，想起妹妹早先说的话。

茜塞尔。

她就在那里，终于安息了。
