sentences.en: The little wooden statue that Olga and Helga had made to serve as the original memorial hadn’t been forgotten, either.
sentences.zh: 奥尔加和赫尔加制作的那座小木雕——最初的纪念物——也没有被遗忘。

sentences.en: It would soon reside in the Vesterland History Museum along with a new exhibit about Sissel and Inger that Mari was overseeing with Olga and Helga’s help.
sentences.zh: 它很快会入驻维斯特兰历史博物馆，与玛丽在奥尔加和赫尔加协助下筹备的、关于茜塞尔和英格的新展览一同展出。

sentences.en: Anna couldn’t imagine anyone better suited to tell Sissel and Inger’s story than their loyal stewards.
sentences.zh: 安娜想不出还有谁比她们忠实的管家更适合讲述茜塞尔和英格的故事。

sentences.en: Well, other than Inger herself.
sentences.zh: 嗯，英格本人除外。

sentences.en: Anna felt a cool hand on her shoulder; she didn’t have to ask who was there. “Do you think she’s going to show?” Anna asked Elsa without turning to look at her. “I’m not sure,” Elsa said thoughtfully, staring at the rushing river just a few feet away.
sentences.zh: 安娜感到一只冰凉的手搭上她的肩；她不用问也知道是谁。“你觉得她会来吗？”安娜没有转头，问艾莎。“我不确定，”艾莎若有所思地说，盯着几步外奔流的河水。

sentences.en: For safety’s sake, Anna insisted the grounds of the memorial now include a wooden fence to keep others from falling in when they visited the site. “It might be too painful for her to come back here again.” Anna hadn’t spoken to Inger since that day at the festival.
sentences.zh: 出于安全考虑，安娜坚持纪念园现在要围一道木栅栏，免得访客来访时跌落河中。“对她来说，再回到这里也许太痛苦了。”自那天节庆之后，安娜再没和英格说过话。

sentences.en: When she had met with the pirates to discuss a new trade agreement, Red was the one who had done the negotiating on Inger’s behalf.
sentences.zh: 当她与海盗会面商讨新的贸易协定时，是瑞德代表英格进行了谈判。

sentences.en: And now that a peace deal had been brokered, Red had sent word to Anna that the pirates would be leaving the fjord in a few days’ time.
sentences.zh: 既然和平协议已经达成，瑞德捎话给安娜，说海盗们几天后就要离开峡湾了。

sentences.en: Anna’s invitation to join them today at the memorial ceremony had gone unanswered. “You don’t think Inger is afraid to meet with the people of Vesterland, do you?” Elsa wondered. “Red said Inger was hoping to meet privately with Jonas and Mari.
sentences.zh: 安娜邀请他们今天来参加纪念仪式的信，没有得到回复。“你该不会以为英格是怕见维斯特兰的人吧？”艾莎疑惑道。“瑞德说英格希望能私下见见乔纳斯和玛丽。

sentences.en: I’m sure they assured her she’s welcome in her homeland again.” Anna looked around at all the people putting the finishing touches on things before the ceremony.
sentences.zh: 我确信他们已向她保证，她在家乡再次受到欢迎。”安娜环顾四周，人们正在仪式前做最后的修饰。

sentences.en: Arendellians and the people of Vesterland had worked overtime to bring the memorial site together so quickly.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔人和维斯特兰人加班加点，才这么快把纪念园建好。

sentences.en: Now, people from both kingdoms were tying blue and purple ribbons, which happened to be Sissel and Inger’s favorite colors, around all the chairs at the service and weaving handmade silk flowers into the canopy covering the statue. “I just want her to be here so she can see for herself how much she and Sissel mean to everyone.
sentences.zh: 此刻，两国的人民正把蓝紫色的丝带——恰是茜塞尔和英格最爱的颜色——系在仪式现场的所有椅子上，并把手工丝绸花编进遮蔽雕像的顶棚里。“我只希望她能来，亲自看看她和茜塞尔对大家有多重要。

sentences.en: Today is their celebration.” “Seriously!” Olaf said, bounding up to them with both a blue silk flower and a purple one. “When was the last time we had two parties to plan in two weeks?” He placed one of his tree-branch arms across his forehead. “I’m exhausted from planning!” “Party pooper,” Kristoff teased as he and Sven joined the others. “All you had to do was spread the word about the memorial.
sentences.zh: 今天是她们的庆典。”“说真的！”奥拉夫蹦跳着跑到他们面前，一手举着一朵蓝丝绸花，一手举着一朵紫丝绸花。“上一次我们两周内要筹备两场聚会是什么时候？”他把一条树枝手臂横在额前，“筹备可把我累坏了！”“扫兴鬼，”克斯托夫和他与斯文一同加入众人时调侃道，“你不过就是去传个话、让大家知道纪念园的事。

sentences.en: It’s not like you had to transport heavy rocks to the site and carve a wooden canopy like me and Sven.” Anna stood on tippy-toes to kiss him. “It all looks great, honey.
sentences.zh: 你又不用像我和斯文那样把重石头运到现场、再雕个木顶棚。”安娜踮起脚尖亲了他一下。“一切都看起来很棒，亲爱的。

sentences.en: I can’t imagine a better tribute to the Vesterland sisters.” “The next party I throw will be your and Kristoff’s engagement party,” Olaf said. “Sven and I already have a theme planned.
sentences.zh: 我想不出比这更好的、献给维斯特兰姐妹的敬意了。”“下一场我来筹办的聚会，就是你和克斯托夫的订婚派对，”奥拉夫说，“我和斯文已经想好主题了。

sentences.en: Right, Sven?” Sven snorted. “Give me a little time off to rest first,” Kristoff said, speaking on his reindeer’s behalf. “I’m still recovering from the Polar Nights festival.” “That’s good, because I want a say on that party theme, too,” Elsa teased and looked at Anna. “It’s too bad you can’t plan your own engagement party.
sentences.zh: 对吧，斯文？”斯文哼了一声。“先给我点休息时间，”克斯托夫替他的驯鹿说道，“极夜节过后我还没缓过来呢。”“那正好，因为那个派对的主题我也想说几句，”艾莎调侃着看向安娜，“只可惜你没法自己筹划自己的订婚派对。

sentences.en: You did such a great job with the Polar Nights.” Anna blushed as Kristoff put his arm around her and pulled her close. “I second that!
sentences.zh: 你把极夜节办得太棒了。”克斯托夫搂住安娜、把她拉近，安娜红了脸。“我附议！

sentences.en: It was the best one ever, I’ll have you know.” He blanched. “No offense to our snow queen.” Elsa laughed. “None taken!” Anna blushed. “Thanks, everyone.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，那是有史以来最棒的一次。”他脸色一白，“对我们的雪之女王绝无冒犯之意。”艾莎大笑。“哪有的事！”安娜红了脸。“谢谢大家。

sentences.en: Considering half the village couldn’t remember who they were for most of the planning stage, things came together rather nicely at the end.” “Only because they have a great leader to help get things done,” Elsa reminded her. “A leader who is good at delegating!” Anna said with a small fist pump. “Which is what I’m going to do now to make sure this ceremony is perfect.” She looked out at the crowd of people again and prayed she’d spot Inger or the pirates.
sentences.zh: 想想看，筹备阶段大半村子的人都不记得自己是谁，最后事情却办得相当漂亮。”“那是因为他们有位好领导帮着把事办成，”艾莎提醒她，“一位善于分派任务的好领导！”安娜小小挥了下拳头。“这正是我现在要做的，好让仪式万无一失。”她再次望向人群，暗暗祈祷能瞥见英格或海盗们。

sentences.en: She didn’t.
sentences.zh: 她没看到。

sentences.en: Kristoff gave her another squeeze as the gray day gave way to peeks of sun through the clouds. “Cheer up.
sentences.zh: 灰蒙蒙的天渐渐透出云缝间的阳光，克斯托夫又轻轻搂紧了她。“开心点。

sentences.en: Even if the pirates don’t come today, I’m sure they appreciate what you’ve done here.
sentences.zh: 就算海盗们今天没来，我也确信他们感激你在这里做的一切。

sentences.en: And something tells me Sissel is somewhere watching.” “Just not as a draugr, right?” Olaf looked momentarily alarmed. “Actually, I like to imagine Sissel almost like Gale—just a lovely afternoon wind gliding by on its way to see the world now that it can,” Elsa offered.
sentences.zh: 而且我有种感觉，茜塞尔正在某处看着呢。”“只是不是以亡灵的样子，对吧？”奥拉夫一时有些惊慌。“其实，我倒愿意把茜塞尔想象得近似风灵——如今她终于自由，就像一阵可爱的午后微风，正滑翔着去见识这个世界，”艾莎说道。

sentences.en: Olaf looked appeased.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫安心了。

sentences.en: The sound of horses approaching in the distance announced King Jonas’s arrival.
sentences.zh: 远处传来的马蹄声宣告了乔纳斯国王的到来。

sentences.en: His carriage came to a stop near the clearing and he stepped out, walking straight over to Anna and Elsa. “Queens Anna and Elsa,” he said, clasping their hands as Mari walked over to join them. “I’m so glad we could do this today, and so quickly!
sentences.zh: 他的马车在空地旁停下，他走下车，径直走向安娜和艾莎。“安娜女王、艾莎女王，”他说着握住她们的手，玛丽也走上前来加入。“真高兴我们今天就能办成，而且还这么快！

sentences.en: Thank you for all your help the past few weeks.” “Vesterland and Arendelle are not only allies and neighbors, we’re friends,” Anna reminded the king. “Nothing could mean more to Elsa and me than the chance to make things right.” “Good.
sentences.zh: 感谢你们过去几周的全力相助。”“维斯特兰和阿伦黛尔不只是盟友和邻居，我们还是朋友，”安娜提醒国王，“对艾莎和我来说，没有什么比纠正过往的机会更有意义了。”“好。

sentences.en: Because we brought a few extra friends along to celebrate.” Mari stepped aside, gesturing with her hands.
sentences.zh: 因为我们还带了几位额外的朋友来同庆。”玛丽向旁边让了让，用手势示意。

sentences.en: Anna watched in surprise as the crowd parted to make way for a familiar-looking band of pirates. “They came!” Olaf said, jumping up and down.
sentences.zh: 安娜惊讶地看着人群分开，让出一队眼熟的海盗。“他们来了！”奥拉夫蹦跳着说。

sentences.en: Anna couldn’t believe her eyes.
sentences.zh: 安娜简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。

sentences.en: The pirates had come after all, and they were all dressed for the occasion in their finest boots and leather vests, hats with feathers atop their heads, each one wearing a blue ribbon for Sissel woven into their hair or tied to their vest.
sentences.zh: 海盗们终究还是来了，而且都为这场场合盛装打扮：最好的靴子、皮马甲，头上戴着插羽毛的帽子，每个人都在头发或马甲上系了一条为茜塞尔而戴的蓝丝带。

sentences.en: Red led the way, holding the arm of her grandmother, Inger, whose attendance was the biggest surprise of all.
sentences.zh: 瑞德走在最前面，挽着祖母英格的胳膊——英格能来，实在是最大的惊喜。

sentences.en: Anna watched as Old Blue Eyes took in the scene around her with wonder.
sentences.zh: 安娜望着“蓝眼睛老奶奶”惊叹地打量着四周的景象。

sentences.en: Inger blinked away tears, but she was smiling.
sentences.zh: 英格眨去眼泪，却面带微笑。

sentences.en: In her hands, she held tight to a bouquet of wildflowers—the same flowers that were woven through the two long white braids in her hair.
sentences.zh: 她双手紧握一束野花——那花正与她两条白色长辫里编着的鲜花一模一样。

sentences.en: Where Inger had found them in the winter, Anna had no idea. “Good to see you, both,” Inger said with a small nod. “We hope we’re not too late.” “Late?
sentences.zh: 安娜不知道英格在这冬天里从哪儿找来这些花。“很高兴见到你们两位，”英格微微点头说，“希望我们不算太晚。”“晚？

sentences.en: Never!
sentences.zh: 绝不会！

sentences.en: We couldn’t start without you,” said Anna as she clasped Inger’s hands and didn’t let go. “We’re glad you’re here.
sentences.zh: 没有你我们没法开始，”安娜说着紧紧握住英格的手不放，“我们很高兴你来了。

sentences.en: It’s so good to see you again.” “And you two as well,” Inger said with a soft smile. “This place has been transformed.
sentences.zh: 能再见到你们真好。”“你们两位也是，”英格温柔地微笑着说，“这地方已经变了样。

sentences.en: It looks so peaceful.
sentences.zh: 看起来这么安宁。

sentences.en: Sissel would be pleased.” “She’s…at peace?” Kristoff couldn’t help asking. “Yes,” Inger said, exhaling softly. “We both are.
sentences.zh: 茜塞尔会欣慰的。”“她……安息了？”克斯托夫忍不住问。“是的，”英格轻轻呼了口气说，“我们俩都是。

sentences.en: My sister’s spirit is now free, and so am I.
sentences.zh: 我妹妹的魂灵如今自由了，我也是。

sentences.en: It’s back to the sea I go with my family.” She tightened her grip on Red’s arm. “We hope you know you’re welcome in Vesterland anytime,” King Jonas told Inger. “It is your homeland, after all.” “We could find you a place, help you settle back in,” Mari added. “There are so many people here who miss you and want to see you again.” She looked over at Olga and Helga, who were hugging and crying at the same time at the sight of Inger.
sentences.zh: 我要和家人们回大海去了。”她更紧地握住瑞德的胳膊。“我们希望你知道，维斯特兰随时欢迎你，”乔纳斯国王对英格说，“毕竟那是你的故乡。”“我们可以给你找个住处，帮你安顿下来，”玛丽补充道，“这里有那么多人想念你、想再见你一面。”她望向奥尔加和赫尔加——两人一看到英格，就又抱又哭。

sentences.en: Inger took one look at her former stewards and her tears flowed harder. “Thank you.
sentences.zh: 英格看了一眼从前的管家，泪水涌得更凶了。“谢谢你们。

sentences.en: And I do appreciate the generous offer.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激这份慷慨的邀请。

sentences.en: It’s been so long since I’ve stood on dry land for any amount of time.” She looked at Red. “But the sea is where I want to spend my remaining years.
sentences.zh: 我已经很久没有在陆地上待过这么久了。”她看着瑞德，“可是大海，才是我想度过余生之处。

sentences.en: It is truly my home now, but it’s not everyone’s.
sentences.zh: 如今它才是我真正的家，但并非每个人都如此。

sentences.en: My granddaughter should have the chance to have a real life in Vesterland.” King Jonas cleared his throat. “Of course, and as a descendant of the royal family, Red could also lay claim to the—” “I’ll stop you right there, King Jonas,” interrupted Red. “While I appreciate the offer to reclaim my family’s royal line, I’m truly like my grandmother.” She looked at the older woman. “I am a pirate and I belong at sea, not in a castle.” The two embraced. “But it is good to know there is somewhere I can call home if ever I tire of the water.” King Jonas nodded. “You will always have a place here.” “We hope you’ll make this memorial space your own and visit often.
sentences.zh: 我的孙女应当有机会在维斯特兰过真正的生活。”乔纳斯国王清了清嗓子。“当然，作为王室的血脉，瑞德也可以主张继承——”“我就在这儿打断您，乔纳斯国王，”瑞德插话道，“虽然我感激您让我重振家族王系的好意，可我真的像我祖母。”“我是个海盗，属于大海，不属于城堡。”两人相拥。“不过知道有处地方可称作家、哪天厌倦了水也能回去，这感觉很好。”乔纳斯国王点了点头。“你在这里永远有个位置。”“我们希望你能把这处纪念园当作自己的地方，常来走走。

sentences.en: Vesterland even has plans for an exhibit about you and Sissel in their museum,” Mari informed her. “Is that right?” Inger said. “I hope Olga and Helga are helping put that together.
sentences.zh: 维斯特兰甚至打算在博物馆里办一个关于你和茜塞尔的展览，”玛丽告诉她。“是吗？”英格说，“我希望奥尔加和赫尔加在帮忙筹备。

sentences.en: They have such wonderful stories about our childhood, and even our nicknames.” She chuckled. “Sissel hated how we all called her ‘Stinky Sissel’ when she ate too much garlic.” Everyone laughed. “Noted!” said Elsa.
sentences.zh: 她们有那么多关于我们童年的美好故事，连我们的外号都知道。”她轻声笑了，“茜塞尔最讨厌我们因为她吃太多大蒜而叫她‘臭茜塞尔’。”大家都笑了。“记住了！”艾莎说。

sentences.en: Olaf giggled loudest of all. “Stinky Sissel is a much better nickname than—” “Don’t say Sinister Sissel!” Anna cut him off. “Well, if you’re all ready, it’s time.” Anna took Inger’s free arm and led her and Red to the front of the waiting crowd by the bench.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫笑得最大声。“‘臭茜塞尔’这外号可比——”“不许说阴森茜塞尔！”安娜截断他的话。“好了，如果大家都准备好了，时候到了。”安娜挽起英格空着的那条胳膊，领着她和瑞德走到长凳旁等候的人群前面。

sentences.en: By now, everyone was holding candles that were lit one by one.
sentences.zh: 此时，每个人都手持蜡烛，被一一点亮。

sentences.en: King Jonas, Mari, and Elsa moved to the front, where Anna joined them, looking out on all the people who had gathered for this important moment in their kingdoms’ shared history.
sentences.zh: 乔纳斯国王、玛丽和艾莎走到前面，安娜也加入他们，望着为这两国共同历史的重要时刻而聚集的所有人。

sentences.en: Her eyes were on Inger’s. “Thank you all for coming today to help us unveil the Vesterland sisters’ memorial,” Anna said. “Their true story is long overdue,” continued Jonas. “And it is the hope of both Vesterland and Arendelle that people will come to this memorial site often to reflect on both sisters’ lives and what they did for their kingdom.” Anna moved to the sheet covering the statue. “And now, may we present, this memorial statue— The Love of Two Vesterland Sisters by Master Sculptor Helmut of Arendelle.” She and Kristoff pulled the sheet away, revealing a hand-carved statue of Sissel and Inger in a tight embrace.
sentences.zh: 她的目光落在英格身上。“感谢各位今天前来，帮我们为维斯特兰姐妹纪念园揭幕，”安娜说。“她们的真实故事早该被讲述，”乔纳斯接着说，“维斯特兰和阿伦黛尔都希望人们能常来这处纪念园，追思两姐妹的一生，以及她们为王国所做的贡献。”安娜走到盖着雕像的罩布前。“现在，请允许我们呈献这尊纪念雕像——阿伦黛尔雕塑大师赫尔穆特作品：《两姐妹之爱》。”她和克斯托夫揭开罩布，露出一尊手工雕刻、两姐妹紧紧相拥的雕像。

sentences.en: They were carved as their younger selves, looking vibrant and hopeful as they stared into one another’s eyes.
sentences.zh: 雕像雕刻的是她们年轻时的模样，两两相望，神采飞扬、充满希望。

sentences.en: This is the way the world should remember them, Anna thought, as a united front; two sisters who fought together for the betterment of Vesterland and who loved each other till their dying days; a young woman lost far too soon and the sister who loved her so much that she spent her life searching for her.
sentences.zh: 世界就该这样记住她们，安娜想，作为一个并肩的整体；两姐妹曾一同为维斯特兰的福祉而奋斗，至死相爱；一个过早逝去的少女，和一个如此爱她、用一生去寻找她的姐姐。

sentences.en: Inger let out a small gasp at the sight of her younger self with Sissel, then rose and made her way slowly to the statue.
sentences.zh: 看到年轻的自己和茜塞尔，英格轻轻倒吸一口气，随后起身，缓缓走向雕像。

sentences.en: Her granddaughter did the same, both of them touching the smooth stone and looking at it in wonder. “Do you like it?” Anna asked shyly, her hand moving to find Elsa’s.
sentences.zh: 孙女也照样做了，两人都抚摸着光滑的石头，惊奇地端详。“你们喜欢吗？”安娜羞涩地问，伸手去牵艾莎的手。

sentences.en: Inger looked at both queens with love in her teary eyes. “It’s perfect.
sentences.zh: 英格含泪的眼里满是爱意，望着两位女王。“它太完美了。

sentences.en: Absolutely perfect.” And just at that moment, a sudden gust of wind rustled through the bare trees, blowing the last of the autumn leaves through the knoll with such force that people held on to their hats and gasped in surprise.
sentences.zh: 绝对完美。”就在此刻，一阵突如其来的风吹过光秃秃的树，把最后几片秋叶猛地卷过草坡，人们只得按住帽子，惊讶地倒吸一口气。

sentences.en: Anna felt a smile come to her lips.

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-Two: Elsa
chapters.en:
“WHAT A DAY!” ANNA DECLARED as she collapsed onto Elsa’s bed in a dramatic swoon. She had changed into her favorite green nightgown and had taken her hair out of its braids. She looks younger like this, Elsa thought. As if she were still that little girl, begging Elsa to build a snowman.

Instead, she was a queen who had saved her kingdom.

Well, with a little help from her older sister, of course.

“Cuddle close, scooch in,” Elsa joked, pulling her sister to her. Anna lay her head on her shoulder, sighing happily.

“I didn’t think we could pull it off,” Anna murmured, cozying up to her sister. “I really didn’t. But in the end everyone came through.”

“A Polar Nights and a memorial celebration,” Elsa declared. “Not to mention my epic birthday surprise! It’s been quite a few weeks. Ones hopefully everyone will remember for years to come. I know I definitely will.”

Anna sighed dreamily. “Ah, memories. So glad to have those back.”

“Agreed,” Elsa concurred. “I stopped by Ahtohallan on the way back from the memorial, and everything seemed back to normal. I was able to pull up all the usual memories. It was nice seeing them again, let me tell you.”

“I bet,” Anna said wistfully. “I wish I could see for myself.”

“Well…” Elsa sat up in bed, her eyes shining with eagerness. “Actually, I have a little gift for you.”

“Gift? But it was just your birthday, not mine.”

“Oh, shush and let me share,” Elsa scolded. She gave her sister a mysterious grin, then closed her eyes, picturing the memory she’d pulled from Ahtohallan just for this occasion. Then she pushed out her hands, sending it through her fingers. When she opened her eyes, she saw a swirl of icy wind, whirling in the middle of the bedroom, forming moving shapes.

“Oh my goodness! It’s our parents. Are they on the ship?” asked Anna, mouth agape.

Elsa watched breathlessly as the scene unfolded: their mother and father, standing in some kind of ship’s cabin.

Mother’s eyes were filled with tears. “Maybe we made a mistake isolating them. Maybe we should have—”

“We did what we thought was best,” their father said firmly. “Only time will tell if it was right or wrong. But I have faith in them. They are young, but they are already so strong. And if anyone can help Elsa, it’s Anna.” He smiled softly. “There’s not much that girl can’t do.”

“You’re right about that,” their mother replied, shaking her head. “Her love could hold up the world.”

Their father nodded. “When the time comes, I truly believe they will do the right thing.”

“For Arendelle?”

“No.” Their father shook his head. “For each other.”

And with that, the shimmery vision faded, the ice dissolving into the air. For a moment, neither sister spoke. They just stared at the spot where their parents had stood. Then Elsa glanced over at Anna, catching her sister swiping a tear from her eyes.

“They really believed in us,” she whispered, her voice hoarse. “The whole time.”

“And they were right,” Elsa told her, feeling her own voice choke up. “I would be nothing without your love.”

She pulled Anna into her arms. They hugged tightly—so tightly that Elsa could barely breathe. But she didn’t care. She had her sister. She had her memories. The kingdom was safe.

The sun would rise again. And life would begin anew.

Suddenly the door banged open. The sisters turned to see Olaf, accompanied by Kristoff and Sven. The snowman carried a thick book of stories in his hand. He waved it at the two sisters.

“When’s our next campout?” he asked. “Because it’s my turn, finally, to tell a spooky story! And I’ve got the best one, too! You thought the draugr was scary? Let me tell you about the dreaded Pesta, who sweeps into town on a broom, bringing pesty pestilence and plague!”

Elsa groaned. She grabbed the book out of Olaf’s hand. Then she whistled for Gale to come through the open window and whisk it away. The Wind Spirit happily obliged.

“Aw! But this was such a good one!” Olaf griped as he watched the book sail through the window and disappear.

“No more scary stories,” Anna scolded, wagging a finger at him. “Only happy endings from here on out!”

Elsa smiled, slinging an arm over her sister’s shoulder. “Happy endings sound good to me,” she agreed. “And lots of memories, shared together.”

~ THE END ~
chapters.zh:
“多好的一天啊！”安娜一边夸张地倒在艾莎床上，一边宣布。

她换上了最爱的绿色睡裙，把头发从辫子里散开。

这样看起来她更年轻了，艾莎想。

仿佛她还是那个小姑娘，央求艾莎堆雪人。

可事实上，她是一位拯救了王国的女王。

嗯，当然也少不了姐姐的一点帮忙。“靠过来，挤一挤，”艾莎开玩笑地要把妹妹拉向自己。

安娜把头靠在她肩上，幸福地叹了口气。“我本以为我们办不到，”安娜依偎着姐姐喃喃道，“我真的以为办不到。

但最后大家都挺过来了。”“一场极夜节，一场纪念庆典，”艾莎宣布，“更别提我那超棒的生日惊喜！

这几个星期可真不寻常。

但愿大家在未来多年都能记得这几个星期。

我肯定会的。”安娜如梦般叹了口气。“啊，记忆。

真高兴把它们找回来了。”“同意，”艾莎赞同道，“从纪念园回来的路上我顺道去了阿托哈兰，一切似乎都恢复了正常。

我能调出所有平常的记忆了。

再次看到它们真让人高兴，跟你说。”“我猜也是，”安娜怅然地说，“真希望我能亲眼看看。”“嗯……”艾莎在床上坐直，眼里闪着期待的光。“其实，我有件小礼物要给你。”“礼物？

可刚过完的是你的生日，不是我的。”“噢，闭嘴听我说，”艾莎嗔怪道。

她神秘地朝妹妹一笑，然后闭上眼睛，回想那个专为此刻从阿托哈兰取出的记忆。

接着她伸出双手，让那段记忆从指间流淌而出。

她睁开眼时，看到一团冰风打着旋，在卧室中央盘旋，凝成活动的影像。“噢，天哪！

是我们的父母。

他们是在船上吗？”安娜目瞪口呆地问。

艾莎屏息看着画面展开：他们的母亲和父亲，站在一间像是船舱的房间里。

母亲的眼里噙着泪水。“也许我们把她们隔离起来是个错误。

也许我们本该——”“我们做了自认为最好的选择，”父亲坚定地说，“是对是错，只有时间能证明。

但我对她们有信心。

她们还年轻，却已经如此坚强。

要说谁能帮到艾莎，那只能是安娜。”他温柔地笑了，“那姑娘几乎无所不能。”“这点你说对了，”母亲摇着头回答，“她的爱足以托起整个世界。”父亲点了点头。“到那时，我真心相信她们会做出正确的事。”“为了阿伦黛尔？”“不，”父亲摇了摇头，“为了彼此。”话音落下，那闪烁的幻象渐渐淡去，冰溶散在空气中。

有片刻，姐妹俩谁都没说话。

她们只是望着父母曾经站立的地方。

接着艾莎瞥向安娜，正好看见妹妹用手抹去眼里的泪。“他们真的一直都相信我们，”她声音沙哑地低语，“自始至终。”“他们说得对，”艾莎告诉她，自己的声音也哽咽了，“没有你的爱，我将一无所有。”她把安娜揽进怀里。

她们紧紧相拥——紧得艾莎几乎喘不过气。

但她不在乎。

她有妹妹在身边。

她拥有她的记忆。

王国平安。

太阳会再次升起。

生活将重新开始。

突然，门被砰地推开。

姐妹俩转头，看见奥拉夫，身后跟着克斯托夫和斯文。

雪人手里捧着一本厚厚的故事书。

他朝两姐妹挥着书。“我们下回露营是什么时候？”他问，“因为终于轮到我讲恐怖故事了！

而且我这个最精彩！

你们觉得那具亡灵很吓人？

让我给你们讲讲可怕的佩斯塔，她骑着扫帚刮进镇子，带来烦人的瘟疫和灾祸！”艾莎叹了口气。

她一把从奥拉夫手里夺过书。

然后她吹口哨唤风灵从敞开的窗口进来，把书卷走。

风之精灵愉快地照做了。“哎！

这故事可好得很呢！”奥拉夫看着书飞出窗外消失，抱怨道。“不许再讲恐怖故事了，”安娜摇着手指训他，“从此往后，只要幸福结局！”艾莎笑了，一条胳膊搭在妹妹肩上。“幸福结局，听起来不错，”她赞同道，“还有好多记忆，我们一起分享。”～ 全文完 ～
